registry.name: Kelvin redefined by fixing the Boltzmann constant
registry.summary: Thermodynamic temperature, defined through the second law by Kelvin's Carnot scale, has been realized since 2019 by fixing $k_B$ exactly. The fixed value came from primary thermometry based on statistical mechanics: acoustic gas thermometry ($u^2=\gamma k_BT/m$), dielectric-constant gas thermometry and Johnson-noise thermometry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Neural quantum states and volume-law entanglement
registry.summary: Neural networks such as restricted Boltzmann machines and transformers serve as variational wavefunctions trained by variational Monte Carlo. An MPS's entanglement is capped at ln χ, but these networks can encode volume-law entanglement with polynomially many parameters (Deng, Li & Das Sarma 2017).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Born–Oppenheimer surfaces drive ab initio MD
registry.summary: The Born–Oppenheimer approximation separates electrons from nuclei, with small parameter (m_e/M)^{1/4}. Ab initio and Car–Parrinello MD move classical nuclei on the electronic ground-state energy surface. The approximation fails at conical intersections, where nonadiabatic methods such as surface hopping take over.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Amplitude estimation speeds up Monte Carlo quadratically
registry.summary: Amplitude amplification estimates an expectation value to error ε with O(1/ε) oracle calls, against O(1/ε²) samples classically (Montanaro 2015). It is the same 1/√N to 1/N jump as from the standard quantum limit to the Heisenberg limit.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Path-integral quantum Monte Carlo and the sign problem
registry.summary: Slicing imaginary time turns the quantum partition function into a classical ensemble of ring polymers that Metropolis sampling can handle. This is exact for bosons, but fermion exchange produces negative weights. That is the sign problem, which is NP-hard in general (Troyer–Wiese 2005).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Trotter splitting: symplectic integrators and quantum gates
registry.summary: Leapfrog and Strang symplectic integrators and split-step Schrödinger solvers use the same operator splitting that compiles e^{-iHt} into gates on a quantum computer. Higher-order Suzuki formulas and their commutator error bounds carry over directly.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Area-law entanglement makes MPS and DMRG efficient
registry.summary: The Schmidt rank across any cut of a matrix product state is at most the bond dimension, so the entanglement entropy obeys S ≤ ln χ. Ground states of gapped 1D Hamiltonians obey an area law (Hastings 2007), so they compress efficiently, and entanglement growth sets the cost of time evolution.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Tensor-network contraction vs quantum-advantage claims
registry.summary: After the random-circuit-sampling advantage claims (Arute et al. 2019), tensor-network contraction simulated the same circuits classically far faster than first estimated. The treewidth of a circuit's tensor network sets the classical cost, so tensor networks mark the moving boundary of quantum advantage.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Bohr–Einstein debates and the EPR argument
registry.summary: The 1927–35 Bohr–Einstein debates and the EPR argument treated completeness and locality as philosophical questions. Bell (1964) turned them into testable inequalities, which is why foundations of QM is where history and philosophy meet the laboratory.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: The quantum revolution, 1900–1927
registry.summary: Blackbody radiation (Planck 1900), the photoelectric effect (Einstein 1905) and atomic spectra with the Bohr model (1913) led to matrix and wave mechanics (1925–26). Spectroscopy drove the experiments, and the episode is the standard case study of theory change.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: No-go theorems as experimental metaphysics
registry.summary: The Bell, Kochen–Specker and PBR theorems turn questions about hidden variables, locality and the reality of the wavefunction into constraints that experiments can test. Philosophy of physics now argues over which premise to give up, such as measurement independence or outcome independence.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Measurement problem and rival interpretations
registry.summary: Unitary evolution and definite measurement outcomes conflict. Copenhagen, Everett's relative states, Bohmian mechanics, GRW collapse and QBism resolve this in different ways, and the meaning of Born-rule probability in many worlds is debated in both fields.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Typicality and ETH as foundations of statistical mechanics
registry.summary: Philosophy of statistical mechanics asks why equilibrium ensembles work. Canonical typicality (almost every pure state of system plus bath has a thermal reduced state) and ETH (every energy eigenstate looks thermal) answer this for isolated quantum systems without ensembles or the ergodic hypothesis.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Eigenproblems and special functions of quantum mechanics
registry.summary: Separation of variables, Sturm–Liouville eigenproblems and orthogonal polynomials (Hermite, Laguerre, Legendre) give the textbook spectra. Green's functions, contour integrals and asymptotic methods underpin perturbation theory, scattering and WKB.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Saddle points, Stokes lines and instantons
registry.summary: Semiclassics evaluates the path integral by stationary phase or steepest descent. Airy functions join WKB solutions at turning points, Stokes phenomena control tunnelling exponents, and Wick rotation turns tunnelling into Euclidean instanton saddles.
registry.map: \int\mathcal Dx\,e^{iS/\hbar}\approx\sum_{\rm cl}A_{\rm cl}\,e^{iS_{\rm cl}/\hbar},\ t\to-i\tau,\ \Gamma\propto e^{-S_E^{\rm inst}/\hbar}

registry.name: Analytic S-matrix: poles, resonances, dispersion
registry.summary: Causality makes partial-wave S-matrices analytic in complex momentum. Bound states are poles on the positive imaginary k axis and resonances are poles below the real axis that give Breit–Wigner peaks. The optical theorem and dispersion relations tie forward amplitudes to total cross sections.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Lippmann–Schwinger equation and the Born series
registry.summary: The outgoing Helmholtz Green's function turns the Schrödinger equation into an integral equation. Iterating it gives the Born series, and its far-field limit gives the scattering amplitude f(θ).
registry.map: \psi=\phi+G_0^{(+)}V\psi,\ G_0^{(+)}(\mathbf r,\mathbf r')=-\frac{m}{2\pi\hbar^2}\frac{e^{ik|\mathbf r-\mathbf r'|}}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r'|}

registry.name: Schmidt decomposition is the singular value decomposition
registry.summary: Arrange a bipartite pure state's amplitudes as a matrix and its SVD is the Schmidt form. The squared singular values are the eigenvalues of the reduced state, so entanglement entropy and Schmidt rank are matrix invariants. The same SVD truncation drives DMRG.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dirac notation and operator algebra
registry.summary: The working tools of QM are linear-algebra results: commutators and simultaneous diagonalisation, unitary changes of basis, ladder-operator algebras, and rigged Hilbert spaces for the continuous spectra of position and momentum.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Spectral theorem as the measurement postulate
registry.summary: States are rays in a Hilbert space and observables are self-adjoint operators. The spectral theorem supplies the possible outcomes (eigenvalues) and projectors that give the Born rule and state update. Gleason's theorem shows this is the only consistent probability measure for dimension ≥ 3.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Berry phase as holonomy of a U(1) connection
registry.summary: The Berry connection is a connection on the line bundle of eigenstates over parameter space. Its curvature 2-form integrates to the Berry phase, and over closed surfaces to integer Chern numbers (Simon 1983). The quantum geometric tensor combines the Fubini–Study metric with the Berry curvature.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

registry.name: Quantum-limited amplifiers for qubit readout
registry.summary: Dispersive readout of superconducting qubits needs Josephson parametric or travelling-wave amplifiers that work near the Caves bound: a phase-insensitive amplifier must add at least half a quantum of noise. The same SQUID and Josephson technology reads out cryogenic detectors.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cryogenic sensors as single-photon detectors
registry.summary: Cryogenic sensors and the noise analysis of instrumentation have become quantum-optics hardware. Transition-edge sensors resolve photon number with about 95% efficiency, and superconducting nanowire detectors reach about 98% efficiency with few-picosecond jitter. Dark counts and dead time are the other figures of merit.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum Fisher information and the Cramér–Rao bound
registry.summary: Optimising the classical Cramér–Rao bound over all quantum measurements gives the quantum Fisher information (Braunstein–Caves 1994). N independent probes give F_Q = N, the standard quantum limit; entangled probes reach up to N², the Heisenberg limit.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Clock uncertainty budgets and Allan deviation
registry.summary: Clock accuracy is quoted as a GUM-style budget of Type B systematic shifts (blackbody, Zeeman, Stark, motional) added in quadrature. Stability is quoted as the Allan deviation, which quantum projection noise ultimately limits. This is how the Al+/Hg+ ratio reached the 17th decimal place.
sources: Rosenband et al. (2008). "Frequency Ratio of Al+and Hg+Single-Ion Optical Clocks; Metrology at the 17th Decimal Place". *Science* 319, 1808. [doi:10.1126/science.1154622](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1154622)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rotation symmetry labels states and selection rules
registry.summary: Rotational invariance of H makes j and m good quantum numbers. The Wigner–Eckart theorem splits every tensor-operator matrix element into a Clebsch–Gordan coefficient times a reduced element, which gives the dipole selection rules.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Atomic parity violation and electron EDM searches
registry.summary: Z-boson exchange mixes S and P states, so the forbidden Cs 6S–7S transition gains a parity-odd amplitude that measures the weak charge Q_W (Wood et al. 1997). Electron-EDM searches in heavy atoms and polar molecules test T, and hence CP, violation; the best bound is |d_e| < 4.1×10^{-30} e·cm (JILA HfF+, 2023).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: PT symmetry and exceptional points
registry.summary: A non-Hermitian Hamiltonian that commutes with the antiunitary PT operator has a real spectrum while the symmetry is unbroken. At the breaking threshold, eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce at an exceptional point: H becomes a non-diagonalisable Jordan block, the eigenvalues meet at a square-root branch point, and the splitting grows as √ε.
sources: Bender & Boettcher (1998). "Real Spectra in Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians Having P T Symmetry". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 5243. [doi:10.1103/physrevlett.80.5243](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevlett.80.5243)

registry.name: Dyson's threefold way fixes chaotic level statistics
registry.summary: Spectra of chaotic systems follow random-matrix statistics (Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit 1984). Antiunitary symmetry picks the ensemble: GOE if T² = +1, GUE if T is broken, GSE if T² = −1. The level-repulsion exponent β is the diagnostic.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kramers degeneracy from T² = −1 for half-integer spin
registry.summary: Time reversal is antiunitary and acts on spin as Θ = e^{-iπS_y/ħ}K, so Θ² = (−1)^{2S}. With an odd number of electrons, every level is at least doubly degenerate unless a magnetic field breaks T. This is the origin of the protected Kramers pairs in topological insulators.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Spin is a projective representation of SO(3)
registry.summary: Angular-momentum operators obey the su(2) algebra, whose irreducible representations give j = 0, 1/2, 1, …. Half-integer spin exists because SU(2) double-covers SO(3): a 2π rotation multiplies a spinor by −1, as seen in neutron interferometry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hidden SO(4) symmetry of the hydrogen atom
registry.summary: On bound states, the angular momentum L and the scaled Runge–Lenz vector K generate so(4) ≅ su(2)⊕su(2). Pauli (1926) used this to obtain the Bohr levels algebraically, and it explains the n² degeneracy across ℓ. SU(3) plays the same role for the 3D isotropic oscillator.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum Noether: conserved generators commute with H
registry.summary: By Wigner's theorem, symmetries act as unitary or antiunitary operators. If a continuous symmetry e^{-iθG/ħ} leaves H invariant, then [G,H] = 0 and the distribution of G is conserved. This is the operator form of Noether's theorem: momentum from translations, J from rotations, charge from U(1).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: BEC breaks U(1); Bogoliubov phonon is the Goldstone mode
registry.summary: The condensate order parameter ψ = √n e^{iθ} breaks the global phase symmetry that goes with atom-number conservation. The gapless Bogoliubov sound mode is the Goldstone boson, and its sound speed sets the Landau critical velocity for superfluid flow.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Time crystals break time-translation symmetry
registry.summary: Wilczek's (2012) equilibrium time crystal is ruled out by the Watanabe–Oshikawa no-go theorem. Instead, periodically driven many-body systems, which conserve quasienergy rather than energy, break the discrete Floquet time-translation symmetry and respond at period 2T. Many-body localization or prethermalization protects this order, which has been seen with trapped ions, NV centres and superconducting qubits.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: The SI second is a caesium hyperfine frequency
registry.summary: Since 1967 the second has been defined by fixing the Cs ground-state hyperfine frequency. Time and frequency are the most precisely realised SI quantities, and the metre is traced to them through the fixed value of c.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Unitary Fermi gas: universality from a missing scale
registry.summary: At a Feshbach resonance the scattering length diverges and drops out, leaving density as the only scale. Dimensional analysis then forces every observable to be a universal number times its free-Fermi-gas value, the Bertsch parameter ξ being one example. Dilute neutron matter shares the same universality.

registry.name: AMO measurements determine α and m_e for CODATA
registry.summary: The fine-structure constant comes from atom-recoil interferometry (h/m for Cs and Rb) and from the Penning-trap electron g-factor combined with QED. These AMO inputs dominate the CODATA values of α, R∞ and m_e, and the ~5σ gap between the Cs and Rb values remains unresolved.

registry.name: Clock ratios test the constancy of α and m_p/m_e
registry.summary: Different transitions depend on α and μ = m_p/m_e with different sensitivities, so repeated ratios between clocks (Al+/Hg+, Yb+ E3/E2, Cs/Sr) bound present-day drifts at the ~10^{-18} per year level. The same ratios search for ultralight dark matter, which would make the constants oscillate.

registry.name: Hydrogen spectroscopy, R∞ and the proton radius
registry.summary: The Rydberg constant and the proton charge radius are fitted together to hydrogen and deuterium transition frequencies. The muonic-hydrogen Lamb shift (2010) gave a radius 4% smaller. The puzzle eased once newer hydrogen measurements and CODATA 2018/2022 moved to about 0.84 fm.

registry.name: Optical clocks and redefining the second
registry.summary: Optical lattice and ion clocks now beat the Cs primary standard by about 100×. The CIPM roadmap therefore plans an optical redefinition of the second around 2030, continuing the 2019 move to defining units by fixed constants.

registry.name: Scientific computing toolkit powers numerical relativity
registry.summary: Numerical relativity is a flagship application of large-scale scientific computing: adaptive mesh refinement, high-order finite-difference and multidomain spectral solvers, constraint damping and parallel HPC turned the Einstein equations into working codes, culminating in the 2005 binary-black-hole breakthrough.

registry.name: Machine learning for GW searches, glitches and inference
registry.summary: Convolutional networks detect compact-binary signals and classify instrumental glitches (Gravity Spy), normalizing-flow simulation-based inference gives full posteriors in seconds, and ML surrogates of numerical-relativity waveforms speed up parameter estimation, complementing matched filtering and stochastic sampling.

registry.name: MCMC and nested sampling for GW source parameters
registry.summary: Posteriors over the ~15 parameters of a compact binary are sampled with Markov-chain Monte Carlo and nested sampling (LALInference, Bilby), direct descendants of the Metropolis algorithm; nested sampling also yields the Bayesian evidence used for model selection and tests of GR.

registry.name: Monte Carlo over geometries: causal dynamical triangulations
registry.summary: Causal dynamical triangulations define the gravitational path integral as a sum over causal simplicial geometries, Wick-rotated and sampled by Markov-chain Monte Carlo as in lattice field theory; simulations find a phase with an extended de Sitter-like 4D geometry whose spectral dimension runs from ~4 at large scales to ~2 at short scales.

registry.name: Well-posed hyperbolic formulations and PDE integrators
registry.summary: The Einstein equations become a stable initial-value problem only in strongly hyperbolic formulations (generalized harmonic, BSSN with moving punctures); they are then evolved by method-of-lines Runge–Kutta with finite differences plus AMR or spectral methods, with constraint damping controlling constraint growth.

registry.name: MERA and holographic codes as discrete AdS
registry.summary: In a tensor network, a boundary region's entropy is bounded by the number of bonds a minimal cut crosses times log χ, a discrete Ryu–Takayanagi formula; MERA's renormalization direction resembles a hyperbolic slice of AdS (Swingle), and holographic codes built from perfect tensors model bulk reconstruction as quantum error correction.
registry.breaks: Exact RT behaviour holds only for special (stabilizer or random) networks with flat entanglement spectra; there is no sub-AdS locality or Einstein dynamics, and MERA's emergent geometry has been argued to be closer to de Sitter or light-cone than to a spatial AdS slice.

registry.name: Hole argument and the meaning of general covariance
registry.summary: Einstein's 1913 hole argument, in which diffeomorphism-related solutions agree outside a region but differ inside it, seemed to make generally covariant field equations indeterministic; its resolution (spacetime points have no identity apart from the metric) let Einstein accept general covariance in 1915 and started the modern substantivalism–relationism debate.

registry.name: Problem of time in canonical quantum gravity
registry.summary: Canonical quantization of GR gives a Hamiltonian constraint (the Wheeler–DeWitt equation) with no external time, the 'frozen formalism'; loop quantum gravity and philosophy of physics both face the task of defining dynamics through relational observables and of saying what change means in a timeless theory.

registry.name: GR as a showcase of mathematical-physics methods
registry.summary: GR brings many mathematical methods together: the Einstein equations as a constrained nonlinear hyperbolic PDE system, Green's-function solutions of linearized gravity, perturbation expansions (post-Newtonian, black-hole perturbation theory) and spin-weighted spherical harmonics for radiation.
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)

registry.name: Euclidean periodicity fixes the Hawking temperature
registry.summary: Wick-rotating the Schwarzschild metric gives a smooth Euclidean geometry only if imaginary time is periodic with period 2πc/κ; since thermal Green's functions are periodic in imaginary time (KMS condition), that period is ħ/k_BT, which is the Hawking temperature (Gibbons–Hawking).

registry.name: Ringdown quasinormal modes as Green's-function poles
registry.summary: Black-hole ringdown is a sum of quasinormal modes: complex frequencies at the poles of the perturbation Green's function in the lower half ω-plane (plus a branch cut that gives late-time tails), computed by Leaver's continued fractions or WKB; they depend only on mass and spin, which enables black-hole spectroscopy.

registry.name: String worldsheets as Riemann surfaces
registry.summary: Perturbative string amplitudes are integrals over moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces; worldsheet conformal invariance makes the theory a 2D CFT, worked with holomorphic functions, contour-integral operator product expansions and modular invariance of the torus amplitude.

registry.name: Retarded Green's function yields the quadrupole formula
registry.summary: In Lorenz gauge, linearized gravity is a sourced wave equation for the trace-reversed perturbation; the same retarded Green's function as in electrodynamics gives the far-zone field and hence the quadrupole formula for gravitational radiation.

registry.name: Random-subsystem entropy gives the Page curve
registry.summary: Averaging subsystem entanglement entropy over Haar-random pure states in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space gives nearly maximal entropy for the smaller factor; applied to a black hole plus its radiation, this gives the Page curve (radiation entropy rises, then falls after the Page time), which unitarity requires and Hawking's calculation misses.

registry.name: Singularity theorems and global causal structure
registry.summary: Global Lorentzian geometry (the Raychaudhuri focusing equation, trapped surfaces, conformal compactification into Penrose diagrams) proves that a trapped surface plus an energy condition implies geodesic incompleteness, so black-hole singularities are generic rather than artifacts of symmetry.

registry.name: Lorentzian geometry is the language of gravity
registry.summary: GR models gravity as curvature of a Lorentzian manifold: free fall is geodesic motion, the equivalence principle is local flatness in normal coordinates, and tidal forces are the Riemann tensor acting through geodesic deviation.

registry.name: Contracted Bianchi identity fixes the Einstein tensor
registry.summary: The contracted Bianchi identity makes the Einstein tensor identically divergence-free, so it can consistently be set equal to a conserved stress–energy tensor; the field equations are a statement in Riemannian geometry about Ricci curvature.

registry.name: Petrov classification and algebraically special metrics
registry.summary: Classifying the Weyl tensor by its principal null directions (Petrov types, Newman–Penrose formalism) organizes the exact solutions; Kerr found the rotating black hole by searching for algebraically special vacuum metrics, and the Goldberg–Sachs theorem links that degeneracy to shear-free null congruences.
sources: Kerr (1963). "Gravitational Field of a Spinning Mass as an Example of Algebraically Special Metrics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 11, 237. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237)

registry.name: Lovelock's theorem defines the routes to modified gravity
registry.summary: In four dimensions the only symmetric, divergence-free rank-2 tensor built from the metric and its first two derivatives is a combination of G_μν and g_μν; every modified-gravity theory escapes this by adding fields (scalar-tensor, Horndeski), higher derivatives (f(R)), extra dimensions or nonlocality.

registry.name: Template-bank metric on the waveform manifold
registry.summary: The fractional SNR lost between neighbouring templates defines a Riemannian metric on source-parameter space, and template banks are lattices laid out with this metric; the related Fisher information matrix gives forecast parameter uncertainties.

registry.name: Ashtekar connection variables recast GR as gauge theory
registry.summary: Rewriting canonical GR with an SU(2) connection and a densitized triad (Ashtekar, later Ashtekar–Barbero) gives it a Yang–Mills-like phase space; holonomies of the connection and fluxes of the triad are the basic variables quantized in loop quantum gravity.

registry.name: Lorentz transformations as isometries of Minkowski metric
registry.summary: Minkowski's reformulation makes Lorentz transformations the isometries of a flat metric of Lorentzian signature; four-vectors and tensors make laws manifestly covariant, and GR reuses the same machinery for curved metrics.

registry.name: VLBI: heterodyne receivers, maser clocks and correlators
registry.summary: The Event Horizon Telescope is an Earth-sized interferometer: each station down-converts 1.3 mm signals with heterodyne receivers and time-stamps them with hydrogen-maser clocks, and correlators combine the recordings into visibilities whose diffraction limit resolves the ~40 μas ring; imaging is then an ill-posed inverse problem solved with regularized and Bayesian methods.

registry.name: Standard quantum limit and squeezed light in GW detectors
registry.summary: Interferometric GW detectors are limited by fundamental instrument noise: photon shot noise and radiation-pressure noise combine into the standard quantum limit, thermal noise follows the fluctuation–dissipation theorem, and injecting squeezed vacuum (frequency-dependent since O4) beats the shot-noise limit.

registry.name: Hellings–Downs correlation and Bayesian evidence in PTAs
registry.summary: A stochastic GW background makes timing residuals correlated between pulsar pairs according to the Hellings–Downs curve; PTA collaborations weigh evidence for it with Bayes factors and frequentist statistics against common-spectrum red noise, reaching ~3–4σ significance in 2023.

registry.name: CPT tests double as Lorentz-invariance tests
registry.summary: The CPT theorem follows from Lorentz invariance plus locality, and in local interacting QFT CPT violation implies Lorentz violation; so kaon mass differences, antihydrogen spectroscopy and Penning-trap particle–antiparticle comparisons constrain Lorentz-violating coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension.

registry.name: AdS isometries equal the boundary conformal group
registry.summary: The isometry group of AdS_{d+1} is SO(d,2), exactly the conformal group of d-dimensional Minkowski space (extended to PSU(2,2|4) for AdS5×S5 and N=4 SYM); this symmetry match underlies the bulk-field/boundary-operator dictionary, where bulk mass fixes the operator's scaling dimension.

registry.summary: Special relativity says physics is invariant under the Poincaré group; Wigner's unitary irreducible representations classify particles by mass and spin, and the double cover SL(2,C) of the Lorentz group gives spinors.

registry.summary: Each Killing vector of a black-hole metric gives a quantity conserved along geodesics (energy from ∂_t, angular momentum from ∂_φ), and Komar integrals define mass and spin; Kerr also has a Killing tensor that gives the Carter constant, a hidden symmetry that makes geodesic motion integrable.

registry.summary: Because diffeomorphisms are a local gauge symmetry, Noether's second theorem gives no gauge-invariant local energy density for gravity; GW energy is defined only by averaging over wavelengths (Isaacson tensor) or as charges at null infinity, where the Bondi mass decreases as waves escape and BMS supertranslation charges are tied to the gravitational memory effect.

registry.name: Scale-free vacuum GR: one simulation serves all masses
registry.summary: The vacuum Einstein equations have no intrinsic length scale, so binary-black-hole simulations are run in units of total mass M and rescale to any mass: times and lengths scale as GM/c^3 and GM/c^2, and strain is (GM/c^2)/D times a universal function. registry.name: Constancy of constants tests the equivalence principle
registry.summary: Local position invariance, part of the Einstein equivalence principle, requires dimensionless constants such as α and m_p/m_e to be the same everywhere and at all times; atomic-clock comparisons, the Oklo natural reactor and quasar spectra bound their drift, and any variation would generically also violate the weak equivalence principle.

registry.summary: After Wick rotation, e^{iS} becomes e^{-S_E}, so lattice QFT is a statistical-mechanics problem sampled by Markov-chain Monte Carlo (heat bath, HMC). It inherits that field's problems: autocorrelation, critical slowing down toward the continuum limit, and the sign problem when the weight is not positive.

registry.name: Tensor networks for lattice gauge theories
registry.summary: In the Hamiltonian formulation, MPS and DMRG simulate 1+1D lattice gauge theories such as the Schwinger model without importance sampling, so they avoid the sign problem at finite density, with a θ term and in real time. Gauss's law can be built into gauge-invariant tensors, and these results benchmark quantum simulators of gauge theories.

registry.name: Particle physics as the archetype of big science
registry.summary: The path from cosmic-ray and accelerator discoveries to the Standard Model is a central case study in the history of physics. The field also defined 'big science': Lawrence's cyclotron laboratory, CERN (1954) as a model of international collaboration, and LHC collaborations with thousands of authors.

registry.name: Naturalness as an argument form
registry.summary: The hierarchy problem rests on naturalness, a fine-tuning argument that philosophy of physics studies as a heuristic. Its past success (the charm-quark mass estimated from K⁰ mixing) and the LHC's null searches for natural new physics have made its epistemic status an open debate.

registry.name: Dispersive hadronic vacuum polarization for muon g−2
registry.summary: Analyticity and the optical theorem turn the measured e⁺e⁻→hadrons cross section into the leading hadronic contribution to the muon g−2 through a Kramers–Kronig-type integral. Tensions among the e⁺e⁻ data sets (CMD-3 versus earlier experiments) and with lattice QCD are why this term decides the Standard Model comparison.

registry.name: Holomorphy and the Virasoro algebra in 2D CFT
registry.summary: In two dimensions the conformal maps are exactly the holomorphic functions, so the stress tensor splits into T(z) and T̄(z̄). Radial quantization turns charges into contour integrals, Ward identities and operator-product expansions follow from the residue theorem, and the Virasoro generators are Laurent coefficients.

registry.name: S-matrix analyticity, dispersion relations and cuts
registry.summary: Causality makes scattering amplitudes analytic in the energy variables, so they obey dispersion relations, the relativistic version of Kramers–Kronig. The optical theorem and Cutkosky rules give the discontinuities across branch cuts, and the modern unitarity method rebuilds loop amplitudes from their cuts.

registry.name: The Feynman propagator is a Green's function
registry.summary: The propagator is the Green's function of the Klein–Gordon (or Dirac) operator, with the iε prescription choosing time-ordered boundary conditions, so the Feynman-diagram expansion is a Born series in Green's functions. Differential equations in the kinematic variables are also a main tool for evaluating loop integrals.

registry.name: Neutrino mixing as a unitary basis change
registry.summary: Flavour and mass eigenstates are related by the unitary PMNS matrix, so oscillation is the time evolution of a superposition of energy eigenstates. The two-flavour formula is the two-level Rabi formula, and the MSW effect is adiabatic passage through an avoided crossing of the matter Hamiltonian's eigenvalues.

registry.name: CKM matrix from bi-unitary diagonalization of Yukawas
registry.summary: Quark mass matrices are diagonalized by separate left and right unitary rotations (a singular-value decomposition), and the CKM matrix is the mismatch between the up- and down-type left rotations. Parameter counting leaves (n−1)(n−2)/2 CP phases, one for three generations, and the Jarlskog invariant measures it independently of basis.

registry.name: Instanton number as a Chern class; index theorem
registry.summary: Instantons are classified by the second Chern (Pontryagin) number of the gauge bundle, and the θ term integrates that characteristic class. The Atiyah–Singer index theorem ties it to the Dirac operator's zero modes, which is the topological content of the axial anomaly.

registry.name: Gauge fields as connections, field strength as curvature
registry.summary: A gauge potential is a connection on a principal bundle and the field strength is its curvature, the same structures as the spin connection and Riemann tensor of general relativity. Wilson loops are holonomies, and a Bianchi identity holds in both.
registry.breaks: The gravitational connection is soldered to the tangent bundle and fixed by the metric; internal gauge connections live on an abstract bundle with no metric to determine them.

registry.name: Collider physics as measurement at scale
registry.summary: Collider experiments use the full measurement chain: calibration, unfolding of detector response, systematic uncertainties as nuisance parameters, and blind analyses. registry.summary: Haloscopes such as ADMX convert dark-matter axions into microwave photons in a magnetized cavity, and the ~10⁻²² W signal makes the scan rate scale as 1/T_sys². Josephson parametric amplifiers at the standard quantum limit, squeezed states (HAYSTAC) and qubit-based photon counting are the enabling detector physics.

registry.name: Shared signal chain: sensors, preamps and noise
registry.summary: In a particle detector, ionization or light becomes charge, which charge-sensitive preamplifiers amplify and shape, with thermal and shot noise setting the equivalent noise charge. Photomultipliers, SiPMs and silicon sensors are common to both nodes, and triggers are real-time filters working under bandwidth limits.

registry.name: The Standard Model as representation theory
registry.summary: The Standard Model is defined by its gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) and by assigning each field to an irreducible representation, while Wigner's unitary Poincaré irreps label particles by mass and spin. Charges, multiplets and allowed couplings follow from group theory.

registry.name: Strong CP problem and the Peccei–Quinn axion
registry.summary: The QCD θ term is P- and T-odd and would give the neutron an electric dipole moment; the bound |d_n| < 1.8×10⁻²⁶ e cm forces |θ̄| ≲ 10⁻¹⁰. The Peccei–Quinn solution makes θ̄ dynamical: the axion, a pseudo-Goldstone boson, relaxes it to zero.

registry.name: CP violation and the CPT theorem
registry.summary: CP violation in kaons and B mesons is the experimental side of discrete-symmetry theory, and by the CPT theorem it implies T violation, since observed directly in both systems. With three generations the CKM matrix carries exactly one physical CP phase.

registry.name: Parity violation built into chiral SU(2)_L
registry.summary: Lee and Yang's 1956 proposal and Wu's 1957 cobalt-60 experiment showed that the weak interaction violates parity maximally. Electroweak theory encodes this by putting only left-handed fermions in SU(2)_L doublets (V−A currents), so the gauge representations themselves break P and C, while CP survives up to the CKM phase.

registry.name: SU(5) and SO(10) embeddings of the Standard Model

registry.name: Graded Lie algebras evade Coleman–Mandula
registry.summary: Coleman–Mandula rules out any Lie-group symmetry of the S-matrix that mixes spacetime and internal symmetries non-trivially. Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius showed that the only loophole is a graded algebra with fermionic generators, which is supersymmetry, whose anticommutator closes on the momentum.

registry.summary: The eightfold way sorts hadrons into flavour-SU(3) octets and decuplets, and the Gell-Mann–Okubo mass formula predicted the Ω⁻. The quark model reads hadrons as colour singlets in tensor products of 3 and 3̄, and the same products list the allowed tetraquark and pentaquark structures.

registry.summary: Quarks sit in the fundamental and gluons in the adjoint of SU(3), and the group invariants C_F = 4/3, C_A = 3 and T_F = 1/2 fix the β-function, the splitting functions and the colour factors. Gluon self-coupling through the non-abelian structure constants gives asymptotic freedom, and large-N_c expansions treat N as a parameter.

registry.summary: Making a global symmetry local forces in a gauge field that couples to the Noether current, and Noether's second theorem says local symmetries give identities rather than new charges. In quantum theory these become the Ward–Takahashi and Slavnov–Taylor identities, which protect charge universality and renormalizability.

The leftover custodial SU(2) gives ρ = 1 at tree level, and the Higgs boson is the radial (amplitude) mode.

This is Nambu's superconductivity analogy carried into hadron physics, and chiral perturbation theory is its low-energy effective theory.

registry.summary: The self-consistent Green's function method computes nuclear spectral functions from Dyson's equation, and its self-energy is a microscopic nucleon-nucleus optical potential, uniting structure and reaction theory with propagator mathematics.

registry.name: Shared detector electronics and noise limits
registry.summary: Nuclear spectroscopy defined the charge-sensitive preamplifier, pulse shaping, photomultiplier and SiPM readout and the Fano and series/parallel noise analysis now generic to instrumentation.

registry.name: Bayesian extraction of QGP transport coefficients
registry.summary: Temperature-dependent eta/s and zeta/s are inferred by Bayesian calibration of hydrodynamic models against flow data, with Gaussian-process emulators and posterior uncertainty, the same parameter-estimation machinery used in cosmology.

registry.name: Bayesian multi-messenger inference of the dense-matter EOS
registry.summary: The neutron-star EOS is inferred by Bayesian combination of chiral-EFT priors, heavy-pulsar masses, NICER pulse profiles and GW tidal deformabilities, using nonparametric (Gaussian-process, neural-network) EOS priors.
registry.breaks: Prior choices at densities without data strongly shape posteriors on the maximum mass and quark-matter questions.

registry.name: Neutron-lifetime puzzle and combining discrepant data
registry.summary: Beam (about 888 s) and bottle (about 878 s) neutron lifetimes disagree by about 4 sigma; PDG scale factors, Birge ratios and Bayesian treatments of unknown systematics are used to combine them, and the choice matters for BBN and |V_ud|.

registry.name: Bayesian EFT truncation errors for nuclear forces
registry.summary: Chiral EFT predictions now carry theory error bars from Bayesian models of the omitted orders in Q/Lambda, treated as random coefficients with a learned scale, an EFT application of statistical inference.

registry.name: Radioactive decay as the model Poisson process
registry.summary: Radioactive decay is the textbook Poisson process: counts have variance equal to the mean, intervals are exponential, and counting statistics, dead-time and background subtraction are the reference examples of uncertainty propagation.
registry.breaks: Detector dead time and electronics make observed counts sub-Poissonian, and very short-lived sources violate stationarity.

registry.name: Neutron and nuclear EDMs as tests of T and CP
registry.summary: A permanent electric dipole moment of the neutron or a nucleus violates P and T; the neutron EDM bound underlies the strong CP problem, and octupole-deformed nuclei such as 225Ra enhance Schiff moments by orders of magnitude.
registry.breaks: Converting EDM limits to CP-violating parameters needs nuclear and hadronic matrix elements with large uncertainties.

registry.name: Parity violation in nuclear beta decay
registry.summary: Wu's 1957 measurement of the electron asymmetry from polarized 60Co showed the weak interaction maximally violates parity, establishing the V-A structure of beta decay.

registry.name: Isospin and Wigner SU(4) symmetry of nuclear forces
registry.summary: Charge independence of nuclear forces makes isospin an SU(2) symmetry with protons and neutrons as a doublet; Wigner's combined spin-isospin SU(4) supermultiplets explain why light-nucleus binding and Gamow-Teller patterns follow the 4-fold degeneracy.
registry.breaks: Isospin is broken by Coulomb forces and the u-d quark mass difference (~1 percent), and SU(4) is broken strongly by spin-orbit forces in heavier nuclei.

registry.name: Elliott SU(3) and interacting-boson dynamical symmetries
registry.summary: Collective rotation emerges from the shell model through Elliott's SU(3) for the harmonic oscillator, and the interacting boson model's U(6) group chains U(5), SU(3) and O(6) give the vibrational, rotational and gamma-soft limits of nuclear spectra.
registry.breaks: Real nuclei lie between limits and spin-orbit coupling breaks Elliott SU(3) beyond the sd shell (pseudo- and quasi-SU(3) partly restore it).

registry.name: Seniority and quasispin: pairing as an SU(2) algebra
registry.summary: Racah's seniority scheme and Kerman's quasispin show that pair creation and annihilation in a j-shell close an SU(2) algebra, which makes the pairing Hamiltonian exactly solvable and explains constant 2+ energies in semi-magic nuclei.
registry.breaks: Seniority is exact only in a single j-shell or with degenerate orbits; multi-j shells and quadrupole forces mix seniorities.

registry.name: Conserved vector current and superallowed ft values
registry.summary: The vector weak current is the Noether current of isospin (CVC), so Fermi matrix elements of superallowed 0+ to 0+ decays are fixed by symmetry; after small isospin-breaking and radiative corrections all ft values agree, which tests CVC and gives |V_ud|.
registry.breaks: Isospin-breaking corrections delta_C are model-dependent and are the leading theory uncertainty.

registry.name: Chiral restoration and O(4) universality
registry.summary: The QCD transition is chiral-symmetry restoration; Pisarski and Wilczek argued that for two massless flavours it falls in the 3D O(4) universality class, and lattice data at physical masses show a crossover with O(4) scaling remnants.
registry.breaks: Explicit quark masses turn the transition into a crossover, and the U(1)_A anomaly strength affects the universality class.

registry.name: Pions as Goldstone bosons organize nuclear forces
registry.summary: Spontaneous breaking of QCD's chiral SU(2)xSU(2) symmetry makes pions light pseudo-Goldstone bosons with derivative couplings; this fixes one-pion exchange as the long-range nuclear force and Weinberg's power counting in Q/Lambda_chi.

registry.name: Nuclear deformation and pairing as broken symmetries
registry.summary: Deformed mean fields break rotational symmetry and BCS pairing breaks particle number; in finite nuclei the broken symmetry shows up as rotational bands (Anderson-tower rotations) and pairing rotations, restored by projection.

registry.name: Linear canonical transforms in Fresnel optics
registry.summary: Paraxial propagation through any ABCD system is the Collins integral, which is the wave (metaplectic) representation of the linear canonical transformation given by the symplectic ray matrix. Free space acts as a Fresnel transform and a thin lens as a quadratic phase. A graded-index medium, whose ray Hamiltonian is a harmonic oscillator, performs a fractional Fourier transform that becomes the full Fourier transform after a quarter period.
registry.breaks: The correspondence is exact only in the paraxial limit. Aberrations make the ray map nonlinear, and the wave propagator then stops being a simple metaplectic integral.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Eikonal equation is the Hamilton–Jacobi equation
registry.summary: The wavefronts S=const of the eikonal equation |∇S|²=n² are level sets of Hamilton's characteristic function, and rays are its characteristics. Hamilton built this characteristic-function method for optics and carried it over to dynamics in 1834–35. Schrödinger later completed this optico-mechanical analogy into wave mechanics.

registry.name: Ray optics as Hamiltonian flow; étendue as Liouville
registry.summary: If the optical axis z is taken as time, rays obey Hamilton's equations with H=−√(n²−p²) and transverse momentum p=n sinθ. Paraxial ABCD matrices are symplectic in the reduced variables (y, nθ). Conservation of étendue and radiance is Liouville's theorem, and it caps solar concentration at n²/sin²θ_sun.
registry.map: H=-\sqrt{n^2(\mathbf q,z)-\mathbf p^2};\ M^TJM=J\ (\det M=1\text{ in }(y,n\theta));\ n^2\,dA\,d\Omega=\text{const}
registry.breaks: Liouville's theorem holds only for lossless systems without scattering. Diffraction blurs the phase-space picture at the scale of λ, where the Wigner function replaces the ray density.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Charged-particle Lagrangian and minimal coupling
registry.summary: The Lorentz force follows from Lagrange's equations with the velocity-dependent potential U=q(φ−v·A), and the canonical momentum p=mv+qA differs from the kinetic momentum. A gauge transformation adds the total derivative q dχ/dt to L and leaves the motion unchanged. This is the classical root of gauge invariance and of the Aharonov–Bohm phase q∮A·dl/ħ.
registry.map: L=\tfrac12mv^2-q\phi+q\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf A;\ \mathbf p=m\mathbf v+q\mathbf A;\ H=\frac{(\mathbf p-q\mathbf A)^2}{2m}+q\phi;\ L\to L+q\frac{d\chi}{dt}
registry.breaks: Classically only the fields matter. That the potentials themselves have physical effects (the Aharonov–Bohm effect) appears only in quantum mechanics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fermat's principle and the principle of least action
registry.summary: Light rays make the optical path stationary in the same way that mechanical trajectories make the action stationary. In Maupertuis' form δ∫p ds=0, ray optics maps onto mechanics with the refractive index in the role of momentum, so Snell's law becomes conservation of momentum parallel to the interface.
registry.breaks: The map holds at fixed energy, which means a single frequency. The particle's speed is proportional to n, while light's phase velocity is c/n. Hamilton and de Broglie resolved this mismatch by distinguishing phase velocity from group velocity.
sources: Hamilton (1834). "On a General Method in Dynamics". *Phil. Trans. R. Soc.* 124, 247. [doi:10.1098/rstl.1834.0017](https://doi.org/10.1098/rstl.1834.0017)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Maxwell's equations from a field action
registry.summary: Extending Hamilton's principle to fields, the inhomogeneous Maxwell equations come out as the Euler–Lagrange equations of the covariant action, and the homogeneous pair is the Bianchi identity of F=dA. Noether's theorem applied to this action gives the energy–momentum tensor. Gauge invariance of the coupling forces charge conservation.
registry.breaks: The canonical Noether tensor is neither symmetric nor gauge invariant and needs the Belinfante improvement. The action also does not settle radiation reaction for point charges.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Photoelasticity: stress made visible by birefringence
registry.summary: Stress makes a transparent solid birefringent in proportion to the difference of principal stresses (the stress-optic law, Brewster 1816). Viewed between crossed polarizers, a loaded model shows isochromatic fringes of σ1−σ2 and isoclinics along the principal directions, the classic tool of experimental stress analysis. The same photoelastic tensor drives acousto-optic modulators.
registry.breaks: The method gives only stress differences and directions integrated through the thickness. Separating the individual principal stresses, or handling 3D bodies, needs extra methods such as stress freezing or scattered-light photoelasticity.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Elastic-solid aether and the Maxwell stress tensor
registry.summary: Fresnel's transverse light waves led Cauchy, Green and MacCullagh to model light as waves in an elastic solid, and MacCullagh's rotationally elastic aether gave equations equivalent to Maxwell's in vacuum. Maxwell expressed electromagnetic forces as stresses in a medium. That is the origin of the stress tensor whose divergence gives the force density.
registry.breaks: An ordinary elastic solid also carries longitudinal waves, which light lacks; this problem sank most elastic-aether theories. Relativity later removed the medium altogether.
sources: Maxwell (1865). "A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field". *Phil. Trans. R. Soc.* 155, 459. [doi:10.1098/rstl.1865.0008](https://doi.org/10.1098/rstl.1865.0008)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Vortex Biot–Savart law: vorticity as current
registry.summary: An incompressible velocity field obeys ∇·u=0 and ∇×u=ω, the same equations as B with source μ0J. Vortex lines therefore induce velocity by the Biot–Savart law: a line vortex acts like a straight wire and a vortex ring like a current loop. Maxwell's 1861 molecular-vortex model ran the analogy the other way, to picture magnetic fields.
registry.map: \mathbf u=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int\frac{\boldsymbol\omega'\times\mathbf R}{R^3}dV'\ \leftrightarrow\ \mathbf B=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int\frac{\mathbf J'\times\mathbf R}{R^3}dV',\ \mathbf R=\mathbf r-\mathbf r'
registry.breaks: Vorticity is carried along and stretched by the velocity it induces (Helmholtz's laws), so vortex dynamics is nonlinear, whereas currents are prescribed. Parallel vortices of the same sign orbit each other instead of attracting the way parallel currents do.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Analogue event horizons in flows and optical fibres
registry.summary: Sound in an irrotational flow travels on an effective acoustic metric, with a horizon where the flow outruns sound. In a fibre, the Kerr index front of a soliton moving at the group velocity acts as a horizon for probe light. Both therefore serve as analogue-gravity platforms for Hawking-type mode conversion.
registry.map: ds^2\propto-(c_s^2-v^2)dt^2-2\mathbf v\cdot d\mathbf x\,dt+d\mathbf x^2;\quad \text{horizon at }|v|=c_s
registry.breaks: Both rely on dispersion near the horizon. The fibre horizon is a moving index perturbation in a dispersive medium, not a flow, and claims of spontaneous Hawking-like emission in optics remain debated.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hydrodynamics of light via the Madelung transform
registry.summary: Writing the paraxial Kerr field as √ρ e^{iφ} turns the NLS into continuity and Euler equations for a compressible fluid. The nonlinearity supplies a pressure, and diffraction supplies a dispersive 'quantum pressure'. Defocusing media then show superfluid-like flow of light, optical vortices, and dispersive shock waves similar to undular bores.
