registry.name: Damped oscillator: prototype susceptibility and FDT
registry.summary: The driven damped oscillator's χ(ω) is the textbook causal response function: its poles lie in the lower half-plane and it satisfies Kramers–Kronig. The fluctuation–dissipation theorem then fixes its thermal noise spectrum from Im χ, and integrating that spectrum recovers equipartition. This sets the thermal-noise floor of AFM cantilevers, torsion balances and gravitational-wave test masses.
sources: Callen & Welton (1951). "Irreversibility and Generalized Noise". *Phys. Rev.* 83, 34. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.83.34](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.83.34)
Kubo (1957). "Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes. I.". *J. Phys. Soc. Jpn.* 12, 570. [doi:10.1143/JPSJ.12.570](https://doi.org/10.1143/JPSJ.12.570)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thermoacoustic engines and refrigerators
registry.summary: A sound wave in a channel with a temperature gradient drives each gas parcel through a Stirling-like cycle of compression, heat exchange with the wall and expansion. Heat can therefore amplify sound (Rijke and Sondhauss tubes, Rayleigh's criterion) or sound can pump heat. Thermoacoustic engines and refrigerators are working heat engines bounded by Carnot.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Sound propagation and absorption from kinetic theory
registry.summary: The adiabatic sound speed and the classical Stokes–Kirchhoff absorption both follow from the hydrodynamic limit of the Boltzmann equation, with attenuation set by viscosity and thermal conduction. When ωτ ~ 1, at high frequency or in a rarefied gas, hydrodynamic acoustics breaks down and BGK-type kinetic models describe the sound instead.
sources: Bhatnagar, Gross & Krook (1954). "A Model for Collision Processes in Gases. I. Small Amplitude Processes in Charged and Neutral One-Component Systems". *Phys. Rev.* 94, 511. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.94.511](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.94.511)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kramers escape and stochastic resonance in a double well
registry.summary: Thermal noise drives hops between the wells of a Duffing-type double-well oscillator at the Kramers rate, which depends on the barrier height and the curvatures at the minimum and the saddle. Adding weak periodic forcing produces stochastic resonance: the response peaks when the mean Kramers residence time is about half the drive period.
sources: Kramers (1940). "Brownian Motion in a Field of Force and the Diffusion Model of Chemical Reactions". *Physica* 7, 284. [doi:10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Lagrangian generates quantum propagation (Dirac–Feynman)
registry.summary: Dirac (1933) noticed that the short-time quantum propagator behaves like exp(iS/ħ), with S the classical action. Feynman built the path integral on this, which made the Lagrangian rather than the Hamiltonian the primary object of quantum dynamics.
sources: Feynman (1948). "Space-Time Approach to Non-Relativistic Quantum Mechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 20, 367. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Bohmian mechanics as quantum Hamilton–Jacobi theory
registry.summary: With ψ=R e^{iS/ħ}, the Schrödinger equation is exactly a Hamilton–Jacobi equation plus Bohm's quantum potential Q (Madelung 1927, Bohm 1952). De Broglie–Bohm theory has particles move along v=∇S/m, the characteristics of this equation, which gives a deterministic hidden-variable interpretation.
registry.breaks: For many particles Q is nonlocal in configuration space and does not weaken as |ψ| shrinks. The motion is first-order, so initial momenta are not free. The mathematics is exact, but the interpretation is contested.
sources: Bohm (1952). "A Suggested Interpretation of the Quantum Theory in Terms of 'Hidden' Variables. I". *Phys. Rev.* 85, 166. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.85.166](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.85.166)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: WKB: Schrödinger reduces to Hamilton–Jacobi
registry.summary: Writing ψ=A e^{iS/ħ} turns the Schrödinger equation into the Hamilton–Jacobi equation at leading order, plus a continuity equation for A. Quantizing the action variables J=∮p dq gives the Bohr–Sommerfeld and EBK rules. Ehrenfest argued that action variables were the right quantities to quantize because they are adiabatic invariants.
registry.breaks: It breaks down at turning points and caustics, where A diverges (Airy matching and the Maslov 1/2 repair this), and wherever the de Broglie wavelength changes quickly.
sources: Schrödinger (1926). "Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem". *Ann. Phys.* 384, 361. [doi:10.1002/andp.19263840404](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19263840404)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hannay angle: classical counterpart of the Berry phase
registry.summary: When an integrable system's parameters are cycled adiabatically, the action J stays invariant but the conjugate angle picks up a geometric shift, the Hannay angle. Berry showed that it is the semiclassical limit of the Berry phase of the quantum state with the same quantum number.
registry.breaks: It requires invariant tori. Chaotic systems have no angle variables, and their adiabatic response takes a different form (geometric magnetism, Berry–Robbins).
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hamilton's principal function as the semiclassical phase
registry.summary: In the stationary-phase evaluation of the path integral, the phase is Hamilton's principal function S(x_b,x_a,t), which generates the classical time-evolution map. The prefactor is its mixed second derivative (the Van Vleck–Gutzwiller propagator), and caustics of the classical family add Maslov phases.
registry.breaks: It fails near caustics and beyond the Ehrenfest time, where classical paths proliferate (chaos). It also fails where no real classical path exists: tunnelling needs complex or Euclidean paths.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Epistemically restricted Liouville mechanics ≈ Gaussian QM
registry.summary: Classical Liouville mechanics with an uncertainty-like limit on what can be known about phase-space points reproduces Gaussian quantum mechanics, including entanglement and teleportation (Bartlett, Rudolph and Spekkens). The genuinely nonclassical resource therefore lies outside it: contextuality, which is equivalent to negativity of the Wigner function.
registry.breaks: The model cannot reproduce non-Gaussian states or operations, Bell violations or Kochen–Specker contextuality, because it is a noncontextual hidden-variable model by construction.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Poisson bracket → commutator (canonical quantization)
registry.summary: Dirac recognized that Heisenberg's commutators obey the algebra of classical Poisson brackets, so quantization replaces {A,B} with [Â,B̂]/iħ. Hamilton's equations then become the Heisenberg equations of motion, and the Liouville equation becomes the von Neumann equation for the density matrix.
registry.map: \{A,B\}\to\tfrac{1}{i\hbar}[\hat A,\hat B];\ \dot A=\{A,H\}\to\dot{\hat A}=\tfrac{i}{\hbar}[\hat H,\hat A];\ \partial_t\rho=\{H,\rho\}\to i\hbar\partial_t\hat\rho=[\hat H,\hat\rho]
registry.breaks: The map is not exact for all observables. The Groenewold–van Hove theorem rules out a consistent quantization of all polynomials, so operator ordering is ambiguous at O(ħ²).
sources: Heisenberg (1925). "Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen". *Z. Phys.* 33, 879. [doi:10.1007/BF01328377](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01328377)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Phase-space QM: Liouville flow to Wigner–Moyal
registry.summary: The Wigner function is a quasi-probability on classical phase space that evolves by the Liouville equation with the Poisson bracket replaced by the Moyal bracket. Quantum optics describes light with Wigner, Husimi-Q and Glauber–Sudarshan-P distributions; Wigner negativity or a singular P function marks a nonclassical state.
registry.map: \partial_tW=\{H,W\}_{\star}=\{H,W\}+O(\hbar^2\,\partial^3H\,\partial^3W);\ \ W\ \text{follows the classical flow exactly if}\ H\ \text{is quadratic}
registry.breaks: W can be negative, so it is not a probability. Moyal corrections at O(ħ²) appear for anharmonic Hamiltonians, so classical Liouville flow is exact only for quadratic H (linear optics).
sources: Glauber (1963). "The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 2529. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Circuit quantization from the node-flux Lagrangian
registry.summary: Superconducting circuits are quantized by writing a Lagrangian in node fluxes, with capacitive energy as kinetic energy and inductive and Josephson energy as potential energy. A Legendre transform makes the charges the conjugate momenta, and one then imposes [Φ,Q]=iħ. Kirchhoff loops and flux quantization act as holonomic constraints.
registry.breaks: Dissipative and non-Lagrangian elements (resistors, nonreciprocal gyrators) need a bath or an extended treatment. Offset charges and compact phase variables need care.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Least action as stationary phase
registry.summary: As ħ→0, Hamilton's principle δS=0 is the stationary-phase condition of the sum over e^{iS/ħ}: only paths near the classical one interfere constructively, just as Fermat's principle emerges from Huygens' wave optics. In imaginary time the same logic picks out minima of the Euclidean action (instantons).
registry.map: \hbar\to0:\ \int\mathcal{D}x\,e^{iS/\hbar}\ \text{dominated by}\ \delta S=0\ \Leftrightarrow\ \frac{d}{dt}\frac{\partial L}{\partial\dot x}=\frac{\partial L}{\partial x}
sources: Feynman (1948). "Space-Time Approach to Non-Relativistic Quantum Mechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 20, 367. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Madelung: condensates as inviscid, irrotational fluids
registry.summary: With ψ=√n e^{iθ}, the Gross–Pitaevskii equation becomes the continuity and Euler equations of an inviscid, irrotational fluid with velocity v=ħ∇θ/m, plus a quantum-pressure term. Kelvin's circulation theorem becomes the topological quantization of circulation around vortex lines, and the Landau criterion sets the critical velocity for dissipation.
registry.map: \mathbf v=\tfrac{\hbar}{m}\nabla\theta;\ \ m\partial_t\mathbf v=-\nabla\big(\tfrac12mv^2+V+gn+Q\big);\ \ \oint\mathbf v\cdot d\mathbf l=\tfrac{h}{m}\ell,\ \ell\in\mathbb Z
registry.breaks: The fluid picture fails inside vortex cores and below the healing length ξ, where quantum pressure dominates. At finite temperature a normal component adds viscosity (the two-fluid model).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Low-Re swimming as a gauge holonomy (Shapere–Wilczek)
registry.summary: At low Reynolds number, a swimmer's net displacement after a cyclic stroke depends only on the loop traced in shape space: it is the holonomy of a gauge connection, as with the Berry phase. For small strokes the displacement is the curvature times the enclosed area, so reciprocal strokes, which enclose no area, cannot swim (Purcell's scallop theorem).
registry.map: \Delta\mathbf x=\oint_{\rm stroke}\mathcal A(s)\,ds\approx\iint\mathcal F\,da,\ \ \mathcal F=d\mathcal A+\mathcal A\wedge\mathcal A;\ \ \text{reciprocal stroke}\Rightarrow\Delta\mathbf x=0
registry.breaks: The connection is non-abelian (it mixes rotations and translations) and comes from the reciprocity of Stokes flow, not from a quantum state. The effect is purely kinematic and dissipative.
sources: Purcell (1977). "Life at low Reynolds number". *Am. J. Phys.* 45, 3. [doi:10.1119/1.10903](https://doi.org/10.1119/1.10903)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum turbulence: Kolmogorov cascades in vortex tangles
registry.summary: Tangles of quantized vortices in superfluid helium and atomic condensates reproduce Kolmogorov's k^{-5/3} spectrum at scales larger than the intervortex spacing. Below that scale, energy moves through vortex reconnections and Kelvin-wave cascades. 2D condensates show inverse cascades and Onsager's negative-temperature vortex clusters.
registry.breaks: There is no viscosity: energy is dissipated by phonon emission and reconnections at the smallest scales. Quantized circulation also imposes a discrete vortex scale that classical turbulence lacks.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kepler–hydrogen: Runge–Lenz vector and hidden SO(4)
registry.summary: The conserved Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector, which keeps Kepler orbits closed (Bertrand's theorem), enlarges the symmetry of the 1/r problem from SO(3) to SO(4). Pauli (1926) used its quantum version to derive the hydrogen spectrum algebraically, and the same symmetry explains hydrogen's accidental n² degeneracy.
registry.map: \mathbf A=\mathbf p\times\mathbf L-mk\,\hat{\mathbf r};\ \ \mathfrak{so}(4):\ E_n=-\frac{mk^2}{2\hbar^2n^2},\ g_n=n^2\ \ (k=Ze^2/4\pi\varepsilon_0)
registry.breaks: Any departure from 1/r (relativity, core penetration, spin–orbit coupling) breaks SO(4). Classically the orbits then precess; quantum mechanically the ℓ-levels split.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rutherford scattering: classical = quantum for 1/r
registry.summary: The Coulomb differential cross section comes out the same from classical orbits, from the first Born approximation and from the exact quantum solution. This accident of the 1/r potential is why Rutherford's classical analysis could reveal the nucleus. For other potentials, features of the classical deflection function (rainbows, glories, orbiting) reappear as stationary-phase points of the partial-wave sum (Ford–Wheeler).
registry.breaks: In general the classical and quantum cross sections differ. Diffraction and shadow scattering make the quantum total cross section of a hard sphere twice its geometric value at high energy, and identical-particle (Mott) interference has no classical analogue.
sources: Born (1926). "Zur Quantenmechanik der Stoßvorgänge". *Z. Phys.* 37, 863. [doi:10.1007/BF01397477](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01397477)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Symplectic splitting ↔ Trotter–Suzuki Hamiltonian simulation
registry.summary: Long-term N-body integration splits H into exactly solvable flows (leapfrog, Wisdom–Holman, Yoshida–Suzuki compositions). Digital quantum simulation uses the same product formulas for e^{-iHt}. The error is set by nested Poisson brackets in the classical case and nested commutators in the quantum case.
registry.breaks: Classical integrators preserve symplecticity, which keeps the energy error bounded; quantum product formulas are exactly unitary. Quantum cost is counted in gates, and the error scales with commutator norms.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ehrenfest theorem: Newton's second law on average
registry.summary: Expectation values obey m d²⟨x⟩/dt² = −⟨V′(x)⟩, Newton's second law for the centroid of a wave packet. The centroid follows the classical trajectory only when ⟨V′(x)⟩=V′(⟨x⟩): for at most quadratic potentials, or for packets narrow compared with the scale over which the force changes.
registry.map: m\frac{d^2\langle\hat x\rangle}{dt^2}=-\langle V'(\hat x)\rangle\approx-V'(\langle\hat x\rangle)\ \ (\text{exact iff}\ V'''=0)
registry.breaks: Wave-packet spreading and anharmonicity spoil the agreement after the Ehrenfest time. The theorem does not imply classical behaviour of individual measurement outcomes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Atom interferometers as gravimeters and Sagnac gyroscopes
registry.summary: Light-pulse atom interferometers turn the classical kinematics of free fall and rotating frames into matter-wave phases. The gravity phase k_eff g T² underlies atomic gravimeters, and the Sagnac phase from Earth's rotation makes atom gyroscopes; when rotation is not the target, the Coriolis terms must be compensated.
registry.breaks: For equal area, the matter-wave Sagnac phase exceeds the optical one by mc²/ħω ~ 10^10, but atom interferometers enclose far smaller areas.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rotation as synthetic magnetism: Coriolis ↔ Lorentz
registry.summary: In a frame rotating at Ω the Coriolis force has the form of a Lorentz force with qB=2mΩ. Rotating condensates therefore form triangular vortex lattices, like type-II superconductors in a field, and as Ω approaches the trap frequency they enter the lowest-Landau-level regime, which resembles the quantum Hall effect.
registry.breaks: The centrifugal term weakens confinement and frees the gas as Ω→ω⊥, which has so far kept rotating gases out of deep fractional-quantum-Hall states. Laser-induced gauge fields avoid this problem.
sources: Bloch, Dalibard & Zwerger (2008). "Many-body physics with ultracold gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 885. [arXiv:0704.3011](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.3011)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Foucault pendulum precession as a holonomy
registry.summary: After one sidereal day, the Foucault pendulum's plane of swing has turned by the solid angle enclosed by its circle of latitude, a holonomy of parallel transport on a sphere. The same geometry gives a spin's Berry phase as −m times the solid angle traced by the field direction.
registry.breaks: Foucault's pendulum transports a real vector (an SO(2) holonomy of the sphere's Levi-Civita connection). Berry's phase is a U(1) phase of a complex state; it scales with m and shows up only relative to another path.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: BGS conjecture: classical chaos ↔ random-matrix spectra
registry.summary: Whether the classical limit is integrable or chaotic fixes the quantum level statistics: Poisson spacings for integrable motion (Berry–Tabor), Wigner–Dyson level repulsion for fully chaotic motion (Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit), and intermediate statistics for mixed KAM phase spaces. Periodic-orbit theory explains why.
registry.map: P_{\rm int}(s)=e^{-s}\ \ \text{vs}\ \ P_{\rm GOE}(s)\approx\frac{\pi s}{2}e^{-\pi s^2/4}
registry.breaks: There are exceptions. Arithmetic chaotic systems, such as billiards on special constant-curvature surfaces, show Poisson statistics, and non-generic integrable systems such as harmonic oscillators do not follow Berry–Tabor.
sources: Bohigas, Giannoni & Schmit (1984). "Characterization of Chaotic Quantum Spectra and Universality of Level Fluctuation Laws". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 1. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.1)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Bosonic Josephson junction: pendulum bifurcation, self-trapping
registry.summary: The mean-field dynamics of a condensate in a double well, in population imbalance z and relative phase φ, is that of a nonrigid pendulum. Raising the interaction parameter Λ through a bifurcation produces macroscopic quantum self-trapping, observed with rubidium in 2005; the large atom number N plays the role of 1/ħ.
registry.breaks: At finite N, quantum fluctuations cause collapse and revival and tunnelling between the two self-trapped states. The classical pendulum is only the N→∞ limit.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Period doubling vs discrete time-crystalline order
registry.summary: Driven dissipative classical systems (Faraday waves, parametrically driven pendula, period-doubling bifurcations) respond robustly at twice the drive period. Discrete time crystals are the many-body quantum version: a period-doubled response that resists drive imperfections and is long-range ordered, seen in trapped ions, NV centres and superconducting processors.
registry.breaks: Classical period doubling relies on dissipation into an attractor. Closed quantum time crystals must avoid Floquet heating through many-body localization or prethermalization, and their rigidity is a many-body effect, although classical many-body time crystals in coupled dissipative oscillators have been proposed.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Chaos, Ehrenfest time and decoherence
registry.summary: Classical chaos stretches a wave packet exponentially, so an isolated chaotic system stops tracking its classical counterpart after the Ehrenfest time, ~λ⁻¹ln(S/ħ), which for Saturn's moon Hyperion is only decades. Environmental decoherence restores the classical Liouville limit. Zurek and Paz argued that the entropy production rate then becomes independent of ħ and is set by the Lyapunov exponents.
registry.breaks: Entropy production at the Lyapunov rate holds in an intermediate range of decoherence strength and is supported numerically, not proven in general.
sources: Zurek (2003). "Decoherence, einselection, and the quantum origins of the classical". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 715. [arXiv:quant-ph/0105127](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0105127)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Lyapunov exponent ↔ OTOC growth and the chaos bound
registry.summary: The out-of-time-order correlator is the quantum version of the squared Poisson bracket {x(t),p}², which measures sensitivity to initial conditions. In semiclassical systems it therefore grows as e^{2λt}, with λ the classical Lyapunov exponent, until the scrambling time. Maldacena, Shenker and Stanford bounded the quantum rate by 2πk_BT/ħ.
registry.breaks: Exponential OTOC growth lasts only until t~λ⁻¹ln(1/ħ_eff). It is absent in many chaotic systems with small local Hilbert spaces (spin-1/2 chains), and unstable saddle points in integrable systems produce it without chaos. The thermal bound has no classical counterpart.
sources: Maldacena, Shenker & Stanford (2016). "A bound on chaos". *JHEP* 08, 106. [arXiv:1503.01409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01409)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ergodicity: classical mixing vs eigenstate thermalization
registry.summary: Classical statistical mechanics rests on chaotic, mixing motion on the energy shell. Its quantum replacement, the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, holds that individual eigenstates of chaotic Hamiltonians already look thermal; Srednicki derived it from Berry's random-wave conjecture for the eigenfunctions of classically chaotic systems.
registry.breaks: ETH concerns eigenstates, not trajectories, and does not need a classical limit (spin-1/2 chains obey it). Many-body localization and quantum many-body scars, named after Heller's periodic-orbit scars, violate it.
sources: Deutsch (1991). "Quantum statistical mechanics in a closed system". *Phys. Rev. A* 43, 2046. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.43.2046](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.43.2046)
Srednicki (1994). "Chaos and quantum thermalization". *Phys. Rev. E* 50, 888. [arXiv:cond-mat/9403051](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9403051)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kicked rotor: chaotic diffusion vs dynamical localization
registry.summary: Chirikov's standard map loses its last KAM torus near K≈0.97, after which momentum diffuses without bound. The quantum kicked rotor follows this diffusion only up to a break time and then localizes in momentum. Fishman, Grempel and Prange mapped this dynamical localization onto Anderson localization, and it was observed with cold atoms in pulsed optical standing waves.
registry.map: p_{n+1}=p_n+K\sin\theta_n,\ \ \theta_{n+1}=\theta_n+p_{n+1};\ \ \langle p^2\rangle_{\rm cl}\approx\tfrac{K^2}{2}n\ \ \text{vs quantum saturation after}\ t^*\propto D/\hbar_{\rm eff}^2
registry.breaks: Localization is a quantum interference effect with no classical counterpart. Noise or decoherence restores classical diffusion, and at quantum resonances (rational ħ_eff/4π) the energy grows ballistically.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Torus quantization (EBK) and Gutzwiller's periodic-orbit sum
registry.summary: Einstein (1917) quantized the actions on invariant tori and noted that the rule fails when the tori are destroyed. KAM theory says which tori survive. For fully chaotic motion, Gutzwiller's trace formula, a stationary-phase evaluation of the path integral, replaces torus quantization with a sum over unstable periodic orbits.
registry.breaks: Mixed phase spaces need both pictures, plus tunnelling between regular and chaotic regions. The periodic-orbit sum diverges because the number of orbits grows exponentially, so it has to be resummed.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gross–Pitaevskii = NLS: matter-wave solitons
registry.summary: In a 1D waveguide the Gross–Pitaevskii equation reduces to the integrable nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Repulsive condensates therefore carry dark solitons and attractive ones bright solitons and soliton trains, all seen in BECs between 1999 and 2002. The same equation governs solitons in optical fibres.
registry.breaks: Transverse confinement and the trap break integrability. In 2D and 3D, dark solitons decay into vortices through the snake instability, and attractive 3D condensates collapse. Beyond mean field, the quantum NLS (Lieb–Liniger) is solved by the Bethe ansatz.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Integrability blocks thermalization: Lax charges and GGE
registry.summary: Classical integrable systems carry an extensive set of conserved quantities generated by a Lax pair. That is why soliton collisions are elastic and FPUT-type lattices recur instead of equilibrating. Quantum integrable systems (Lieb–Liniger, the quantum NLS) likewise fail to thermalize and relax to a generalized Gibbs ensemble, as the quantum Newton's cradle experiment showed.
registry.breaks: Quantum conserved charges constrain relaxation only if they are local or quasi-local. In both the classical and quantum cases, weak integrability breaking gives prethermal plateaus and eventually thermalization.
sources: Zabusky & Kruskal (1965). "Interaction of 'Solitons' in a Collisionless Plasma and the Recurrence of Initial States". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 15, 240. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.15.240](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.15.240)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Harmonic oscillator: normal modes to ladder operators
registry.summary: Any small oscillation about equilibrium, once reduced to normal modes, quantizes to the quantum harmonic oscillator. The classical complex amplitude becomes the ladder operator a, giving the equally spaced spectrum ħω(n+1/2) that is the template for phonons, photons and quasiparticles.
registry.breaks: The zero-point energy ħω/2 and the discrete exchange of energy have no classical counterpart. The equal level spacing is why the classical and quantum frequencies coincide.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Bogoliubov transformation: normal modes of a condensate
registry.summary: Linearizing about the condensate gives a quadratic bosonic Hamiltonian that a Bogoliubov transformation diagonalizes. This is normal-mode analysis with a symplectic rather than orthogonal transformation, and it yields phonon-like quasiparticles. In traps, the low-lying collective modes (the Kohn dipole mode at the trap frequency, breathing and quadrupole modes) are measured like classical normal modes.
registry.breaks: Classical normal-mode analysis has no counterpart to the u,v mixing of creation and annihilation operators, which produces quantum depletion and a two-mode-squeezed ground state.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ion-crystal normal modes as the quantum bus
registry.summary: Ions in a linear Paul trap form a Coulomb crystal whose small oscillations split into normal modes (centre of mass, breathing, ...). These quantized modes mediate the Cirac–Zoller and Mølmer–Sørensen entangling gates and set the effective spin–spin couplings used in trapped-ion quantum simulation.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ring-polymer isomorphism for quantum statistics
registry.summary: Discretizing the imaginary-time path integral maps a quantum particle at temperature T onto a classical ring polymer of P beads joined by harmonic springs. Classical molecular dynamics or Monte Carlo (PIMD, RPMD) can then compute quantum equilibrium properties, and the ring's normal modes are used to integrate and thermostat it efficiently.
registry.breaks: It is exact only for equilibrium statics. Real-time quantum dynamics (RPMD) is an approximation, and fermions bring a sign problem.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Vacuum Rabi splitting vs classical normal-mode splitting
registry.summary: Two coupled resonators show an avoided crossing of width 2g, and the classical strong-coupling criterion g>κ,γ is the same as the quantum one. The single-excitation vacuum Rabi doublet of cavity QED matches this classical normal-mode splitting quantitatively.
registry.breaks: The anharmonic √n ladder of a two-level emitter (photon blockade, collapse and revival, number-dependent Rabi frequencies) has no linear classical counterpart. Only that ladder proves quantum strong coupling.
sources: Jaynes & Cummings (1963). "Comparison of quantum and semiclassical radiation theories with application to the beam maser". *Proc. IEEE* 51, 89. [doi:10.1109/PROC.1963.1664](https://doi.org/10.1109/PROC.1963.1664)

Wallraff et al. (2004). "Strong coupling of a single photon to a superconducting qubit using circuit quantum electrodynamics". *Nature* 431, 162. [doi:10.1038/nature02851](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02851)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Field quantization = quantizing normal modes
registry.summary: Expanding the electromagnetic field in cavity normal modes turns it into a set of uncoupled harmonic oscillators, just as normal-mode analysis decouples a chain of masses. Quantizing each mode gives photons, Planck's spectrum and vacuum fluctuations.
registry.map: H=\sum_k\hbar\omega_k\big(a_k^\dagger a_k+\tfrac12\big),\quad \hat{\mathbf E}(\mathbf r)=\sum_k\mathcal E_k\big(a_k\mathbf u_k(\mathbf r)+\mathrm{h.c.}\big)
registry.breaks: Classical equipartition, k_BT per mode, gives the Rayleigh–Jeans catastrophe. Quantizing the mode energies removes it.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Optical molasses and the MOT as a damped oscillator
registry.summary: Doppler cooling produces a velocity-dependent force F=−βv (hence 'optical molasses'), and the magneto-optical trap adds a restoring force −κx, so trapped atoms are damped, usually overdamped, harmonic oscillators. Random photon recoils supply the fluctuating force, and fluctuation–dissipation sets the Doppler limit.
registry.map: m\ddot x=-\beta\dot x-\kappa x+F_{\rm rand}(t),\ \ k_BT=\frac{D_p}{\beta}\ \Rightarrow\ k_BT_D=\frac{\hbar\Gamma}{2}
registry.breaks: Sub-Doppler (Sisyphus) cooling and the recoil limit depend on optical pumping between internal states and on quantized photon momentum, which the damped-oscillator picture leaves out.
sources: Raab et al. (1987). "Trapping of Neutral Sodium Atoms with Radiation Pressure". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 59, 2631. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.2631](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.2631)

registry.name: Damped oscillator: friction requires a bath
registry.summary: Classical damping γ=ω₀/Q cannot come from a Hamiltonian for the oscillator alone. Quantum mechanically it comes from coupling to a bath (Caldeira–Leggett), which in the Markov limit gives a Lindblad equation with jump operators a and a†. The mean amplitude decays exactly as in the classical case, and fluctuation–dissipation adds thermal and zero-point noise.
registry.map: \dot\rho=-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}[H,\rho]+\kappa(\bar n+1)\mathcal D[a]\rho+\kappa\bar n\,\mathcal D[a^\dagger]\rho,\ \ \kappa=\omega_0/Q,\ \ \langle a\rangle\propto e^{-\kappa t/2}
registry.breaks: The Lindblad form needs weak coupling and a Markovian bath. Strongly damped or low-temperature quantum Brownian motion is non-Markovian and has no exact Lindblad description.
sources: Lindblad (1976). "On the generators of quantum dynamical semigroups". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 48, 119. [doi:10.1007/BF01608499](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01608499)

registry.name: Critical damping is an exceptional point
registry.summary: Written as a first-order system, the damped oscillator has a non-Hermitian 2×2 dynamical matrix. At critical damping, γ=2ω₀, its eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce at an exceptional point, whose Jordan-block signature is the t e^{−γt/2} solution. Coupled gain/loss oscillators undergo their PT-symmetry-breaking transition at the same kind of point.
registry.breaks: Non-Hermitian quantum Hamiltonians describe post-selected or mean-field dynamics. Real quantum gain and loss add noise (Lindblad terms), which limits sensing enhanced by exceptional points.
sources: Bender & Boettcher (1998). "Real Spectra in Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians Having PT Symmetry". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 5243. [arXiv:physics/9712001](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/9712001)

registry.name: Mechanical resonator driven into the quantum regime
registry.summary: The mechanical element of an optomechanical system is a classical damped, driven oscillator whose frequency and damping are shifted by radiation pressure (optical spring, optical damping). Sideband cooling with κ<ω_m brings its mean phonon number below one, where zero-point motion and measurement backaction become observable.
registry.map: m(\ddot x+\Gamma_m\dot x+\omega_m^2x)=F_{\rm th}+F_{\rm rad};\quad Q_mf_m>k_BT/h\ \text{for one coherent oscillation per thermal phonon}
registry.breaks: Backaction noise, the standard quantum limit and nonclassical motional states are beyond the classical oscillator, which captures only the mean response.
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

registry.name: Coherent states: the quantum oscillator that moves classically
registry.summary: A classically driven oscillator, or a classical current radiating into a mode, produces a coherent state: a displaced vacuum whose mean position and momentum follow the classical trajectory with constant minimum uncertainty. Glauber made it the reference classical state of light, with Poissonian photon counts.
registry.breaks: The correspondence holds only for quadratic Hamiltonians, and vacuum-level quadrature noise remains. States with sub-Poissonian statistics or negative Wigner functions have no classical counterpart.
sources: Glauber (1963). "The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 2529. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529)

registry.name: Walking droplets: a hydrodynamic pilot-wave analogue
registry.summary: Droplets bouncing on a bath vibrated vertically just below the Faraday (parametric) threshold are propelled by their own wave field. This macroscopic version of de Broglie's pilot wave shows quantized orbits, tunnelling-like crossings and wave-like statistics.
registry.breaks: The wave lives in real 3D space, not configuration space, so the system is local and cannot produce entanglement or Bell violations. The early single- and double-slit interference claims (Couder & Fort 2006) were not reproduced in later controlled experiments.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Mathieu/Kapitza ↔ Floquet theory and high-frequency expansion
registry.summary: Floquet theory began in classical mechanics, with Hill's lunar equation, Floquet (1883) and the Mathieu equation. The quasienergies of a quantum Floquet Hamiltonian correspond to Floquet exponents, and Kapitza's effective potential for the inverted pendulum is the leading term of the high-frequency expansion used in Floquet engineering.
registry.breaks: The classical parametric instability becomes unbounded Floquet heating in interacting quantum systems. Many-body Floquet phases (time crystals, anomalous Floquet topology) have no single-oscillator counterpart.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Transmon as quantum pendulum and Duffing oscillator
registry.summary: The transmon Hamiltonian is a quantum pendulum, and its eigenproblem in the charge basis is the Mathieu equation. Expanded about the minimum it is a weakly anharmonic (Duffing/Kerr) oscillator. Driven Duffing bistability gives bifurcation readout, and parametric pumping gives Josephson parametric amplifiers.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Paul trap: Mathieu stability and Kapitza pseudopotential
registry.summary: An ion in an RF quadrupole field obeys the Mathieu equation and is confined when (a,q) lies inside the first stability region. Its slow secular motion sits in a ponderomotive pseudopotential, the same averaging that stabilizes Kapitza's inverted pendulum, with residual micromotion at the drive frequency.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Degenerate parametric amplification → squeezing
registry.summary: Pumping an oscillator at twice its frequency amplifies one quadrature and de-amplifies the other. Classically this squeezes the thermal noise of a mechanical resonator (Rugar & Grütter 1991). In optics and Josephson circuits the same phase-sensitive gain squeezes vacuum fluctuations, which gravitational-wave interferometers inject to beat the shot-noise limit.
registry.map: \hat X_1\to e^{r}\hat X_1,\ \ \hat X_2\to e^{-r}\hat X_2;\ \ \Delta X_2^2=\tfrac14e^{-2r}\ (\text{vacuum}:\ \tfrac14)
registry.breaks: Below threshold, classical parametric squeezing inside a resonator is capped at 3 dB and never goes below zero-point noise. Sub-vacuum noise is the quantum resource.
sources: Caves (1981). "Quantum-mechanical noise in an interferometer". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 1693. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693)

registry.name: Larmor precession: spin behaves as a gyroscope
registry.summary: A magnetic moment μ=γS in a field feels a torque that makes its angular momentum precess, like a gyroscope under gravity. Because the spin Hamiltonian is linear in S, the Heisenberg equation for ⟨S⟩ is exactly this classical precession, which is the basis of the Bloch equations, NMR/MRI and spin-qubit control.
registry.breaks: Only the mean precesses classically; individual measurements give quantized ±ħ/2. The electron's g≈2 also differs from the gyromagnetic ratio q/2m of a classical rotating charge.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hamilton–Jacobi separability and the Carter constant
registry.summary: Carter showed that the Hamilton–Jacobi equation for Kerr geodesics separates in Boyer–Lindquist coordinates. Separation gives a fourth constant Q (from a Killing tensor) beyond μ, E and L_z, making the motion Liouville-integrable. Bound orbits therefore have action–angle variables and three fundamental frequencies, which is the basis of EMRI waveform modelling.
sources: Carter (1968). "Global Structure of the Kerr Family of Gravitational Fields". *Phys. Rev.* 174, 1559. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.174.1559](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.174.1559)

registry.name: Hamilton–Jacobi flow as holographic renormalization
registry.summary: Slice asymptotically AdS spacetime radially in a Hamiltonian (ADM-like) way. The on-shell gravitational action, as a functional of boundary data, then obeys a Hamilton–Jacobi equation. The radial coordinate plays the role of the renormalization scale, and the Hamiltonian constraint becomes the RG (Callan–Symanzik) equation of the dual field theory.
sources: de Boer et al. (2000). "On the holographic renormalization group". *JHEP* 08, 003. [doi:10.1088/1126-6708/2000/08/003](https://doi.org/10.1088/1126-6708/2000/08/003)

registry.name: ADM: GR as a constrained Hamiltonian system
registry.summary: ADM put GR in Hamiltonian form, with the spatial metric and its conjugate momentum as the canonical pair. Lapse and shift are Lagrange multipliers that enforce the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints (Dirac constrained dynamics), so the Hamiltonian vanishes on shell, as for a reparametrized particle. Numerical relativity's 3+1 evolution is built on this split and monitors the constraints.
registry.map: H=\int d^3x\,(\alpha\mathcal H+\beta^i\mathcal H_i)+H_\partial,\ \ \mathcal H\approx0,\ \mathcal H_i\approx0,\ \ \{\gamma_{ij}(x),\pi^{kl}(y)\}=\delta_{(i}^k\delta_{j)}^l\delta^3(x-y)
registry.breaks: Production codes (BSSN, CCZ4, generalized harmonic) reformulate the equations for strong hyperbolicity and give up the canonical structure, so constraints are damped rather than preserved symplectically.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cyclic coordinates and Killing vectors for geodesics
registry.summary: Geodesics solve the Euler–Lagrange equations of L = ½ g_μν ẋ^μ ẋ^ν. In Schwarzschild and Kerr, t and φ are cyclic coordinates, so their conjugate momenta are conserved: energy and axial angular momentum, the Noether charges of the Killing vectors ∂_t and ∂_φ. As in the Kepler problem, this reduces orbits to quadratures.
registry.map: \mathcal L=\tfrac12g_{\mu\nu}\dot x^\mu\dot x^\nu,\ \ p_t=-E,\ p_\phi=L_z\ \text{conserved since}\ \partial_t\mathcal L=\partial_\phi\mathcal L=0

registry.name: Least action for the metric: Einstein–Hilbert action
registry.summary: In November 1915 Hilbert obtained the field equations by extending least action to the metric. A well-posed variational problem with fixed boundary metric needs the Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary term, and that term's Euclidean value gives the black-hole entropy.
sources: Gibbons & Hawking (1977). "Action integrals and partition functions in quantum gravity". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2752. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752)

registry.name: Fermat's principle: gravity as an optical medium
registry.summary: In a static spacetime, light rays extremize optical path length (Fermat's principle in the Fermat metric). In weak fields this acts like a medium with refractive index n ≈ 1 − 2Φ/c². That index gives the 1.75″ solar deflection and lensing, and the Shapiro delay is the extra optical path.
registry.breaks: Exact only for static (or, generalized, stationary) spacetimes; the medium is non-dispersive, and the factor 2 in n includes spatial curvature (PPN γ), so a purely Newtonian corpuscle bends only half as much.
sources: Shapiro (1964). "Fourth Test of General Relativity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 789. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.789](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.789)

registry.name: Crystal defects as torsion and curvature
registry.summary: In the continuum theory of defects (Kondo, Bilby, Kröner), dislocations are the torsion and disclinations the curvature of the crystal's material connection, and Katanaev–Volovich recast defect theory as three-dimensional Riemann–Cartan gravity. Along the same lines, Sakharov's induced gravity reads the Einstein–Hilbert action as a 'metric elasticity' of the vacuum.
registry.breaks: A crystal has a reference lattice, Euclidean signature and quadratic strain energy. Gravity has no preferred background, Lorentzian signature, and dynamics set by curvature itself. GR is torsion-free, so dislocations map to Einstein–Cartan rather than Einstein gravity.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Love numbers: from Earth tides to neutron-star mergers
registry.summary: A. E. H. Love introduced dimensionless numbers for the tidal deformation of the elastic Earth. Generalized to relativistic stars, they define the tidal deformability Λ, which enters the inspiral phase at 5PN order. GW170817 bounded Λ for neutron stars and so constrained the dense-matter equation of state; black-hole Love numbers vanish in four-dimensional GR.
registry.breaks: For neutron stars the response is dominated by the fluid interior, so Λ measures compactness and the equation of state rather than a shear modulus; crust elasticity is a small correction.
sources: Hinderer (2008). "Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars". *Astrophys. J.* 677, 1216. [doi:10.1086/533487](https://doi.org/10.1086/533487)

Flanagan & Hinderer (2008). "Constraining neutron-star tidal Love numbers with gravitational-wave detectors". *Phys. Rev. D* 77, 021502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.77.021502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.77.021502)

registry.name: Accretion disks as viscous Keplerian shear flows
registry.summary: Thin accretion disks around black holes are modelled as viscous Keplerian shear flows (Shakura–Sunyaev α-disks), with turbulent stresses ν = αc_sH carrying angular momentum outward. The inner edge sits near the ISCO, which sets the radiative efficiency. Keplerian rotation is hydrodynamically Rayleigh-stable, so the turbulence must be magnetic (the magnetorotational instability).

registry.name: Acoustic metric and analogue Hawking radiation
registry.summary: Linear sound in an irrotational, barotropic, inviscid flow obeys a massless wave equation on an effective acoustic metric. Where the flow becomes supersonic there is a sonic horizon, whose surface gravity is set by the velocity gradient. Unruh predicted thermal phonon emission at T = ħκ/(2πk_B); the stimulated effect was seen in water waves and the spontaneous effect in BECs.
registry.map: ds^2_{\rm ac}=\frac{\rho}{c_s}\big[-c_s^2dt^2+(d\mathbf x-\mathbf v\,dt)^2\big],\ \ T=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi k_B},\ \ \kappa=|\partial_n(c_s-v_\perp)|_{\rm hor}
registry.breaks: Only the kinematics carries over: the acoustic metric does not obey Einstein's equations (no gravitational back-reaction), short-wavelength dispersion breaks the effective Lorentz invariance near the horizon, the fluid has a preferred frame, and the temperatures are tiny.
sources: Unruh (1981). "Experimental Black-Hole Evaporation?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 46, 1351. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.1351](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.1351)

registry.name: Draining vortex as analogue Kerr: superradiance
registry.summary: A draining-bathtub vortex is an analogue rotating black hole. It has an ergoregion where the flow outruns the wave speed and a horizon where the inflow does. Waves with ω < mΩ_H are amplified by extracting rotational energy, as in Zel'dovich superradiance and the Penrose process; this was observed with surface waves by Torres et al. (2017).
registry.breaks: The effective metric is not a vacuum Einstein solution and has no inner horizon or singularity; the lab system has dissipation and dispersion, and the observed amplification used absorption at the vortex core rather than a true horizon.

registry.name: CFD shock-capturing in relativistic hydrodynamics
registry.summary: Numerical relativity writes the relativistic Euler/MHD equations in conservation form (the Valencia formulation) and solves them with Godunov-type high-resolution shock-capturing schemes and approximate Riemann solvers taken from CFD. This is essential for neutron-star mergers, where Kelvin–Helmholtz instability at the shear layer amplifies magnetic fields.

registry.name: Fluid/gravity duality and the viscosity bound
registry.summary: Long-wavelength perturbations of black-brane horizons in AdS obey the relativistic Navier–Stokes equations of the dual plasma, order by order in gradients. Transport coefficients are computed from the horizon, giving η/s = ħ/(4πk_B) for Einstein-gravity duals, a value compared with the quark–gluon plasma. The membrane paradigm anticipated this by treating the stretched horizon as a viscous fluid membrane.

registry.name: Gregory–Laflamme as Rayleigh–Plateau instability
registry.summary: Black strings (Schwarzschild × a line, in D ≥ 5) are unstable to long-wavelength ripples (Gregory–Laflamme), which Cardoso–Dias mapped onto the Rayleigh–Plateau break-up of a fluid column. Numerically the string pinches self-similarly into a cascade of black-hole beads, much as fluid jets do.
registry.breaks: Exists only in higher dimensions with extended directions. The fluid map is quantitative only in fluid/gravity or large-D limits, and the role of surface tension is played by horizon area–entropy, not by a material interface.

registry.name: Holographic turbulence and AdS turbulent instability
registry.summary: Through fluid/gravity duality, turbulent flows of a 2+1-dimensional conformal fluid correspond to dynamical AdS₄ black branes whose horizons develop fractal structure tied to the cascade. Relatedly, global AdS is weakly turbulently unstable: arbitrarily small perturbations cascade energy to ever shorter scales and collapse into black holes.

registry.name: Newtonian mechanics as the low-speed limit of SR
registry.summary: Galilean transformations are the c→∞ contraction of Lorentz transformations, and Newton's second law, momentum and kinetic energy are the leading terms of their relativistic forms; the limit is where absolute simultaneity and separate conservation of mass are lost.
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Annalen der Physik* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)

registry.name: Effective potential: Kepler problem vs Schwarzschild
registry.summary: Schwarzschild geodesics reduce exactly to a one-dimensional effective-potential problem like Kepler's, plus an attractive −GML²/(mc²r³) term. That term makes bound orbits precess, because the closed-orbit condition of Bertrand's theorem fails. It also removes the centrifugal barrier at small radius, which creates the innermost stable circular orbit at 6GM/c² and an unstable photon orbit at 3GM/c².
registry.breaks: Here r is the areal radius and the radial equation is in proper time; energy enters as E², so the Newtonian total energy is recovered only in the weak-field limit.

registry.name: Perihelion advance and light bending as orbit corrections
registry.summary: GR adds a 3GMu²/c² term to the Kepler problem's Binet equation. Bound orbits then precess by 6πGM/[c²a(1−e²)] per orbit: 43″/century for Mercury, about 4.2°/yr periastron advance for the Hulse–Taylor pulsar, and now seen in the S2 star at Sgr A*. Unbound photon trajectories bend by 4GM/(c²b), twice the Newtonian value.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [doi:10.12942/lrr-2014-4](https://doi.org/10.12942/lrr-2014-4)

registry.name: Kepler orbits decaying by gravitational radiation
registry.summary: A compact binary's inspiral is a slow sequence of Keplerian ellipses that lose energy and angular momentum to quadrupole radiation: the semimajor axis shrinks and the eccentricity decays (Peters–Mathews). The effective-one-body method extends the reduced-mass reduction of the two-body problem by mapping the relativistic binary onto a single particle in a deformed Schwarzschild metric.

Buonanno & Damour (1999). "Effective one-body approach to general relativistic two-body dynamics". *Phys. Rev. D* 59, 084006. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.59.084006](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.59.084006)

registry.name: Conservation laws forbid monopole and dipole GWs
registry.summary: Mass conservation and linear-momentum conservation make the monopole and mass-dipole moments radiate nothing, so the leading gravitational radiation is quadrupolar. The waves carry away energy, angular momentum (which circularizes orbits) and linear momentum; the last gives merged black holes recoil kicks of up to thousands of km/s.

registry.name: Collisions and the CM frame, relativistically
registry.summary: Newtonian collision analysis carries over to four-momentum conservation. The centre-of-mass frame becomes the frame of the invariant mass √s, and kinetic energy lost in a perfectly inelastic collision reappears as rest mass. Reaction thresholds follow from setting √s equal to the total final rest energy.

registry.name: Celestial perturbation theory and triples in GW sources
registry.summary: Celestial mechanics' osculating-element and secular-averaging methods are used for post-Newtonian eccentric and precessing binaries. In hierarchical triples, von Zeipel–Lidov–Kozai oscillations raise the inner binary's eccentricity until gravitational radiation can merge it, a proposed channel for LIGO–Virgo mergers and for eccentric LISA sources.

registry.name: Equivalence principle: tides become curvature
registry.summary: A freely falling frame removes uniform gravity exactly, the way a change of frame removes fictitious forces. What no frame removes is the tidal tensor ∂_i∂_jΦ, which becomes the Riemann curvature in the geodesic-deviation equation. Its trace, Poisson's equation, is the Newtonian limit of the 00 Einstein equation.

registry.name: Fictitious forces, equivalence principle, frame dragging
registry.summary: Inertial forces in accelerating and rotating frames are proportional to inertial mass, just as gravity is proportional to gravitational mass. Einstein made this the equivalence principle, tested by Eötvös-type and MICROSCOPE experiments and by gravitational redshift. GR's gravitomagnetic field acts like a Coriolis force from local inertial frames dragged by a rotating mass (Thirring), and Gravity Probe B and LAGEOS measured it.
registry.breaks: The equivalence is only local: no change of frame removes tidal (second-derivative) effects, and frame dragging is not a rigid global rotation, since its rate falls off as J/r³.

registry.name: Choptuik critical collapse as a saddle bifurcation
registry.summary: Tuning initial data to the threshold between dispersal and black-hole formation drives the evolution towards a universal, discretely self-similar critical solution. In phase space this solution is a codimension-one saddle on the separatrix, and its single unstable mode λ fixes the mass-scaling exponent γ = 1/λ. This is the saddle-and-separatrix picture of bifurcation theory, with universality as in critical phenomena.
sources: Choptuik (1993). "Universality and scaling in gravitational collapse of a massless scalar field". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 9. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9)

registry.name: Mixmaster chaos near cosmological singularities
registry.summary: Approaching a generic spacelike singularity (BKL), Bianchi IX 'Mixmaster' spacetimes bounce through Kasner epochs governed by a map that is chaotic, like the Gauss map of continued fractions. Equivalently, the dynamics is a billiard in hyperbolic space, and coordinate-invariant fractal methods later confirmed the chaos.

registry.name: Black-hole quasinormal modes as damped normal modes
registry.summary: Linear perturbations of Schwarzschild and Kerr reduce to one-dimensional wave equations with a potential barrier near the photon sphere. registry.name: Lighthill's acoustic quadrupole and GW quadrupole
registry.summary: In Lighthill's acoustic analogy, free turbulence radiates sound as a quadrupole because mass and momentum conservation remove monopole and dipole sources. registry.name: Vibrating string and the relativistic string
registry.summary: The relativistic string's Nambu–Goto action is the worldsheet area, the analogue of a particle's proper time. In conformal gauge it gives the one-dimensional wave equation of a stretched string. The Fourier normal modes become oscillators whose quantized excitation number N sets the mass spectrum, so the string's particle content is the normal-mode spectrum of a vibrating string.

registry.name: Acoustic vs relativistic Doppler effect
registry.summary: The acoustic Doppler shift depends separately on source and observer speeds relative to the medium. The relativistic shift depends only on their relative velocity and includes a purely transverse redshift from time dilation, measured by Ives–Stilwell. Historically, Voigt (1887) found Lorentz-like transformations by demanding invariance of the wave equation.
registry.breaks: Sound has a preferred frame (the medium); only the linear acoustic wave equation has a Lorentz-like symmetry with c_s, while the fluid itself is Galilean, which is also why analogue spacetimes hold only for perturbations.

When their frequency difference matches the acoustic frequency and the parametric gain R exceeds 1, the acoustic mode rings up exponentially, as in a pumped parametric oscillator; Advanced LIGO first observed this in 2014. registry.summary: Dirac's rule replaces Poisson brackets by commutators divided by iħ, which turns Hamilton's equations into Heisenberg's. Canonical transformations become unitary ones, and the phase-space generators of symmetries become charge operators; for fields the equal-time bracket of φ and π becomes the canonical commutator.

registry.name: Dynamic aperture, resonance overlap and Arnold diffusion

KAM tori bound the stable motion, while Chirikov resonance overlap and slow diffusion set the dynamic aperture and beam lifetime; Laskar's frequency-map analysis, developed for Solar System stability, is now used to design rings.
sources: Hénon & Heiles (1964). "The applicability of the third integral of motion: Some numerical experiments". *Astron. J.* 69, 73. [doi:10.1086/109234](https://doi.org/10.1086/109234)

registry.name: Topological solitons, winding numbers and instantons
registry.summary: Kinks, vortices, monopoles, Skyrmions and Yang–Mills instantons are all finite-energy or finite-action field configurations labeled by homotopy winding numbers and bounded below by Bogomolny bounds. Once quantized, solitons become particles: Coleman showed the sine-Gordon soliton is the massive Thirring fermion, and Skyrmions model baryons.

registry.name: Integrability: KdV, Virasoro and 2D field theory
registry.summary: The second Hamiltonian structure of the KdV equation is the classical Virasoro algebra, and the KdV conserved charges become the quantum integrals of motion of 2D CFT. Lax pairs and inverse scattering carry over to integrable QFTs with factorized S-matrices and to the Bethe-ansatz spin chains that give anomalous dimensions in planar N=4 super-Yang–Mills.

registry.name: Synchronized neutrino oscillations from self-interaction
registry.summary: When neutrino–neutrino forward scattering dominates the spread of vacuum frequencies Δm²/2E, neutrinos of all energies lock into a common precession at one synchronized frequency, much like mean-field (Kuramoto-type) locking of oscillators with all-to-all coupling. This 'synchronized oscillation' regime matters in supernovae and the early universe.
registry.breaks: The neutrino dynamics is conservative spin precession in a strong collective field, not dissipative phase attraction to a limit cycle, and the locked state can become unstable (bipolar and multi-angle modes).

registry.name: Neutrino flavor mixing as coupled pendulums
registry.summary: Two coupled pendulums have normal modes rotated by a mixing angle and exchange energy at the beat frequency, which maps onto flavor states as rotated mass eigenstates with P=sin²2θ sin²(Δm²L/4E). Slowly tuning one pendulum through resonance gives adiabatic transfer at an avoided crossing, the MSW effect, with the matter potential playing the role of the detuning.
registry.breaks: Pendulums exchange classical energy, while neutrinos have quantum probability amplitudes. Real symmetric spring couplings cannot produce the CP phase, which needs three flavors and complex mixing, and wave-packet decoherence has no simple mechanical counterpart.

registry.name: Free fields as infinitely many normal modes
registry.summary: In the continuum limit a chain of masses and springs, with each mass also tied to the ground by a spring, becomes the Klein–Gordon field, and Fourier normal modes decouple it into independent oscillators. Quantizing each mode gives Fock space, so particles are the quanta of normal modes.

registry.name: Neutral-kaon mixing as coupled damped oscillators
registry.summary: K⁰ and K̄⁰ evolve under a non-Hermitian 2×2 Hamiltonian M−iΓ/2, which matches two coupled oscillators whose normal modes (K_S, K_L) have very different damping and beat at Δm. In this picture CP violation is a non-reciprocal coupling between the oscillators, so a mechanical model needs gyroscopic or rotating-frame couplings.
registry.breaks: The interference of decay amplitudes into shared final states (ππ), quantum measurement of strangeness, and the CPT structure of M and Γ have no classical analogue.

registry.name: Misalignment: axion field as a Hubble-damped oscillator
registry.summary: The homogeneous axion field is a damped oscillator with Hubble friction 3H: it stays frozen while overdamped (m_a≪3H) and starts oscillating once m_a~3H. After that its number density is an adiabatic invariant (E/ω) that dilutes as a⁻³ and fixes the cold-dark-matter relic abundance, and large initial angles add pendulum anharmonicity.
registry.breaks: The friction comes from cosmic expansion, not dissipation, so energy redshifts instead of heating a bath, and m_a(T) switches on through QCD effects near the QCD transition.

High-Q torsion pendulums limited by thermal noise (Eöt-Wash type) have pushed the allowed Yukawa range down to tens of micrometers, which excludes two large extra dimensions at the millimeter scale.

registry.name: Breit–Wigner lineshape = driven damped resonance
registry.summary: A resonance's cross-section has the Lorentzian of a driven damped oscillator, with ω²→s, γω→MΓ, Q=M/Γ, and the ringdown time corresponding to the lifetime ħ/Γ. LEP fitted the Z lineshape this way to fix M_Z and Γ_Z, and its invisible width gave three light neutrino species.

registry.name: Mach cone and Cherenkov cone
registry.summary: A charged particle moving faster than light's phase velocity in a medium emits a wavefront cone with the same geometry as the Mach cone of a supersonic body. The cone angle measures β, the principle behind RICH particle identification, threshold counters and Super-K's rings.
registry.breaks: Cherenkov light is linear coherent emission from medium polarization, with a dispersive n(ω) that makes the angle and threshold frequency-dependent and the emitted energy tiny (Frank–Tamm). Sonic booms are nonlinear shocks.

registry.summary: The confining flux tube between static quarks vibrates transversely like a string fixed at both ends, and the zero-point energy of its normal modes (ω_n=nπ/r) gives the universal Lüscher correction −π(D−2)/(24r) to the linear potential. Lattice QCD confirms it.

registry.name: Hill's equation and alternating-gradient focusing
registry.summary: Transverse betatron motion in a ring obeys Hill's equation, a parametric oscillator driven by the periodic focusing K(s), so beam stability is a Floquet/Mathieu stability problem. Alternating-gradient focusing stabilizes the beam the way fast driving stabilizes the Kapitza pendulum, tunes must avoid parametric resonances, and the Courant–Snyder invariant is the action of the motion.

registry.summary: Naive perturbation theory for the Duffing oscillator produces secular terms that grow like εt, much as loop corrections produce logarithms of the cutoff. Poincaré–Lindstedt removes them by renormalizing the frequency, and the Chen–Goldenfeld–Oono renormalization-group method shows that the RG flow of amplitude and phase is the multiple-scales amplitude equation.

registry.name: Flavor pendulum: collective neutrino modes as a top
registry.summary: In a dense neutrino–antineutrino gas the flavor polarization vectors obey precession equations that reduce exactly to a gyroscopic (spherical) pendulum, a heavy top whose spin is set by the neutrino–antineutrino asymmetry. Bipolar collective flavor conversion in the inverted mass ordering is the inverted pendulum falling over (Hannestad, Raffelt, Sigl & Wong 2006).
registry.breaks: The mapping is exact only in the homogeneous, single-angle, two-flavor limit. Multi-angle effects and spatial inhomogeneity (fast flavor instabilities) go beyond the pendulum.

registry.name: Muon g−2: spin precession of a relativistic gyroscope
registry.summary: The muon spin in a storage ring precesses like a torqued gyroscope (dS/dt=μ×B), and the experiment measures the difference between the spin and cyclotron frequencies, which is proportional to a_μ. Thomas–BMT precession adds an electric-field term that vanishes at the 'magic' γ≈29.3, which is why the electrostatic focusing does not spoil the measurement.
registry.breaks: Spin is intrinsic with g≈2, so the ratio of moment to angular momentum differs from a classical body. Thomas precession is a relativistic kinematic effect, and the spin direction is read out through parity-violating decay.

registry.name: Regge trajectories from a rotating relativistic string
registry.summary: Modeling a meson as a rigid rotating string of tension σ with its ends moving at c, the energy and angular momentum integrals give J=M²/(2πσ), a linear Regge trajectory. With σ≈0.18 GeV² the predicted slope α'≈0.88 GeV⁻² matches the observed ~0.9 GeV⁻².
registry.breaks: This is a classical idealization with massless ends: quark masses, the quantum intercept α₀ and string breaking all modify it.

registry.name: Nuclear rainbows from the classical deflection function
registry.summary: Semiclassical (Ford–Wheeler) scattering identifies the WKB phase shift with the classical action, so the deflection function Θ(l) = 2 dδ_l/dl follows from orbits in the nuclear plus Coulomb potential. Where Θ has an extremum the classical cross section diverges, giving nuclear and Coulomb rainbows whose Airy patterns in light heavy-ion elastic scattering map the optical potential deep inside the nucleus.

registry.name: Gamow factor as the action through the barrier
registry.summary: The α-decay rate of Gamow and Gurney–Condon is a classical assault frequency v/2R times the WKB penetrability. Its exponent is the Hamilton–Jacobi action of the forbidden orbit under the Coulomb barrier, where the momentum is imaginary, and evaluating it gives the Geiger–Nuttall law; the same exponent sets the Gamow peak of stellar fusion.

registry.summary: Intermediate-energy collisions and hadronic afterburners are modelled with Boltzmann–Uehling–Uhlenbeck (Vlasov) transport. Hamilton's equations in the nuclear mean field carry the one-body phase-space density (Liouville flow, solved with test particles), plus Pauli-blocked collisions, and the directed and elliptic flow these simulations produce constrain the dense-matter equation of state.

registry.name: Bohr Hamiltonian: a quantized collective Lagrangian
registry.summary: The Bohr collective model takes generalized coordinates (quadrupole deformation β, γ plus three Euler angles), writes a classical kinetic energy with a deformation-dependent mass tensor, and quantizes it in curved collective space with the Pauli prescription. Vibrator, γ-soft and rotor spectra are limits of this one Lagrangian.

registry.name: Spontaneous fission along the least-action path
registry.summary: Spontaneous-fission half-lives are computed by tunnelling through a multidimensional deformation landscape along the path that minimizes the WKB action. This is Jacobi's form of the Maupertuis principle in a collective space with a position-dependent inertia tensor, so the dynamical path differs from the static minimum-energy path.

registry.name: Rayleigh–Ritz: from vibrating plates to nuclei
registry.summary: The variational bound used throughout ab initio nuclear theory (variational Monte Carlo, truncated-basis no-core shell model, Hartree–Fock references) descends from Rayleigh's quotient for the frequencies of vibrating systems and Ritz's 1909 method for elastic plates. The quantum Rayleigh–Ritz principle is the same eigenvalue minimization.

registry.name: Pressure and shear inside the proton
registry.summary: The gravitational form factors of the energy–momentum tensor (including the D-term) are read as a continuum-mechanics stress tensor: a radial pressure p(r) and shear force s(r) inside the proton, with von Laue's equilibrium condition ∫p r² dr = 0 and a mechanical radius. First extractions came from deeply virtual Compton scattering, and the EIC will map them.
registry.breaks: Local 3D densities of a relativistic, recoiling bound state depend on the frame (Breit frame vs light front), and whether p(r) is a physical pressure is debated.

registry.name: Love numbers: from Earth tides to Lambda
registry.summary: The tidal deformability measured from GW170817's inspiral phase is built on the Love number k_2, which A. E. H. Love introduced for the elastic tidal response of the Earth. For a neutron star k_2 measures how centrally condensed the fluid is, so the measurement bounds EOS stiffness and radius.
registry.breaks: The neutron-star k_2 is a relativistic fluid response computed from perturbed TOV equations. Crust rigidity contributes negligibly, unlike the Earth's elastic Love numbers.

registry.name: Neutron-star crust as an elastic solid
registry.summary: The neutron-star crust is a Coulomb crystal whose shear modulus is set by the nuclear charges and lattice spacing. Its elastic response governs starquakes and crust breaking, the largest 'mountain' that could radiate continuous gravitational waves, and the torsional shear modes proposed for magnetar-flare QPOs.

registry.name: Heavy-ion fireballs as relativistic viscous fluids
registry.summary: Navier–Stokes hydrodynamics, made relativistic and causal (Israel–Stewart, second order), is the standard model of the heavy-ion fireball: pressure gradients turn the almond-shaped overlap into elliptic flow v_2, and fits to v_n extract the shear viscosity much as viscous damping is measured in a classical flow. Bjorken's boost-invariant expansion is an exact similarity solution of these equations.

registry.name: QCD critical point in the liquid–gas dynamic class
registry.summary: Near the conjectured QCD critical point the slow modes are diffusive baryon density coupled to shear flow, exactly as at a liquid–gas critical point. That places it in Hohenberg–Halperin Model H, with the same critical slowing down, divergent conductivity and bulk-viscosity peak, and fluctuating hydrodynamics is used to predict the proton-cumulant signals.

registry.name: Perfect liquid: eta/s of the QGP vs ordinary fluids
registry.summary: Shear viscosity, defined by Newton's law of viscous stress, is compared across fluids through η/s, the relativistic analogue of kinematic viscosity. The QGP sits near ħ/4πk_B, about an order of magnitude below helium, nitrogen or water at their minima, which makes it the most nearly ideal (Euler) fluid known.

registry.name: Irrotational and viscous liquid-drop fission dynamics
registry.summary: The descent from saddle to scission is modelled as flow of an incompressible nuclear fluid. Irrotational (Werner–Wheeler) flow gives the collective inertia, and adding two-body viscosity through Navier–Stokes (Davies–Sierk–Nix) slows the descent, stretches the neck and lowers fragment kinetic energies. Measured kinetic energies and prescission neutrons calibrate the dissipation.
registry.breaks: Nuclear dissipation is mostly one-body (nucleons hitting the moving surface), not two-body viscosity, because the nucleon mean free path is comparable to the nuclear size.

registry.name: Convective mixing sets s- and i-process yields
registry.summary: Neutron-capture nucleosynthesis depends on classical fluid instabilities. In AGB stars, partial mixing at convective boundaries forms the ¹³C pocket that powers the main s-process, convective-reactive ingestion of hydrogen into helium-burning zones drives the i-process, and in core-collapse supernovae Rayleigh–Taylor fingers carry fresh ⁵⁶Ni outward, as seen in SN 1987A.

registry.name: Fission as Rayleigh's charged-drop instability
registry.summary: Bohr–Wheeler fission is Rayleigh's instability of a charged liquid drop: surface tension restores and Coulomb repulsion drives the quadrupole mode, and the sphere loses stability when E_C = 2E_S (fissility x = 1). Because the liquid-drop barrier vanishes for the heaviest nuclei, they survive only through shell corrections, and the final neck rupture parallels Rayleigh–Plateau pinch-off.

registry.name: Heavy quarks as Brownian particles in the QGP
registry.summary: Charm and bottom quarks (M ≫ T) random-walk through the QGP like colloids in a viscous liquid. A Langevin equation with drag and momentum diffusion, tied together by the Einstein relation, describes their thermalization, and the spatial diffusion coefficient extracted from heavy-flavour R_AA and v_2 is a key transport parameter.
registry.breaks: Stokes drag 6πηa assumes a continuum fluid around a large sphere. The heavy quark is pointlike, comparable to the medium's interparticle spacing, and its drag comes from colour interactions with relativistic corrections, not from viscous boundary layers.

registry.name: Jet energy loss as a wave-turbulent gluon cascade
registry.summary: Medium-induced radiation from a jet in the QGP becomes a cascade of democratic gluon branchings. It carries energy at a constant rate from the leading parton to soft gluons and into the medium, with a Kolmogorov–Zakharov fixed-point spectrum, which explains why the lost energy reappears at large angles.

registry.name: Turbulent cascade in early QGP thermalization
registry.summary: Before hydrodynamics applies, the over-occupied gluon fields left by the collision thermalize through a self-similar, constant-flux energy cascade toward high momenta. This is a Kolmogorov–Zakharov-type wave turbulence (a non-thermal fixed point), the same idea as the Richardson–Kolmogorov cascade in fluids.

registry.name: Bohr's classical stopping power
registry.summary: Bohr's 1913 stopping theory is impulse-approximation Coulomb scattering: a fast ion passing an electron at impact parameter b gives it Δp = 2Ze²/(4πε0 b v). Integrating over b between a close-collision cutoff and the adiabatic cutoff v/ω gives the logarithmic energy loss that Bethe later made quantum, the basis of range–energy relations, Bragg peaks and detector response.

Rutherford's cross section is also exact in quantum mechanics, deviations from it still show where the nuclear force begins (closest approach, Coulomb barrier), and for heavy ions with Sommerfeld parameter η ≫ 1 classical trajectories stay quantitative.

registry.summary: By Bertrand's theorem only the oscillator and Kepler potentials have every bound orbit closed, and that classical degeneracy is why the oscillator gives large shell gaps at 2, 8, 20, 40. In realistic wells, periodic-orbit theory (Balian–Bloch, Strutinsky, the Gutzwiller trace formula) writes the oscillating level density, the shell correction behind magic numbers and superheavy stability, as a sum over the shortest closed orbits.

registry.summary: A rotating charged liquid drop follows the classical sequence of rotating fluid masses.
