registry.name: Rotating resonant cavities as modern Michelson–Morley
registry.summary: Modern isotropy tests compare the resonance frequencies of orthogonal cryogenic optical or microwave cavities on rotating platforms; any direction dependence of c shifts their beat note, which bounds photon-sector Standard-Model-Extension coefficients near the 10^-17–10^-18 level.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)
Colladay & Kostelecký (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [doi:10.1103/physrevd.58.116002](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.58.116002)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Blandford–Znajek: spinning hole as unipolar inductor
registry.summary: A Kerr black hole threaded by magnetic flux behaves like Faraday's spinning-disk dynamo: frame dragging drives an EMF across field lines, currents close through the force-free magnetosphere and the horizon's resistance, and rotational energy leaves as Poynting flux; this is the leading model for jets from magnetically arrested disks.
sources: Blandford & Znajek (1977). "Electromagnetic extraction of energy from Kerr black holes". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 179, 433. [doi:10.1093/mnras/179.3.433](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/179.3.433)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gravitoelectromagnetism and frame dragging
registry.summary: For weak fields and slow sources the metric perturbations h_00 and h_0i act as gravito-electric and gravito-magnetic potentials obeying Maxwell-like equations sourced by mass density and mass current; frame dragging (Lense–Thirring, measured by Gravity Probe B and LAGEOS) is the gravitomagnetic field of a spinning mass.
registry.map: h_{00}\leftrightarrow\phi,\ h_{0i}\leftrightarrow A_i,\ \rho\leftrightarrow\rho_q,\ \rho\mathbf v\leftrightarrow\mathbf J,\ \epsilon_0\to-1/(4\pi G)
registry.breaks: Holds only at linear order and for slow motion; factors of 2 and 4 depend on convention because the source is a spin-2 tensor; like masses attract, there are no negative masses or gravitational dipole radiation, and full GR is nonlinear.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gauge connections: vector potential vs Christoffel
registry.summary: The vector potential is a U(1) connection whose curvature is F and whose holonomy is the Aharonov–Bohm phase; in GR the Christoffel (or spin) connection plays the same role, Riemann is its curvature, and parallel transport around a loop measures it, so both are theories of connections on bundles.
registry.breaks: Gravity gauges spacetime itself (diffeomorphisms) and adds a metric/tetrad with no Maxwell counterpart; the Einstein–Hilbert action is linear in curvature while Maxwell's is quadratic, and there is no fixed background.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Proca photon vs massive graviton (Stückelberg, vDVZ)
registry.summary: A photon mass breaks gauge invariance, but the massless limit is smooth because the Stückelberg scalar decouples; the same Stückelberg trick applied to Fierz–Pauli massive gravity exposes a helicity-0 mode that does not decouple (vDVZ discontinuity), cured nonlinearly by Vainshtein screening and dRGT; both masses are bounded by wave dispersion (m_γ ≲ 10^-18 eV, m_g ≲ 10^-23 eV).
registry.breaks: The spin-1 massless limit is continuous and the spin-2 one is not: the graviton's scalar mode couples to T and changes linear-order light bending to 3/4 of the GR value; massive gravity also has the Boulware–Deser ghost, which Proca lacks.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Lorenz gauge ↔ harmonic gauge in linearized gravity
registry.summary: Linearized GR is a gauge theory of h_{μν} with δh_{μν} = ∂_μξ_ν + ∂_νξ_μ; in Lorenz (de Donder) gauge the trace-reversed perturbation obeys a sourced wave equation solved by retarded potentials exactly like A^μ, and the residual gauge freedom gives TT gauge with two transverse polarizations, as Coulomb/radiation gauge does for light.
registry.breaks: The field is rank 2 (helicity ±2 vs ±1); the gauge group is linearized diffeomorphisms, which beyond linear order become non-abelian and act on spacetime itself; source conservation ∂T = 0 is consistent only at linear order.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ashtekar variables: GR as an SU(2) gauge theory
registry.summary: Ashtekar recast GR's phase space as an SU(2) connection A^i_a conjugate to a densitized triad E^a_i that acts as a non-abelian 'electric field'; loop quantum gravity then quantizes Wilson-loop holonomies and electric fluxes, so area becomes discrete like quantized flux lines.
registry.breaks: Gravity adds the Hamiltonian and diffeomorphism constraints, which have no Yang–Mills counterpart, and the Barbero–Immirzi parameter γ; discrete area is a prediction of the quantization, not of the gauge-theory form.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Einstein–Maxwell theory: charged black holes
registry.summary: The traceless Maxwell stress–energy tensor sources Einstein's equations; solving the coupled Einstein–Maxwell system gives the Reissner–Nordström and Kerr–Newman black holes, with inner and outer horizons and an extremal limit Q = M in geometrized units.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kaluza–Klein: Maxwell from five-dimensional gravity
registry.summary: Compactifying 5D general relativity on a circle turns the off-diagonal metric components g_{μ5} into a U(1) gauge field obeying Maxwell's equations, with charge as momentum around the circle and gauge transformations as reparametrizations of the extra coordinate; it is the template for gauge fields from geometry in string compactifications.
registry.map: ds_5^2=g_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu dx^\nu+\phi^2(dy+\kappa A_\mu dx^\mu)^2;\ y\to y-\kappa\lambda\Leftrightarrow A_\mu\to A_\mu+\partial_\mu\lambda
registry.breaks: An extra radion scalar φ appears and must be stabilized; charge quantization ties e to the circle radius, and the minimal theory cannot produce chiral fermions, which string theory gets from richer compactifications.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Covariant Lorentz force as relativistic dynamics
registry.summary: The covariant Lorentz force dp^μ/dτ = qF^{μν}u_ν is the prototype relativistic equation of motion: the antisymmetry of F keeps u·u fixed, so rest mass is conserved, and it gives the relativistic cyclotron frequency qB/(γm) that forced the move from cyclotrons to synchrotrons.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: E and B as components of one Lorentz tensor
registry.summary: Under a boost E and B mix as components of the antisymmetric tensor F^{μν} = ∂^μA^ν − ∂^νA^μ, so magnetism is electrostatics seen from a moving frame; E² − c²B² and E·B are the Lorentz invariants that classify fields.
registry.map: F'^{\mu\nu}=\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^\nu{}_\beta F^{\alpha\beta};\ \mathbf E'_\perp=\gamma(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)_\perp,\ \mathbf E'_\parallel=\mathbf E_\parallel
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Ann. Phys.* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Membrane paradigm: horizon as a 377 Ω conductor
registry.summary: For external static observers the stretched horizon behaves as a 2D conducting membrane whose surface charges and currents terminate field lines, with surface resistivity equal to the impedance of free space; a charge lowered toward a hole has its field lines drawn onto the horizon like the induced charge on a conducting sphere.
registry.breaks: The membrane is a fictitious bookkeeping surface with no charge carriers, and it is teleological: it responds to fields before they arrive. The description fails for observers falling through the horizon.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fresnel drag as relativistic velocity addition
registry.summary: Fizeau (1851) found that light in flowing water is dragged by the fraction 1 − 1/n² of the flow speed, which Fresnel put down to partial ether drag; von Laue (1907) showed it is exactly the first-order relativistic addition of c/n and v.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kerr multipole moments and the no-hair theorem
registry.summary: A stationary spacetime has Geroch–Hansen mass and current multipole moments analogous to those of a static charge distribution; for Kerr all of them are fixed by M and a, so an independent measurement of the quadrupole −Ma² (EMRIs with LISA, ringdown spectroscopy, pulsar–black-hole timing) tests the no-hair theorem.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Multipole radiation: Larmor to the quadrupole formula
registry.summary: Gravitational radiation is organized by the same multipole expansion as EM radiation, but conservation of mass and momentum removes the monopole and dipole terms, so the leading emission comes from the reduced mass quadrupole with power ∝ (d³Q/dt³)², paralleling Larmor's ∝ (d²p/dt²)².
registry.map: P_{GW}=\frac{G}{5c^5}\langle\dddot Q_{ij}\dddot Q_{ij}\rangle\ \leftrightarrow\ P_{EM}=\frac{\mu_0\ddot p^2}{6\pi c}
registry.breaks: Gravity is spin-2 and has one sign of charge, so there is no dipole radiation; it is nonlinear, the radiated energy itself gravitates (Isaacson tensor, memory), and the expansion uses tensor rather than vector harmonics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Superradiance: Kerr black hole as an amplifier
registry.summary: Waves with ω < mΩ_H that scatter off a Kerr hole are amplified by tapping its rotation (Zel'dovich–Starobinsky superradiance, the wave form of the Penrose process); Bekenstein read this as stimulated emission paired with spontaneous Hawking emission, and a mirror or a massive field's own potential turns the gain into a laser-like 'black-hole bomb' instability.
registry.breaks: The gain comes from horizon rotation, not population inversion, and it saturates as the hole spins down; ultralight-boson clouds (current research) radiate continuous GWs rather than light.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Stabilized lasers and Fabry–Pérot cavities in GW detectors
registry.summary: Interferometric GW detection rests on laser engineering: 1064 nm Nd:YAG-based lasers frequency-stabilized by Pound–Drever–Hall locking, mode-cleaner cavities, km-scale Fabry–Pérot arms, and power/signal recycling that builds up hundreds of kW of circulating light, which sets the shot-noise floor.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Transformation optics: spacetime geometry as a medium
registry.summary: Maxwell's equations on a curved spacetime, or in transformed coordinates, are the same as those in flat space with an impedance-matched anisotropic medium ε = μ (Plebanski; Gordon's optical metric for moving media); transformation optics inverts the map to design cloaks and metamaterial analogues of black holes, Einstein rings and cosmic strings.
registry.breaks: Only light propagation on a fixed geometry is mimicked, with no gravitating dynamics; dispersion and loss restrict it to narrow bands, and g_{0i} ≠ 0 requires magnetoelectric coupling.
sources: Leonhardt (2006). "Optical Conformal Mapping". *Science* 312, 1777. [doi:10.1126/science.1126493](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1126493)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fibre-optical event horizons and analogue Hawking light
registry.summary: A soliton in a fibre raises the refractive index through the Kerr effect; in its co-moving frame, probe light slower than the pulse cannot cross the front, which forms black/white-hole horizon pairs, and the frequency conversion observed there is the stimulated analogue of Hawking emission.
registry.breaks: Strong optical dispersion regularizes the trans-Planckian region, so the spectrum is not exactly thermal; there is no gravity, entropy or backreaction, and claims of spontaneous analogue Hawking photons in bulk glass are disputed.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Squeezed light from OPOs beats detector shot noise
registry.summary: Optical parametric oscillators (χ(2) down-conversion below threshold) generate squeezed vacuum that is injected at the dark port, cutting shot noise by about 2–3 dB in LIGO and Virgo since O3; in O4 a 300 m filter cavity rotates the squeezing angle with frequency so that radiation-pressure noise is not raised at low frequency.
sources: Walls (1983). "Squeezed states of light". *Nature* 306, 141. [doi:10.1038/306141a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/306141a0)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Parametric down-conversion ≡ particle creation
registry.summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion and Hawking, Unruh or cosmological particle creation are the same Bogoliubov transformation of mode operators: the output is a two-mode squeezed vacuum that looks thermal when one partner mode is traced out, with the temperature set by the squeeze parameter.
registry.map: \hat b_1=\cosh r\,\hat a_1+\sinh r\,\hat a_2^\dagger,\ \langle n\rangle=\sinh^2r;\ \text{Hawking: }\tanh r=e^{-\pi\omega/\kappa}\ (\hbar=c=1)
registry.breaks: In optics the pump is an external classical field acting through a χ(2) medium; in gravity the 'pump' is the spacetime geometry, and the partner modes lie behind a horizon.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Vacuum Cherenkov radiation bounds Lorentz violation
registry.summary: Cherenkov emission needs v > c/n; if Lorentz violation made the vacuum photon phase speed lower than a particle's maximal speed, charged particles above a threshold would radiate in vacuum, so the survival of TeV–PeV electrons and protons from cosmic-ray and gamma-ray sources bounds Standard-Model-Extension coefficients.
sources: Colladay & Kostelecký (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [doi:10.1103/physrevd.58.116002](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.58.116002)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dipole radiation as a signature of scalar–tensor gravity
registry.summary: GR forbids gravitational dipole radiation, but in scalar–tensor theories bodies with different scalar charges (sensitivities) emit scalar dipole radiation at −1PN relative to the quadrupole, just as an EM dipole radiates when charge-to-mass ratios differ; binary-pulsar and GW inspiral timing bound it tightly.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radiation reaction: Abraham–Lorentz vs 2.5PN
registry.summary: Radiation back-reacts on its source: through the Abraham–Lorentz(–Dirac) force for charges and the Burke–Thorne 2.5PN potential for masses, whose integration gives the Peters–Mathews inspiral and chirp; the gravitational self-force programme (MiSaTaQuWa) mirrors the DeWitt–Brehme treatment of point charges.
registry.breaks: EM reaction is dipolar (third time derivative) and gravitational reaction is quadrupolar (fifth derivative, 2.5PN); the gravitational self-force is gauge dependent, and the runaway solutions of ALD have no clean gravitational analogue.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Accelerated-charge radiation and the Unruh bath
registry.summary: Seen from the co-accelerating frame, the Larmor radiation of a uniformly accelerated charge is emission and absorption of zero-energy Rindler photons from the thermal Unruh bath (Higuchi–Matsas–Sudarsky 1992); this ties a classical radiation formula to the Unruh effect and to the equivalence-principle puzzle of whether a supported charge radiates.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Black-hole scattering: partial waves, glory, orbiting
registry.summary: Wave scattering by a black hole is solved with the partial-wave and Regge-pole methods of Mie theory; the cross section shows a backward glory and orbiting oscillations tied to the photon sphere, and in the eikonal limit its Regge poles are the quasinormal modes.
registry.breaks: A black hole is a perfect absorber with a long-range 1/r potential (Coulomb-like phase, divergent forward cross section), unlike a finite dielectric sphere.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: HBT intensity interferometry → Bose–Einstein femtoscopy
registry.summary: Hanbury Brown and Twiss measured star sizes from intensity correlations. Goldhaber, Goldhaber, Lee and Pais (1960) found the same Bose–Einstein enhancement for like-sign pions, and LHC experiments now use it to measure femtometre source radii in pp, p–Pb and Pb–Pb collisions.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Beam optics: ray-transfer matrices for magnet lattices
registry.summary: Transverse beam dynamics uses ABCD ray-transfer matrices: drifts are free propagation, quadrupoles are thin lenses, and a FODO cell of alternating converging and diverging lenses gives net focusing (strong focusing). Chromaticity is the beam-optics version of chromatic aberration and is corrected with sextupoles.
registry.breaks: A quadrupole focuses in one transverse plane and defocuses in the other, so net focusing needs alternating gradients. Beams also have emittance (Liouville in 6D phase space), space charge and nonlinear resonances, which passive optics lacks.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Diffractive elastic pp scattering as Fraunhofer diffraction
registry.summary: High-energy elastic pp scattering (TOTEM at 13 TeV) shows a forward peak and a diffraction dip, like the Airy pattern of an absorbing disc in the momentum transfer √(−t). The optical theorem ties the forward amplitude to σ_tot, and a black disc would have σ_el/σ_tot = 1/2.
registry.breaks: The proton is grey (σ_el/σ_tot ≈ 0.26 at 13 TeV) and grows with energy (Froissart ln²s). Its amplitude has a real part and spin dependence, so a single disc cannot fit the dip depth.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Axion-induced vacuum birefringence and dichroism
registry.summary: With the coupling g a E·B, only the photon polarization component parallel to an external B mixes with an axion-like particle. A magnetized vacuum therefore becomes dichroic (real conversion) and birefringent (virtual axions), which PVLAS-type polarimeters search for. An oscillating axion background rotates linear polarization; this is the proposed explanation for a ~2–3σ hint of CMB cosmic birefringence.
registry.map: -\tfrac{g_{a\gamma\gamma}}{4}aF_{\mu\nu}\tilde F^{\mu\nu}=g_{a\gamma\gamma}\,a\,\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\ \Rightarrow\ \text{only }\mathbf E_\gamma\parallel\mathbf B_{\rm ext}\text{ mixes}
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Flavour oscillation as birefringence; MSW as adiabatic following
registry.summary: Two neutrino flavours behave like two linear polarizations, and the mass eigenstates like the axes of a birefringent plate, so the conversion probability has the same form as light leaking through crossed polarizers. Solar MSW conversion is the analogue of light adiabatically following the axes of a slowly twisted birefringent medium (the Poincaré/Bloch-sphere picture).
registry.breaks: There are three flavours with a CP-violating phase and an absolute mass ordering, while light has only two polarization states. The phase comes from mass differences, not refractive-index differences.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Maxwell theory as abelian Yang–Mills
registry.summary: Covariant electrodynamics is the U(1) case of Yang–Mills theory: the same action, field strength and field equations. Yang–Mills adds a commutator term that makes gluons and W bosons self-interacting, while photons do not interact with each other.
registry.breaks: The non-abelian commutator gives cubic and quartic self-couplings, asymptotic freedom and confinement, none of which classical electromagnetism has.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Haloscope: axions drive a resonant microwave cavity
registry.summary: In a static field B₀, dark-matter axions act as an oscillating effective current g ȧ B₀. This current drives the TM₀₁₀ mode of a tuned cavity when ω = m_a c²/ħ, as in Sikivie's haloscope (ADMX, HAYSTAC). Sensitivity depends on standard cavity quantities: mode form factor, volume, Q and tuning range.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Waveguide cutoff modes = Kaluza–Klein mass tower
registry.summary: Confining a massless field in compact transverse directions quantizes its transverse momentum. Each guided mode then follows a massive-particle dispersion relation along the free direction, with the cutoff frequency playing the role of the Kaluza–Klein mass.
registry.breaks: Conducting walls impose Dirichlet/Neumann conditions instead of periodicity, so TE/TM spectra (and the missing TM zero mode) differ from a KK circle, and the waveguide geometry produces no gauge field.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: RF cavities accelerate collider beams
registry.summary: Beams gain energy from the longitudinal E field of the TM₀₁₀ mode of resonant cavities. The achievable gradient (~30–40 MV/m for superconducting niobium in the ILC, ~70–100 MV/m for normal-conducting X-band in CLIC) sets the length and cost of linear colliders.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Axion electrodynamics: modified Maxwell equations
registry.summary: Adding g a E·B to the Maxwell Lagrangian gives effective charge and current densities proportional to ∇a and ȧ. These are the field equations behind haloscopes, helioscopes and stellar-cooling bounds. The same equations with constant θ = π describe the magnetoelectric response of topological insulators.

registry.name: Kaluza–Klein: electromagnetism from a fifth dimension
registry.summary: Five-dimensional general relativity on a small circle reduces to 4D gravity plus Maxwell theory plus a scalar. The off-diagonal metric components g_{μ5} play the role of A_μ, and U(1) gauge transformations are reparametrizations of the circle. This is the ancestor of modern large and warped extra-dimension models.

registry.name: Magnetic monopoles: Dirac quantization and GUT monopoles
registry.summary: A magnetic charge makes Maxwell's equations symmetric, and Dirac showed that a single monopole would force electric charge to be quantized. Breaking a simple GUT group down to U(1)_em necessarily creates 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles of mass ~M_X/α. Their predicted overabundance helped motivate inflation; MoEDAL and IceCube searches have found none.

registry.name: Quantized Maxwell field: the first quantum field theory
registry.summary: A normal-mode expansion turns the free Maxwell field into independent harmonic oscillators, and quantizing them (Dirac 1927) gives photons. Gauge redundancy forced the Coulomb-gauge, Gupta–Bleuler and later BRST treatments that became the template for quantizing every gauge field.
registry.map: H=\sum_{\mathbf k,\lambda=\pm}\hbar\omega_k\left(a^\dagger_{\mathbf k\lambda}a_{\mathbf k\lambda}+\tfrac12\right),\quad [a_{\mathbf k\lambda},a^\dagger_{\mathbf k'\lambda'}]=\delta_{\mathbf k\mathbf k'}\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}

registry.name: Gauge transformations and the covariant derivative
registry.summary: The freedom A→A+∂χ of electromagnetic potentials, paired with a local phase change of charged matter fields, is the gauge principle. Yang and Mills extended it to non-abelian groups, where A becomes a matrix-valued connection and the potentials become the fundamental fields.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Aharonov–Bohm phase as the Wilson loop
registry.summary: The Aharonov–Bohm phase around a solenoid is the holonomy of the U(1) connection. Wilson made these parallel transporters the basic lattice variables (link variables) and used the Wilson loop as the order parameter for confinement (area law).
registry.map: U_{x,\mu}=e^{iagA_\mu(x)},\quad W(C)=\prod_{\ell\in C}U_\ell\to e^{\frac{iq}{\hbar}\oint_C\mathbf A\cdot d\mathbf l}=e^{iq\Phi_B/\hbar}
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thomas–BMT spin precession and the magic momentum
registry.summary: The muon g−2 experiment measures how much faster the spin precesses (Thomas–BMT equation) than the momentum rotates, in a 1.45 T storage ring with field mapped by proton NMR. At γ = 29.3 (3.094 GeV/c) the motional-E term from electrostatic focusing cancels, so a_μ follows from ω_a and B alone. Fermilab's final result (2025) reached 127 ppb.
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

registry.name: Weizsäcker–Williams photons in ultraperipheral collisions
registry.summary: Lorentz contraction flattens an ultrarelativistic charge's field into a transverse pancake, equivalent to a flux of quasi-real photons with a spectrum ∝ Z²α/ω. With the Z⁴ enhancement, Pb–Pb ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC act as a photon–photon collider, where light-by-light scattering and γγ→ℓℓ are measured.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: E·B invariant as the chiral-anomaly density
registry.summary: The pseudoscalar Lorentz invariant FF̃ ∝ E·B is the U(1) Chern–Pontryagin density. As a total derivative it has no classical effect, but it sources the ABJ anomaly: π⁰→γγ, and chiral charge pumping when E and B are parallel (the chiral magnetic effect).
sources: Adler (1969). "Axial-Vector Vertex in Spinor Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 177, 2426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: The photon as the unbroken U(1)_em combination
registry.summary: Maxwell theory is the massless U(1) that survives when the Higgs breaks SU(2)_L×U(1)_Y. The electron charge is fixed by g, g′ and the weak mixing angle, and the Z is the orthogonal, massive combination — classical electrodynamics is the low-energy remnant of electroweak theory.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Shockley–Ramo theorem: signals from weighting fields
registry.summary: The current that a drifting charge induces on a readout electrode (silicon strips and pixels, wire chambers, TPC pads) follows from Green's reciprocity. One solves Laplace's equation with that electrode at unit potential and all others grounded, and the induced current is the charge's velocity dotted into this weighting field.

registry.name: Coulomb's law as the photon propagator
registry.summary: The Green's function of Poisson's equation is the Fourier transform of the static one-photon-exchange propagator 1/q². In the Born approximation, tree-level exchange of a massless boson gives the 1/r potential and a massive one gives Yukawa's e^{-mr}/r.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Vacuum polarization: the vacuum as a dielectric
registry.summary: Virtual e⁺e⁻ pairs screen a bare charge the way bound charges do in a dielectric, so the effective charge grows at short distances (the Uehling potential). The running α(Q²) behaves like a scale-dependent permittivity, rising from 1/137 to about 1/128 at m_Z.
registry.breaks: Lorentz invariance forces εμ = 1 for the vacuum (there is no rest frame), the response depends on q² rather than on frequency alone, and the screening is UV-divergent. The bare charge cannot be observed, so it has to be renormalized.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Asymptotic freedom as vacuum paramagnetism
registry.summary: Since εμ = 1 for a relativistic vacuum, antiscreening (ε < 1) is the same thing as paramagnetism (μ > 1). In the Nielsen–Hughes picture, the Pauli paramagnetism of spin-1 gluons outweighs their orbital Landau diamagnetism and quark screening, which gives the sign of the QCD β-function.
registry.breaks: The picture is one-loop and perturbative. It says nothing directly about confinement, and the constant chromomagnetic background it uses is unstable (Nielsen–Olesen).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Magnetic spectrometry: momentum from track curvature
registry.summary: Collider detectors measure momentum from how much charged tracks bend in solenoid or toroid fields (the 3.8 T CMS solenoid, the ATLAS toroids), designed from Biot–Savart field maps. Because the sagitta shrinks as 1/p, momentum resolution degrades in proportion to p.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: MAC-E filter: adiabatic magnetic collimation (KATRIN)
registry.summary: Tritium β electrons spiral along a field that falls by ~10⁴ from the source to the analysing plane. Adiabatic invariance of the magnetic moment converts transverse into longitudinal energy, so an electrostatic retarding potential becomes a sharp high-pass filter. KATRIN used this to set m_ν < 0.45 eV (90% CL, 2025).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: 2D multipole expansion of accelerator magnets
registry.summary: Accelerator magnet fields are written as a complex 2D multipole series: dipoles bend, quadrupoles focus, sextupoles correct chromaticity and octupoles damp instabilities. LHC magnet quality is specified by the error coefficients b_n and a_n, in units of 10⁻⁴ at R_ref = 17 mm.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Electric dipole moments as P- and T-odd multipoles
registry.summary: A permanent EDM along a particle's spin is odd under both P and T, so by CPT it signals CP violation. Electron (ACME, JILA) and neutron EDM limits probe CP violation far beyond the tiny CKM-phase prediction and constrain baryogenesis models.
registry.map: H=-\mu\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf B-d\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E,\quad P,T:\ \boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E\to-\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: E1/M1 radiative transitions in quarkonium
registry.summary: Radiative decays such as ψ(2S)→γχ_cJ (E1) and J/ψ→γη_c (M1) obey the same multipole selection rules and rate formulas as atomic transitions. They were used to map the charmonium and bottomonium spectra and to test potential models.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Plasma frequency as photon mass: Anderson's route to Higgs
registry.summary: Transverse waves in a plasma obey ω² = ω_p² + c²k², the dispersion relation of a massive photon. From plasmons and the Meissner effect, Anderson (1963) argued that gauge bosons can gain mass without a leftover Goldstone boson. Englert–Brout, Higgs and Guralnik–Hagen–Kibble made this precise, and it became electroweak symmetry breaking.
registry.breaks: A plasma picks out a rest frame and breaks Lorentz invariance, and its longitudinal plasmon is not the W's longitudinal mode. The Higgs vacuum is Lorentz-invariant and has a physical scalar left over.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Euler–Heisenberg: the QED vacuum as a Kerr medium
registry.summary: Integrating out the electron leaves four-photon operators suppressed by 1/m_e⁴, which act as a third-order susceptibility χ⁽³⁾ of the vacuum. This predicts light-by-light scattering, observed by ATLAS and CMS in ultraperipheral Pb–Pb collisions, and vacuum birefringence in strong fields, which has not yet been seen in the laboratory.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Strong-field QED at the laser intensity frontier
registry.summary: Chirped-pulse amplification pushes laser fields toward the Schwinger critical field. Once the normalized amplitude a₀ ≫ 1, multiphoton processes stop being perturbative in the laser field, so nonlinear Compton scattering and multiphoton Breit–Wheeler pair creation (SLAC E144) are computed with laser-dressed Volkov propagators (Furry picture).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cherenkov and transition-radiation particle ID
registry.summary: RICH and DIRC detectors measure β from the Cherenkov angle, which together with the tracker momentum gives the mass and separates π, K and p (LHCb, ALICE, Belle II). Transition-radiation detectors such as the ATLAS TRT separate electrons from pions using the γ-dependence of transition-radiation yield.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cherenkov light as the neutrino detector
registry.summary: Water and ice detectors (Super-K, SNO, IceCube) see neutrino interactions through the Cherenkov cones of the charged secondaries. A sharp ring marks a muon and a fuzzy ring an electron shower, and the cone direction points back to the source. At EeV energies, coherent Askaryan radio emission from the shower's charge excess takes over (ARA, RNO-G).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Synchrotron loss sets collider size and choice of particle
registry.summary: The relativistic Larmor (Liénard) power of a charge on a circular orbit grows as γ⁴/R², so the energy lost per turn limits circular e⁺e⁻ machines (the size of FCC-ee and CEPC). This pushes designs toward linear colliders or muons, which radiate (m_e/m_μ)⁴ ≈ 5×10⁻¹⁰ times less.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Angular ordering from coherent soft radiation
registry.summary: In the QED Chudakov effect, a fresh e⁺e⁻ pair radiates soft photons mainly inside its opening angle, because outside it the pair looks neutral and the two amplitudes cancel. The same coherence orders successive gluon emissions in angle, which underlies angular-ordered parton showers and the hump-backed plateau of hadron spectra in jets.
registry.breaks: Gluons carry colour and radiate themselves (C_A vs C_F). Colour-interference terms beyond leading N_c and non-global logarithms have no QED counterpart.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Bremsstrahlung, radiation length and EM showers
registry.summary: High-energy electrons lose energy by bremsstrahlung (the QED version of radiation from a decelerated charge) and photons convert to pairs over 9X₀/7. Alternating these processes builds an electromagnetic shower whose depth grows like ln E, which is the basis of electromagnetic calorimetry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (Project 8)
registry.summary: Single β-decay electrons trapped in a magnetic field emit femtowatt cyclotron radiation, and its relativistic frequency gives their energy. Project 8 measured a first tritium spectrum and neutrino-mass limit this way (2023) and aims for ~40 meV sensitivity with atomic tritium.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Soft-photon theorem: classical radiation from sudden kicks
registry.summary: The low-frequency Liénard–Wiechert spectrum of charges whose velocities change suddenly is exactly Weinberg's soft factor multiplying any QED amplitude. Its 1/ω photon number is the infrared divergence, which Bloch–Nordsieck summation over unresolved soft photons removes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Classical self-energy and radiation reaction → mass renormalization
registry.summary: A point electron's field energy diverges linearly as its radius goes to zero, and Abraham–Lorentz radiation reaction has runaway solutions. QED softens the divergence to a logarithm (Weisskopf 1939, through positron screening) and absorbs it into the observed mass — the first renormalization.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Coherent forward scattering → refractive index (MSW)
registry.summary: A medium's refractive index is fixed by the forward scattering amplitude of its scatterers, the same physics as the optical theorem. Wolfenstein applied this to neutrinos: charged-current forward scattering on electrons gives ν_e an extra potential √2 G_F N_e, which changes the effective mixing in the Sun and Earth.
registry.map: n-1=\frac{2\pi N f(0)}{k^2},\quad V_{CC}=\sqrt2\,G_FN_e,\quad \sigma_{\rm tot}=\frac{4\pi}{k}{\rm Im}f(0)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thomson → Klein–Nishina: Compton scattering at tree level
registry.summary: The classical Thomson cross-section 8πr_e²/3 is the ω→0 limit of the tree-level QED Klein–Nishina result. The low-energy theorem guarantees this limit holds to all orders, and Compton scattering was the first QED amplitude checked against experiment.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Coherent vs incoherent diffraction as speckle statistics
registry.summary: In diffractive vector-meson production off nuclei, the coherent cross section is the square of the configuration-averaged amplitude and the incoherent part is its variance (Good–Walker). This is the same split as specular versus diffuse speckle scattering in the statistical optics of random media. The coherent t-spectrum images the average gluon density and the incoherent one its event-by-event fluctuations, a key saturation probe at the EIC.
registry.breaks: The average runs over quantum configurations of nucleons and gluon hot spots in the target, not over a classical ensemble of scatterers. Saturation also makes the amplitude non-linear in the density.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: HBT intensity interferometry becomes femtoscopy
registry.summary: Hanbury Brown–Twiss intensity interferometry was invented to measure stellar diameters and became femtoscopy in nuclear physics. Two-pion Bose–Einstein correlations (the GGLP effect, 1960) measure the space-time size of the emitting source, and the HBT radii R_out, R_side and R_long test hydrodynamic expansion and freeze-out. The 'HBT puzzle' (R_out/R_side ≈ 1, against early hydro predictions) was resolved by improved hydrodynamic modelling.
registry.map: C_2(\mathbf q)=1+\lambda|\tilde S(\mathbf q)|^2\approx1+\lambda e^{-R_o^2q_o^2-R_s^2q_s^2-R_l^2q_l^2}\ \leftrightarrow\ g^{(2)}=1+|g^{(1)}|^2
registry.breaks: Stellar HBT measures the spatial coherence of light from a static, distant source. Femtoscopy uses massive identical hadrons from an expanding source, so it measures homogeneity regions tied to the flow, needs Coulomb and strong final-state corrections, and gives anticorrelations for fermions.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Nucleon tomography from GPDs
registry.summary: Fourier-transforming generalized parton distributions over transverse momentum transfer gives impact-parameter densities. Exclusive processes at the EIC therefore work as a tomograph that images quarks and gluons in the transverse plane at each momentum fraction x. Interference of DVCS with the calculable Bethe–Heitler amplitude supplies the phase, playing the role of a holographic reference wave.
registry.breaks: What is imaged is a distribution in x and b_⊥ (or a Wigner quasi-distribution), not a real-space picture. GPDs enter observables through convolution integrals that cannot be uniquely inverted, unlike an optical Fourier transform.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Form factors as Fourier transforms of charge density
registry.summary: In the Born approximation, the elastic electron-scattering form factor is the Fourier transform of the charge density, just as the Fraunhofer amplitude is the Fourier transform of an aperture. Hofstadter's diffraction minima mapped nuclear charge distributions, and the slope at Q^2=0 gives the rms radius. The Sachs form factors G_E and G_M extend this to the nucleon.
registry.map: F(\mathbf q)=\int\rho(\mathbf r)e^{i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf r}d^3r\ \leftrightarrow\ U(\mathbf k_\perp)\propto\int A(\mathbf x)e^{-i\mathbf k_\perp\cdot\mathbf x}d^2x;\ \ \langle r_E^2\rangle=-6\frac{dG_E}{dQ^2}\Big|_0
registry.breaks: For the nucleon, size and Compton wavelength are comparable, so recoil spoils the 3D Breit-frame Fourier interpretation; only 2D transverse densities in the infinite-momentum frame are rigorous. Two-photon exchange also breaks the one-photon (Born) picture and is the leading explanation of the Rosenbluth versus polarization-transfer discrepancy.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Neutron optics: refractive index from scattering length
registry.summary: Slow neutrons travel through matter with a refractive index n = 1 − λ^2 N b_c/2π set by the coherent nuclear scattering length, so they refract and are totally reflected below a critical angle. Neutron guides and supermirrors at research reactors and spallation sources, and ultracold-neutron storage bottles, are built on this geometric optics. The Fermi pseudopotential 2πħ^2 N b_c/m is the zero-energy limit of the nuclear optical potential.
registry.breaks: For most materials n < 1, so the reflection is external rather than internal. The index scales as λ^2 instead of following an electronic resonance, and gravity and absorption visibly bend and weaken the beams.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Glauber diffraction theory to Glauber initial states
registry.summary: Glauber's eikonal multiple-scattering theory extended Fresnel–Kirchhoff diffraction to composite targets through the profile function 1 − e^{iχ}. Its Monte Carlo descendant gives the participant number, binary-collision number and initial eccentricities that seed every hydrodynamic flow calculation. The same Roy Glauber founded the quantum theory of optical coherence.
registry.map: \Gamma(\mathbf b)=1-e^{i\chi(\mathbf b)},\ \ f(\mathbf q)=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int d^2b\,e^{i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf b}\Gamma(\mathbf b);\ \ N_{\rm coll}=\sigma_{NN}^{\rm inel}T_{AB}(b)
registry.breaks: The Monte Carlo Glauber model used for flow keeps only the geometric overlap of nucleons and the inelastic NN cross section. It drops the wave-optical phases of the original theory.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Nuclear diffraction scattering and the black disk
registry.summary: High-energy hadron and α scattering on nuclei shows the Fraunhofer pattern of an absorbing disk, with minima at kRθ ≈ 3.83 and 7.02. The total cross section is σ_tot = 2πR^2, half elastic shadow and half absorption, which is the extinction paradox of optics. Coulomb-dominated heavy-ion scattering (large Sommerfeld parameter η) shows Fresnel diffraction and nuclear rainbows instead.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Optical pumping for polarized nuclear targets and beams
registry.summary: Circularly polarized laser light transfers angular momentum to atoms. Spin-exchange optical pumping through Rb makes polarized 3He, which serves as an effective polarized neutron target, and strained GaAs photocathodes deliver ~85–90% polarized electron beams at JLab. These beams made the recoil-polarization measurement of G_E/G_M possible, which revealed its disagreement with Rosenbluth separation.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Reactor criticality as a Helmholtz eigenproblem
registry.summary: In one-group diffusion theory the critical reactor flux satisfies the Helmholtz equation ∇^2φ + B^2φ = 0. Its fundamental shapes (cos, J_0, sin(πr/R)/r) and geometric buckling eigenvalues are the same as the cavity-mode solutions of electromagnetism. Criticality means the material buckling (k∞ − 1)/L^2 equals the geometric buckling.
registry.breaks: φ is a diffusing density, not a wave, so there is no phase or interference. Boundary conditions apply at an extrapolated surface rather than at conducting walls, and only the fundamental mode survives while higher harmonics decay.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: RF and crab cavities for the EIC
registry.summary: Electron and ion beams at CEBAF, RHIC and the EIC are accelerated and bunched by the TM010 modes of resonant cavities, many of them superconducting. The EIC adds crab cavities, transverse-deflecting modes that tilt the bunches so they collide head-on despite a 25 mrad crossing angle.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Spin vs orbital split of photon and gluon angular momentum
registry.summary: Splitting a gauge field's angular momentum into spin and orbital parts depends on the gauge, and the problem is the same for the photon (optical spin versus orbital angular momentum) and the gluon (ΔG versus L_g in the proton spin budget). The Jaffe–Manohar (canonical) and Ji (kinetic, gauge-invariant) decompositions correspond to canonical versus kinetic momentum under minimal coupling p → p − qA.
registry.map: \mathbf J_\gamma=\epsilon_0\int[\mathbf E\times\mathbf A_\perp+E_i(\mathbf r\times\nabla)A_{\perp i}]d^3r\ \leftrightarrow\ \tfrac12=\tfrac12\Delta\Sigma+\Delta G+L_q+L_g

registry.name: Equivalent-photon approximation for photoproduction
registry.summary: The Lorentz-contracted field of a fast charge is equivalent to a flux of quasi-real photons proportional to Z^2α (Fermi 1924, Weizsäcker–Williams 1934). This underlies photoproduction at the EIC (Q^2 → 0) and the photonuclear and photon–photon physics of ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC, which serve as EIC precursors.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ultrastrong magnetic fields in heavy-ion collisions
registry.summary: In off-central collisions the Lorentz-contracted Liénard–Wiechert fields of the spectator protons produce eB ~ m_π^2 (~10^14 T), the strongest magnetic fields known. They last a few fm/c, extended by Faraday induction in the conducting QGP. These fields drive searches for the chiral magnetic effect and for charge splittings in directed flow and Λ polarization; the 2022 STAR isobar blind analysis found no predefined CME signature.
registry.map: B\simeq\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{Ze\gamma v}{b^2},\ \ eB\sim m_\pi^2\ (\sim10^{14}\ \mathrm T);\ \ \mathbf J_{\rm CME}=\frac{e^2}{2\pi^2}\mu_5\mathbf B\ (\text{natural units})

registry.name: Spin–orbit coupling: atomic vs nuclear
registry.summary: Atomic spin–orbit coupling comes from the magnetic field in the electron's rest frame, with the Thomas factor ½. Mayer and Jensen's strong nuclear spin–orbit term, which produces the magic numbers, has the same L·S form. In relativistic mean-field theory it comes out of the same Dirac reduction, applied to the large scalar and vector nuclear potentials.
registry.map: H_{so}^{\rm at}=\frac{1}{2m^2c^2}\frac{1}{r}\frac{dV}{dr}\mathbf L\cdot\mathbf S\ \leftrightarrow\ H_{so}^{\rm nuc}\propto\frac{1}{r}\frac{d(V-S)}{dr}\mathbf l\cdot\mathbf s
registry.breaks: The nuclear term is not electromagnetic and is far larger relative to level spacings. Its sign lowers j = l + ½ and creates intruder states, while in atoms spin–orbit is a fine-structure correction of order α^2 with the opposite ordering.
sources: Mayer (1949). "On Closed Shells in Nuclei. II". *Phys. Rev.* 75, 1969. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.75.1969)

registry.name: Coulomb barrier and electron screening in fusion
registry.summary: Fusion and α-decay rates are set by tunnelling through the electrostatic barrier Z1Z2e^2/4πε0r, so the Gamow factor exp(-2πη) is pure Coulomb physics. Atomic electrons screen the bare charge and raise low-energy laboratory cross sections by exp(πηU_e/E); this must be removed before S-factors are used for stars, where plasma (Debye) screening takes its place. Measured screening potentials often exceed the adiabatic electrostatic estimate.
registry.map: V_C=\frac{Z_1Z_2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0r},\ \ \eta=\frac{Z_1Z_2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0\hbar v},\ \ \frac{\sigma_{\rm scr}}{\sigma_{\rm bare}}\approx e^{\pi\eta U_e/E}
sources: Gamow (1928). "Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes". *Z. Phys.* 51, 204. [doi:10.1007/BF01343196](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343196)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Coulomb energy of a charged drop sets the fission limit
registry.summary: The Coulomb term of the semi-empirical mass formula is the electrostatic self-energy of a uniformly charged sphere. Bohr–Wheeler fission theory balances it against surface tension for l=2 shape deformations, which gives the fissility x = E_C/2E_S and the liquid-drop limit Z^2/A ≈ 50. This is the nuclear version of Rayleigh's 1882 instability of a charged conducting droplet.
registry.breaks: A conducting drop carries surface charge while the nucleus carries volume charge, so the critical ratios differ. Real fission barriers, spontaneous fission and the existence of superheavy elements beyond x≈1 come from quantum shell corrections and tunnelling, not from classical electrostatics.
sources: Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)
Weizsäcker (1935). "Zur Theorie der Kernmassen". *Z. Phys.* 96, 431. [doi:10.1007/BF01337700](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01337700)

registry.name: Yukawa potential as a screened Coulomb Green's function
registry.summary: Yukawa built the nuclear force by giving the electrostatic field a mass. The static potential is the Green's function of the screened Poisson equation and reduces to Coulomb's law as μ→0; its range ħ/m_πc ≈ 1.4 fm predicted the pion. One-pion exchange is still the long-range part of every modern chiral-EFT potential.
registry.breaks: The pion is a pseudoscalar isovector, so one-pion exchange has spin–isospin and tensor structure that Coulomb's law lacks. The short-range core, two-pion exchange and three-nucleon forces have no electrostatic analogue.
sources: Yukawa (1935). "On the Interaction of Elementary Particles. I". *Proc. Phys.-Math. Soc. Jpn.* 17, 48. [doi:10.11429/ppmsj1919.17.0_48](https://doi.org/10.11429/ppmsj1919.17.0_48)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fermi density effect in ionization energy loss
registry.summary: At high βγ the polarization of the medium screens distant collisions and reduces the relativistic rise of the Bethe stopping power by the density-effect term δ. δ depends on the medium's dielectric response through its plasma frequency. Fermi's 1940 dielectric treatment showed that the same polarization field radiates Cherenkov light wherever ε(ω) > 1/β^2.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Debye screening of colour and quarkonium melting
registry.summary: Free colour charges screen the static quark–antiquark potential the same way mobile charges screen a Coulomb field, with dielectric function ε(k) = 1 + m_D^2/k^2. Heavy quarkonia therefore dissolve once the Debye length becomes smaller than their size. Matsui and Satz proposed J/ψ suppression as a QGP signature on this basis.
registry.breaks: Colour is non-Abelian and magnetic screening is non-perturbative. The imaginary part of the in-medium potential (Landau damping) dominates dissociation, and at the LHC charm quarks recombine to regenerate J/ψ.
sources: Matsui & Satz (1986). "J/ψ suppression by quark-gluon plasma formation". *Phys. Lett. B* 178, 416. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8)

registry.name: MAC-E filter: adiabatic magnetic collimation in KATRIN
registry.summary: KATRIN's MAC-E filter uses a slowly varying magnetic field, so the adiabatic invariant p_⊥^2/B turns almost all transverse momentum of tritium β electrons into longitudinal motion against an electrostatic retarding potential. This gives an energy resolution ΔE/E = B_min/B_max and sub-eV limits on the neutrino mass.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Flow eccentricities as multipole moments of the fireball
registry.summary: The initial shape of the fireball is decomposed into azimuthal multipole moments of its entropy density, the eccentricities ε_n, and hydrodynamics turns them almost linearly into flow harmonics v_n. A deformed nucleus adds its quadrupole (β_2) to ε_2, so flow data now image the deformation of 238U and 129Xe. This links back to nuclear quadrupole moments.

registry.breaks: These are 2D cylindrical moments of an entropy density, not 3D spherical moments of a charge. The response is viscous and partly non-linear rather than a static field.

registry.name: Nuclear multipole moments and deformation
registry.summary: Nuclear charge and current distributions are described by the same spherical multipoles as in electrostatics. Magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments test the shell model (Schmidt lines, single-particle Q), and the intrinsic quadrupole of a deformed nucleus is the l=2 multipole of its surface. Both are measured through the quadrupole–field-gradient coupling in atomic hyperfine structure and through Coulomb-excitation B(E2) values.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Laser isotope separation
registry.summary: When isotope shifts exceed the Doppler width, narrow-band lasers can selectively ionize or dissociate one isotope (AVLIS on atomic vapour, molecular schemes on UF6). The technique is used for uranium enrichment, for laser-ionized radioactive beams, and increasingly for medical-isotope precursors.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Muonic-hydrogen laser spectroscopy of the proton radius
registry.summary: Pulsed laser spectroscopy of the 2S–2P Lamb shift in muonic hydrogen, at about 6 μm, gave a proton charge radius of 0.84 fm, ten times more precise than before; it started the proton-radius puzzle. Frequency-comb spectroscopy of ordinary hydrogen and new electron-scattering data now largely agree with it.
sources: Pohl et al. (2010). "The size of the proton". *Nature* 466, 213. [doi:10.1038/nature09250](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09250)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Laser-driven inertial fusion of D–T
registry.summary: Inertial confinement fusion uses lasers as the driver. NIF's 192 frequency-tripled (351 nm) Nd:glass beams heat a hohlraum whose X-rays implode a D–T capsule, and since December 2022 some shots have released more fusion energy than the laser energy delivered to the target. Nonlinear-optical frequency conversion, beam smoothing and laser–plasma instabilities set the performance limits.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Laser spectroscopy of radii and moments of rare isotopes
registry.summary: Collinear and resonance-ionization laser spectroscopy measure the spins, magnetic and quadrupole moments and charge radii of short-lived isotopes from hyperfine structure and isotope shifts. The results reveal shell closures, halos and unexpected radius trends such as the large radii of neutron-rich calcium, and the method has reached nobelium. Resonance laser ion sources also provide element-selective radioactive beams.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Giant dipole resonance as a nuclear plasmon
registry.summary: The giant dipole resonance, in which protons oscillate against neutrons, is a nuclear analogue of the localized surface plasmon of a metal nanoparticle. Both are a single Lorentzian collective dipole mode that exhausts the dipole sum rule (Thomas–Reiche–Kuhn in nuclei, the f-sum rule in optics). Metal-cluster physicists describe the cluster's Mie plasmon in the same language.
registry.breaks: The restoring force is the nuclear symmetry energy, not Coulomb attraction, and both fluids move. The GDR energy falls with size (~A^-1/3), whereas the quasi-static plasmon frequency ω_p/√3 does not depend on size.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Light-by-light scattering in ultraperipheral collisions
registry.summary: The QED vacuum's Euler–Heisenberg four-photon coupling is the vacuum analogue of an optical χ^(3) Kerr nonlinearity. It was first seen as light-by-light scattering γγ → γγ in ultra-peripheral Pb–Pb collisions, using the quasi-real photon clouds of the nuclei (ATLAS evidence 2017, later CMS and ATLAS observations). The related Breit–Wheeler process γγ → e+e− is also measured there.
registry.map: \mathcal L_{\rm EH}=\frac{2\alpha^2}{45m_e^4}\big[(\mathbf E^2-\mathbf B^2)^2+7(\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B)^2\big]\ \ (\text{natural units})
registry.breaks: The Euler–Heisenberg Lagrangian is only the low-energy limit ω ≪ m_e, and UPC photon pairs at GeV energies probe the full box diagram. Laser vacuum-birefringence searches such as PVLAS have not yet reached the effective-Lagrangian signal.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: VUV frequency comb for the Th-229 nuclear clock
registry.summary: The 8.36 eV isomer of 229Th was excited with VUV lasers in 2024 and resolved with a VUV frequency comb made by cavity-enhanced seventh-harmonic generation of an infrared comb. The comb measured the transition's frequency ratio to the 87Sr optical clock and resolved its nuclear electric-quadrupole splitting in a CaF2 host. This makes a nuclear transition a candidate optical clock with enhanced sensitivity to variations of fundamental constants.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cherenkov and transition-radiation detectors
registry.summary: Cherenkov emission (cosθ_C = 1/nβ, Frank–Tamm photon yield) and transition radiation (yield ∝ γ) are the basis of threshold counters, ring-imaging Cherenkov detectors and TRDs. These identify electrons, pions and other hadrons in nuclear-physics spectrometers and the EIC's ePIC detector, and water-Cherenkov detectors use the same light to detect neutrinos. The Cherenkov angle gives β, which together with momentum gives the particle's mass.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gamma-decay multipolarity is multipole radiation
registry.summary: Nuclear γ transitions are classified as electric and magnetic 2^L-pole radiation and follow the selection rules of classical multipole radiation (EL parity (-1)^L, ML parity (-1)^(L+1)). Weisskopf single-particle estimates are the antenna formulas with nuclear transition moments inserted, and each extra multipole order costs a factor of about (kR)^2 ~ 10^-3–10^-5. That suppression is why high-L or very low-energy transitions give long-lived isomers such as the 8.4 eV M1 isomer of 229Th.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Bremsstrahlung, radiation length and showers
registry.summary: Above the critical energy, electrons lose energy mainly by bremsstrahlung in nuclear Coulomb fields, the relativistic radiation of a decelerated charge. The radiation length X0 then sets how electromagnetic showers develop in calorimeters. Because the radiative-to-collisional loss ratio grows roughly as EZ, β shielding puts low-Z material first.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Synchrotron radiation and Sokolov–Ternov polarization
registry.summary: Synchrotron power scales as γ^4/ρ^2; it limits the energy of electron storage rings and sets the EIC electron ring at up to 18 GeV. Spin-flip synchrotron emission self-polarizes stored electrons antiparallel to the field (Sokolov–Ternov, 92.4%), which HERA exploited. The EIC needs both helicities and self-polarization is slow, so it instead refreshes bunches from a polarized source while fighting radiative depolarization.

registry.name: LPM suppression and QCD radiative energy loss
registry.summary: When the formation time of a radiated quantum exceeds the mean free path, successive scatterings act coherently and suppress the radiation; for bremsstrahlung in dense matter this is the Landau–Pomeranchuk–Migdal effect. The BDMPS-Z and GLV radiative energy loss of quarks and gluons in the QGP is its non-Abelian version, governed by the transport coefficient q̂.
registry.breaks: The radiated gluon carries colour and rescatters itself, which gives ΔE ∝ q̂L^2 rather than the QED scaling. The medium is also a rapidly expanding, strongly coupled plasma rather than a static solid.

registry.name: Cyclotron radiation spectroscopy of tritium β electrons
registry.summary: Project 8 measures β-electron energies from the frequency of their cyclotron radiation, f_c = eB/2πγm_e (~26 GHz near 1 T), picked up in a waveguide; the signal power is the Larmor power of a circulating charge. The goal is the neutrino mass from the tritium endpoint, and the experiment has already set a first tritium limit.

registry.name: Laser Compton backscattering gamma sources
registry.summary: Backscattering laser or FEL photons off relativistic electrons (inverse Compton scattering) produces tunable, quasi-monoenergetic, highly polarized MeV γ beams, as at HIγS. These beams are used to measure photonuclear cross sections and giant resonances, and for nuclear resonance fluorescence assays that identify specific isotopes.

registry.name: Photon attenuation: photoelectric, Compton, pair
registry.summary: Gamma-ray detection and shielding rest on the photon–matter cross sections of light-scattering theory: photoabsorption, Compton scattering with the Klein–Nishina cross section (which reduces to Thomson's σ_T at low energy), and pair production. Together these set the exponential attenuation coefficient μ(E,Z). The Compton edge and continuum seen in every γ spectrum follow directly from Compton kinematics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Compton scattering off the nucleon: Thomson to DVCS
registry.summary: Real Compton scattering off the nucleon has the low-energy structure of light scattering: a Thomson amplitude fixed by charge and mass, then a Rayleigh-like ω^2 term set by the electric and magnetic polarizabilities. The values α_E ≈ 11×10^-4 fm^3 and β_M ≈ 2.5×10^-4 fm^3 show the proton is a very stiff object. Deeply virtual Compton scattering is the same process in the Bjorken limit, where it accesses GPDs and the Ji spin sum rule.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Compton profiles and Bjorken scaling
registry.summary: X-ray Compton profiles and Bjorken scaling in deep inelastic scattering are both impulse-approximation results. At large momentum transfer the probe scatters off quasi-free constituents, so the cross section depends on a single scaling variable and measures their momentum distribution: J(p_z) for electrons, q(x) for quarks. y-scaling in quasi-elastic electron–nucleus scattering is the intermediate case, for nucleons.
registry.breaks: Partons are confined and relativistic, so the scaling variable is a light-cone momentum fraction and the final state hadronizes instead of escaping. QCD radiation also produces logarithmic scaling violations (DGLAP), which atomic Compton profiles do not have.
sources: Bjorken (1969). "Asymptotic Sum Rules at Infinite Momentum". *Phys. Rev.* 179, 1547. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.179.1547](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.179.1547)

registry.name: Optical model as nuclear Mie scattering
registry.summary: Elastic nucleon–nucleus scattering is described by a complex potential whose imaginary part absorbs flux into other channels. This is the quantum counterpart of Mie scattering by a sphere with a complex refractive index: both use partial-wave series, separate elastic from absorption cross sections and obey the optical theorem. The name 'optical model' (the 'cloudy crystal ball') comes directly from this analogy.
registry.map: \nabla^2\psi+k^2n^2\psi=0\ \leftrightarrow\ n^2(\mathbf r)=1-\frac{U(\mathbf r)}{E},\ U=-(V+iW)f(r);\ \ \sigma_{\rm tot}=\frac{4\pi}{k}{\rm Im}f(0)
registry.breaks: Mie theory is vectorial, with two coefficient series a_n and b_n for polarization, and uses a local, energy-independent index. The nuclear potential is scalar plus spin–orbit, energy-dependent and nonlocal, and the long-range Coulomb field distorts the partial waves of charged projectiles.

registry.name: Coherent backscattering, speckle and weak localization
registry.summary: Time-reversed paths in a disordered medium interfere constructively. For light this gives the coherent-backscattering cone; for electrons it gives the weak-localization correction to the resistance. Universal conductance fluctuations are electronic speckle, a sample-specific fingerprint. Hanbury Brown–Twiss correlations reappear as electron antibunching and shot noise.
registry.breaks: Light has no Fermi statistics, and for it absorption and moving scatterers play the role of dephasing. 3D Anderson localization of light has not been convincingly shown, and claims for TiO2 powders are contested.

registry.name: The phase problem: crystallography and phase retrieval
registry.summary: A far-field diffraction pattern is the squared Fourier transform of the scattering density, so the phase is lost. Crystallography's Patterson and direct methods and optics' iterative phase retrieval (Gerchberg–Saxton, Fienup) attack the same problem. Combined with oversampling they gave coherent diffractive imaging at synchrotrons and XFELs, and Gabor invented holography for electron microscopy.

registry.name: Electron optics: Snell's law and Veselago lens at p–n junctions
registry.summary: Ballistic Dirac electrons crossing a graphene p–n junction refract according to Snell's law with an effective index ∝ ±k_F. On the hole side the index is negative, so a p–n junction acts as a Veselago lens (Cheianov–Fal'ko–Altshuler). Klein tunnelling sets the angle-dependent transmission, and focusing has been seen in hBN-encapsulated devices.
registry.breaks: λ_F is comparable to device features, so ray optics is only approximate. Smooth junctions collimate electrons toward normal incidence instead of imaging. Pseudospin conservation (Klein tunnelling) has no optical counterpart, and disorder and electron–electron scattering limit coherence.

registry.name: SQUID double slit and Josephson Fraunhofer pattern
registry.summary: A DC SQUID is a two-slit interferometer for the condensate, and the critical current of one wide junction in a field follows the single-slit Fraunhofer pattern. In general I_c(Φ) is the modulus of the Fourier transform of the critical-current density J_c(x), and Fourier-optics inversion (Dynes–Fulton) uses this to image supercurrent paths.
registry.breaks: The phase belongs to a macroscopic condensate, not to a light field, and the junction dynamics are nonlinear. The pattern is distorted by self-screening (β_L≳1) and by a Josephson length λ_J shorter than the junction. The measured quantity is a critical current, not an intensity.
sources: Josephson (1962). "Possible new effects in superconductive tunnelling". *Phys. Lett.* 1, 251. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0)

registry.name: Electron quantum optics with quantum Hall edge channels
registry.summary: Chiral quantum Hall edge channels serve as lossless one-way beam paths and quantum point contacts as tunable beam splitters. Together they build electronic Mach–Zehnder and Fabry–Pérot interferometers, which show Aharonov–Bohm oscillations and electronic Hanbury Brown–Twiss and Hong–Ou–Mandel effects. Fabry–Pérot interferometry has also measured the braiding phase of ν=1/3 anyons.
registry.breaks: Electrons are fermions, so they antibunch and obey Pauli exclusion. Coulomb charging effects dominate small Fabry–Pérot devices, and interactions between edge channels cause dephasing and energy relaxation, which limit visibility in a way photons do not.

registry.name: Neumann's principle: crystal system fixes optical class
registry.summary: The dielectric tensor must be invariant under the crystal's point group. Cubic crystals are optically isotropic; tetragonal, trigonal and hexagonal ones are uniaxial; orthorhombic, monoclinic and triclinic ones are biaxial. Birefringence and the optic axes therefore act as structural probes, as in polarizing microscopy of minerals.

registry.name: Valley-selective circular dichroism in TMD monolayers
registry.summary: Broken inversion in MoS2- and WSe2-type monolayers gives opposite Berry curvature and orbital moment at the K and K' valleys. With C3 symmetry this makes σ+ light excite only K and σ− only K'. Helicity therefore writes and reads valley polarization (valleytronics) and reveals the valley Zeeman splitting.

registry.name: Magneto-optics: Faraday and Kerr rotation read M
registry.summary: Magnetization makes the dielectric tensor gyrotropic, with an antisymmetric off-diagonal part proportional to M. The two circular polarizations then see different indices, rotating linear polarization in transmission (Faraday) and reflection (MOKE). Kerr microscopy images domains and skyrmions, and garnet ferrimagnets are used in optical isolators.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Nematics as field-switchable birefringent wave plates
registry.summary: A nematic is a uniaxial birefringent medium with its optic axis along the director. Jones-calculus retardation between crossed polarizers, switched by the field-driven Fréedericksz transition, is how every LCD works. Cholesterics add selective Bragg reflection of one circular polarization, and q-plates with a patterned director imprint Pancharatnam–Berry phases.

registry.name: Quantized conductance as electron-waveguide mode counting
registry.summary: In the Landauer–Büttiker picture a point contact is an electron waveguide. Each transverse mode that rises above cutoff as the contact widens adds 2e²/h to the conductance, just as TE/TM modes open in a metal waveguide.
registry.breaks: Electrons are fermions filled up to E_F, so only modes at the Fermi energy carry current and the contact resistance h/(2e²N) is intrinsic. Spin degeneracy and interactions (the 0.7 anomaly) have no counterpart in a lossless EM waveguide.

registry.name: Graphene's universal πα absorption
registry.summary: Interband transitions of massless Dirac electrons give a frequency-independent sheet conductivity e²/4ħ. Putting it into the Fresnel transmission of a conducting sheet shows that a suspended monolayer absorbs πα≈2.3% of visible light, so a transmission measurement reads off the fine-structure constant.

registry.name: Long Josephson junction as a superconducting stripline
registry.summary: A long Josephson junction is a parallel-plate transmission line that carries a slow Swihart mode. Its nonlinear phase obeys the sine-Gordon equation, whose kink solitons are fluxons each carrying one flux quantum. Superconducting coplanar resonators and junction-embedded transmission lines are the microwave hardware of circuit QED and traveling-wave parametric amplifiers.

registry.name: Axion electrodynamics in topological insulators
registry.summary: A 3D topological insulator adds a θE·B term to the Maxwell Lagrangian, with θ=π fixed by time reversal. This gives a quantized magnetoelectric effect, image magnetic monopoles and a half-quantized surface Hall conductance once T is broken at the surface. THz Faraday and Kerr rotations quantized in units of α are the observable signature.

registry.name: Emergent electromagnetism of skyrmions
registry.summary: A conduction electron whose spin follows a magnetic texture picks up a Berry phase that acts as an emergent vector potential. Each skyrmion carries one emergent flux quantum h/e, which produces the topological Hall effect, and moving skyrmions induce an emergent electric field.

registry.name: London equation: the vector potential gives the photon a mass
registry.summary: In a superconductor the supercurrent is proportional to the vector potential, which is gauge invariant only once the condensate phase gradient is included. Combined with Ampère's law this expels B over the London depth (the Meissner effect): a frequency-independent counterpart of the skin depth, and the condensed-matter case of the Anderson–Higgs mechanism.

registry.name: Gauge-invariant phase difference and flux quantization
registry.summary: Josephson physics depends on the gauge-invariant phase difference, in which the line integral of the vector potential enters as an Aharonov–Bohm-type phase. Fluxoid quantization in units of h/2e follows, and so does the fact that SQUIDs read out the loop integral of A. The AC Josephson relation ties voltage to frequency, which is the basis of the voltage standard.

registry.name: Chiral anomaly driven by the invariant E·B
registry.summary: Parallel E and B pump charge between Weyl nodes of opposite chirality at a rate set by the Lorentz invariant E·B (the dual-field invariant of covariant electrodynamics), through the chiral lowest Landau level. This is the Adler–Bell–Jackiw anomaly in a crystal (Nielsen–Ninomiya), and it predicts negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, which current-jetting artefacts complicate.

registry.name: Magnetostatic energy, demagnetizing fields and domains
registry.summary: Describing a magnetized body by its bound magnetic charges and currents gives the demagnetizing field and its dipolar self-energy. That energy produces shape anisotropy and, balanced against exchange and crystalline anisotropy, breaks ferromagnets into domains and stabilizes bubble and dipolar-skyrmion textures.

registry.name: Coulomb blockade from dot capacitance
registry.summary: Adding one electron to a quantum dot costs the charging energy e²/2C. C and the dot–gate capacitance matrix come from electrostatic boundary-value problems, and gate-defined dots are designed with Poisson/Laplace solvers. Blockade needs E_C≫k_BT and tunnel resistances well above h/e², and the capacitances set the shape of the Coulomb diamonds.

registry.name: Drude: one response function for optics and DC transport
registry.summary: The Drude permittivity of fields-in-matter and the Drude conductivity of transport are the same causal response function. The DC resistivity, the plasma edge in reflectivity and the free-carrier absorption are three views of it. Kramers–Kronig relations and the f-sum rule let infrared spectra be read as transport.

registry.name: Lorentz oscillator = polar optical phonon (LST relation)
registry.summary: The Lorentz-oscillator permittivity of an ionic crystal is the response of its polar optical phonons. The macroscopic field splits LO from TO modes (Lyddane–Sachs–Teller relation), gives total reflection in the reststrahlen band between them, and mixes phonons with photons into phonon-polaritons.

registry.name: Rytova–Keldysh screening and 2D exciton binding
registry.summary: Thin-film electrostatics of a polarizable sheet gives a potential that is logarithmic below the screening length r0 and 1/r beyond it. This explains the non-hydrogenic Rydberg series and the ~0.5 eV exciton binding energies of monolayer TMDs. Changing the dielectric surroundings (encapsulation) shifts the gap and the binding energy, an approach called Coulomb engineering.

registry.name: Quantum origin of dia-, para- and ferromagnetic χ
registry.summary: The susceptibility that fields-in-matter takes as an input is quantum mechanical. By the Bohr–van Leeuwen theorem, classical statistics gives zero magnetization. Condensed matter supplies the actual sources: Landau diamagnetism, Pauli and Curie paramagnetism, and exchange-driven order. For free electrons the Landau term is −1/3 of the Pauli term.

Exchange theory supplies the cause: Weiss's molecular field is the mean field of Heisenberg exchange, which gives a Curie–Weiss susceptibility above T_c and spontaneous magnetization below it.

registry.summary: A superconductor absorbs only above ħω=2Δ (Mattis–Bardeen), and far-infrared measurements of this edge were among the first gap measurements. It is well defined, up to the polarization quantum eR/Ω, as the Berry phase of the occupied Bloch states (King-Smith–Vanderbilt). Changes in P (piezoelectric, ferroelectric, Thouless pumping) are what DFT computes and what experiments measure.

registry.name: Diode lasers: inversion between quasi-Fermi levels
registry.summary: In a semiconductor laser, population inversion is a separation of the electron and hole quasi-Fermi levels in a forward-biased p–n junction. Gain appears when the Bernard–Duraffourg condition holds. Double heterostructures and quantum wells confine both carriers and light, and Fermi–Dirac band filling takes the place of two-level atoms.

registry.name: Exciton-polariton lasing without inversion
registry.summary: When excitons couple strongly to microcavity photons they form polaritons, which can condense and emit coherent light with no population inversion: a polariton laser. The large exciton binding energy of TMD monolayers allows room-temperature polaritons, and polariton condensation in TMDs is under active study.

registry.name: Laser threshold as a Ginzburg–Landau transition
registry.summary: Near threshold the single-mode laser amplitude obeys a Ginzburg–Landau equation: the field is the order parameter and gain minus loss plays the role of reduced temperature (Haken; DeGiorgio–Scully). Above threshold a U(1) phase is chosen spontaneously, and diffusion of that phase, a Goldstone-like mode, sets the Schawlow–Townes linewidth.
registry.breaks: A laser is driven-dissipative and far from equilibrium, and its noise comes from spontaneous emission, not temperature. With few modes there is no true symmetry breaking, so the phase diffuses and the linewidth is finite. There is no gauge field, hence no Meissner or Higgs counterpart.

The result is photonic band structures, band gaps, defect states and slow-light band edges, computed with the electronic-structure toolkit (plane-wave expansion, tight-binding coupled resonators).

registry.name: High-harmonic generation in solids probes band structure
registry.summary: Strong-field HHG, first developed in atomic gases, also works in bulk crystals (ZnO and others). There it comes from intraband currents of Bloch-oscillating carriers in nonparabolic bands plus interband recombination, the three-step model adapted to bands. The cutoff grows linearly with field rather than quadratically, and harmonic spectra allow all-optical reconstruction of the band structure.
