registry.name: Ultrafast demagnetization and spintronic THz emitters
registry.summary: Femtosecond pulses demagnetize Ni in under a picosecond (Beaurepaire et al. 1996) and switch ferrimagnets such as GdFeCo all-optically. The ultrafast spin currents involved are converted to charge currents by the inverse spin Hall effect, which makes ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers broadband THz emitters. Whether spin-flip scattering or superdiffusive transport dominates is still debated.

registry.summary: Mid-infrared pumping of apical-oxygen phonons in stripe-ordered LESCO and in YBCO produces a transient c-axis optical response resembling superconductivity above T_c, with similar claims for K3C60. The interpretation is contested: heating, inhomogeneity and the analysis of reflectivity are all debated. Reports of transient Meissner-like diamagnetism are recent and unconfirmed.

registry.name: Floquet engineering of Chern bands with circular light
registry.summary: A strong circularly polarized drive dresses Bloch bands. In the high-frequency expansion it opens a Haldane-type mass at Dirac points and creates Chern bands (Oka–Aoki). Floquet–Bloch states have been seen on topological-insulator surfaces by tr-ARPES, and a light-induced anomalous Hall effect in graphene. Helical-waveguide photonic Floquet insulators use the same idea.

registry.name: Drifts from static field geometry
registry.summary: Gradient-B and curvature drifts and magnetic mirrors arise from non-uniform static magnetic fields computed from Biot–Savart and Ampère. Adiabatic invariants link to the magnetic moment of current loops.

registry.name: Aerosol and cloud scattering in forcing
registry.summary: Aerosol direct and cloud albedo effects are Mie scattering with size-dependent efficiency; the sky's blue and clouds' white arise from the same Rayleigh-to-Mie crossover.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Compton and Rayleigh scattering in X-ray imaging
registry.summary: Compton and Rayleigh scattering govern X-ray attenuation, scatter degradation of radiographs and CT contrast, and dose deposition.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Light scattering in tissue and diffuse optics
registry.summary: Tissue optics relies on Mie/Rayleigh scattering and the diffusion approximation to radiative transfer to image and measure oxygenation in turbid media.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thermodynamics derived from statistical mechanics
registry.summary: Every classical-thermodynamic potential is the logarithm of a partition function, and the laws become theorems about counting states. Thermodynamics is the macroscopic shadow of the ensemble.
registry.map: U=-\partial_\beta\ln Z,\ F=-k_BT\ln Z,\ S=k_B\ln W
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Onsager theory and efficiency at maximum power
registry.summary: In the Onsager linear-response regime a tightly coupled engine at maximum power has η=η_C/2, the first-order term of Curzon–Ahlborn. The thermoelectric figure of merit ZT is a ratio of Onsager coefficients.
sources: Van den Broeck (2005). "Thermodynamic Efficiency at Maximum Power". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 190602. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.190602](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.190602)
Onsager (1931). "Reciprocal Relations in Irreversible Processes. I.". *Phys. Rev.* 37, 405. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.37.405](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.37.405)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Stochastic and microscopic heat engines
registry.summary: Stochastic thermodynamics defines heat and work for a single colloid in a modulated optical trap, which has been run as a micrometre-scale Stirling engine. Thermodynamic uncertainty relations add a bound: power, efficiency and power fluctuations cannot all be optimal.
sources: Blickle & Bechinger (2012). "Realization of a micrometre-sized stochastic heat engine". *Nat. Phys.* 8, 143. [doi:10.1038/nphys2163](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys2163)

Pietzonka & Seifert (2018). "Universal Trade-Off between Power, Efficiency, and Constancy in Steady-State Heat Engines". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 190602. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.190602](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.190602)

registry.name: Critical working media for heat engines
registry.summary: An engine whose working substance sits near a critical point can approach Carnot efficiency at finite power. The diverging heat capacity can outweigh critical slowing down in suitable universality classes, and Ising-model engines test the idea.
sources: Campisi & Fazio (2016). "The power of a critical heat engine". *Nat. Commun.* 7, 11895. [doi:10.1038/ncomms11895](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms11895)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Maxwell's demon, Gibbs paradox and the second law
registry.summary: Entropy read as missing information resolves both the Gibbs mixing paradox (distinguishability is information) and Maxwell's demon (erasing the demon's memory costs k_BT ln 2 per bit). The Kelvin–Planck statement survives once information is booked as a thermodynamic resource.
sources: Landauer (1961). "Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process". *IBM J. Res. Dev.* 5, 183. [doi:10.1147/rd.53.0183](https://doi.org/10.1147/rd.53.0183)
Bérut et al. (2012). "Experimental verification of Landauer's principle linking information and thermodynamics". *Nature* 483, 187. [doi:10.1038/nature10872](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature10872)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Third law from quantum ground states
registry.summary: Nernst's theorem follows from quantum statistics: a non-degenerate ground state gives S→0, and degenerate gases have C∝T (fermions) or T^{3/2} (bosons) and phonons C∝T³. The classical ideal gas, with S∝ln T, violates the third law.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: H-theorem: a dynamical second law
registry.summary: Boltzmann's H-function is minus the entropy, and the Stosszahlansatz makes dH/dt≤0. Loschmidt's reversibility paradox and Zermelo's recurrence paradox show that the arrow of time comes from the low-entropy initial condition and from coarse-graining.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Second law as the average of fluctuation theorems
registry.summary: The Clausius inequality is the mean of an exact trajectory identity: the integral fluctuation theorem gives <Δs_tot> ≥ 0 by Jensen's inequality, and Jarzynski gives <W> ≥ ΔF. Single trajectories can violate the second law, but only with exponentially small probability.
registry.map: \langle e^{-\Delta s_{tot}/k_B}\rangle=1\Rightarrow\langle\Delta s_{tot}\rangle\ge0;\ \langle e^{-\beta W}\rangle=e^{-\beta\Delta F}\Rightarrow\langle W\rangle\ge\Delta F
sources: Jarzynski (1997). "Nonequilibrium Equality for Free Energy Differences". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 78, 2690. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2690](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2690)
Seifert (2012). "Stochastic thermodynamics, fluctuation theorems and molecular machines". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 75, 126001. [arXiv:1205.4176](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.4176)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Bose condensation obeys Clausius–Clapeyron
registry.summary: In the p–T plane the ideal Bose gas behaves like a first-order condensation in momentum space. Its transition line p_c∝T^{5/2} obeys Clausius–Clapeyron with a latent heat of (5/2)k_BT ζ(5/2)/ζ(3/2) per particle.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Nucleation as thermally activated barrier crossing
registry.summary: A metastable phase decays across a first-order transition by Kramers escape over the free-energy barrier of the critical nucleus. Surface tension and the difference in chemical potential between the phases set the height of that barrier.
sources: Kramers (1940). "Brownian motion in a field of force and the diffusion model of chemical reactions". *Physica* 7, 284. [doi:10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Liquid–gas critical point in the 3D Ising class
registry.summary: The end point of the liquid–vapour line, where the Clausius–Clapeyron latent heat vanishes, has 3D Ising exponents (β≈0.326, γ≈1.237). Critical opalescence is the visible sign of the diverging compressibility.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Lattice-gas isomorphism: fluids and magnets
registry.summary: The substitution n_i=(1+s_i)/2 maps a lattice gas exactly onto the Ising model, with chemical potential corresponding to field and coexistence to h=0. This is why liquid–gas, binary-alloy and uniaxial-magnet critical points share exponents.
sources: Lee & Yang (1952). "Statistical Theory of Equations of State and Phase Transitions. II. Lattice Gas and Ising Model". *Phys. Rev.* 87, 410. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.87.410](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.87.410)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Van der Waals and Maxwell construction as mean field
registry.summary: The van der Waals equation is the mean-field (Landau) theory of the liquid–gas transition. The Maxwell equal-area construction resolves its loop, and it predicts the mean-field exponents β=1/2 and δ=3.
registry.breaks: Real fluids have 3D Ising exponents (β≈0.326), not mean-field ones; van der Waals neglects the fluctuations that dominate below d=4.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Potentials as logarithms of partition functions
registry.summary: Each Legendre-transformed potential belongs to an ensemble: S to the microcanonical, F to the canonical, Ω to the grand canonical and G to the isothermal–isobaric. Response functions such as C_V and κ_T are variances in the matching ensemble.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Onsager reciprocity as dynamical Maxwell relations
registry.summary: Maxwell relations follow from the symmetry of second derivatives of a state function, and Onsager's L_ij=L_ji follows from microscopic reversibility. Both yield cross-effect equalities, such as the Kelvin relation Π=TS between the Peltier and Seebeck coefficients.
registry.map: (\partial S/\partial V)_T=(\partial p/\partial T)_V\ \leftrightarrow\ J_i=\sum_jL_{ij}X_j,\ L_{ij}=L_{ji}
registry.breaks: Maxwell relations are exact equilibrium identities of a state function. Onsager symmetry needs time-reversal invariance (L_ij(B)=L_ji(-B)), holds only in linear response, and has no generating potential beyond the dissipation function.
sources: Onsager (1931). "Reciprocal Relations in Irreversible Processes. I.". *Phys. Rev.* 37, 405. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.37.405](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.37.405)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Landau functions and the convexity of potentials
registry.summary: A coarse-grained Landau free energy can be non-convex, but the true thermodynamic potential is its convex envelope (Legendre–Fenchel). The stability conditions C_V>0 and κ_T>0 select the Maxwell construction, and spinodals mark where they fail locally.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Harris criterion: when disorder changes universality
registry.summary: Weak quenched bond disorder is relevant at a clean critical point when dν<2, equivalently α>0. The system then flows to a random fixed point with new exponents, so whether disorder matters is decided by the clean universality class.
sources: Harris (1974). "Effect of random defects on the critical behaviour of Ising models". *J. Phys. C* 7, 1671. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/7/9/009](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/7/9/009)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Epidemic thresholds as absorbing-state transitions
registry.summary: SIS and contact-process epidemics are absorbing-state transitions of a non-equilibrium steady state, in the directed-percolation class on lattices. On scale-free networks the heterogeneous mean-field threshold vanishes for γ≤3.
sources: Pastor-Satorras & Vespignani (2001). "Epidemic Spreading in Scale-Free Networks". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 86, 3200. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.86.3200](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.86.3200)
Hinrichsen (2000). "Non-equilibrium critical phenomena and phase transitions into absorbing states". *Adv. Phys.* 49, 815. [arXiv:cond-mat/0001070](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0001070)

registry.name: Critical phenomena on scale-free networks
registry.summary: Ising, percolation and epidemic transitions on networks are controlled by moments of the degree distribution. For P(k)~k^{-γ} the exponents depend on γ, and for γ≤3 the Ising T_c diverges and the percolation threshold vanishes because <k²> diverges.
registry.map: T_c^{\text{Ising}}\propto\langle k^2\rangle/\langle k\rangle;\ p_c=\frac{\langle k\rangle}{\langle k^2\rangle-\langle k\rangle}
sources: Dorogovtsev, Goltsev & Mendes (2008). "Critical phenomena in complex networks". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 1275. [arXiv:0705.0010](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.0010)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: MBL l-bits as emergent integrability
registry.summary: Fully many-body-localized systems have an extensive set of quasi-local conserved l-bits, an emergent counterpart of the integrals of motion of Bethe-ansatz models. Both evade ordinary thermalization: integrable systems relax to a generalized Gibbs ensemble, and MBL systems retain memory of local initial conditions.
registry.breaks: Bethe-ansatz integrability is fine-tuned and destroyed by generic perturbations, whereas l-bits are quasi-local and claimed to be robust. Whether MBL survives the thermodynamic limit is disputed (Sierant et al. 2024).
sources: Nandkishore & Huse (2015). "Many-Body Localization and Thermalization in Quantum Statistical Mechanics". *Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 6, 15. [arXiv:1404.0686](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.0686)

Basko, Aleiner & Altshuler (2006). "Metal–insulator transition in a weakly interacting many-electron system with localized single-particle states". *Ann. Phys.* 321, 1126. [arXiv:cond-mat/0506617](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506617)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Weak localization as a failure of Boltzmann transport
registry.summary: Boltzmann (Drude) transport adds scattering probabilities and so ignores interference. Coherent backscattering along time-reversed paths gives the weak-localization correction, logarithmic in 2D, and the Boltzmann description fails completely at the Ioffe–Regel limit k_F l ~ 1.
sources: Abrahams et al. (1979). "Scaling Theory of Localization: Absence of Quantum Diffusion in Two Dimensions". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 42, 673. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.673](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.673)

registry.name: One-parameter scaling theory of localization
registry.summary: The 'gang of four' recast Anderson localization as an RG flow of the dimensionless conductance g with system size. Because β(g)<0 for all g in d≤2, there is no metal there. In d=3 an unstable fixed point g_c is the mobility edge, a critical point with ν≈1.57 (orthogonal class).
sources: Abrahams et al. (1979). "Scaling Theory of Localization: Absence of Quantum Diffusion in Two Dimensions". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 42, 673. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.673](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.673)
Anderson (1958). "Absence of Diffusion in Certain Random Lattices". *Phys. Rev.* 109, 1492. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.109.1492](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.109.1492)

registry.name: Directed percolation and absorbing states
registry.summary: Absorbing-state transitions in driven systems (the contact process, epidemics, catalysis) generically belong to the directed-percolation class, which is percolation with a preferred time direction.
sources: Hinrichsen (2000). "Non-equilibrium critical phenomena and phase transitions into absorbing states". *Adv. Phys.* 49, 815. [arXiv:cond-mat/0001070](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0001070)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Percolation as a universality class
registry.summary: Percolation is a geometric critical point with its own exponents, which obey the same scaling and hyperscaling relations as thermal transitions. In 2D they are known exactly from Coulomb-gas and SLE methods.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fortuin–Kasteleyn: percolation is the q→1 Potts model
registry.summary: The random-cluster representation writes the q-state Potts partition function as a sum over bond clusters weighted by q^{N_c}. Taking q→1 gives bond percolation and q=2 gives Ising, whose spin correlations equal FK-cluster connectivities. This is also the basis of Swendsen–Wang cluster Monte Carlo.
sources: Fortuin & Kasteleyn (1972). "On the random-cluster model: I. Introduction and relation to other models". *Physica* 57, 536. [doi:10.1016/0031-8914(72)90045-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-8914(72)90045-6)
Swendsen & Wang (1987). "Nonuniversal critical dynamics in Monte Carlo simulations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 58, 86. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.86](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.86)

registry.name: Real-space RG for percolation
registry.summary: Kadanoff's block-spin idea applied to percolation renormalizes the occupation probability cell by cell, p'=R_b(p). The nontrivial fixed point approximates p_c, and ν follows from the linearized flow. Percolation is the cleanest teaching case of position-space RG.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Aging and FDT violation in glassy dynamics
registry.summary: Spin glasses out of equilibrium age, and their two-time response and correlation violate the FDT in a quasi-universal way that defines an effective temperature T/X. The dynamical solution of mean-field models ties X to the Parisi order-parameter function.
sources: Cugliandolo & Kurchan (1993). "Analytical solution of the off-equilibrium dynamics of a long-range spin-glass model". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 173. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.173](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.173)

registry.name: Edwards–Anderson: Ising with quenched random bonds
registry.summary: The Edwards–Anderson spin glass is the Ising Hamiltonian with random-sign couplings. Frustrated plaquettes, not disorder by itself, destroy ferromagnetic order (a Mattis gauge transform removes unfrustrated disorder), and the order parameter becomes q_EA.
registry.map: H=-\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}J_{ij}s_is_j,\ J_{ij}=\pm J;\ q_{EA}=\overline{\langle s_i\rangle^2}
sources: Edwards & Anderson (1975). "Theory of spin glasses". *J. Phys. F* 5, 965. [doi:10.1088/0305-4608/5/5/017](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4608/5/5/017)

registry.name: SK model: exact mean field for spin glasses
registry.summary: The infinite-range SK model is the spin-glass analogue of Curie–Weiss. Mean field is exact there, but it needs replicas and Parisi's replica-symmetry breaking. TAP equations give the self-consistent local magnetizations, including the Onsager reaction term.
sources: Sherrington & Kirkpatrick (1975). "Solvable Model of a Spin-Glass". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 35, 1792. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.1792](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.1792)
Thouless, Anderson & Palmer (1977). "Solution of 'Solvable model of a spin glass'". *Phil. Mag.* 35, 593. [doi:10.1080/14786437708235992](https://doi.org/10.1080/14786437708235992)
Parisi (1979). "Infinite Number of Order Parameters for Spin-Glasses". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 43, 1754. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1754](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1754)

registry.name: Droplet scaling vs RSB in finite dimensions
registry.summary: Fisher–Huse droplet theory describes short-range spin glasses by zero-temperature RG scaling, with a stiffness exponent θ and a single pair of pure states. It is the main rival to the mean-field RSB picture, and which is right in d=3 is unsettled.
sources: Fisher & Huse (1986). "Ordered Phase of Short-Range Ising Spin-Glasses". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 56, 1601. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.1601](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.1601)

registry.name: Maximum-entropy models of neural data
registry.summary: Maximizing entropy subject to measured means and pairwise correlations gives exactly a pairwise Ising (Boltzmann-machine) distribution. Fitted to retinal spike trains, it showed that weak pairwise correlations imply strongly collective states. Boltzmann-machine learning minimizes the KL divergence to the data.
registry.map: \max S[p]\ \text{s.t.}\ \langle s_i\rangle,\langle s_is_j\rangle\Rightarrow p\propto e^{\sum h_is_i+\sum J_{ij}s_is_j}
sources: Jaynes (1957). "Information Theory and Statistical Mechanics". *Phys. Rev.* 106, 620. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.106.620](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.106.620)
Schneidman et al. (2006). "Weak pairwise correlations imply strongly correlated network states in a neural population". *Nature* 440, 1007. [arXiv:q-bio/0512013](https://arxiv.org/abs/q-bio/0512013)

registry.name: Diffusion models reverse a Fokker–Planck process
registry.summary: Score-based diffusion models add noise to data with an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (Langevin) SDE, then generate samples by integrating the time-reversed SDE, whose drift contains the learned score ∇ln p_t. Stochastic gradient descent is itself often modelled as Langevin dynamics at an effective temperature.
sources: Sohl-Dickstein et al. (2015). "Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics". *ICML*. [arXiv:1503.03585](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.03585)
Song et al. (2021). "Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations". *ICLR*. [arXiv:2011.13456](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.13456)

registry.name: Boltzmann machines are inverse Ising models
registry.summary: Hopfield networks and Boltzmann machines are Ising or spin-glass Hamiltonians with learned couplings. Learning fits J_ij and h_i until model correlations match data (the inverse Ising problem), and sampling uses Glauber or Metropolis dynamics.
registry.map: P(s)\propto e^{-E(s)},\ E=-\tfrac12\sum w_{ij}s_is_j-\sum b_is_i;\ \Delta w_{ij}\propto\langle s_is_j\rangle_{\text{data}}-\langle s_is_j\rangle_{\text{model}}
sources: Hopfield (1982). "Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 79, 2554. [doi:10.1073/pnas.79.8.2554](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.79.8.2554)
Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski (1985). "A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines". *Cognitive Science* 9, 147. [doi:10.1207/s15516709cog0901_7](https://doi.org/10.1207/s15516709cog0901_7)

registry.name: Mean-field limits of neural networks
registry.summary: At infinite width, training a two-layer network becomes a nonlinear PDE for the density of neurons in parameter space: a mean-field theory exact at large N, like Curie–Weiss. Approximate message passing is the TAP equations applied to inference problems.
sources: Mei, Montanari & Nguyen (2018). "A mean field view of the landscape of two-layer neural networks". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 115, E7665. [arXiv:1804.06561](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06561)

registry.name: Renormalization group and deep learning
registry.summary: Coarse-graining layer by layer in deep networks resembles block-spin RG. One variational-RG scheme maps exactly onto stacked restricted Boltzmann machines, and networks trained on 2D Ising samples learn block-spin-like features.
registry.breaks: RG by design keeps only long-wavelength information. Generic learning keeps whatever predicts the target and need not have a fixed point or a scale hierarchy, and the exact mapping holds for one variational scheme only.
sources: Mehta & Schwab (2014). "An exact mapping between the Variational Renormalization Group and Deep Learning". [arXiv:1410.3831](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3831)

registry.name: Mermin–Wagner and the limits of 2D order
registry.summary: The Mermin–Wagner theorem, a statement about thermal fluctuations of Goldstone modes in equilibrium ensembles, forbids continuous-symmetry long-range order at T>0 in d≤2. That leaves room for BKT quasi-long-range order and makes a 2D ideal Bose gas uncondensable.
sources: Mermin & Wagner (1966). "Absence of Ferromagnetism or Antiferromagnetism in One- or Two-Dimensional Isotropic Heisenberg Models". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 17, 1133. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.17.1133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.17.1133)

registry.name: Maxwell–Boltzmann as the Boltzmann-equation fixed point
registry.summary: The stationary solution of the Boltzmann collision integral is the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution, the one-particle marginal of the canonical ensemble. Kinetic theory thus derives ensemble equilibrium dynamically, given molecular chaos.
registry.map: C[f]=0\Leftrightarrow f\propto e^{-\beta m(\mathbf v-\mathbf u)^2/2}

registry.name: Static fluctuation–response identities
registry.summary: The static limit of the fluctuation–dissipation theorem equates susceptibilities with ensemble variances. C_V, χ and κ_T measure the fluctuations of energy, magnetization and particle number, so a diverging response at criticality is the same thing as diverging fluctuations.
sources: Kubo (1957). "Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes. I.". *J. Phys. Soc. Jpn.* 12, 570. [doi:10.1143/JPSJ.12.570](https://doi.org/10.1143/JPSJ.12.570)

registry.name: Fokker–Planck stationary state is the Boltzmann distribution
registry.summary: With detailed balance and the Einstein relation D=k_BT/γ, the Smoluchowski equation relaxes to P∝e^{-βU}. Langevin thermostats and Metropolis Monte Carlo are built to sample the canonical ensemble this way.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Jarzynski free energies as partition-function ratios
registry.summary: Jarzynski's equality computes the equilibrium ratio Z_B/Z_A from non-equilibrium work samples. It is used to extract free energies from single-molecule pulling and from fast-switching simulations, alongside thermodynamic integration.

registry.name: Mean field as a variational bound on Z
registry.summary: Weiss and Bragg–Williams mean-field theory is the optimal product-state trial in the Gibbs–Bogoliubov–Feynman inequality. That makes it a controlled variational approximation to ln Z, exact when each spin has infinitely many neighbours.

registry.name: Information engines and feedback fluctuation theorems
registry.summary: Measurement and feedback (Maxwell's demon, the Szilard engine) enter the second law through the mutual information. The Sagawa–Ueda equality generalizes Jarzynski, and Landauer erasure closes the cycle. Both have been tested in colloidal and single-electron experiments.
sources: Sagawa & Ueda (2010). "Generalized Jarzynski Equality under Nonequilibrium Feedback Control". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 104, 090602. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.090602](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.104.090602)

registry.name: TASEP and KPZ: exactly solvable non-equilibrium models
registry.summary: TASEP is solved exactly by the Bethe ansatz and by a matrix-product ansatz, which give its boundary-driven phase diagram. Its height function is a discrete KPZ interface whose fluctuations follow the Tracy–Widom laws of random matrices.
sources: Derrida et al. (1993). "Exact solution of a 1D asymmetric exclusion model using a matrix formulation". *J. Phys. A* 26, 1493. [doi:10.1088/0305-4470/26/7/011](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/26/7/011)

registry.name: Exact solutions as benchmarks for phase transitions
registry.summary: Onsager's solution of the 2D Ising model was the first proof that a partition function can become non-analytic, which settled whether statistical mechanics can describe phase transitions at all. Vertex and Bethe-ansatz models supply further exact critical points.
sources: Onsager (1944). "Crystal Statistics. I. A Two-Dimensional Model with an Order-Disorder Transition". *Phys. Rev.* 65, 117. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.65.117)

registry.name: Exact exponents anchor universality classes
registry.summary: Exactly solved models fix the exponents of whole classes, for example 2D Ising (α=0 log, β=1/8, γ=7/4, ν=1). Baxter's eight-vertex model has continuously varying exponents, which shows that naive universality can fail along marginal lines.
sources: Onsager (1944). "Crystal Statistics. I. A Two-Dimensional Model with an Order-Disorder Transition". *Phys. Rev.* 65, 117. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.65.117)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Onsager transfer-matrix solution of 2D Ising
registry.summary: The transfer-matrix method in the solvable-models note is how the 2D Ising model was solved. Z=Tr T^N reduces to the largest eigenvalue, which gives T_c, the logarithmic specific heat and β=1/8.
sources: Onsager (1944). "Crystal Statistics. I. A Two-Dimensional Model with an Order-Disorder Transition". *Phys. Rev.* 65, 117. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.65.117)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Six-vertex F-model and KT-type transitions
registry.summary: The six-vertex F-model, the XXZ chain and the Lieb–Liniger gas are exactly solvable realizations of Kosterlitz–Thouless physics. Through the BCSOS mapping the F-model transition is an infinite-order roughening transition, and the gapless phases are Luttinger liquids with quasi-long-range order.
sources: van Beijeren (1977). "Exactly solvable model for the roughening transition of a crystal surface". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 38, 993. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.993](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.993)

Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum Boltzmann equation and BE/FD equilibria
registry.summary: With Pauli-blocking and Bose-enhancement factors (1±f) in the collision integral (Uehling–Uhlenbeck, Nordheim), the stationary state becomes the Bose–Einstein or Fermi–Dirac distribution. This is the basis of electron and phonon Boltzmann transport.
registry.map: C[f]\propto\int[f_3f_4(1\pm f_1)(1\pm f_2)-f_1f_2(1\pm f_3)(1\pm f_4)]\Rightarrow f=(e^{\beta(\epsilon-\mu)}\mp1)^{-1}
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: The lambda transition and the 3D XY class
registry.summary: Interacting Bose condensation, as in helium-4, is a continuous transition in the 3D XY (O(2)) class. The space-shuttle value α≈-0.0127 is the most precisely measured critical exponent. The ideal Bose gas falls instead in the spherical-model class.
sources: Lipa et al. (2003). "Specific heat of liquid helium in zero gravity very near the lambda point". *Phys. Rev. B* 68, 174518. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.68.174518](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.68.174518)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: 2D Bose gas: no BEC but a BKT superfluid
registry.summary: An ideal 2D Bose gas has no condensate at T>0, because the Bose–Einstein integral diverges. With interactions it becomes superfluid by vortex unbinding at the BKT transition, at phase-space density nλ²≈ln(ξ/g̃), as observed in trapped atomic gases.
sources: Hadzibabic et al. (2006). "Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless crossover in a trapped atomic gas". *Nature* 441, 1118. [arXiv:cond-mat/0605291](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0605291)

Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Non-equilibrium universality classes
registry.summary: Directed percolation, KPZ and conserved-sandpile classes extend universality to steady states without detailed balance. They carry independent dynamic exponents and lack the fluctuation–dissipation constraints of equilibrium classes.
sources: Hinrichsen (2000). "Non-equilibrium critical phenomena and phase transitions into absorbing states". *Adv. Phys.* 49, 815. [arXiv:cond-mat/0001070](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0001070)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dynamic RG for KPZ and driven interfaces
registry.summary: Wilson's RG extended to stochastic PDEs (dynamic RG) gives the KPZ exponents. Galilean invariance fixes χ+z=2, and in 1+1D z=3/2 and χ=1/2 exactly, the standard example of RG for non-equilibrium universality.
sources: Kardar, Parisi & Zhang (1986). "Dynamic Scaling of Growing Interfaces". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 56, 889. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dynamic critical phenomena and critical slowing down
registry.summary: Near T_c the relaxation time diverges as τ~ξ^z. The Hohenberg–Halperin dynamic classes (models A–J) depend on conservation laws and mode couplings as well as static symmetry, and the dynamic susceptibility probes them through the FDT.
sources: Hohenberg & Halperin (1977). "Theory of dynamic critical phenomena". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 49, 435. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.49.435](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.49.435)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thermodynamics extended to quantum systems
registry.summary: Quantum thermodynamics keeps the laws (energy balance, Clausius inequality, Carnot bound) but defines work and heat for density matrices and open-system maps. Coherence and entanglement act as additional resources or costs.
registry.map: dU=\mathrm{Tr}(\dot\rho H)+\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\dot H)=\dot Q+\dot W;\ \Delta S\ge\beta Q
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum heat engines and refrigerators
registry.summary: Otto, Carnot and absorption cycles run with qubits, oscillators and spins as working media; the Carnot bound survives with thermal baths. Non-thermal (squeezed, coherent) reservoirs can exceed η_C because they are not heat in the classical sense.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Third law and second laws in the quantum regime
registry.summary: The unattainability principle has been derived and quantified for quantum systems: cooling time diverges as T→0, with a bound set by the bath's density of states. For small systems the second law splits into a family of single-shot conditions.
sources: Masanes & Oppenheim (2017). "A general derivation and quantification of the third law of thermodynamics". *Nat. Commun.* 8, 14538. [arXiv:1412.3828](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3828)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Anderson localization and MBL in cold atoms
registry.summary: Optical speckle and quasiperiodic lattices made matter-wave Anderson localization directly visible (exponential density profiles), and interacting fermions in quasiperiodic lattices kept memory of an initial density wave, the first MBL signature.
sources: Billy et al. (2008). "Direct observation of Anderson localization of matter waves in a controlled disorder". *Nature* 453, 891. [arXiv:0804.1621](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.1621)
Schreiber et al. (2015). "Observation of many-body localization of interacting fermions in a quasirandom optical lattice". *Science* 349, 842. [arXiv:1501.05661](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.05661)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: MBL-protected discrete time crystals
registry.summary: Generic periodically driven many-body systems heat to infinite temperature. MBL prevents this and allows period-doubled spatiotemporal order, the discrete time crystal, which is stable to perturbations of the drive.
sources: Else, Bauer & Nayak (2016). "Floquet Time Crystals". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 117, 090402. [arXiv:1603.08001](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.08001)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hatano–Nelson: non-Hermitian localization from flux lines
registry.summary: Non-Hermitian quantum mechanics as a field grew from the statistical mechanics of flux lines pinned by columnar defects in superconductors. An imaginary vector potential (tilted field) delocalizes Anderson states, the first non-Hermitian localization transition and the ancestor of the non-Hermitian skin effect.
sources: Hatano & Nelson (1996). "Localization Transitions in Non-Hermitian Quantum Mechanics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 77, 570. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.570](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.570)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Level statistics: Poisson vs Wigner–Dyson
registry.summary: Spectral statistics diagnose both Anderson/MB localization and quantum chaos: localized states give Poisson level spacings, and ergodic or extended states give random-matrix (GOE) repulsion. The ratio ⟨r⟩ is the standard order parameter for the MBL transition.
sources: Oganesyan & Huse (2007). "Localization of interacting fermions at high temperature". *Phys. Rev. B* 75, 155111. [arXiv:cond-mat/0610854](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0610854)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Many-body localization as ETH failure
registry.summary: MBL is the main known mechanism by which an interacting, non-integrable quantum system violates ETH. Eigenstates have area-law entanglement and Poisson level statistics, and local memory survives forever.
sources: Nandkishore & Huse (2015). "Many-Body Localization and Thermalization in Quantum Statistical Mechanics". *Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 6, 15. [arXiv:1404.0686](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.0686)

Basko, Aleiner & Altshuler (2006). "Metal–insulator transition in a weakly interacting many-electron system with localized single-particle states". *Ann. Phys.* 321, 1126. [arXiv:cond-mat/0506617](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506617)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Measurement-induced transitions and percolation
registry.summary: In monitored random circuits, the zeroth Rényi entanglement entropy maps exactly onto a minimal cut through a percolation cluster. The measurement-induced volume-to-area-law transition therefore becomes classical percolation in this limit, and higher Rényi entropies flow to distinct non-percolation classes.
sources: Skinner, Ruhman & Nahum (2019). "Measurement-Induced Phase Transitions in the Dynamics of Entanglement". *Phys. Rev. X* 9, 031009. [arXiv:1808.05953](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05953)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Percolation thresholds for photonic cluster states
registry.summary: Probabilistic fusion gates build random lattices of entangled photons, and a cluster state usable for universal measurement-based computation exists only above the bond-percolation threshold. Renormalizing the percolated lattice yields a regular resource, so loss tolerance is a percolation problem.
sources: Kieling, Rudolph & Eisert (2007). "Percolation, Renormalization, and Quantum Computing with Nondeterministic Gates". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 99, 130501. [arXiv:quant-ph/0611140](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0611140)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: SYK model began as a quantum spin glass
registry.summary: The Sachdev–Ye random all-to-all Heisenberg magnet, introduced to study a quantum spin-glass/spin-liquid transition, became (as SYK) the canonical maximally chaotic quantum system. Random couplings, large-N and replica tools come straight from spin-glass theory.
sources: Sachdev & Ye (1993). "Gapless spin-fluid ground state in a random quantum Heisenberg magnet". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 3339. [arXiv:cond-mat/9212030](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9212030)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Spin-glass ground states and quantum annealing
registry.summary: NP-hard optimization problems map onto spin-glass (Ising) ground-state searches. Quantum annealing replaces thermal fluctuations with a transverse field, and RSB landscapes and small gaps at first-order transitions limit its speedup.
sources: Kadowaki & Nishimori (1998). "Quantum annealing in the transverse Ising model". *Phys. Rev. E* 58, 5355. [arXiv:cond-mat/9804280](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9804280)
Lucas (2014). "Ising formulations of many NP problems". *Front. Phys.* 2, 5. [arXiv:1302.5843](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.5843)

registry.name: Toric-code threshold as a random-bond Ising transition
registry.summary: Optimal decoding of the surface code under independent bit-flip noise maps onto the 2D random-bond Ising model on the Nishimori line. The error threshold p_c≈10.9% is that model's ordering transition, and spin-glass replica tools now analyze qLDPC codes.
sources: Dennis et al. (2002). "Topological quantum memory". *J. Math. Phys.* 43, 4452. [arXiv:quant-ph/0110143](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0110143)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum gases as statistical-mechanics laboratories
registry.summary: Dilute ultracold Bose and Fermi gases realize textbook equilibrium statistical mechanics (ideal and weakly interacting BE/FD gases, BEC, degenerate Fermi pressure) with tunable interactions and traps.
sources: Dalfovo et al. (1998). "Theory of Bose-Einstein condensation in trapped gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 71, 463. [arXiv:cond-mat/9806038](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9806038)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Why isolated quantum systems look thermal
registry.summary: ETH supplies the quantum-mechanical foundation that equilibrium statistical mechanics assumes. Individual energy eigenstates already give microcanonical expectation values for few-body observables, so ergodicity is not needed.
sources: D'Alessio et al. (2016). "From quantum chaos and eigenstate thermalization to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics". *Adv. Phys.* 65, 239. [arXiv:1509.06411](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06411)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Negative absolute temperature in optical lattices
registry.summary: A Bose–Hubbard gas with an upper-bounded energy spectrum (via band truncation and attractive U) was prepared at negative temperature, the textbook two-level-system case realized for motional degrees of freedom. It also revived the Gibbs-vs-Boltzmann entropy debate.
sources: Braun et al. (2013). "Negative Absolute Temperature for Motional Degrees of Freedom". *Science* 339, 52. [arXiv:1211.0545](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.0545)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ensemble equivalence from eigenstate thermalization
registry.summary: Under ETH the diagonal ensemble of a quench equals the microcanonical ensemble, which by ensemble equivalence equals the canonical one for local observables. Integrable systems need a generalized Gibbs ensemble instead.
sources: D'Alessio et al. (2016). "From quantum chaos and eigenstate thermalization to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics". *Adv. Phys.* 65, 239. [arXiv:1509.06411](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06411)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Canonical typicality from entanglement
registry.summary: For almost every pure state of a large system plus bath with fixed total energy, the reduced state of a small subsystem is close to canonical. Entanglement with the bath, not ensemble averaging over ignorance, explains the canonical ensemble.
sources: Popescu, Short & Winter (2006). "Entanglement and the foundations of statistical mechanics". *Nat. Phys.* 2, 754. [arXiv:quant-ph/0511225](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0511225)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Wick rotation: Z as an imaginary-time path integral
registry.summary: Tr e^{-βH} is a Feynman path integral over paths periodic in imaginary time with period βħ. Quantum statistical mechanics in d dimensions is therefore classical statistical mechanics of polymers or fields in d+1 dimensions, which is the basis of path-integral Monte Carlo for helium.
sources: Feynman (1953). "Atomic Theory of the λ Transition in Helium". *Phys. Rev.* 91, 1291. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.91.1291](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.91.1291)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Landauer, demons and quantum resource theories
registry.summary: Landauer erasure, Szilard engines and Maxwell demons generalize to qubits, where entanglement and coherence change the bookkeeping (negative conditional entropy can allow work extraction during erasure). Resource theories of athermality replace the free energy with a family of Rényi free energies for single-shot processes.
sources: Parrondo, Horowitz & Sagawa (2015). "Thermodynamics of information". *Nat. Phys.* 11, 131. [doi:10.1038/nphys3230](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys3230)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thermal entropy as eigenstate entanglement entropy
registry.summary: In a thermalizing pure state, a subsystem's entanglement entropy equals the thermodynamic entropy at the effective temperature (volume law). This was measured in a quantum gas microscope, where entanglement entropy became thermal entropy.
sources: Kaufman et al. (2016). "Quantum thermalization through entanglement in an isolated many-body system". *Science* 353, 794. [arXiv:1603.04409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.04409)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Information is physical: qubits and thermodynamics
registry.summary: Quantum information inherits Shannon theory and Landauer's principle. Reversible unitary gates dissipate nothing in principle, but resetting ancillas and measurement records costs at least k_BT ln2 per bit.
sources: Landauer (1961). "Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process". *IBM J. Res. Dev.* 5, 183. [doi:10.1147/rd.53.0183](https://doi.org/10.1147/rd.53.0183)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Shannon, von Neumann and entanglement entropy
registry.summary: The von Neumann entropy of a reduced density matrix is the quantum Shannon entropy and measures entanglement for pure bipartite states. It reduces to Gibbs entropy for thermal states.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Shannon theory in quantum key distribution
registry.summary: QKD security and channel capacities are written in entropies inherited from Shannon. The BB84 key rate uses the binary entropy h(Q), and the Holevo bound and quantum relative entropy generalize classical mutual information.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Integrability, GGE and the quantum Newton's cradle
registry.summary: Bethe-ansatz-integrable systems such as the Lieb–Liniger gas have extensively many conserved charges and do not thermalize to a Gibbs state. Trapped 1D Bose gases (the quantum Newton's cradle, Tonks–Girardeau gases) showed this, and the steady state is a generalized Gibbs ensemble.
sources: Kinoshita, Wenger & Weiss (2006). "A quantum Newton's cradle". *Nature* 440, 900. [doi:10.1038/nature04693](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04693)
Kinoshita, Wenger & Weiss (2004). "Observation of a One-Dimensional Tonks-Girardeau Gas". *Science* 305, 1125. [doi:10.1126/science.1100700](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1100700)

Lieb & Liniger (1963). "Exact Analysis of an Interacting Bose Gas. I. The General Solution and the Ground State". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 1605. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.1605](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.1605)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Blackbody radiation shift in optical clocks
registry.summary: The ambient Planck field Stark-shifts clock transitions by an amount ∝T⁴. It is a leading systematic of optical lattice clocks and has driven cryogenic clocks with fractional BBR uncertainty near 10^{-20}.
sources: Hassan et al. (2025). "Cryogenic Optical Lattice Clock with 1.7×10^{-20} Blackbody Radiation Stark Uncertainty". [arXiv:2506.05304](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05304)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Bose–Einstein condensation from quantum statistics to atoms
registry.summary: The BEC critical temperature from Bose–Einstein statistics, nλ³=ζ(3/2), was realized in 1995 in dilute alkali gases. Trapped gases modify the density of states (T_c∝N^{1/3}ω) but test the same counting.
sources: Dalfovo et al. (1998). "Theory of Bose-Einstein condensation in trapped gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 71, 463. [arXiv:cond-mat/9806038](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9806038)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Indistinguishability and the symmetrization postulate
registry.summary: Bose and Fermi statistics follow from the symmetrization postulate for identical particles, and Gibbs' 1/N! (the resolution of the mixing paradox) is its classical limit. Thermal states are density operators ρ=e^{-βH}/Z in the postulates' formalism.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thermal light: Bose–Einstein photon statistics
registry.summary: A single mode of blackbody radiation has a Bose–Einstein (geometric) photon-number distribution with variance n̄²+n̄, which is the origin of Hanbury Brown–Twiss bunching g²(0)=2. Coherent states are Poissonian, so photon statistics distinguish thermal from laser light.
sources: Glauber (1963). "Coherent and Incoherent States of the Radiation Field". *Phys. Rev.* 131, 2766. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.131.2766](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.131.2766)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Classical and quantum non-equilibrium dynamics
registry.summary: Master equations, linear response and fluctuation theorems carry over from classical stochastic systems to open and closed quantum many-body systems. The Lindblad equation is the quantum Markov master equation.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: KPZ superdiffusion in quantum spin chains
registry.summary: Infinite-temperature spin transport in the isotropic Heisenberg chain is superdiffusive with z=3/2, and the spin profile matches the KPZ scaling function. This was observed with a quantum gas microscope.
registry.breaks: Classical KPZ comes from a noisy, non-integrable growth equation. In the integrable Heisenberg chain the higher moments of the transferred magnetization deviate from Tracy–Widom, so only part of the KPZ phenomenology carries over.
sources: Ljubotina, Žnidarič & Prosen (2019). "Kardar-Parisi-Zhang Physics in the Quantum Heisenberg Magnet". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 210602. [arXiv:1903.01329](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.01329)
Wei et al. (2022). "Quantum gas microscopy of Kardar-Parisi-Zhang superdiffusion". *Science* 376, 716. [arXiv:2107.00038](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00038)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Boundary-driven quantum NESS and matrix products
registry.summary: Boundary-driven Lindblad spin chains are the quantum counterpart of boundary-driven exclusion processes. Their steady states can be solved by matrix-product ansätze like Derrida's ASEP solution, giving exact currents and quantum NESS phase diagrams.
sources: Prosen (2011). "Exact Nonequilibrium Steady State of a Strongly Driven Open XXZ Chain". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107, 137201. [arXiv:1106.2978](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.2978)

Derrida et al. (1993). "Exact solution of a 1D asymmetric exclusion model using a matrix formulation". *J. Phys. A* 26, 1493. [doi:10.1088/0305-4470/26/7/011](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/26/7/011)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Transport coefficients from scattering cross sections
registry.summary: The Boltzmann collision integral takes its input from quantum scattering theory: dσ/dΩ fixes the mean free path, and Chapman–Enskog transport cross sections fix viscosity and conductivity. In ultracold gases the s-wave σ=8πa² sets thermalization and evaporative cooling.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: ETH implies the fluctuation–dissipation theorem
registry.summary: The smooth function f_O(E,ω) in the ETH ansatz fixes both the spectral function and the symmetrized correlator of O. Their ratio is the equilibrium FDT at the temperature of the eigenstate, so single eigenstates satisfy the FDT.
sources: D'Alessio et al. (2016). "From quantum chaos and eigenstate thermalization to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics". *Adv. Phys.* 65, 239. [arXiv:1509.06411](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.06411)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thermal noise and cooling of mechanical oscillators
registry.summary: A mechanical resonator's thermal force noise follows from the FDT applied to its susceptibility, and cavity sideband cooling engineers a colder effective bath. The asymmetry between Stokes and anti-Stokes sidebands (∝ n̄+1 vs n̄) is the quantum FDT, used as a primary thermometer.
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum FDT and the standard quantum limit
registry.summary: The quantum FDT, with ħω coth(ħω/2k_BT) in place of 2k_BT, gives zero-point noise that sets the standard quantum limit of linear amplifiers and interferometers. Squeezing redistributes this noise between quadratures and cannot remove it.
sources: Callen & Welton (1951). "Irreversibility and Generalized Noise". *Phys. Rev.* 83, 34. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.83.34](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.83.34)
Clerk et al. (2010). "Introduction to quantum noise, measurement, and amplification". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1155. [arXiv:0810.4729](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.4729)

registry.name: Doppler cooling as Brownian motion in light
registry.summary: Optical molasses is a Langevin system: radiation pressure provides linear friction and random spontaneous-emission recoils provide momentum diffusion. The Einstein relation k_BT=D_p/α gives the Doppler limit k_BT_D=ħΓ/2.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Caldeira–Leggett: quantum Brownian motion
registry.summary: A particle linearly coupled to an Ohmic bath of oscillators obeys the classical Langevin equation at high T, but in quantum form it decoheres spatial superpositions at a rate ∝ γ(Δx/λ_th)². Classical friction and quantum decoherence come from one bath spectral density.
sources: Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Path integral approach to quantum Brownian motion". *Physica A* 121, 587. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4)

registry.name: Lindblad equation as the quantum master equation
registry.summary: The Lindblad equation is the quantum version of the Pauli master equation and Fokker–Planck dynamics. Its diagonal part in the energy basis is a classical rate equation with detailed balance, and quantum trajectories are a stochastic unravelling like Langevin paths.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kramers escape and instanton tunnelling rates
registry.summary: Kramers' thermal escape rate and the Langer–Coleman–Caldeira–Leggett imaginary-time instanton rate are two limits of one rate theory. Below the crossover temperature T_0=ħω_b/2πk_B, macroscopic quantum tunnelling replaces activation, as observed in Josephson junctions.
sources: Hänggi, Talkner & Borkovec (1990). "Reaction-rate theory: fifty years after Kramers". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 62, 251. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.62.251](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.62.251)
Caldeira & Leggett (1983). "Path integral approach to quantum Brownian motion". *Physica A* 121, 587. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum-jump stochastic thermodynamics
registry.summary: Unravelling Lindblad dynamics into quantum-jump trajectories assigns heat to each emitted or absorbed quantum. Full-counting statistics of these currents obey Gallavotti–Cohen symmetries and TURs (with quantum corrections), mirroring classical stochastic thermodynamics.
sources: Esposito, Harbola & Mukamel (2008). "Nonequilibrium fluctuations, fluctuation theorems, and counting statistics in quantum systems". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1665. [arXiv:0811.3717](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.3717)

registry.name: Quantum fluctuation theorems
registry.summary: Jarzynski and Crooks relations hold for closed quantum systems when work is defined by two projective energy measurements. Strong coupling and coherence complicate the definition of heat.
sources: Esposito, Harbola & Mukamel (2008). "Nonequilibrium fluctuations, fluctuation theorems, and counting statistics in quantum systems". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1665. [arXiv:0811.3717](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.3717)
Jarzynski (1997). "Nonequilibrium Equality for Free Energy Differences". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 78, 2690. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2690](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.2690)

registry.name: Kibble–Zurek measurement of BEC critical exponents
registry.summary: Quenching a homogeneous Bose gas through T_c freezes in defects and coherence domains whose size scales as τ_Q^{ν/(1+zν)}. This measured ν≈0.5 and z≈1.4 in homogeneous gases, and trapped-gas correlation-length measurements gave ν≈0.67 (3D XY).

registry.name: Entanglement entropy at quantum critical points
registry.summary: At a 1+1D quantum critical point the ground-state entanglement entropy grows as (c/3) ln L, so the central charge that labels the universality class can be read off from entanglement. Gapped phases obey an area law instead.

registry.summary: Suzuki–Trotter decomposition maps the d-dimensional transverse-field Ising model at T=0 onto an anisotropic (d+1)-dimensional classical Ising model. The quantum critical point therefore sits in the (d+1)D Ising class, with imaginary time acting as an extra dimension and z=1.

registry.name: Gross–Pitaevskii and BCS–BEC crossover as mean field
registry.summary: The Gross–Pitaevskii equation is the Hartree mean-field theory of a condensate, with the macroscopic wavefunction as Landau order parameter. registry.summary: Atoms coupled to one cavity mode interact all-to-all, so the Dicke/Hepp–Lieb superradiant transition is mean-field exact. A BEC in a pumped cavity realized it as self-organization into a checkerboard lattice, an open-system phase transition with a Landau order parameter ⟨a⟩.

registry.name: The four laws of black-hole mechanics
registry.summary: Stationary black holes obey laws formally identical to the four laws of thermodynamics, with surface gravity as temperature and area as entropy. Hawking radiation made the identification physical, because κ really is a temperature of order ħκ/2πck_B.

registry.name: Generalized second law and negative heat capacity
registry.summary: Bekenstein's generalized second law, d(S_outside+S_BH)≥0, extends the second law to horizons. A Schwarzschild black hole has negative heat capacity, C=-8πGM²k_B/ħc, so it heats up as it evaporates.

registry.name: Tolman–Ehrenfest: temperature in a gravitational field
registry.summary: In thermal equilibrium in a static spacetime, temperature is not uniform. The local temperature satisfies T√(-g_00)=const, so heat has weight and the zeroth law is modified by redshift. This is used for stellar and neutron-star interiors and is the local form of Hawking temperature redshifting.

registry.summary: Jacobson derived Einstein's equations by imposing the Clausius relation δQ=TdS on every local Rindler horizon, using the Unruh temperature and area-entropy. This suggests that gravity is thermodynamics of underlying microscopic degrees of freedom; entropic-gravity proposals build on the idea but are contested.

registry.name: Black-hole chemistry: van der Waals-like P–V criticality
registry.summary: With Λ treated as pressure P=-Λ/8πG and the black-hole mass as enthalpy, charged AdS black holes have a liquid–gas-like coexistence line ending at a critical point with mean-field exponents and a universal ratio P_cv_c/T_c=3/8. Holographic heat engines run cycles in this extended phase space.
registry.breaks: The 'volume' is a thermodynamic conjugate rather than a container volume, there is no microscopic molecular picture, and treating Λ as a variable is itself an assumption. The resemblance to van der Waals extends to the mean-field equation of state only.

registry.name: Euclidean gravity partition function
registry.summary: Gibbons and Hawking computed black-hole thermodynamics from a canonical partition function: the Euclidean action of the black hole, smooth only if imaginary time has period ħ/k_BT_H, gives F=-k_BT ln Z and the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy. Negative heat capacity makes the flat-space canonical ensemble unstable unless the system is boxed (York) or in AdS.

registry.name: Unruh effect: the vacuum as a Gibbs state
registry.summary: Restricted to a Rindler wedge, the Minkowski vacuum is exactly a thermal density matrix of the boost generator (Bisognano–Wichmann), satisfying the KMS condition at T_U=ħa/2πck_B. Accelerated detectors respond with detailed-balance ratios e^{-ħω/k_BT_U}. De Sitter and black-hole horizons are thermal for the same reason: periodicity in imaginary time.

registry.summary: In AdS/CFT the von Neumann entropy of a boundary region equals the area of the minimal bulk surface anchored on it, divided by 4G. This generalizes Bekenstein–Hawking to arbitrary regions and makes entanglement the building block of geometry.

registry.name: Kramers escape theory was built for nuclear fission
registry.summary: Kramers' 1940 theory of thermally activated escape over a barrier was motivated by Bohr–Wheeler fission and treated the fissioning nucleus as a Brownian particle in a viscous medium. registry.name: Radioactive decay as a Poisson process
registry.summary: Decay is a memoryless Markov process: counts are Poisson, waiting times exponential, and decay chains obey Bateman's linear master equations. Counting statistics and dead-time corrections in nuclear detectors use the same stochastic-process tools.

registry.name: Shape phase transitions in finite nuclei
registry.summary: As nucleon number changes, nuclei go from spherical vibrators to deformed rotors through quantum shape phase transitions. Their Landau-theory description uses the quadrupole deformation as order parameter, and analytic critical-point symmetries such as X(5) and E(5) describe nuclei at the transition, which finite size rounds into crossovers.

registry.name: QCD critical point in the 3D Ising class
registry.summary: A QCD critical endpoint, if it exists, lies in the 3D Ising (Z₂) universality class. (T, μ_B) map linearly onto Ising (t, h), and net-proton cumulant ratios scale with powers of ξ (κσ²∝ξ⁷), so beam-energy scans hunt for non-monotonic kurtosis. Finite-size scaling of cumulants is used to locate it.

registry.name: Relativistic mean-field theory of dense matter
registry.summary: The Walecka σ–ω model replaces meson fields by their mean values, a Hartree mean-field theory in the spirit of Weiss. It reproduces nuclear saturation and gives a stiff neutron-star EOS, and Skyrme and RMF density functionals remain the main EOS inputs beyond ab initio densities.

registry.name: BCS pairing in nuclei
registry.summary: Odd–even mass staggering, gaps in even–even spectra and reduced moments of inertia show that nucleons pair as in a superconductor. registry.name: SRG and V_low-k: Wilsonian RG for nuclear forces
registry.summary: The similarity renormalization group (and IMSRG) is a continuous unitary RG flow that decouples high- and low-momentum states, the Wilsonian idea of integrating out short distances while keeping observables. It makes nuclear many-body calculations converge and generates induced three-body forces, the analogue of irrelevant couplings generated under RG.

registry.name: Efimov physics as an RG limit cycle
registry.summary: Renormalizing the three-boson problem with contact interactions needs a three-body force whose coupling runs periodically in ln Λ: an RG limit cycle rather than a fixed point. This produces discrete scale invariance and the Efimov ratio 22.7, seen in cold atoms, light nuclei and halo systems.

registry.name: Spin ice and Pauling's residual entropy
registry.summary: On the pyrochlore lattice of Dy₂Ti₂O₇ and Ho₂Ti₂O₇, the 'two-in, two-out' rule is Pauling's ice rule for protons in water ice, so the ground state is macroscopically degenerate. Heat-capacity measurements recovered Pauling's residual entropy of $\frac R2\ln\frac32$ per mole of spins, an apparent exception to the third law that only weak residual interactions acting over very long equilibration times can lift.

registry.name: Motility-induced phase separation as liquid–gas coexistence
registry.summary: Self-propelled particles that slow down where crowded separate into dense and dilute phases without any attraction (motility-induced phase separation). To leading order the dynamics maps onto an effective free energy, giving a spinodal at $d\ln v/d\ln\rho<-1$ and a coexistence that resembles the liquid–gas transition.
registry.breaks: There is no equilibrium free energy: binodals do not follow a Maxwell construction on $\mu_{\rm eff}$, and mechanical pressure need not balance in the usual way. Gradient terms can also produce reverse Ostwald ripening and microphase separation.

registry.name: Jamming as a critical point of disordered packings
registry.summary: Athermal packings jam at the isostatic point, where the mean contact number reaches $z_c=2d$. Above it, excess contacts and shear modulus scale as powers of $\phi-\phi_J$, as near a critical point. Liu and Nagel's jamming phase diagram links this to the glass transition, and the infinite-dimensional replica solution ties jamming to marginal stability and full replica-symmetry breaking (the Gardner phase).

registry.name: Weak localization and scaling theory in metals
registry.summary: Constructive interference of time-reversed backscattering paths lowers the conductance of disordered metals (weak localization). A magnetic field or dephasing cuts it off, and it leaves universal conductance fluctuations of order $e^2/h$. One-parameter scaling in the dimensionless conductance $g$ predicts that all states localize in 1D and 2D (without spin–orbit coupling) and that 3D has a mobility edge.

registry.name: Altland–Zirnbauer classes become the tenfold way
registry.summary: The ten symmetry classes of disordered Hamiltonians, built from time-reversal, particle–hole and chiral symmetry (Altland–Zirnbauer), are the same ten classes that classify gapped topological insulators and superconductors. In each dimension the classes with a nontrivial invariant are those whose boundary modes cannot be Anderson-localized, one of the routes to the periodic table (Schnyder–Ryu–Furusaki–Ludwig, Kitaev).

registry.name: Quantum Hall plateau transition as Anderson localization
registry.summary: Quantized plateaus need disorder: states in the Landau-level tails are Anderson-localized and leave $\sigma_{xy}$ unchanged, while only one energy per level is extended. The plateau-to-plateau transition is a localization–delocalization critical point with $\nu\approx2.6$ (Chalker–Coddington network), not the classical-percolation value $4/3$, and its width shrinks as $T^{\kappa}$.

registry.name: Gelation is percolation
registry.summary: Flory–Stockmayer gelation theory is percolation on a Bethe lattice, and the sol–gel transition of crosslinking polymers is a connectivity-percolation threshold, with the gel fraction as order parameter and percolation scaling for the finite clusters. Close to the gel point, 3D percolation exponents replace the Flory–Stockmayer mean-field values (de Gennes, Stauffer).

registry.name: Dilute magnetic alloys: RKKY makes spin glasses
registry.summary: The canonical spin glasses are dilute magnetic alloys (CuMn, AuFe) whose moments couple by RKKY exchange, which oscillates in sign with distance. Random positions therefore give random-sign couplings, the physical basis of the Edwards–Anderson model, and the susceptibility cusp at $T_f$ marks the freezing; insulating spin glasses such as Eu$_x$Sr$_{1-x}$S arise instead from competing ferro- and antiferromagnetic exchange.

registry.name: Frustration with and without disorder
registry.summary: Both start from frustration: when the couplings around a loop have a negative product, no spin arrangement satisfies all of them, and many low-energy states result. With quenched random couplings the spins freeze into a spin glass with Edwards–Anderson order $q$. Geometric frustration on clean triangular, kagome or pyrochlore lattices can instead give order by disorder, spin ice or a quantum spin liquid, and a little bond disorder often turns such magnets into spin glasses.
registry.breaks: A spin glass needs quenched randomness and freezes into a static random state governed by replica-symmetry breaking. A spin liquid is clean, can stay dynamic down to T=0 and is characterised by long-range entanglement and fractionalized excitations, which have no spin-glass counterpart.
sources: Edwards & Anderson (1975). "Theory of spin glasses". *J. Phys. F* 5, 965. [doi:10.1088/0305-4608/5/5/017](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4608/5/5/017)

registry.name: Spin-glass theory of the structural glass transition
registry.summary: Mean-field $p$-spin glasses have a dynamical transition at $T_d$, whose equations coincide with mode-coupling theory of supercooled liquids, and a Kauzmann-like entropy crisis at $T_K$; together these form the random first-order transition theory of glasses (Kirkpatrick, Thirumalai, Wolynes). Aging, rugged landscapes and replica methods carry over, culminating in the exact solution for hard spheres in infinite dimensions.
registry.breaks: Structural glasses have no quenched disorder; it is self-generated. The sharp mean-field $T_d$ becomes a crossover in finite dimensions, and the Edwards–Anderson Ising spin glass (full RSB, continuous transition) belongs to a different class from the one-step RSB models that mimic glasses.

registry.name: Topological entanglement entropy
registry.summary: In a gapped 2D phase the entanglement entropy of a region obeys an area law with a universal constant correction, $S_A=\alpha L-\gamma$, where $\gamma=\ln\mathcal D$ is set by the anyons' quantum dimensions (Kitaev–Preskill, Levin–Wen). This information-theoretic quantity detects topological order without a local order parameter; $\gamma=\ln2$ for the toric code and $\mathbb Z_2$ spin liquids.

registry.name: Bethe ansatz and spinons in Heisenberg chains
registry.summary: Bethe's 1931 solution of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg chain founded the Bethe ansatz; its elementary excitations are spin-1/2 spinons, created in pairs, with the des Cloizeaux–Pearson dispersion. Neutron scattering on chain compounds such as KCuF₃ sees the predicted two-spinon continuum instead of sharp magnons.

registry.name: Kitaev honeycomb model and Kitaev materials
registry.summary: Kitaev's honeycomb model, with bond-dependent Ising couplings, is solved exactly by writing the spins as Majorana fermions in a static $\mathbb Z_2$ gauge field; it has gapped and gapless spin liquids and, in a magnetic field, a non-Abelian phase. Jackeli and Khaliullin showed that edge-sharing $j=1/2$ magnets approximate it, launching the search in iridates and α-RuCl₃, whose reported half-quantized thermal Hall effect remains contested.

registry.name: Degenerate electrons and phonon gas in solids
registry.summary: Conduction electrons form a degenerate Fermi gas: only a fraction $k_BT/E_F$ near the Fermi surface is excited, giving the Sommerfeld heat capacity $\gamma T$, Pauli paramagnetism and the Fermi–Dirac carrier statistics of semiconductors. Phonons are a Bose gas with zero chemical potential and give the Debye $T^3$ law, so a metal's low-temperature heat capacity is $\gamma T+\beta T^3$.

registry.name: Excitons as composite bosons: 2D exciton condensates
registry.summary: Interlayer excitons in transition-metal-dichalcogenide double layers are long-lived composite bosons that, at low temperature and density, should Bose-condense, which in 2D means a BKT superfluid. Experiments on TMD double layers report signatures of exciton condensation and excitonic insulators.
registry.breaks: Excitons behave as bosons only when $n_Xa_X^2\ll1$; at higher density, exchange between their fermionic constituents and screening dissociate them into an electron–hole plasma (the excitonic Mott transition). Disorder and finite lifetime further limit coherence.

registry.name: BCS–BEC crossover: Cooper pairs to Bose condensate
registry.summary: Cooper's bound state exists only because the filled Fermi sea blocks the states below $k_F$. As the attraction grows, large overlapping Cooper pairs turn continuously into tightly bound bosonic molecules that Bose-condense, so $T_c$ rises from the exponentially small BCS value to about $0.218\,T_F$; this crossover was realised with Feshbach-tuned ultracold fermions.
registry.breaks: A conventional superconductor is not a BEC of preformed pairs: the pair size far exceeds the spacing between pairs, and $T_c$ is set by pair breaking, not by the onset of phase coherence.

Colloidal and polymer glasses show aging and fluctuation–dissipation violations, which are described with an effective temperature.

registry.name: Active particles break fluctuation–dissipation
registry.summary: Active Brownian particles obey Langevin dynamics plus persistent self-propulsion, so long-time diffusion far exceeds the Stokes–Einstein value and the fluctuation–dissipation theorem fails. Mechanical pressure on a wall can depend on the wall potential, so pressure is not in general a state function.

registry.name: Active matter as a driven non-equilibrium steady state
registry.summary: Self-propulsion injects energy at every particle and breaks detailed balance locally, so active fluids are non-equilibrium steady states with nonzero entropy production. Active lattice gases are exclusion processes with persistent hopping, and the signatures of driven systems (currents, long-range correlations, giant number fluctuations $\Delta N\propto N^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha>1/2$) appear in flocks and active nematics.

registry.name: Boltzmann equation for Bloch electrons
registry.summary: The semiclassical Boltzmann equation with Bloch velocities, a Fermi–Dirac equilibrium and a relaxation time gives the Drude conductivity, Hall coefficient, thermopower and Wiedemann–Franz law; only states within $k_BT$ of the Fermi surface contribute. Where electron–electron collisions conserve momentum, as in graphene's Dirac fluid, the same kinetic theory gives electron hydrodynamics and violations of Wiedemann–Franz.

registry.name: Kinetic theory of the phonon gas
registry.summary: Lattice heat conduction is the kinetic theory of a phonon gas: the Peierls–Boltzmann equation gives $\kappa=\tfrac13C_Vv\ell$, the dilute-gas formula. Only Umklapp collisions relax crystal momentum, so $\kappa$ grows exponentially on cooling until boundary scattering takes over; when momentum-conserving normal processes dominate, phonons flow hydrodynamically and carry second sound.

The same Kubo formula, evaluated for Bloch bands, gives TKNN's quantized Hall conductance.

registry.summary: The magnetic inelastic neutron cross-section is proportional to the dynamic structure factor $S(\mathbf q,\omega)$, which the fluctuation–dissipation theorem equates to the absorptive susceptibility $\chi''(\mathbf q,\omega)$ times a Bose factor. Magnon dispersions, critical scattering near $T_c$ and spinon continua are therefore measured response functions, and detailed balance between $\pm\omega$ serves as a built-in check.

registry.name: Quantum–classical mapping and Hertz–Millis theory
registry.summary: In imaginary time a quantum transition in $d$ dimensions becomes a classical one in $d+z$ dimensions, so Landau–Ginzburg–Wilson theory, the RG and the Ginzburg criterion carry over. Hertz–Millis theory applies this to metallic magnets: Landau damping gives $z=3$ for ferromagnets and $z=2$ for antiferromagnets, and a quantum critical fan opens above $g_c$, bounded by $k_BT\sim|g-g_c|^{z\nu}$.
