registry.name: Self-avoiding polymers are the n→0 O(n) model
registry.summary: De Gennes showed that self-avoiding-walk statistics are the $n\to0$ limit of the $O(n)$ spin model, with $1/N$ playing the role of reduced temperature. A polymer's size exponent is therefore a critical exponent, computable by the $\epsilon$ expansion and Monte Carlo ($\nu\approx0.588$ in 3D, exactly $3/4$ in 2D); Flory's mean-field $3/(d+2)$ is close but not exact.
sources: Flory (1949). "The Configuration of Real Polymer Chains". *J. Chem. Phys.* 17, 303. [doi:10.1063/1.1747243](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1747243)

Wilson (1971). "Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena. I. Renormalization Group and the Kadanoff Scaling Picture". *Phys. Rev. B* 4, 3174. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3174](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3174)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum critical scaling and ω/T collapse
registry.summary: A zero-temperature transition has $\xi\sim|g-g_c|^{-\nu}$ and $\xi_\tau\sim\xi^z$. Above it temperature is the only scale, so responses collapse onto functions of $\hbar\omega/k_BT$, and universality classes carry over from classical ones (the transverse-field Ising chain has 2D Ising exponents). Heavy-fermion metals such as CeCu$_{6-x}$Au$_x$ show $\omega/T$ scaling with anomalous exponents that no known class reproduces.
sources: Sachdev & Keimer (2011). "Quantum criticality". *Physics Today* 64, 29. [arXiv:1102.4628](https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.4628)
Kadanoff (1966). "Scaling laws for Ising models near Tc". *Physics* 2, 263. [doi:10.1103/PhysicsPhysiqueFizika.2.263](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysicsPhysiqueFizika.2.263)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Mermin–Wagner, anisotropy and order in 2D magnets
registry.summary: The Mermin–Wagner theorem forbids order at $T>0$ in isotropic 2D Heisenberg magnets. Parent cuprates such as La₂CuO₄ therefore show only exponentially growing correlations, $\xi\propto e^{2\pi\rho_s/k_BT}$, and order through weak interlayer coupling. Ising anisotropy evades the theorem, giving Onsager-class transitions in Rb₂CoF₄ and long-range order in monolayer CrI₃.
sources: Mermin & Wagner (1966). "Absence of Ferromagnetism or Antiferromagnetism in One- or Two-Dimensional Isotropic Heisenberg Models". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 17, 1133. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.17.1133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.17.1133)
Onsager (1944). "Crystal Statistics. I. A Two-Dimensional Model with an Order-Disorder Transition". *Phys. Rev.* 65, 117. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.65.117](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.65.117)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Lattice spin models as effective magnet Hamiltonians
registry.summary: Exchange between local moments gives the Heisenberg Hamiltonian, and crystal-field or exchange anisotropy reduces it to the Ising or XY models of statistical mechanics, so real magnets are where those models are tested. Neutron and susceptibility data on FeF₂ (3D Ising) and Rb₂CoF₄ (2D Ising), among others, confirm the predicted universality classes.
registry.map: H=-\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}J_{ij}\mathbf S_i\cdot\mathbf S_j-D\sum_i(S_i^z)^2\ \xrightarrow{D\gg J}\ -J\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\sigma_i\sigma_j
registry.breaks: Real moments are quantum: spin-1/2 fluctuations shrink the ordered moment and can destroy order. Dipolar, RKKY or longer-range couplings can also change the universality class.
sources: Ising (1925). "Beitrag zur Theorie des Ferromagnetismus". *Z. Phys.* 31, 253. [doi:10.1007/BF02980577](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02980577)
Heisenberg (1928). "Zur Theorie des Ferromagnetismus". *Z. Phys.* 49, 619. [doi:10.1007/BF01328601](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01328601)

registry.name: Vicsek flocks: a moving XY model beating Mermin–Wagner
registry.summary: The Vicsek model is an XY ferromagnet whose spins are velocities that also move the particles, so alignment is coupled to density by self-advection. Toner and Tu showed that this coupling allows true long-range polar order in 2D, which Mermin–Wagner forbids for the equilibrium XY model.
registry.breaks: There is no Hamiltonian or Boltzmann weight. The flocking transition is discontinuous, proceeding through travelling bands as a phase-separation scenario, rather than an XY critical point, and setting $v_0\to0$ recovers the equilibrium XY model without long-range order.
sources: Vicsek et al. (1995). "Novel Type of Phase Transition in a System of Self-Driven Particles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1226. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226)

registry.name: Landau–de Gennes theory of liquid crystals
registry.summary: The nematic order parameter is a traceless symmetric tensor $Q_{ij}$, and because symmetry allows a $\mathrm{tr}\,Q^3$ term, Landau theory predicts a first-order isotropic–nematic transition (weakly first order in practice), with Maier–Saupe theory as its microscopic mean-field counterpart. De Gennes mapped the nematic–smectic-A transition, a complex density-wave order parameter coupled to director fluctuations, onto the Ginzburg–Landau theory of superconductors.
sources: de Gennes (1992). "Soft matter". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 64, 645. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.64.645](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.64.645)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: DMFT: Weiss mean field for quantum lattices
registry.summary: Dynamical mean-field theory replaces a site's lattice environment by a self-consistent, frequency-dependent bath, the quantum analogue of the Weiss molecular field, and is exact in infinite dimensions with hopping scaled as $t\propto1/\sqrt d$. Because it keeps all local quantum fluctuations it captures the Mott metal–insulator transition that static mean field misses, and cluster extensions restore short-range spatial correlations.
sources: Georges, Kotliar, Krauth & Rozenberg (1996). "Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated fermion systems and the limit of infinite dimensions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 68, 13. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.68.13](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.68.13)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: BCS as mean field; Ginzburg–Landau as its Landau theory
registry.summary: BCS theory is a self-consistent mean-field decoupling in the pair amplitude $\Delta$. Gor'kov showed that near $T_c$ it reduces to Ginzburg–Landau theory, a Landau expansion in a complex order parameter minimally coupled to $\mathbf A$. Because the Ginzburg number of clean low-$T_c$ metals scales as $(k_BT_c/E_F)^4$, the fluctuation region is too narrow to observe and mean-field exponents are effectively exact.
registry.breaks: The order parameter is not gauge-invariant, and fluctuations of $\mathbf A$ can make the transition weakly first order (Halperin–Lubensky–Ma). In short-coherence-length superconductors a real fluctuation window opens.
sources: Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer (1957). "Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 108, 1175. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Where mean field fails: phase fluctuations in cuprates
registry.summary: Short coherence lengths (1–2 nm), low superfluid density and quasi-2D layering raise the cuprates' Ginzburg number by many orders of magnitude over BCS metals, and YBCO shows 3D-XY critical behaviour near $T_c$. In underdoped samples $T_c$ tracks the superfluid stiffness (Uemura scaling), and a Nernst signal and diamagnetism persist above $T_c$, suggesting that phase fluctuations rather than gap closing set $T_c$ (Emery–Kivelson).
sources: Keimer et al. (2015). "From quantum matter to high-temperature superconductivity in copper oxides". *Nature* 518, 179. [doi:10.1038/nature14165](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14165)
Lee, Nagaosa & Wen (2006). "Doping a Mott insulator: Physics of high-temperature superconductivity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 78, 17. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410445](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410445)

registry.name: Wilson's numerical RG solves the Kondo problem
registry.summary: The antiferromagnetic Kondo coupling is marginally relevant: Anderson's poor-man's scaling makes it grow as the bandwidth is reduced, generating the scale $T_K$. Wilson's numerical renormalization group followed this flow nonperturbatively to the screened Fermi-liquid fixed point (Wilson ratio $R_W=2$), the RG's first nonperturbative success outside critical phenomena.
sources: Wilson (1975). "The renormalization group: Critical phenomena and the Kondo problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 47, 773. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.47.773](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.47.773)
Kondo (1964). "Resistance Minimum in Dilute Magnetic Alloys". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 32, 37. [doi:10.1143/PTP.32.37](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.32.37)

registry.name: Flat-band stiffness bounds T_BKT in moiré superconductors
registry.summary: A 2D superconductor orders by BKT, so its $T_c$ is bounded by the superfluid stiffness. In magic-angle graphene's flat bands the conventional stiffness, proportional to bandwidth, is tiny, and a quantum-geometric term set by the band's quantum metric (bounded below by its Chern number) is proposed to supply it; recent kinetic-inductance measurements report stiffness consistent with that term.
registry.map: k_BT_{\rm BKT}=\frac{\pi}{2}D_s(T_{\rm BKT}^-),\quad D_s=D_s^{\rm conv}+D_s^{\rm geom},\ D_s^{\rm geom}\propto\int g_{\mu\nu}(\mathbf k)\,d^2k
sources: Cao et al. (2018). "Unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle graphene superlattices". *Nature* 556, 43. [arXiv:1803.02342](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02342)

Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)

registry.name: Mermin–Wagner and BKT physics in atomically thin crystals
registry.summary: Two-dimensional superconductors (ion-gated MoS₂, few-layer NbSe₂, oxide interfaces) are analysed as vortex-unbinding transitions, using $V\propto I^3$ at $T_{\rm BKT}$ and the universal stiffness jump. In van der Waals magnets, easy-plane anisotropy gives 2D-XY behaviour, while Ising anisotropy (monolayer CrI₃) allows true long-range order despite Mermin–Wagner.
registry.map: V\propto I^{a(T)},\ a(T_{\rm BKT})=3;\quad \rho_s(T_{\rm BKT}^-)=\tfrac{2}{\pi}k_BT_{\rm BKT}
sources: Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)

registry.name: Two meanings of 'topological' order
registry.summary: Both go beyond Landau's local order parameter. The BKT transition is the unbinding of vortices, defects classified by $\pi_1(S^1)=\mathbb Z$; topological order instead labels gapped $T=0$ phases by ground-state degeneracy and anyons. In both, proliferating point excitations destroy the ordered phase: free vortices above $T_{\rm BKT}$, and thermally excited anyons in a 2D toric code at any $T>0$.
registry.breaks: The BKT phase is gapless with quasi-long-range order and has neither topological degeneracy nor long-range entanglement. Topological order is a gapped quantum phase that in 2D does not survive any nonzero temperature. 'Topological' refers to real-space defects in one case and to global ground-state structure in the other.
sources: Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)

registry.name: First law in a comoving volume gives the fluid equation
registry.summary: Applying dU=−p dV adiabatically to a comoving volume gives the cosmological continuity equation, so each component's equation of state w=p/ρ fixes ρ∝a^{-3(1+w)}. A cosmological constant (w=−1) keeps its density fixed as the volume grows; its negative pressure balances the energy books.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Virial thermostat: stars heat up as they lose energy
registry.summary: For a star in hydrostatic equilibrium the virial theorem gives total energy E=−K, so radiating energy away makes it contract and heat up (Kelvin–Helmholtz contraction). The same negative heat capacity keeps nuclear burning self-regulating: excess energy expands and cools the core.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Saha equation and cosmic recombination
registry.summary: Chemical equilibrium μ_p+μ_e=μ_H between ideal gases gives the Saha equation. Photons outnumber baryons by 1/η≈1.6×10⁹, so hydrogen only recombines near k_BT≈0.3 eV, far below the 13.6 eV binding energy, and this sets the last-scattering surface.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Metastable and coexisting phases as dark-matter detectors
registry.summary: Bubble chambers such as PICO keep a fluorocarbon superheated, as a metastable liquid. A nuclear recoil that deposits enough energy inside the critical radius nucleates a bubble (Seitz theory), and the threshold is tuned so electron recoils do not. Dual-phase xenon TPCs run at liquid–vapour coexistence so that drifted electrons are pulled into the gas, where they produce the S2 signal.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Clausius–Clapeyron runaway greenhouse sets the HZ inner edge
registry.summary: Water-vapour pressure rises exponentially with temperature, so warming adds more greenhouse gas. Once the atmosphere is mostly steam, outgoing thermal radiation saturates near 280 W m⁻² (the Simpson–Nakajima limit) and the oceans evaporate. This defines the inner edge of the habitable zone.
sources: Kasting, Whitmire & Reynolds (1993). "Habitable Zones around Main Sequence Stars". *Icarus* 101, 108. [doi:10.1006/icar.1993.1010](https://doi.org/10.1006/icar.1993.1010)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Condensation curves and equilibrium chemistry in exoplanets
registry.summary: Clouds form where a species' partial pressure meets its Clausius–Clapeyron saturation curve along the atmosphere's pressure–temperature profile: silicate and iron clouds on hot giants, KCl and Na₂S on cooler ones. Baseline compositions come from minimizing the Gibbs free energy. JWST spectra are read as departures from that baseline caused by vertical quenching and photochemistry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: White-dwarf crystallization and phase separation
registry.summary: The core of a cooling white dwarf is a Coulomb plasma that freezes when the coupling Γ reaches about 175. Latent heat, plus oxygen sinking as the carbon–oxygen mixture phase-separates (a binary-mixture phase diagram), slows the cooling. Gaia sees this as a pile-up in the white-dwarf cooling sequence.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Adiabatic gradient, Γ₁ and stellar stability
registry.summary: Stellar stability criteria are thermodynamic response functions. Convection starts when the radiative gradient exceeds ∇_ad (Schwarzschild criterion), and partial ionization lowers both ∇_ad and Γ₁. A star is dynamically unstable if its pressure-weighted Γ₁ drops below 4/3, and helioseismology measures Γ₁ inside the Sun to test the equation of state.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Γ₁<4/3 instabilities: core collapse and pair instability
registry.summary: Some processes absorb energy without raising the pressure: iron photodisintegration and electron capture in collapsing cores, and electron–positron pair creation in very massive oxygen cores. They push Γ₁ below 4/3 and trigger collapse. Pair instability produces (pulsational) pair-instability supernovae and a predicted black-hole mass gap.
sources: Woosley, Heger & Weaver (2002). "The evolution and explosion of massive stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 74, 1015. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.74.1015)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Friends-of-friends halos and cosmic-web percolation
registry.summary: The friends-of-friends halo finder links particles closer than b≈0.2 times the mean separation, so its halos are continuum-percolation clusters. Percolation statistics of over- and underdense regions were also an early quantitative test of the cosmic web's connected, filamentary topology.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Reionization as percolation of ionized bubbles
registry.summary: Ionized regions around early galaxies grow and merge until they form a spanning cluster. Simulations and upcoming 21-cm maps are interpreted by treating this overlap phase as a percolation transition, using cluster-size and topology statistics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Degenerate-matter equation of state for compact stars
registry.summary: Counting states of indistinguishable fermions in the grand-canonical ensemble gives a pressure that survives at T=0; this equation of state, with Sommerfeld finite-temperature and ionic heat-capacity corrections, sets white-dwarf structure and cooling ages.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: 21-cm spin temperature as a two-level Boltzmann ratio
registry.summary: The populations of hydrogen's two hyperfine levels define a spin temperature through the Boltzmann factor. T_s is a weighted mean of the CMB, gas-kinetic and Lyman-α colour temperatures (Wouthuysen–Field coupling). The 21-cm signal appears in absorption when T_s is below T_CMB and in emission when it is above.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Negative heat capacity and gravothermal catastrophe in clusters
registry.summary: The virial theorem gives self-gravitating systems a negative heat capacity, which the canonical ensemble cannot represent (ensembles become inequivalent). A core that loses heat to its halo contracts and gets hotter, so isothermal spheres are unstable once the centre-to-edge density ratio exceeds 709. Globular clusters therefore undergo core collapse, which binary heating halts.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Entropic/emergent gravity as a MOND-like alternative
registry.summary: Verlinde proposed that gravity is an entropic force arising from information on holographic screens. He later proposed that de Sitter entropy adds an 'apparent dark matter' force that scales like MOND, with a₀~cH₀. The idea is speculative and contested.
registry.breaks: It has no accepted derivation from microphysics, and key steps assume Newton's law. Its galaxy-scale predictions are under strain from dwarf-galaxy, cluster and Solar System tests.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Lynden-Bell violent relaxation as maximum-entropy statistics
registry.summary: Lynden-Bell maximized the coarse-grained entropy of a collisionless system whose fine-grained phase-space density is conserved. That incompressibility acts like an exclusion principle and gives a Fermi–Dirac-like distribution. It explains why rapid collapse gives every star the same velocity dispersion regardless of mass.
registry.breaks: Relaxation stops before it is complete as the potential settles. The predicted equilibria have infinite mass, and simulated (NFW-like) halos do not follow Lynden-Bell's distribution.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: CMB as a Bose–Einstein photon gas
registry.summary: The CMB is the most precisely measured Planck spectrum (FIRAS, T0=2.7255 K). Expansion redshifts frequency and temperature together, so the Bose–Einstein form survives. Late energy release would leave a chemical-potential (μ) distortion, now bounded at |μ|<9×10⁻⁵.
sources: Mather et al. (1994). "Measurement of the cosmic microwave background spectrum by the COBE FIRAS instrument". *Astrophys. J.* 420, 439. [doi:10.1086/173574](https://doi.org/10.1086/173574)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Thermal history: g_*, entropy conservation, relic neutrinos
registry.summary: In the radiation era the universe is a quantum ideal gas of relativistic species. Energy and entropy densities count boson degrees of freedom, with fermions weighted by 7/8, and comoving entropy is conserved. Electron–positron annihilation heats photons but not the already decoupled neutrinos, giving T_ν/T_γ=(4/11)^{1/3} and N_eff≈3.044.
sources: Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fuzzy dark matter as a degenerate Bose field
registry.summary: Ultralight bosons (m~10⁻²² eV) have such large occupation numbers that they behave as a classical wave obeying the Schrödinger–Poisson equations. Their kiloparsec de Broglie wavelengths form solitonic, condensate-like cores, and gravitational relaxation can condense Bose stars. Claims that all axion dark matter forms one coherent BEC are disputed.
sources: Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten (2017). "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 95, 043541. [arXiv:1610.08297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.08297)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fermi degeneracy pressure and the Chandrasekhar limit
registry.summary: Electron degeneracy pressure P∝n^{5/3} softens to P∝n^{4/3} once electrons are relativistic. An n=3 polytrope then has a single allowed mass, the Chandrasekhar limit. The same Fermi-gas physics for neutrons, plus nuclear forces, sets the maximum mass of neutron stars.
sources: Chandrasekhar (1931). "The Maximum Mass of Ideal White Dwarfs". *Astrophys. J.* 74, 81. [doi:10.1086/143324](https://doi.org/10.1086/143324)
Oppenheimer & Volkoff (1939). "On Massive Neutron Cores". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 374. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.374](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.374)

registry.name: Degenerate cores and the helium flash
registry.summary: In low-mass red giants the helium core is electron-degenerate, so its pressure barely depends on temperature. When helium ignites, the core heats without expanding, which defeats the virial thermostat, and the runaway helium flash continues until degeneracy is lifted. At the other extreme, blackbody radiation pressure dominates in massive stars.

registry.name: Adhesion model: Zel'dovich flow as Burgers/KPZ
registry.summary: Adding a small viscosity to the Zel'dovich approximation gives the Burgers equation for the comoving velocity, which a Cole–Hopf transform linearizes. Written for the velocity potential it is the noiseless KPZ equation, and its shocks reproduce the sheets, filaments and nodes of the cosmic web.

registry.name: Solar flares as self-organized-criticality avalanches
registry.summary: Flare energies follow a power law across many decades. Lu and Hamilton modelled the coronal magnetic field as a slowly driven sandpile whose reconnection avalanches reproduce that distribution, which made flares a leading astrophysical example of self-organized criticality.
registry.breaks: Waiting-time statistics show memory and clustering that simple SOC does not predict, and the power-law index varies. A power law alone does not prove criticality, and the underlying physics is MHD reconnection.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Boltzmann hierarchy, Silk damping, non-equilibrium recombination
registry.summary: CMB anisotropies come from solving the linearized photon Boltzmann equation with a Thomson collision term (the multipole hierarchy in CAMB/CLASS). The photons' finite mean free path lets the photon–baryon fluid diffuse, which erases the small-scale peaks (Silk damping). Peebles' rate equation shows that recombination lags behind Saha equilibrium.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: SIDM halos as a conducting gas, then gravothermal collapse
registry.summary: With σ/m~1 cm² g⁻¹, dark-matter self-scattering conducts heat like a dilute gas. It first builds an isothermal core, which addresses the cusp–core problem. Because the core has negative heat capacity, it can then undergo gravothermal collapse as globular clusters do, a process now invoked for unusually dense subhalos.
sources: Tulin & Yu (2018). "Dark matter self-interactions and small scale structure". *Phys. Rep.* 730, 1. [arXiv:1705.02358](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02358)

registry.name: Thermal freeze-out sets the relic annihilation cross-section
registry.summary: Integrating the Boltzmann equation over momenta gives a rate equation for the dark-matter number density. Annihilations freeze out once n⟨σv⟩ falls below H, at m/T≈20–25. Matching the observed Ω_DM fixes the 'thermal' ⟨σv⟩≈3×10⁻²⁶ cm³ s⁻¹ that gamma-ray searches in dwarf galaxies aim to test.

registry.name: Collisionless Boltzmann and Jeans equations for the Galaxy
registry.summary: Two-body relaxation times are far longer than the Galaxy's age, so stars obey the collisionless Boltzmann (Vlasov) equation. Its velocity moments, the Jeans equations, turn Gaia kinematics into a measurement of the local dark-matter density. The Gaia phase spiral is a collisionless system caught partway through phase mixing.

registry.breaks: There is no collision term and so no H-theorem: the system relaxes by phase mixing and violent relaxation, not toward a Maxwellian.

registry.name: Neutrino trapping and diffusion in core collapse
registry.summary: Above about 10¹² g cm⁻³ the neutrino mean free path (∝E_ν⁻²) is far smaller than the core, so neutrinos are trapped. They leak out by diffusion from a neutrinosphere over about 10 s, with nearly Fermi–Dirac spectra. Supernova simulations solve the Boltzmann transport equation for them, and the ~13 s neutrino burst from SN 1987A confirmed the timescale.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gamow peak: Maxwellian tail times tunnelling
registry.summary: A thermonuclear rate is the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution multiplied by the Coulomb-tunnelling probability. The product peaks at the Gamow energy, about 6 keV for the pp reaction in the solar core where k_BT≈1.35 keV. The resulting steep temperature dependence, for example a ⁸B neutrino flux ∝T_c^{~24}, makes solar neutrinos a sensitive thermometer of the core.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Stochastic inflation: inflaton Langevin dynamics
registry.summary: Averaged over a Hubble patch, the inflaton gets a random kick of size H/2π per e-fold from modes crossing the horizon. It therefore obeys a Langevin equation, and its probability distribution a Fokker–Planck equation. This underlies eternal inflation and the first-passage (stochastic-δN) predictions of non-Gaussian tails that matter for primordial black holes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Excursion sets: halo mass function as first passage
registry.summary: Smoothing the linear density field on ever smaller scales makes δ perform a random walk in the variance S=σ²(M). The halo mass function is the distribution of first crossings of the collapse barrier δ_c≈1.686, which reproduces Press–Schechter including its ad hoc factor of 2.
registry.breaks: The walk is Markovian only for a sharp-k filter. Realistic filters and ellipsoidal collapse need non-Markovian corrections and moving barriers.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kompaneets equation and the Sunyaev–Zel'dovich effect
registry.summary: Repeated Compton scattering off Maxwellian electrons makes photons diffuse in frequency according to a Fokker–Planck equation, the Kompaneets equation. Its n² stimulated-emission term makes the steady state a Bose–Einstein distribution. In hot cluster gas it shifts CMB photons to higher frequency, producing the thermal SZ y-distortion used to find clusters.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Diffusive shock acceleration as a random walk with escape
registry.summary: Charged particles scattered by magnetic turbulence random-walk back and forth across a shock. Each crossing cycle gives a fixed fractional energy gain, and each cycle carries a fixed probability of escaping downstream. The competition produces a power law, E⁻² for a strong shock; energy-dependent diffusion through the Galaxy then steepens it to the observed ~E⁻²·⁷.

registry.name: Dust coagulation: Smoluchowski kinetics and Brownian growth
registry.summary: Grain growth in protoplanetary disks is modelled with the Smoluchowski coagulation equation. Collision kernels come from Brownian motion for small grains and from turbulence and drift for larger ones. Gas drag in the Epstein (kinetic) regime sets the stopping time and Stokes number, which control settling, radial drift and the bouncing and fragmentation barriers.

registry.name: Fokker–Planck stellar dynamics: relaxation, friction, evaporation
registry.summary: Chandrasekhar treated the cumulative effect of weak stellar encounters as Brownian motion: a Fokker–Planck equation with a drag term (dynamical friction) and a velocity-diffusion term. In star clusters this drives mass segregation and the evaporation of stars scattered above the escape speed, about 0.7% of a Maxwellian per relaxation time.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radiative diffusion as a photon random walk
registry.summary: Inside a star a photon travels only up to about a centimetre before it is scattered or absorbed, so energy moves by diffusion. Fick's law with a Rosseland-mean opacity gives the radiative temperature gradient. Escaping the solar core takes 10⁴–10⁵ yr, compared with R/c≈2 s for a straight path.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Stochastically excited p-modes as noise-driven oscillators
registry.summary: Solar acoustic modes are damped and also driven by random forcing from convection near the surface. Each behaves like a Langevin oscillator whose power spectrum is a Lorentzian with a linewidth set by the damping rate. This model is the basis of mode fitting in helioseismology and in asteroseismology of solar-like stars.

registry.name: Kibble–Zurek defect formation and the monopole problem
registry.summary: When a symmetry breaks, causally disconnected regions pick independent vacua, leaving at least one defect per correlation volume; Zurek fixed the frozen correlation length using critical exponents. GUT monopoles made this way would overclose the universe, a key motivation for inflation. The scaling has been tested in superfluid helium, liquid crystals and cold atoms.

registry.name: Magnetic pressure and MHD thermodynamics

registry.name: Relaxed states and Taylor relaxation

registry.name: Debye–Hückel screening

registry.name: Strongly coupled one-component plasma

registry.name: Statistical mechanics in magnetic fields (Bohr–van Leeuwen)

registry.name: Nonequilibrium stat mech and Vlasov kinetics

registry.name: Nonequilibrium cascades as driven steady states

registry.name: Collisional transport and neoclassical theory

registry.name: Plasma fundamentals and Boltzmann kinetics
registry.summary: Plasma collision operators (Landau, Lenard–Balescu, Fokker–Planck) are the Coulomb-interaction versions of the Boltzmann collision integral, with a Coulomb logarithm cutoff set by Debye screening.

registry.name: Boltzmann equation to Vlasov equation
registry.summary: Vlasov is the Boltzmann equation with the collision term dropped and a self-consistent mean field added; the H-theorem fails for it, yet Landau damping gives effective irreversibility via phase mixing.
registry.map: C[f]\to 0,\; \mathbf F\to q(\mathbf E[f]+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B[f])
registry.breaks: Vlasov is time-reversible and conserves all Casimirs; damping is phase mixing, not entropy production.

registry.name: Landau damping and the H-theorem
registry.summary: Both explain relaxation of a distribution function; Boltzmann's is entropy-producing via collisions, Landau's is collisionless via resonant wave-particle energy exchange and phase mixing.
registry.breaks: Landau damping conserves entropy and is reversible in principle; collisional H-theorem increases entropy.

registry.name: Collisionless solar wind and Knudsen number
registry.summary: Solar wind has large Knudsen number, so Boltzmann-equation exospheric models predict non-Maxwellian electron and ion distributions and heat flux, the origin of Parker-like kinetic closures beyond fluid theory.

registry.name: X-ray Thomson scattering and FDT
registry.summary: XRTS measures the dynamic structure factor of warm dense matter, which by the fluctuation–dissipation theorem encodes density response, temperature (detailed balance) and collective modes.

registry.name: Conductivity, Kubo formula and Spitzer
registry.summary: Plasma resistivity and transport coefficients can be derived from Kubo formulas, with Spitzer resistivity as the kinetic limit; Onsager symmetry constrains cross-coefficients such as thermoelectric terms.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dielectric response, FDT and Landau damping
registry.summary: The plasma dielectric function is a linear response function; its imaginary part gives Landau damping, and the FDT links it to thermal density fluctuations (dynamic structure factor, collective scattering).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Random-walk transport and Fokker–Planck
registry.summary: Diffusive transport estimates, Fokker–Planck collision operators and quasilinear theory in plasmas treat turbulent or collisional scattering as a random walk in space or velocity.

registry.name: Magnetic field-line and particle diffusion
registry.summary: Charged-particle scattering by magnetic fluctuations gives pitch-angle diffusion and cosmic-ray transport; stochastic field lines yield Rechester–Rosenbluth diffusion, a random-walk with correlation length.

registry.name: Stochastic acceleration and diffusive shock acceleration
registry.summary: Fermi acceleration is a random-walk process in momentum and space; diffusive shock acceleration solves a diffusion–advection equation yielding a universal power-law spectrum.

registry.name: Entropy production in collisionless plasma
registry.summary: Entropy in weakly collisional plasma turbulence is cascaded to fine velocity-space scales (phase-space cascade) and dissipated by collisions, tied to Gibbs-entropy and fluctuation-theorem language.

registry.name: Dynamo onset as a bifurcation

registry.name: Debye screening as mean-field theory

registry.name: Landau theory of instability onset

registry.name: RG and turbulence scaling

registry.name: 2D Coulomb systems and melting

registry.name: Network science of biological regulation and spreading

registry.summary: A condensate in a double well follows a two-mode Bose–Hubbard Hamiltonian that maps onto the junction Hamiltonian behind charge qubits and transmons: number imbalance plays the role of Cooper-pair number and relative phase the role of φ. registry.breaks: Atoms are neutral and conserve total number, so there is no 2e charging, gate charge or electromagnetic environment. Large population imbalance gives nonlinear self-trapping. Large N and slow (Hz–kHz) dynamics mean the atomic junction is not a practical qubit.

registry.name: s-wave scattering length sets condensate interactions
registry.summary: At ultracold energies only s-wave scattering survives, so interactions reduce to a contact pseudopotential g = 4πħ²a/m in the Gross–Pitaevskii equation. Feshbach resonances, a bound-state resonance of partial-wave theory, tune a through zero and infinity, enabling the BEC–BCS crossover and Feshbach molecules.
registry.breaks: The contact pseudopotential fails near resonance, where na³ is not small and three-body losses and effective-range terms matter.

registry.name: Quantum trajectories grew out of laser-cooling theory

registry.name: Lindblad dephasing is the dynamics of decoherence
registry.summary: Tracing out the environment under the Born–Markov approximation gives a Lindblad equation. Its dephasing term damps coherences between pointer states exponentially, at a rate set by their separation, which quantifies einselection.
registry.breaks: Non-Markovian or strongly coupled environments give decoherence that is not of Lindblad form, with memory effects and coherence revivals.

registry.name: Error correction and DFS undo decoherence
registry.summary: Error correction treats decoherence as a channel with Kraus operators E_k and recovers the encoded state when the Knill–Laflamme conditions hold. Collective environment coupling gives decoherence-free subspaces, the passive limit of the same algebra, where protected code spaces replace pointer states.

registry.name: Qubit T1 and T2 as measured decoherence
registry.summary: Superconducting circuits are macroscopic quantum systems whose coherence is limited by TLS defects, quasiparticles, and flux and charge noise, so T1/T2 measurements and noise spectroscopy are direct studies of decoherence. The transmon design suppresses charge-noise dephasing exponentially.

registry.name: Influence functional and Caldeira–Leggett decoherence
registry.summary: Integrating a harmonic bath out of the path integral gives the Feynman–Vernon influence functional. For an ohmic bath at high temperature this yields the Caldeira–Leggett master equation and the standard estimate that a superposition of separation Δx decoheres faster than it relaxes by a factor (Δx/λ_th)².
registry.breaks: Valid only for high temperature and ohmic, Markovian baths. At low temperature the master equation is not of Lindblad form and needs corrections.

registry.name: Two dynamics in the postulates: the measurement problem
registry.summary: The textbook postulates combine unitary Schrödinger evolution with a projection (Born-rule) postulate for measurement. The tension between the two is the measurement problem, and interpretations differ by which postulate they drop, reinterpret or modify (many-worlds, Bohm, collapse models, QBism).

registry.name: High-frequency (Magnus) expansion gives Floquet Hamiltonians
registry.summary: Time-dependent perturbation theory in 1/ω (Magnus or van Vleck expansion) gives an effective static Floquet Hamiltonian. It explains Kapitza stabilization, coherent destruction of tunnelling and engineered Peierls phases, and its breakdown signals heating toward infinite temperature.
registry.breaks: In interacting many-body systems the series is only asymptotic. It holds for prethermal times that grow exponentially in ω/J.

registry.name: Quantum jumps observed in cavity and circuit QED
registry.summary: Cavity damping and spontaneous emission are the canonical Lindblad dissipators. Continuous photon counting and homodyne readout in cavity and circuit QED record individual quantum trajectories, from photon-number jumps in a Rydberg-atom cavity to the mid-flight reversal of a transmon's jump.

registry.name: Exceptional-point sensing versus quantum noise limits
registry.summary: Near an order-n exceptional point, eigenvalue splitting responds to a perturbation as ε^{1/n}, which seems to promise sensors with diverging susceptibility. Quantum-noise analyses find the signal-to-noise gain largely cancels because eigenvector coalescence (the Petermann factor) amplifies noise too, so EP-enhanced metrology remains contested.
registry.breaks: The square-root response exists only in the eigenfrequencies. Once fundamental quantum noise is included, the Fisher information per resource does not diverge.

registry.name: Random-circuit sampling rests on Porter–Thomas statistics
registry.summary: Quantum-advantage experiments sample from deep random circuits whose output probabilities follow the Porter–Thomas distribution of chaotic, Haar-like states. Cross-entropy benchmarking relies on this random-matrix statistics, and classical spoofing algorithms exploit departures from it.

registry.summary: Chaotic dynamics spreads local information into nonlocal correlations, which is what an error-correcting encoding does. OTOC decay measures this spreading, Hayden–Preskill decoding treats black-hole scrambling as a code, and random circuits produce near-optimal codes.

registry.name: Gutzwiller trace formula: periodic orbits to spectra
registry.summary: Stationary-phase evaluation of the trace of the propagator writes the density of states of a chaotic system as a sum over classical periodic orbits. Berry's diagonal approximation and Sieber–Richter orbit pairs then reproduce random-matrix form factors, explaining the Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit universality.
registry.breaks: The orbit sum diverges exponentially. Beyond the Heisenberg time it needs resummation, and it only applies in the semiclassical limit.

registry.summary: In ETH systems the entanglement entropy of a small subsystem in a mid-spectrum eigenstate equals the thermal entropy (a volume law, as in Page's random states). sources: Martinez et al. (2016). "Real-time dynamics of lattice gauge theories with a few-qubit quantum computer". *Nature* 534, 516. [arXiv:1605.04570](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.04570)
Belyansky et al. (2024). "High-Energy Collision of Quarks and Mesons in the Schwinger Model: From Tensor Networks to Circuit QED". [arXiv:2307.02522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02522)

registry.name: Second quantization: QM of many particles is QFT
registry.summary: Non-relativistic many-body quantum mechanics in Fock space is a free or interacting quantum field theory; relativistic QFT adds Lorentz invariance, antiparticles and particle number non-conservation.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Neutrino flavour as a precessing pseudo-spin
registry.summary: Two-flavour oscillation is spin-1/2 precession in an effective magnetic field; the oscillation formula is the Rabi formula, and collective oscillations in dense neutrino gases map onto interacting spin models.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Isospin and flavour multiplets via SU(2) recoupling
registry.summary: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and the Wigner-Eckart theorem developed for angular momentum organize isospin and flavour multiplets, decay branching ratios and helicity amplitudes of hadrons.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: MSW conversion as an adiabatic level crossing
registry.summary: Resonant flavour conversion in the Sun is an avoided crossing of matter-dressed mass eigenstates; adiabatic following gives near-complete conversion and the non-adiabatic hopping probability is the Landau-Zener formula.
sources: Parke (1986). "Nonadiabatic Level Crossing in Resonant Neutrino Oscillations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 57, 1275. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.1275](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.1275)
Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Schrieffer-Wolff elimination as integrating out
registry.summary: Adiabatic elimination of high-energy states by second-order perturbation theory (Schrieffer-Wolff) gives effective Hamiltonians, the same logic as integrating out heavy fields; Fermi's four-fermion coupling is W exchange at second order.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Golden rule and decay widths
registry.summary: Fermi's golden rule is the non-relativistic form of the relativistic decay-rate and cross-section formulas built from Feynman amplitudes and Lorentz-invariant phase space.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Supersymmetric quantum mechanics
registry.summary: Witten introduced SUSY QM as a toy model of supersymmetry breaking (Witten index); it became a tool for exactly solvable potentials through shape invariance and partner Hamiltonians.
sources: Witten (1981). "Dynamical breaking of supersymmetry". *Nucl. Phys. B* 188, 513. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(81)90006-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(81)90006-7)

registry.name: Quarkonium as hydrogen of QCD
registry.summary: Charmonium and bottomonium spectra follow from a Schrodinger equation with a Coulomb-plus-linear (Cornell) potential, organized like hydrogen and positronium levels with fine and hyperfine splittings.
registry.breaks: Confinement (linear term) has no atomic analogue; relativistic corrections and coupled open-flavour channels matter above threshold.
sources: Eichten et al. (1975). "Spectrum of Charmed Quark-Antiquark Bound States". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 34, 369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.369)

registry.name: Theta vacua as Bloch states; WZ terms as Berry phases
registry.summary: Large gauge transformations make the Yang-Mills vacuum periodic, and theta plays the role of Bloch quasi-momentum in a periodic potential; Wess-Zumino-Witten terms are Berry phases of the low-energy fields.
sources: Jackiw & Rebbi (1976). "Vacuum Periodicity in a Yang-Mills Quantum Theory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 37, 172. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.172](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.172)

registry.name: Wilson loops are non-abelian holonomies
registry.summary: The Aharonov-Bohm phase is a U(1) holonomy; Yang-Mills Wilson loops are its non-abelian generalization, and degenerate adiabatic transport produces the same Wilczek-Zee non-abelian connection.
sources: Aharonov & Bohm (1959). "Significance of Electromagnetic Potentials in the Quantum Theory". *Phys. Rev.* 115, 485. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.115.485](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.115.485)
Wu & Yang (1975). "Concept of nonintegrable phase factors and global formulation of gauge fields". *Phys. Rev. D* 12, 3845. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.12.3845](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.12.3845)
Wilczek & Zee (1984). "Appearance of Gauge Structure in Simple Dynamical Systems". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 2111. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111)

registry.name: Instantons from double wells to QCD
registry.summary: Euclidean instantons that compute tunnelling splitting in a double well become Yang-Mills instantons, which break U(1)_A through the anomaly and mix the theta vacua.

registry.name: Feynman path integral from particles to fields
registry.summary: The QFT generating functional is the particle path integral with paths replaced by field configurations; stationary phase gives the classical field equations and Gaussian integrals give propagators and Wick's theorem.

registry.name: Born series as tree-level perturbation theory
registry.summary: The Lippmann-Schwinger Born series is the non-relativistic limit of the Feynman-diagram expansion: first Born approximation equals tree-level one-boson exchange (Yukawa/Coulomb), and the optical theorem is S-matrix unitarity.
registry.map: f_{\rm Born}=-\frac{m}{2\pi\hbar^2}\tilde V(\mathbf q)\leftrightarrow\mathcal M\propto\frac{g^2}{q^2+m^2};\ \sigma_{\rm tot}=\frac{4\pi}{k}\mathrm{Im}f(0)

registry.name: Near-threshold states and universality
registry.summary: Hadrons near a two-body threshold (deuteron, X(3872)) are governed by a large scattering length, the same universal physics as Feshbach-tuned cold atoms, including Efimov-type three-body effects.

registry.name: Quantized EM field as free QFT
registry.summary: Quantum optics' mode expansion of the field, Fock and coherent states are the canonical quantization of free Maxwell theory; Glauber coherent states are the quantum states closest to classical fields.

registry.name: Single-photon detectors in particle detectors

registry.name: Squeezed-state receivers for axion haloscopes

registry.name: Thorium-229 nuclear clock

registry.name: Proton radius from hydrogen and muonic hydrogen

registry.name: Multipole selection rules for atomic and nuclear photons
registry.summary: Gamma transitions in nuclei obey the same multipole selection rules and Wigner-Eckart structure as atomic E1/M1/E2 lines; Weisskopf estimates and conversion electrons parallel atomic radiative and Auger channels.

registry.name: Hoyle state as an alpha-particle condensate
registry.summary: The 7.65 MeV Hoyle state of carbon-12 that enables triple-alpha burning has been described as a dilute gas of alpha clusters occupying one orbital, a nuclear analogue of a Bose condensate.

It gives the same exponential transmission law, which is used to design RF heating schemes.

registry.name: Adiabatic invariant μ ↔ conserved quantum number
registry.summary: The magnetic moment μ that makes mirrors work is the gyration action, the classical counterpart of the quantum adiabatic theorem. Under slow change the Landau-level index is conserved, and μ=(n+1/2)|q|ħ/m. Ehrenfest's adiabatic hypothesis made this exact link in the old quantum theory.
registry.breaks: In fusion plasmas n\sim10^7 for 10 keV electrons at 5 T, so only the classical invariant matters there. Classical μ is conserved only asymptotically (exponentially small breaking), while the quantum theorem needs a spectral gap.

The scattering parameter decides between the collective (plasmon) and non-collective regimes, and the fit gives T_e, n_e and ionization.

registry.name: Coulomb logarithm: Rutherford cross section, quantum cutoff
registry.summary: Plasma collision operators (Landau, Lenard–Balescu, Fokker–Planck) integrate the Rutherford cross section over impact parameters. Debye screening cuts the integral off at large distance. At short distance the cutoff is the larger of the classical closest-approach distance and the de Broglie wavelength, and for hot electrons (T_e≳10Z² eV) that is the quantum one.

registry.name: Brillouin light–sound coupling: optomechanics vs SBS
registry.summary: In stimulated Brillouin scattering, a laser decays into scattered light plus an ion-acoustic wave driven by the ponderomotive force. This is the plasma counterpart of the radiation-pressure or electrostrictive coupling of light to a mechanical mode in Brillouin optomechanics. Both obey the same phase-matched three-wave coupled-mode equations.

registry.name: Photon in plasma: effective mass ħω_p; plasmons
registry.summary: Transverse waves in a plasma obey ω²=ω_p²+c²k², a massive Klein–Gordon dispersion. So photons in a plasma act as quasiparticles of mass ħω_p/c², which lets them decay into neutrino pairs in stars. Quantized longitudinal Langmuir oscillations are plasmons.

Apparent superluminal motion in AGN jets follows from the light-travel-time kinematics of relativistic ejecta. Both are special-relativistic kinematics layered on top of curved-spacetime ray tracing.

registry.name: Energy conditions, area theorem and generalized 2nd law
registry.summary: Through the Raychaudhuri equation and the Einstein equations, the null energy condition makes horizon area non-decreasing (Hawking's area theorem, the 'second law'). Hawking radiation carries a negative energy flux across the horizon, so it violates the NEC and the area can shrink. Bekenstein's generalized second law then replaces the area theorem.

registry.summary: The inspiral gives the component masses and spins and the ringdown gives the remnant's mass and spin, so the horizon areas before and after merger can be compared. Analyses of GW150914 and later high-SNR events find A_f > A₁ + A₂ with high confidence. This is an observational test of the second law of black-hole mechanics.

registry.name: AdS black holes as thermal CFT states (Hawking–Page)
registry.summary: In AdS/CFT a large AdS–Schwarzschild black hole is dual to the boundary CFT at temperature T_H, with entropy A/4G equal to the CFT's thermal entropy. The Hawking–Page transition between thermal AdS and the black hole maps to the confinement/deconfinement transition of the gauge theory, and quasinormal decay maps to thermalization.
registry.map: T_H=T_{\rm CFT},\ S_{BH}=\frac{A}{4G}=S_{\rm CFT};\ \ T_{\rm HP}=\frac{3}{2\pi\ell}\ (\text{AdS}_5,\ \hbar=c=k_B=1)\leftrightarrow T_{\rm deconf}
registry.breaks: Small AdS black holes have negative heat capacity and are unstable, like asymptotically flat ones. The duality is cleanest at large N and strong coupling.

registry.name: Horizon area quanta and black-hole entropy in LQG
registry.summary: LQG's discrete area spectrum lets one count the spin-network punctures of an isolated horizon. The count gives an entropy proportional to area, which equals A/4 only for one value of the Barbero–Immirzi parameter (γ ≈ 0.24–0.27, depending on the counting scheme). It also predicts a universal −(3/2) ln A correction.
registry.breaks: Matching A/4 requires fixing γ by hand, and Hawking radiation itself has not been derived from the LQG dynamics.

registry.name: Hawking radiation as curved-spacetime particle creation
registry.summary: Hawking radiation is a result of QFT in curved spacetime. The in-vacuum of a collapsing geometry, carried through the horizon's exponential redshift, is thermal for late-time observers. Its Bogoliubov coefficients give a Planck spectrum at T_H = ħκ/2πck_B, and the same calculation gives cosmological particle creation and the Unruh effect.

registry.name: D-brane microstate counting reproduces A/4G
registry.summary: Strominger and Vafa counted BPS bound states of D-branes that carry the charges of a five-dimensional extremal black hole. Their degeneracy reproduces the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy exactly, the first statistical-mechanical derivation of black-hole entropy. Near-extremal extensions also reproduce Hawking emission with the correct greybody factors.
registry.breaks: The count is controlled only for supersymmetric or near-extremal black holes. Schwarzschild-like black holes far from extremality are not covered.

registry.name: Islands and the Page curve from holographic entropy
registry.summary: The Ryu–Takayanagi formula, extended to quantum extremal surfaces, computes the entropy of black-hole radiation. For an evaporating black hole coupled to a bath, a new extremal surface (an island) appears after the Page time, and the entropy then follows the unitary Page curve. AdS/CFT also gives the main argument that evaporation is unitary, because the dual CFT evolves unitarily.

registry.name: Schwarzschild and Kerr as exact vacuum solutions
registry.summary: The black-hole note studies the horizons, ergospheres and geodesics of the same metrics the exact-solutions note derives. Schwarzschild is the unique spherically symmetric vacuum solution (Birkhoff), Kerr is its rotating generalisation, and Reissner–Nordström and Kerr–Newman are the charged versions. Uniqueness theorems make Kerr–Newman the stationary end state of collapse (no-hair).

registry.name: No-hair theorems vs black-hole scalarization
registry.summary: In GR the no-hair and uniqueness theorems force stationary vacuum black holes to be Kerr, and many scalar–tensor theories also admit Kerr. Einstein–scalar–Gauss–Bonnet couplings, motivated by string α′ corrections, evade the theorems through spontaneous scalarization and give hairy black holes. Their deviations from Kerr are targets for ringdown and imaging tests.
registry.breaks: Scalarized solutions can be unstable, and some of these theories have ill-posed evolution equations. Current observations do not distinguish them from Kerr.

registry.name: Kerr quasinormal modes set the merger ringdown
registry.summary: A merger remnant rings down as a sum of damped Kerr quasinormal modes, whose complex frequencies follow from Teukolsky perturbation theory and depend only on the final mass and spin. Measuring two or more modes over-determines (M, a) and so tests the no-hair theorem (black-hole spectroscopy).

registry.name: Superradiance: black-hole spins as boson detectors
registry.summary: A rotating black hole amplifies waves with ω < mΩ_H, which is the wave version of the Penrose process. An ultralight boson whose Compton wavelength matches the horizon builds a superradiant cloud that spins the hole down and emits nearly monochromatic gravitational waves. Measured black-hole spins and searches for continuous waves therefore bound the masses of axion-like particles.

registry.summary: A compact object spiralling into a massive black hole completes ~10⁵ orbits in LISA's band. By Ryan's theorem, its phase evolution encodes all the mass and current multipoles of the central spacetime. Checking that they obey Kerr's relation tests the no-hair theorem more precisely than any electromagnetic probe can.

registry.summary: Writing g = η + h and choosing harmonic (Lorenz) gauge turns the Einstein equations into a sourced wave equation. In transverse-traceless gauge two polarizations travel at c. Far from a slow source the leading retarded solution is the quadrupole formula, and its Isaacson energy flux drives binary inspirals.

registry.name: Linearized Einstein equations from entanglement first law

That condition is equivalent to the bulk metric perturbation obeying the linearized Einstein equations. Holographic renormalization likewise identifies the Fefferman–Graham coefficients of a bulk solution with the boundary stress tensor.

registry.name: Einstein equation as an equation of state
registry.summary: Jacobson (1995) derived the Einstein equations by requiring the Clausius relation δQ = T dS on every local Rindler horizon, using the Unruh temperature and an entropy proportional to area. This result underpins emergent and entropic-gravity proposals in which the field equations are thermodynamic rather than fundamental.
registry.breaks: The derivation assumes local equilibrium and an area law. With higher-curvature entropy or out-of-equilibrium horizons it needs extra terms, and whether gravity is truly emergent remains contested.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Semiclassical Einstein equation and backreaction
registry.summary: QFT in curved spacetime feeds back into geometry through the semiclassical Einstein equation, whose source is the renormalized expectation value of the stress tensor. Renormalizing ⟨T⟩ produces the conformal trace anomaly. That anomaly drives the backreaction of evaporating black holes and anomaly-driven cosmologies.
registry.breaks: The equation fails when stress-tensor fluctuations are comparable to the mean, for example in macroscopic superpositions of mass, where stochastic gravity or full quantum gravity is needed.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Einstein equations from worldsheet conformal invariance
registry.summary: The closed string's massless spectrum contains a spin-2 graviton. Requiring the worldsheet sigma model on a curved background to stay conformally invariant (vanishing beta functions) imposes Einstein's equations coupled to the dilaton and B-field, plus α′ corrections. GR is therefore the low-energy limit of string theory.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Local Minkowski structure: SR as GR's tangent space
registry.summary: By the equivalence principle, every freely falling frame is locally Minkowskian. GR replaces the global η_{μν} of special relativity by a curved g_{μν} whose tangent space at each point carries the Lorentz group, and SR laws hold to first order in Riemann normal coordinates. Curvature is exactly what no Lorentz transformation can remove.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Loop quantum cosmology: FLRW big bang becomes a bounce
registry.summary: Quantizing the homogeneous FLRW sector with loop (holonomy) variables gives an effective Friedmann equation with a ρ² correction. The big-bang singularity of the classical FLRW solution is replaced by a bounce at a critical density of order the Planck density.
registry.breaks: The bounce is derived in symmetry-reduced minisuperspace. Whether full LQG reproduces it, and how inhomogeneities behave, is not settled.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: de Sitter and FLRW as arenas of particle creation
registry.summary: The exact de Sitter and FLRW solutions are the standard backgrounds of QFT in curved spacetime. They host Parker's cosmological particle creation in an expanding FLRW universe, the Bunch–Davies vacuum, and the Gibbons–Hawking temperature of the de Sitter horizon, whose fluctuations seed inflationary perturbations.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Extra polarizations and dipole radiation beyond GR
registry.summary: GR predicts two tensor polarizations and emission that starts at quadrupole order. Scalar–tensor theories add a breathing mode and dipole radiation from binaries with unequal sensitivities, entering at −1PN. Massive gravity adds dispersion and up to six polarizations. Waveform models capture these effects as deviations in the PN coefficients or as ppE terms.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: GW170817 speed of gravity prunes Horndeski theories
registry.summary: In Horndeski theories, couplings of the scalar to curvature (the G_{4,X}, G_{5,X} and G_{5,φ} terms) make tensor waves travel at a speed different from c on a cosmological background. GW170817 and GRB 170817A arrived 1.7 s apart after ~40 Mpc, bounding the gravity–light speed difference at the 10⁻¹⁵ level. This eliminated most such dark-energy models and also bounds Lorentz violation in the gravity sector.
registry.breaks: The bound applies at LIGO frequencies (~100 Hz). Theories whose c_T deviates only at much lower frequencies, near the cutoff scale of the dark-energy effective theory, are not excluded by it.
sources: LIGO, Virgo, Fermi GBM & INTEGRAL (2017). "Gravitational Waves and Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 848, L13. [arXiv:1710.05834](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05834)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Curvature-squared terms from quantum fields: R² gravity
registry.summary: Renormalizing quantum matter fields on a curved background requires R² and R_{μν}R^{μν} counterterms in the gravitational action. Starobinsky's 1980 inflation model began as a quantum correction driven by the trace anomaly. Its R² term is now the prototype f(R) theory, which is equivalent to GR plus a scalar field (the scalaron).
registry.map: f(R)=R+\frac{R^2}{6M^2}\ \Leftrightarrow\ \text{GR}+\text{scalaron of mass }M;\ \ \mathcal L_{\rm ct}\supset a_1R^2+a_2R_{\mu\nu}R^{\mu\nu}
sources: Sotiriou & Faraoni (2010). "f(R) theories of gravity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 451. [arXiv:0805.1726](https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1726)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: NR mergers calibrate inspiral–merger–ringdown waveforms
registry.summary: Since Pretorius (2005), 3+1 simulations of binary black-hole and neutron-star mergers have supplied the strong-field merger stage that post-Newtonian theory cannot reach. Effective-one-body models, phenomenological models and NR surrogates are calibrated against NR catalogues and used as matched-filter templates. The simulations also fix the Kerr remnant whose ringdown ends the signal.
registry.map: h^{\rm IMR}=h^{\rm PN/EOB}_{\rm insp}\oplus h^{\rm NR}_{\rm merger}\oplus\sum_{\ell mn}A_{\ell mn}e^{-i\omega_{\ell mn}t}
registry.breaks: NR covers only the last tens of orbits and samples mass ratio, spin and eccentricity sparsely. Templates therefore interpolate, and they rely on PN/EOB for the early inspiral.
sources: Pretorius (2005). "Evolution of Binary Black-Hole Spacetimes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 121101. [arXiv:gr-qc/0507014](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0507014)
Blanchet (2014; updated 2024). "Post-Newtonian Theory for Gravitational Waves". *Living Rev. Relativ.* [arXiv:1310.1528](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1528)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Numerical holography: Einstein equations in AdS
registry.summary: Characteristic and 3+1 numerical-relativity methods were carried over to asymptotically AdS spacetimes to model far-from-equilibrium, strongly coupled plasmas. In the dual picture, horizon formation in the bulk is thermalization on the boundary. Colliding shock-wave simulations (Chesler–Yaffe) give hydrodynamization times relevant to heavy-ion collisions.
registry.map: \text{bulk horizon formation}\leftrightarrow\text{boundary thermalization};\ \ \langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\rm CFT}\propto g^{(d)}_{\mu\nu}\ (\text{Fefferman–Graham})
registry.breaks: AdS has a timelike boundary that needs boundary conditions with no counterpart in asymptotically flat NR. The dual is N=4 SYM, not QCD.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Binary-pulsar orbital decay confirms quadrupole formula
registry.summary: The orbital period of the binary pulsar PSR B1913+16 decays as the Peters–Mathews quadrupole energy loss predicts, to about 0.2%. This was the first, indirect evidence that gravitational waves carry energy. The double pulsar J0737−3039 now tests the same formula to about 10⁻⁴.
sources: Hulse & Taylor (1975). "Discovery of a pulsar in a binary system". *Astrophys. J.* 195, L51. [doi:10.1086/181708](https://doi.org/10.1086/181708)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Strong-field tests of GR with compact-binary signals
registry.summary: The PPN approach of fitting parametrized deviations from GR carried over to gravitational-wave data. LVK analyses test GR through shifts in the post-Newtonian phase coefficients, inspiral–merger–ringdown consistency, ringdown spectroscopy, and a graviton-mass bound from dispersion (m_g ≲ 1.3×10⁻²³ eV/c²). These probe the dynamical strong-field regime that solar-system and pulsar tests cannot reach.
registry.breaks: Unlike the PPN framework, there is no complete theory-agnostic parametrization of the strong field. Waveform systematics can mimic deviations.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

registry.name: Pulsar timing: from binary-pulsar tests to PTAs
registry.summary: PTAs extract nanohertz residuals with the same timing models built to test GR with binary pulsars (Shapiro delay, periastron advance, orbital decay). The expected quadrupolar Hellings–Downs correlation is itself a test that the waves are spin-2 and transverse-traceless, because scalar or vector polarizations give different overlap functions.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

registry.name: Local Lorentz invariance as a pillar of the EEP
registry.summary: The Einstein equivalence principle combines the weak equivalence principle, local Lorentz invariance and local position invariance, and Schiff's conjecture ties the three together. Michelson–Morley-type and clock-comparison experiments therefore test the same principle as Eötvös and redshift experiments. They are analysed jointly in Will's THεμ/PPN framework and in the gravity sector of the Standard-Model Extension.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Primordial GWs from amplified vacuum fluctuations
registry.summary: On an FLRW background, each tensor polarization of linearized gravity obeys the mode equation of a massless, minimally coupled scalar. Inflation therefore amplifies its vacuum fluctuations exactly as in cosmological particle creation. The result is a nearly scale-invariant stochastic background whose power is set by the Hubble rate during inflation (the tensor-to-scalar ratio r).
registry.breaks: The background has not yet been detected (only bounds on r). Late-time astrophysical backgrounds come from classical sources, not vacuum amplification.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Planck-scale discreteness vs Lorentz-invariance bounds
registry.summary: Discrete or emergent spacetimes generically predict Planck-suppressed modified photon dispersion. Arrival-time bounds from gamma-ray bursts push the linear-order scale past the Planck energy, which disfavours lattice-like discreteness. Causal sets avoid the bound because Poisson sprinkling is statistically Lorentz invariant, and deformed rather than broken symmetry is another way out.
registry.breaks: Quadratic-order effects (∝E⁴/E_Pl²) remain far below current sensitivity. Not every approach predicts dispersion: asymptotic safety and CDT make no generic Lorentz-violating prediction.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rindler horizons and the Unruh effect
registry.summary: A uniformly accelerated observer follows an orbit of a Lorentz boost (hyperbolic motion) and sees a Rindler horizon. Restricted to the Rindler wedge, the Minkowski vacuum is thermal with respect to the boost generator (Bisognano–Wichmann), which gives the Unruh temperature. Near any non-extremal horizon the geometry is approximately Rindler, so this flat-spacetime effect is the core of Hawking radiation.
registry.map: x^2-c^2t^2=\frac{c^4}{a^2};\ \rho_{\rm R}\propto e^{-2\pi K_{\rm boost}},\ k_BT_U=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c}\leftrightarrow k_BT_H=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi c}
registry.breaks: The Unruh temperature for laboratory accelerations is tiny (~4×10⁻²¹ K per m s⁻²), so it has not been observed directly.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Primordial black holes as dark matter
registry.summary: PBHs are a non-particle dark-matter candidate; Hawking evaporation removes those below about 5e14 g and gamma-ray and CMB limits constrain slightly heavier ones, while lensing and GW limits leave the asteroid-mass window open.
sources: Carr et al. (2021). "Constraints on primordial black holes". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 84, 116902. [arXiv:2002.12778](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12778)

registry.name: Black-hole superradiance probes ultralight bosons
registry.summary: A boson whose Compton wavelength matches a Kerr black hole forms hydrogen-like bound states that grow by superradiance while omega < m Omega_H, spinning the hole down; measured BH spins and continuous GW searches exclude axion masses near 1e-13 to 1e-11 eV.

registry.name: The cosmological constant problem
registry.summary: Lorentz invariance forces vacuum energy to enter the Einstein equations as rho_vac g_munu, so QFT zero-point energy, the Higgs potential and the QCD condensate all contribute to Lambda; naive estimates exceed the observed (2.2 meV)^4 by 50-120 orders of magnitude.
registry.map: \langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\rm vac}=-\rho_{\rm vac}g_{\mu\nu}\Rightarrow\Lambda_{\rm eff}=\Lambda+8\pi G\rho_{\rm vac}/c^4,\ \rho_{\rm obs}\approx(2.2\,\text{meV})^4

registry.name: Gravity as a gauge theory of the Lorentz group
registry.summary: Gauging local Lorentz (Poincare) invariance gives the spin connection as gauge potential and the Riemann tensor as its field strength, so GR in tetrad form shares the fibre-bundle structure of Yang-Mills.

registry.name: Higgs inflation is a scalar-tensor theory
registry.summary: A large non-minimal coupling xi h^2 R makes the SM Higgs the inflaton; transforming to the Einstein frame flattens the potential into the same plateau as Starobinsky R+R^2 gravity, giving n_s near 0.965 and r near 0.003.

registry.name: Sub-millimetre tests of the inverse-square law
registry.summary: ADD extra dimensions turn Newtonian gravity into a steeper power law below the compactification radius, parametrized as a Yukawa correction; torsion-balance tests of Newton's law below 0.1 mm bound n=2 ADD radii to tens of micrometres.

registry.name: Worldline EFT (NRGR) for compact binaries
registry.summary: Non-relativistic GR treats compact bodies as point particles on worldlines with finite-size operators (tidal Love numbers) and integrates out potential and radiation gravitons with Feynman diagrams and dimensional regularization, the EFT toolkit of QCD applied to post-Newtonian inspirals.

registry.name: Amplitudes compute post-Minkowskian binary dynamics
registry.summary: On-shell scattering amplitudes, unitarity cuts and the eikonal give the conservative two-body Hamiltonian order by order in G (post-Minkowskian), now at 3PM-5PM, feeding EOB waveform models for LIGO and LISA.

registry.summary: Collapsing domain walls of QCD-coupled axions, cosmic strings and QCD-scale phase transitions all produce stochastic GW backgrounds peaking near nanohertz; PTA spectra are fitted against these alongside supermassive-binary models.

registry.summary: Perturbative quantum gravity is QFT applied to the metric: expand g=eta+kappa h, quantize the massless spin-2 field with gauge fixing and ghosts as in Yang-Mills; the coupling kappa^2=32 pi G has mass dimension -2, so the theory is non-renormalizable and needs a UV completion.

registry.name: GR as an effective field theory
registry.summary: Power counting in E/M_Pl makes GR a predictive EFT: the Einstein-Hilbert term is leading, R^2 terms are suppressed, and the long-distance quantum correction to the Newtonian potential is computable and cutoff-independent, exactly like chiral perturbation theory.

registry.name: Double copy: gravity = (gauge theory)^2
registry.summary: Tree and loop gravity amplitudes are obtained from Yang-Mills amplitudes by replacing colour factors with kinematic numerators that obey the same Jacobi identities (BCJ), generalizing the KLT relations of string theory; the classical double copy maps Coulomb to Schwarzschild.

registry.name: String compactifications as BSM model building
registry.summary: Calabi-Yau, orbifold and brane-world compactifications generate gauge groups, chiral matter, axions, moduli and hidden sectors; BSM phenomenology inherits candidates (axiverse, moduli, GUT-like groups) and constraints (swampland conjectures) from string vacua.
registry.breaks: The landscape of vacua is so large that few sharp low-energy predictions follow; no compactification uniquely reproduces the SM.

registry.name: Compactified dimensions and the hierarchy problem
registry.summary: String theory needs six extra dimensions; large (ADD) or warped (Randall-Sundrum) extra dimensions lower the fundamental gravity scale to TeV, and the RS warp factor is a slice of AdS5, so hierarchy models and holography share one geometry.

registry.name: Superstrings require supersymmetry
registry.summary: Removing the bosonic-string tachyon and including fermions requires worldsheet supersymmetry, which with GSO projection yields spacetime supersymmetry; superstring compactifications are the main UV source of SUSY and supergravity model building.
registry.breaks: Low-scale (TeV) SUSY is not predicted by string theory; the SUSY-breaking scale is unconstrained and LHC has not seen superpartners.

registry.name: Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation
registry.summary: The same consistency principle that fixes SM hypercharges (gauge anomaly cancellation) fixes superstring gauge groups: gauge and gravitational anomalies of 10D supergravity cancel only for SO(32) or E8xE8 via the Green-Schwarz counterterm.

registry.summary: Wigner's classification defines an elementary particle as an irreducible unitary representation of the Poincare group, labelled by mass and spin (or helicity for m=0); spinor-helicity and little-group scaling in modern amplitudes are the same construction.

Naive estimates of ρ_vac exceed the observed ~6×10⁻²⁷ kg m⁻³, about (2.3 meV)⁴, by up to ~120 orders of magnitude: the cosmological constant problem.

registry.name: CMB dipole: our motion through the relic radiation
registry.summary: A Lorentz boost turns an isotropic blackbody into a blackbody whose temperature depends on direction. The 3.36 mK CMB dipole implies the Solar System moves at ~370 km/s, and Planck detected the accompanying aberration and Doppler modulation of the small-scale anisotropies. The CMB frame is a cosmological rest frame, not a violation of relativity.

registry.name: Cosmological redshift vs special-relativistic Doppler
registry.summary: At low z the cosmological redshift looks like a Doppler shift with v≈cz, and any FLRW redshift can be built from infinitesimal Doppler shifts parallel-transported along the photon path. The recession velocity in Hubble's law is not a Lorentz velocity, however.
registry.breaks: Recession speeds v=Hd exceed c beyond the Hubble sphere, and z records the expansion between emission and reception, not a relative velocity in one inertial frame. Converting z to a velocity with the SR formula gives wrong distances at z≳0.5.

registry.name: Cosmic-ray muons: time dilation observed
registry.summary: Muons produced by cosmic rays ~15 km up reach sea level only because their 2.2 μs lifetime is dilated by γ~10–50. Rossi and Hall's 1941 measurement of muon flux against altitude was one of the first direct confirmations of relativistic time dilation.

registry.name: Superluminal motion and Doppler boosting in jets

registry.summary: Hot accretion flows onto Sgr A* and M87* are collisionless because Coulomb collision times exceed inflow times, so ions and electrons decouple. registry.name: Transonic winds and acoustic/Alfvén horizons
registry.summary: Parker's wind passes through a sonic critical point. This transonic flow is the time-reverse of Bondi accretion, whose sonic surface is an acoustic horizon in Unruh's analogue-gravity sense. The Alfvén critical surface, which Parker Solar Probe crossed in 2021, likewise cuts the outer wind off from the Sun for Alfvén waves.
registry.breaks: The wind is an outflow, so its horizon is white-hole-like. Its critical point is set by gravity plus pressure rather than by geometry alone, and a 10⁶ K plasma swamps any analogue Hawking emission; only the classical causal structure carries over.

Correlations between partner photons could then test information loss; this is the AnaBHEL experiment.

The photon sphere and the shadow size then depend on frequency: the effect is negligible at EHT's 230 GHz but significant at low radio frequencies.

registry.name: Charged-particle orbits around magnetized black holes
registry.summary: Wald's solution for a uniform field in Kerr spacetime allows gyration, drifts and adiabatic invariants to be studied in curved spacetime. The field shifts the ISCO, makes orbits chaotic and enables a magnetic Penrose process for charged particles.
