registry.name: Horizon as a unipolar inductor (membrane paradigm)
registry.summary: A spinning horizon threaded by magnetic flux acts like a rotating conductor that generates an EMF ~Ω_HΦ, with the circuit closing through the magnetosphere. This is the same unipolar-inductor picture as the Io–Jupiter flux-tube circuit and pulsar magnetospheres; in the membrane paradigm the horizon has a surface resistivity of 377 Ω.
registry.breaks: The horizon is a causal boundary, not a material conductor. Its 'resistivity' is a teleological boundary condition fixed by the metric, it carries no real charges, and the energy comes from negative-energy states in the ergosphere rather than from a moving body.

registry.name: Gravitating 'plasma': Jeans instability and Einstein–Vlasov
registry.summary: The Vlasov–Poisson system for self-gravitating collisionless matter (the Newtonian limit) is plasma kinetics with the sign of the interaction flipped. The squared plasma frequency turns negative, so oscillations become the Jeans instability, and gravitational Landau damping also exists. The relativistic version is the Einstein–Vlasov system.
registry.breaks: With one-sign charge there is no Debye screening and no neutralizing background, hence the Jeans swindle. Self-gravitating systems are non-extensive, have negative heat capacity, and relax violently rather than towards Maxwellians.

registry.name: Chameleon screening vs Debye screening
registry.summary: Both cut off a 1/r force through a mass that depends on the environment. Debye shielding by mobile charges gives a Yukawa potential whose length λ_D is set by density and temperature. A chameleon scalar's effective mass grows with ambient density, so fifth forces are Yukawa-suppressed in dense environments.
registry.breaks: Debye screening is the linear response of charges of both signs. Chameleon screening is a nonlinear self-interaction whose thin-shell suppression depends on the source's Newtonian potential. Vainshtein screening works through derivatives and involves no mass at all, and gravity itself, with one-sign charge, cannot be Debye-screened.

registry.name: Field amplification in neutron-star mergers
registry.summary: The Kelvin–Helmholtz instability at the contact layer of merging neutron stars drives a small-scale turbulent dynamo that amplifies fields toward magnetar strength within milliseconds, and an MRI dynamo follows in the remnant disk. This controls jet launching and outflows like GRB 170817A, but GRMHD resolves it only partly.

registry.name: Constraint damping: ∇·B=0 vs Einstein constraints
registry.summary: Both are hyperbolic evolutions that carry elliptic constraints, which hold analytically but drift numerically. Constraint damping in Z4/CCZ4 and generalized-harmonic codes and hyperbolic divergence cleaning in MHD use the same trick: turn the violation into a damped field that propagates away.
registry.breaks: Einstein's constraints generate diffeomorphisms, so their violation mixes with the gauge choice. ∇·B=0 is a topological identity with no gauge content, and constrained transport can enforce it exactly, which has no GR counterpart.

registry.summary: PMNS and CKM are both 3x3 unitary matrices that arise because mass and weak-interaction bases are misaligned. They share the parametrization (three angles and one Dirac phase, plus two Majorana phases for PMNS) and the Jarlskog invariant that controls CP violation. T2K, NOvA, DUNE and Hyper-K measure leptonic CP violation as the difference between nu_mu->nu_e and the antineutrino channel.
registry.breaks: CKM angles are small and hierarchical while PMNS angles are large. Neutrino masses may be Majorana (seesaw) rather than Yukawa. Matter effects mimic a CP asymmetry in long-baseline data.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gauge-anomaly cancellation fixes SM charges
registry.summary: SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) is consistent only because gauge and mixed gauge-gravitational anomalies cancel within each generation, quarks against leptons. This requires N_c = 3 and the observed hypercharges, and it implies charge quantization. Witten's global SU(2) anomaly further requires an even number of doublets.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Axial anomaly: eta' mass and pi0 -> gamma gamma
registry.summary: QCD has no ninth Goldstone boson because the anomaly and instantons break U(1)_A ('t Hooft). The Witten-Veneziano relation ties the eta' mass to the topological susceptibility, and the pi0 -> gamma gamma rate, fixed by the anomaly coefficient, confirms N_c = 3.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fermi theory as the EFT of W exchange; SMEFT
registry.summary: Fermi's four-fermion contact interaction is the low-energy limit of W exchange. It violates unitarity below about 1 TeV, which pointed to the weak scale. It is the template for SMEFT, where dimension-6 operators suppressed by Lambda^2 parametrize heavy new physics in electroweak and Higgs data.

registry.name: Weak effective Hamiltonian and Wilson coefficients
registry.summary: Flavor-changing decays are computed with a weak effective Hamiltonian obtained by integrating out W, Z and top. The operator product expansion separates short-distance Wilson coefficients, run from m_W to m_b with anomalous dimensions, from long-distance hadronic matrix elements. New physics shows up as shifts such as C_9 and C_10 in b -> s l l.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Chiral perturbation theory: EFT of QCD's Goldstones
registry.summary: Spontaneous breaking of SU(3)_L x SU(3)_R to SU(3)_V makes the pions, kaons and eta pseudo-Goldstone bosons. Chiral perturbation theory (Weinberg, Gasser-Leutwyler) is the EFT that expands in p/Lambda_chi, with Lambda_chi of about 4 pi f_pi, roughly 1 GeV. Its leading term gives the GMOR relation.
registry.map: \mathcal L_2=\frac{f^2}{4}{\rm Tr}(\partial_\mu U\partial^\mu U^\dagger)+\frac{f^2B}{2}{\rm Tr}(MU^\dagger+UM^\dagger)\Rightarrow m_\pi^2=B(m_u+m_d)

registry.summary: Affleck and Ludwig treated the impurity as a conformal boundary condition of a 1+1D chiral CFT, obtaining the non-Fermi-liquid exponents and residual entropy of the overscreened multichannel Kondo fixed point.

registry.name: Entanglement scaling reads off the central charge
registry.summary: At a 1+1D critical point the entanglement entropy grows as (c/3) ln L, so DMRG and tensor-network simulations extract CFT central charges and operator dimensions directly from ground states.

registry.name: Quantum critical points as CFTs
registry.summary: Many z=1 quantum critical points are described by conformal field theories (e.g. O(N) Wilson-Fisher in 2+1D) whose finite-T response is universal and Planckian (tau ~ hbar/k_BT); holographic CFTs model strongly coupled transport.

registry.name: FQH edges and wavefunctions from CFT
registry.summary: Edges of quantum Hall states are chiral CFTs, and bulk wavefunctions are CFT conformal blocks: the Laughlin state from a U(1) boson, the Moore-Read Pfaffian from the Ising CFT, whose sigma fields become non-abelian anyons.

registry.name: Goldstone EFT: pions and magnons
registry.summary: Chiral perturbation theory's EFT of Goldstone bosons describes magnons: antiferromagnetic magnons are relativistic-like (O(3) sigma model, omega ~ k) while ferromagnetic ones are type-B Goldstones (omega ~ k^2) that count once per pair of broken generators.

registry.name: Fermi-surface EFT: BCS as the marginal instability
registry.summary: Treating the Fermi liquid as an EFT with RG scaling toward the Fermi surface shows only forward and BCS couplings survive, and an attractive BCS coupling is marginally relevant and runs to a gap.

registry.name: Emergent QED in quantum spin ice
registry.summary: The low-energy theory of a U(1) quantum spin liquid on the pyrochlore lattice is compact U(1) gauge theory: gapless emergent photons with omega ~ k, gapped electric charges (spinons) and magnetic monopoles.
registry.breaks: The emergent speed of light is ~meV scale and lattice-cut off; the emergent fine-structure constant and charges are not tied to QED's, and Lorentz invariance is only approximate.

registry.summary: Z2 topological order (toric code, Z2 spin liquids) is the deconfined phase of Wegner's Z2 lattice gauge theory; anyons are its electric charges and fluxes, and the Wilson-loop perimeter law is the condensed-matter signature of deconfinement.

registry.name: Kondo temperature as dimensional transmutation
registry.summary: The antiferromagnetic Kondo coupling is marginally relevant, so it grows at low energy like an asymptotically free coupling and generates a scale T_K exactly as Lambda_QCD emerges; Wilson's numerical RG solved it.

registry.name: Anderson-Higgs mechanism: photon mass = W mass
registry.summary: A superconductor's Cooper-pair condensate eats the phase Goldstone mode and gives the photon a mass 1/lambda_L (Meissner effect), the same abelian Higgs mechanism that gives W and Z masses from the Higgs vev.
registry.map: m_\gamma c^2=\frac{\hbar c}{\lambda_L},\ \lambda_L^{-2}=\mu_0n_se^2/m\ \leftrightarrow\ m_W=\tfrac12gv;\ \Delta\leftrightarrow\langle H\rangle,\ 2e\leftrightarrow g
registry.breaks: The SC condensate is a composite of electrons, non-relativistic and in a medium with a preferred frame; the electroweak condensate is (as far as known) elementary and Lorentz invariant, and its gauge group is non-abelian.

registry.name: Higgs amplitude mode in superconductors
registry.summary: The Higgs boson is the amplitude oscillation of the condensate; superconductors have the same mode at energy 2Delta, observed in Raman and terahertz pump-probe experiments.
registry.breaks: In a superconductor the mode sits at the pair-breaking edge and can decay into quasiparticles; its observation needs coupling via a CDW or nonlinear drive since it is Raman- but not dipole-active.

registry.name: Color superconductivity in dense quark matter
registry.summary: At high baryon density attractive one-gluon exchange in the color antitriplet channel makes quarks Cooper-pair near the Fermi surface; in the CFL phase the diquark condensate Higgses all eight gluons (color Meissner effect).

registry.summary: If chromomagnetic monopoles condense, chromoelectric flux is squeezed into tubes just as magnetic flux is in a type-II superconductor, giving a linear quark potential with string tension sigma.

registry.summary: Three cosmological facts need physics beyond the Standard Model: dark matter, the baryon asymmetry and inflation. registry.name: Dark matter requires physics beyond the Standard Model
registry.summary: No Standard Model particle can be the astrophysical dark matter, because neutrinos are too light and too hot. Its gravitational evidence is therefore the strongest empirical case for new particles, and each BSM model maps to its own direct, indirect, collider and structure-formation signatures.

registry.summary: After the QCD transition, the axion field starts oscillating from a misaligned initial angle, and these coherent oscillations redshift like cold matter. For f_a~10¹¹–10¹² GeV they give the observed density, which ties the strong-CP solution to galactic halos.

registry.name: Stellar energy-loss bounds on light particles
registry.summary: Any light, weakly coupled particle made in a stellar plasma escapes freely and carries energy away. The red-giant-branch tip, horizontal-branch star counts (R-parameter) and white-dwarf cooling bound g_aγγ≲0.66×10⁻¹⁰ GeV⁻¹, g_ae~10⁻¹³ and the neutrino magnetic moment, rivalling laboratory searches.

registry.name: SN 1987A burst duration bounds new particles
registry.summary: SN 1987A's ~10 s neutrino signal shows the proto-neutron star cooled by neutrino diffusion. Extra free-streaming emission of axions, dark photons or sterile neutrinos would have shortened it, which bounds axion–nucleon couplings (m_a≲10–20 meV) and leaves a 'trapping' window open for strongly coupled heavier particles.

registry.name: Baryon asymmetry: measured by cosmology, explained by BSM
registry.summary: Cosmology measures η_B≈6.1×10⁻¹⁰, and BBN and the CMB agree on it. Particle physics must generate this value through Sakharov's conditions: B violation, C and CP violation, and a departure from equilibrium supplied by the expansion or by a first-order phase transition.

registry.name: Relic abundance from Boltzmann freeze-out
registry.summary: Thermal relics follow a Boltzmann equation on the FRW background, and annihilation stops once n⟨σv⟩ drops below H at x_f=m/T_f≈20–25. registry.name: Cosmological-constant and Higgs-mass naturalness
registry.summary: Both are UV-sensitivity problems of effective field theory. Vacuum-energy corrections scale as Λ_UV⁴ against an observed (2.3 meV)⁴, just as Higgs-mass corrections scale as Λ_UV², and the same remedies (SUSY, extra dimensions, relaxation, anthropic selection) are tried on both.
registry.breaks: TeV-scale SUSY or compositeness can cancel δm_H², but no known symmetry cancels vacuum energy while letting SUSY be broken. The cosmological-constant problem is still ~60 orders of magnitude off with a TeV cutoff, and it involves gravity directly.

registry.name: GUT monopole problem motivated inflation
registry.summary: Breaking a simple GUT group down to a subgroup containing U(1)_em leaves nontrivial π₂ of the vacuum manifold. The Kibble mechanism then makes about one monopole per horizon volume, enough to overclose the universe, and Guth designed inflation partly to dilute them. GUT-scale vacuum energy remains a natural inflation scale, with V^{1/4}≲1.4×10¹⁶ GeV from r<0.036.

registry.name: Collider vs direct-detection complementarity
registry.summary: In simplified-mediator and Higgs-portal models the same couplings set both LHC missing-energy rates (mono-jet, invisible Higgs decays with BR<0.107) and nuclear-recoil rates. Collider limits therefore map onto the σ_SI–m_χ plane and dominate below a few GeV, where recoils are too soft to detect.

registry.name: LHC data calibrate air-shower hadronic models
registry.summary: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays collide at √s≈430 TeV per nucleon pair, so reading composition from X_max and muon counts means extrapolating hadronic models (EPOS-LHC, Sibyll, QGSJET) tuned at the LHC, including forward LHCf data and the 2025 oxygen runs. The observed muon excess in air showers, the 'muon puzzle', points to mismodelled forward hadron production.

registry.name: Cosmic rays as particle physics's first beam
registry.summary: Before accelerators, cloud chambers and emulsions exposed to cosmic rays revealed the positron (1932), the muon (1936), the pion (1947) and strange particles. The detector lineage now runs the other way: collider-style silicon trackers, calorimeters and magnetic spectrometers fly as AMS-02, DAMPE and Fermi-LAT.

registry.name: Pion decay links neutrinos, γ-rays and cosmic rays
registry.summary: Accelerated hadrons hitting gas or photons make pions. Charged pions decay to neutrinos with E_ν≈E_p/20 and neutral pions to γ-rays with E_γ≈E_p/10, so decay kinematics tie the neutrino, γ-ray and cosmic-ray fluxes of TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane together.

registry.name: Neutrino astronomy runs on particle-physics neutrinos
registry.summary: Neutrino telescopes need particle-physics inputs: cross sections, oscillation parameters and flavour identification. In return they supply natural beams at TeV–PeV energies and Mpc–Gpc baselines that no accelerator reaches, which test oscillations, neutrino decay and Lorentz invariance.
sources: IceCube Collaboration (2013). "Evidence for High-Energy Extraterrestrial Neutrinos at the IceCube Detector". *Science* 342, 1242856. [arXiv:1311.5238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5238)

registry.name: Neutrino fog: CEvNS in dark-matter detectors
registry.summary: Coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering, first observed by COHERENT, gives nuclear recoils that look like WIMP recoils. Solar ⁸B neutrinos mimic a ~6 GeV WIMP and atmospheric and DSNB neutrinos set a 'fog' that slows sensitivity gains; XENONnT and PandaX-4T reported first ~2.6–2.7σ indications of ⁸B CEvNS in 2024.

registry.name: Water-Cherenkov detection scaled to km³ telescopes
registry.summary: IceCube, KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD reuse the Kamiokande/Super-K water-Cherenkov technique at gigaton scale in ice or sea water. The same detectors treat atmospheric neutrinos as background for astronomy and as signal for oscillation physics (DeepCore, ORCA).

registry.name: pp-chain and CNO neutrinos test stellar fusion
registry.summary: Hydrogen burning makes stars neutrino sources, and the measured pp, ⁷Be, ⁸B and CNO fluxes confirm the stellar energy source directly. Neutrino energy losses (plasma, pair and Urca processes) drive late stellar evolution.

registry.name: Core-collapse supernova neutrinos
registry.summary: About 99% of the ~3×10⁵³ erg released in core collapse leaves as neutrinos of all flavours over ~10 s. Kamiokande-II, IMB and Baksan caught about 25 events from SN 1987A, confirming the picture, and Super-K-Gd, JUNO, DUNE and IceCube now await a Galactic burst and the diffuse supernova neutrino background.

registry.name: Solar neutrinos and the standard solar model
registry.summary: Solar neutrino fluxes from Homestake to Borexino tested the standard solar model, and SNO showed the deficit came from flavour conversion, not from the model. Helioseismology independently confirmed the model's sound-speed profile, and Borexino's CNO flux now probes the solar metallicity problem.

registry.name: CMB bounds on the sum of neutrino masses
registry.summary: Massive relic neutrinos turn from radiation into matter after recombination, which changes the early ISW effect and the CMB lensing potential. Planck bounds Σm_ν below about 0.12 eV, which complements the model-independent kinematic tritium bound from KATRIN.

registry.name: Neutrino free-streaming suppresses matter clustering
registry.summary: Relic neutrinos do not cluster below their free-streaming scale, so small-scale matter power drops by ΔP/P≈−8f_ν. With BAO fixing the expansion history, DESI DR1 plus CMB gives Σm_ν<0.072 eV (95%), pressing against the 0.059 eV minimum for normal ordering.

registry.name: Astrophysical neutrino flavour ratios
registry.summary: Over cosmic baselines oscillations average out, so a pion-decay source ratio of 1:2:0 arrives at Earth as about 1:1:1. IceCube's measured flavour composition, including ν_τ candidates and a Glashow-resonance event near 6.3 PeV, tests the source mechanism and new physics such as neutrino decay or Lorentz violation.

registry.name: Collective neutrino flavour conversion in supernovae
registry.summary: Near a proto-neutron star, ν–ν forward scattering makes flavour evolution a nonlinear many-body problem, with spectral swaps and fast flavour instabilities. These may change neutrino heating behind the shock and r-process conditions, but how much they matter for the explosion is unresolved.

registry.name: MSW resonance in the solar density profile
registry.summary: Coherent forward scattering on solar electrons adds the potential √2 G_F n_e, so ⁸B neutrinos cross the resonance adiabatically and leave as ν₂ with P_ee≈sin²θ₁₂≈0.3. Low-energy pp neutrinos keep the vacuum-averaged P_ee≈0.55, and Borexino measured the transition between the two.

registry.name: N_eff limits on light sterile neutrinos
registry.summary: An eV-scale sterile neutrino with the mixing suggested by the LSND, MiniBooNE and gallium anomalies would be thermalised before BBN, adding ΔN_eff≈1 and ~1 eV to Σm_ν. Planck's N_eff=2.99±0.17 and mass bounds exclude it unless self-interactions or lepton asymmetries suppress production; extra dark radiation as a Hubble-tension fix is proposed but disfavoured.
sources: Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

registry.name: keV sterile neutrinos as warm dark matter
registry.summary: A keV sterile neutrino produced by oscillations (Dodelson–Widrow) or resonantly (Shi–Fuller) is warm dark matter whose free-streaming suppresses dwarf-scale power. Lyman-α and satellite counts combined with X-ray limits on ν_s→νγ exclude non-resonant production, and the claimed 3.5 keV line remains contested.

registry.name: Effective field theory of inflation
registry.summary: Inflationary perturbations are treated as the Goldstone mode π of broken time translations, with operators ordered by derivatives as in chiral perturbation theory. A reduced sound speed predicts f_NL^equil∝(1−c_s²)/c_s², and heavy fields leave oscillatory 'cosmological collider' signals in the squeezed bispectrum.

registry.name: EFT tower for dark-matter–nucleus scattering
registry.summary: Direct-detection rates come from an EFT chain. Mediator-scale operators run down to quark and gluon operators, nucleon matrix elements (σ_πN, spin fractions) and chiral EFT match them to nucleons, and the result is a basis of Galilean-invariant non-relativistic operators — the same tower used for flavour physics and nuclear forces.

registry.name: Lattice QCD crossover in the early universe
registry.summary: Lattice QCD shows the quark–hadron transition near 156 MeV is a smooth crossover, so it leaves no bubbles and no strong gravitational-wave signal. The lattice equation of state supplies g_*(T), and the topological susceptibility χ(T) feeds WIMP and axion relic-abundance calculations.

registry.name: Weak freeze-out sets neutrino decoupling and n/p
registry.summary: Weak rates Γ≈G_F²T⁵ fall below the Hubble rate at T≈1 MeV, so neutrinos decouple. Electron–positron annihilation then heats the photons, giving T_ν=(4/11)^{1/3}T_γ and N_eff=3.044, and the frozen n/p≈1/7 fixes primordial helium Y_p≈0.25; the Fermi constant thereby shapes the expansion history.
sources: Weinberg (1967). "A Model of Leptons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 19, 1264. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.19.1264](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.19.1264)

registry.name: Higgs inflation and electroweak vacuum stability
registry.summary: With a large nonminimal coupling ξ|H|²R (ξ~10⁴), the measured Higgs can act as the inflaton and gives Starobinsky-like predictions n_s≈0.965 and r≈0.003. Conversely, the running Higgs quartic turns negative near 10¹⁰–10¹¹ GeV, so the metastable electroweak vacuum constrains the Hubble scale during inflation and reheating.
sources: Starobinsky (1980). "A new type of isotropic cosmological models without singularity". *Phys. Lett. B* 91, 99. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(80)90670-X)

registry.name: Dense QCD and the neutron-star equation of state
registry.summary: Neutron-star cores reach several times nuclear saturation density, where QCD is nonperturbative and lattice QCD fails because of the sign problem. Masses ≳2 M_⊙, NICER radii and GW170817 tidal deformability constrain the equation of state, testing hyperons, deconfined quark matter and colour superconductivity, while perturbative QCD bounds the high-density end.

registry.name: Plasma frequency as photon mass for axion resonance
registry.summary: In a plasma the photon acquires an effective mass ħω_p, so axion–photon (and dark-photon) conversion is resonant where m_a c² = ħω_p. This underlies radio-line searches for axion dark matter converting in neutron-star magnetospheres, tunable plasma haloscopes that set ω_p with wire metamaterials, and resonant dark-photon production in the Sun. Stellar-plasma emission (Primakoff, plasmon decay) is also behind stellar-cooling bounds on axions and neutrino dipole moments.

registry.name: Hypermagnetic helicity, the anomaly and inverse cascades
registry.summary: Above the electroweak scale, helical hypercharge magnetic fields source baryon and lepton number through the U(1)_Y anomaly. Their evolution (the inverse helicity cascade in MHD turbulence and helicity decay at the electroweak crossover) can therefore generate or wash out the baryon asymmetry (Giovannini–Shaposhnikov 1998; Kamada–Long 2016).

registry.name: Sphaleron rate set by hot gauge-plasma kinetics
registry.summary: Baryon-violating sphaleron transitions in the hot electroweak plasma run through soft magnetic modes (k ~ g²T) that hard particles overdamp via Landau damping. Arnold–Son–Yaffe and Bödeker showed Γ_sph ∝ α_w^5 T^4 ln(1/α_w); Bödeker's effective theory is a Langevin equation equivalent to Ohmic magnetic diffusion with a colour conductivity. Plasma kinetics thus fixes the rate used in baryogenesis and washout calculations.

registry.name: Dark plasmas: instabilities constrain charged dark matter
registry.summary: If dark matter carries charge under a dark U(1) or a millicharge, halos behave as collisionless plasmas. In cluster mergers, Weibel and two-stream instabilities could isotropize and decelerate dark matter far faster than binary scattering, so plasma growth rates rather than cross-sections set Bullet-Cluster-type bounds on the dark fine-structure constant.
registry.breaks: Whether the instabilities grow and saturate fast enough to transfer momentum is contested; later analyses argued earlier bounds were overestimated. Magnetized dark plasmas also behave differently.

registry.name: Bullet Cluster: plasma shock versus collisionless DM
registry.summary: In the merging Bullet Cluster (1E 0657-56) ram pressure slows the X-ray intracluster plasma, which drives a Mach ≈ 3 bow shock, while the lensing mass passes through with the galaxies. The offset is key evidence for collisionless particle dark matter and bounds its self-interaction. The same shock is a laboratory for collisionless-shock physics and electron–ion equilibration.

registry.name: Parker bound: galactic dynamo limits GUT monopoles
registry.summary: Grand unification predicts superheavy 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles. Monopoles crossing the Galaxy would be accelerated by its magnetic field and drain its energy faster than the galactic dynamo regenerates it (~10^8 yr), which gives the Parker bound on the monopole flux. This dynamo constraint on GUT cosmology, together with the monopole overabundance problem, helped motivate inflation.

registry.name: g−2 from cyclotron versus spin precession
registry.summary: The muon g−2 storage ring (BNL, Fermilab) measures ω_a = ω_s − ω_c, the beat between spin precession and cyclotron gyration in a uniform 1.45 T field. It uses electrostatic quadrupole focusing and the magic momentum 3.09 GeV/c (γ ≈ 29.3), which cancels the β×E term. Electron g−2 uses one electron in a Penning trap, whose magnetron motion is the E×B drift: single-particle orbit theory as a precision instrument.

registry.name: Laser and beam plasmas as advanced-accelerator R&D
registry.summary: The laser–plasma toolkit (chirped-pulse-amplified lasers, beam–plasma interaction, plasma lenses, wakefield staging) is the advanced-accelerator line in collider strategy studies, and collider luminosity targets translate back into required driver average power, kHz repetition rates and wall-plug efficiency for the plasma community.

registry.name: Beamstrahlung and laser radiation reaction share χ
registry.summary: At linear-collider interaction points the collective field of one nanometre-scale bunch acts on the other like an ultra-intense laser. Particles pinch (disruption), radiate (beamstrahlung) and convert photons to pairs, governed by the same quantum-nonlinearity parameter χ (Υ) that defines the radiation-reaction and QED-plasma regime of multi-PW laser–plasma experiments. Beam–beam codes and QED-PIC codes use the same locally-constant-field emission rates.

registry.name: Plasma wakefield accelerators as compact collider drivers
registry.summary: Plasma waves sustain accelerating fields near the cold wave-breaking limit, 10–100 GV/m against ~100 MV/m in RF cavities, so laser- or beam-driven wakefield stages are the candidate route to compact multi-TeV lepton colliders; collider requirements (energy spread, emittance preservation, wall-plug efficiency, positron acceleration, staging) define the field's open problems.

registry.name: High-field superconducting magnets: colliders and tokamaks
registry.summary: Collider energy scales as B·R and tokamak fusion power at fixed β as B^4, so both push the same conductors. These are Nb–Ti (LHC, 8.3 T), Nb3Sn (HL-LHC triplets ~11 T, ITER toroidal-field and central-solenoid coils) and REBCO high-temperature superconductors (the 20 T CFS/MIT SPARC model coil, 2021; candidate FCC-hh dipoles and muon-collider solenoids). Both fields share quench protection, stress management and cryogenics.

registry.name: AWAKE: proton-driven wakefields from the LHC injectors
registry.summary: AWAKE at CERN sends 400 GeV SPS proton bunches (the LHC injector beam) into a 10 m rubidium plasma; the bunch, far longer than λ_p, undergoes the seeded self-modulation instability into microbunches that resonantly drive a wake, which accelerated injected electrons to ~2 GeV (2018). Proton bunches store ~20–130 kJ, enough in principle for single-stage acceleration to TeV energies.

registry.name: Electron cloud and two-stream instability in the LHC
registry.summary: Synchrotron-light photoelectrons multiply by secondary emission into an electron cloud in the LHC beam screen. This non-neutral plasma adds cryogenic heat load and drives the electron–proton two-stream instability, tune shifts and emittance growth. It is analysed with plasma linear-instability theory and particle-in-cell codes, and mitigated by beam scrubbing and low-secondary-yield coatings.

registry.name: Hillas criterion: cosmic accelerators versus colliders
registry.summary: Any accelerator must keep the particle's gyroradius inside the accelerating region, so maximum energy scales as field times size. 8.33 T dipoles on a 2.8 km bending radius give the LHC 7 TeV, while the Hillas criterion applied to supernova-remnant, AGN-jet and cluster shocks bounds cosmic-ray energies up to ~10^20 eV (√s ≈ 430 TeV on a proton target).
registry.breaks: Shock acceleration is stochastic: repeated diffusive crossings in turbulent, self-generated fields produce power-law spectra, and β_s≪1 plus radiative or escape losses lower E_max. Colliders accelerate coherently with RF in fixed guide fields and deliver near-monoenergetic beams.
sources: Blandford & Ostriker (1978). "Particle acceleration by astrophysical shocks". *Astrophys. J.* 221, L29. [doi:10.1086/182658](https://doi.org/10.1086/182658)

registry.name: Jet quenching as stopping power in a QCD plasma
registry.summary: Energy loss of a fast parton crossing the QGP is computed like charged-particle stopping in a plasma. It has three parts: collisional loss with a Coulomb logarithm cut off by the Debye mass (Bjorken 1982; Braaten–Thoma), a jet transport coefficient q̂ that is a transverse-momentum (Fokker–Planck) diffusion coefficient, and radiative loss with Landau–Pomeranchuk–Migdal coherence (BDMPS).
registry.breaks: For coloured partons radiative loss dominates and grows as L² (BDMPS). Non-relativistic plasma stopping has no counterpart, since bremsstrahlung there is negligible.

registry.name: Machine learning for triggers and tokamak control
registry.summary: HEP developed low-latency deep learning for triggers, fast surrogate simulation and anomaly detection; fusion has its counterparts in neural disruption predictors (Kates-Harbeck et al. 2019) and reinforcement-learning magnetic control on TCV (Degrave et al. 2022). Both need microsecond-scale FPGA inference, rare-event detection under class imbalance, and simulation-trained models that survive domain shift to the real machine.

registry.name: Gaseous detectors are controlled Townsend discharges
registry.summary: Geiger and proportional counters, MWPCs, drift chambers, GEMs, Micromegas and RPCs amplify ionization by Townsend avalanches. They must stay below the Raether limit (αd ≈ 20, ~10^8 electrons), where avalanches become streamers and sparks; this is the breakdown physics of gas discharges (Townsend coefficients, Paschen curves, streamer theory). RPCs run deliberately in avalanche or streamer mode, and detector ageing is plasma polymerization, the same chemistry as plasma deposition.

registry.name: Geiger counters discovered the radiation belts
registry.summary: Van Allen's Geiger–Müller counters on Explorer 1 and 3 (1958) saturated in trapped-particle regions, which is how the radiation belts were discovered. Space-plasma particle instruments descend from nuclear and particle detectors (scintillators, silicon, magnetic spectrometers such as AMS-02). LHC front-end electronics and satellites face the same single-event effects and radiation-hardness engineering.

registry.name: Shock-accelerated cosmic rays as neutrino sources
registry.summary: Diffusive shock acceleration gives power-law protons whose pp and pγ collisions make pions. Pion decays yield neutrinos carrying ~5% of the proton energy, with flavor ratio ≈1:1:1 at Earth and a spectrum that tracks the parent. This is the hadronic-source signature IceCube seeks (TXS 0506+056, the Galactic plane), although coronal sources such as NGC 1068 may accelerate by turbulence or reconnection instead.

registry.name: MSW potential and plasma frequency: medium dispersion
registry.summary: Coherent forward scattering on electrons gives electron neutrinos the potential V = √2 G_F n_e (Wolfenstein 1978), just as forward scattering of photons on free electrons gives the refractive term ω_p² ∝ n_e. Both shift the dispersion in proportion to electron density, and resonant MSW level crossings (adiabatic or Landau–Zener) parallel mode conversion at resonances in inhomogeneous plasmas.
registry.breaks: The MSW potential is a flavor-dependent weak-interaction effect (~10^-11 eV in the solar core) that acts through mixing rather than giving a mass or cutoff. Photon refraction is electromagnetic and produces a cutoff at ω = ω_p.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

registry.name: Neutrino quantum kinetics as matrix-valued Vlasov
registry.summary: Neutrino transport with oscillations obeys quantum kinetic equations (Sigl–Raffelt 1993) for flavor density matrices. They combine free streaming, a commutator with a self-consistent mean-field Hamiltonian (vacuum, MSW and ν–ν refraction) and collisions. This is the structure of a Vlasov system with a self-consistent field, so mean-field, quasilinear and moment-closure methods transfer from plasma kinetics.

registry.name: Fast flavor instability from plasma dispersion relations
registry.summary: In supernova cores and neutron-star mergers, neutrino–neutrino forward scattering makes flavor evolution collective. Linearizing the off-diagonal flavor density matrix gives a dispersion relation whose complex roots signal the fast flavor instability, analysed like a beam–plasma instability (Izaguirre, Raffelt & Tamborra 2017). A crossing in the angular electron-lepton-number distribution plays the role of a bump-on-tail, and Landau-damping and quasilinear-saturation ideas carried over.

registry.name: Chiral magnetic effect as an α-dynamo
registry.summary: In a plasma with chiral imbalance μ_5 (early universe, proto-neutron stars, heavy-ion collisions) the anomaly drives a current along B: the chiral magnetic effect. This current enters the induction equation exactly like the mean-field α-effect, giving a chiral dynamo (chiral plasma instability) that amplifies helical fields while the anomaly drains μ_5 (Boyarsky, Fröhlich & Ruchayskiy 2012; Rogachevskii et al. 2017).

registry.breaks: The classical α-effect is a statistical property of helical turbulence. The chiral α is microscopic, fixed by the anomaly coefficient, and decays as chirality-flipping (electron-mass) scattering erases μ_5 at low temperature.

registry.name: Magnetic helicity is an abelian Chern–Simons term
registry.summary: Magnetic helicity H = ∫A·B d³x is the abelian Chern–Simons functional. It measures the linking of field lines (Moffatt 1969) and is exactly conserved in ideal MHD because E·B = 0 (Woltjer 1958). Through the axial anomaly it trades with fermion chirality so that N_5 + (e²/4π²)H is conserved, the bridge behind chiral MHD and anomaly-driven baryogenesis.
registry.map: H=\int\mathbf A\cdot\mathbf B\,d^3x,\quad \frac{dH}{dt}=-2\int\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\,d^3x,\quad \partial_\mu j_5^\mu=\frac{e^2}{2\pi^2}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B
registry.breaks: Classical helicity is continuous and conserved only approximately (resistivity, reconnection). Non-abelian Chern–Simons number changes by integers between topologically distinct vacua via instantons and sphalerons.
sources: Adler (1969). "Axial-Vector Vertex in Spinor Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 177, 2426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426)

registry.name: Field-theory action principles for Vlasov–Maxwell
registry.summary: Vlasov–Maxwell is a classical field theory: Low (1958) gave its Lagrangian, and Morrison, Marsden and Weinstein gave its noncanonical Lie–Poisson Hamiltonian structure. Gyrokinetic field theories and structure-preserving variational particle-in-cell schemes derive from such actions, and Martin–Siggia–Rose functional integrals treat plasma-turbulence statistics with the generating-functional machinery of QFT.
registry.breaks: The Vlasov bracket is noncanonical with Casimir invariants and is never quantized. MSR integrals weight stochastic histories, not quantum amplitudes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gyrokinetics as a scale-separated effective theory
registry.summary: Gyrokinetics removes fast gyration (ω ≪ Ω_c) with a gyrophase-averaging Lie transform ordered in ρ* = ρ/L, keeps the magnetic moment as an adiabatic invariant, and adds corrections order by order. Structurally this is like integrating out a heavy scale in an EFT such as NRQED or HQET, with ρ* as the power-counting parameter.
registry.breaks: Gyrokinetics is a classical asymptotic phase-space reduction with no loops, renormalization or running couplings. Its orderings (δf/f ~ ρ*) are imposed rather than symmetry-protected, and they fail in steep edge pedestals.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: MHD as the effective theory of a one-form symmetry
registry.summary: With no magnetic monopoles, magnetic flux conservation is a one-form global symmetry. Grozdanov, Hofman and Iqbal (2017) recast relativistic dissipative MHD as the hydrodynamic effective theory of that symmetry, organized by a derivative expansion with symmetry-allowed transport coefficients. Frozen-in flux and Alfvén waves then follow from symmetry plus EFT power counting.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Strong-field QED in the laser–plasma QED regime
registry.summary: At intensities ≳10^23 W/cm² (a0 of a few hundred) plasma electrons reach χ ~ 1, where nonlinear Compton emission and multiphoton Breit–Wheeler pair creation dominate. Their rates are Feynman diagrams in the Furry picture with Volkov-dressed propagators, inserted as Monte Carlo processes in QED-PIC codes. SLAC E-144 first observed them in the 1990s, and Schwinger pair creation at E_S is the non-perturbative limit.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Debye-screened potential is the Yukawa potential
registry.summary: A massive boson's static propagator 1/(k²+m²) Fourier-transforms to the Yukawa potential. A plasma's static longitudinal dielectric function ε(k)=1+1/(k²λ_D²) turns the Coulomb propagator into 1/(k²+λ_D⁻²), giving the same potential with λ_D in place of the Compton wavelength. Hence 'Yukawa systems' for dusty plasmas and the 'Debye mass' of thermal field theory.
registry.breaks: Debye screening is a collective, temperature-dependent medium effect. It applies to static longitudinal fields only (static magnetic fields are unscreened), needs N_D≫1 for linearity, and has no associated free particle; the Yukawa range comes from the rest mass of a quantum exchanged in vacuum.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Renormalization group for MHD turbulence
registry.summary: Field-theory machinery moved into turbulence theory. Wyld's diagrammatic expansion, Kraichnan-type renormalized closures and Wilsonian RG were applied to randomly forced MHD (Fournier, Sulem & Pouquet 1982) and to magnetized-plasma turbulence, yielding renormalized eddy viscosity and resistivity and infrared fixed points that set inertial-range exponents.
registry.breaks: There is no small parameter (the ε-expansion is extrapolated to large ε), and mean-field anisotropy (critical balance) and intermittency are not captured.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Vacuum polarization as screening, asymptotic freedom
registry.summary: A running coupling is a scale-dependent dielectric function. QED vacuum polarization by virtual pairs screens a bare charge so α grows at short distance, as a polarizable medium or plasma screens a test charge. In QCD, gluon self-interaction overcompensates (antiscreening), giving asymptotic freedom.
registry.breaks: Plasma screening comes from real thermal charges and is exponential beyond λ_D. Vacuum screening is Lorentz-invariant, involves only virtual pairs and is merely logarithmic, so the charge is never fully screened. Equilibrium plasmas have no antiscreening counterpart.
sources: Gross & Wilczek (1973). "Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1343. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343)

registry.name: Coulomb logarithm by dimensional regularization
registry.summary: The Coulomb logarithm reflects a collision integral divergent at both ends: the Boltzmann binary-collision operator diverges at large impact parameter and the Lenard–Balescu collective operator at small. Brown, Preston and Singleton (2005) continued the kinetic equations to d dimensions (Boltzmann for d>3, Lenard–Balescu for d<3) and cancelled the poles at d=3 as in dimensional regularization. This fixes ln Λ, with its constant term, for stopping power and temperature equilibration.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Antimatter non-neutral plasmas enable CPT tests
registry.summary: Antihydrogen for CPT-symmetry tests (ALPHA's 1S–2S line matches hydrogen to ~2×10⁻¹²) is made by merging antiproton and positron non-neutral plasmas in Penning–Malmberg traps. The process relies on one-component-plasma techniques developed for strongly magnetized, strongly coupled non-neutral plasmas: rotating-wall compression, evaporative and cyclotron cooling, and plasma-mode diagnostics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Electroweak magnetogenesis as a dynamo seed
registry.summary: Gradients of the Higgs-field phase during electroweak symmetry breaking can generate magnetic fields (Vachaspati 1991), and helical fields from the electroweak or QCD epochs inverse-cascade to larger scales. This is a primordial alternative to the Biermann battery for seeding galactic and cluster dynamos.
registry.breaks: With m_H = 125 GeV the Standard-Model electroweak transition is a smooth crossover, which weakens bubble-collision magnetogenesis. The surviving field strengths and coherence lengths may also be too small without strong amplification.
sources: Parker (1955). "Hydromagnetic Dynamo Models". *Astrophys. J.* 122, 293. [doi:10.1086/146087](https://doi.org/10.1086/146087)

registry.name: Plasmon mass and the Anderson–Higgs mechanism
registry.summary: Transverse electromagnetic waves in a plasma obey ω² = ω_p² + c²k², the dispersion of a massive (Proca) photon. Anderson (1963) used the plasmon and the Meissner effect to argue that a gauge field can gain mass without losing gauge invariance by absorbing the would-be Goldstone mode. Englert–Brout and Higgs made the idea relativistic in 1964, and it gives the W and Z their masses.
registry.breaks: The plasma mass belongs to a thermal medium in a preferred frame (longitudinal and transverse modes differ) and involves no spontaneously broken symmetry: a normal plasma does not screen static magnetic fields. The electroweak mass comes from a Lorentz-invariant vacuum condensate, as in a superconductor's Meissner effect.
sources: Englert & Brout (1964). "Broken Symmetry and the Mass of Gauge Vector Mesons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 321. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

registry.name: Colour Debye screening in the quark–gluon plasma
registry.summary: Free colour charges in the quark–gluon plasma screen chromoelectric fields as electrons and ions screen a test charge, with Debye mass m_D ~ gT. Once the screening length falls below a quarkonium radius the heavy-quark pair unbinds (Matsui–Satz J/ψ suppression), and lattice Polyakov-loop correlators measure the screening.
registry.breaks: Chromomagnetic fields are screened only non-perturbatively, at g²T. The coupling is not small near T_c, so perturbative m_D is unreliable, and the plasma is non-abelian, relativistic and quantum.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Strongly coupled QGP and strongly coupled Coulomb plasmas
registry.summary: The near-perfect-fluid QGP invited comparison with classical strongly coupled plasmas. A coupling parameter Γ (potential over kinetic energy) of order 1–10 puts the sQGP in the liquid range of one-component and Yukawa plasmas. Classical colour molecular dynamics borrowed from OCP simulations reproduces liquid-like transport, and in both systems shear viscosity is lowest near the liquid–gas crossover.
registry.breaks: The QGP is relativistic and quantum (its η/s ≈ 1/4π sits near a conjectured quantum bound with no classical analogue), non-abelian with confinement, and has a running coupling. Dusty plasmas are classical, abelian and strongly damped by neutral gas.
sources: Thomas et al. (1994). "Plasma Crystal: Coulomb Crystallization in a Dusty Plasma". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 73, 652. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.652](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.652)

registry.name: Hard thermal loops are non-abelian Vlasov theory
registry.summary: The leading soft-field response of a hot gauge plasma is the hard-thermal-loop effective action of Braaten–Pisarski and Frenkel–Taylor. Linearized Vlasov equations for hard colour-charged quasiparticles reproduce it exactly (Blaizot–Iancu; Kelly, Liu, Lucchesi & Manuel), including gluon plasmons with ω_pl = m_D/√3, Debye screening and Landau damping of space-like (ω<k) gluons.
registry.breaks: Covariant derivatives make the Vlasov equation non-abelian (colour precession, Wong equations). Beyond leading order, collisions and the soft magnetic scale g²T require Bödeker's effective theory or the lattice.
sources: Malmberg & Wharton (1964). "Collisionless Damping of Electrostatic Plasma Waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 184. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184)

registry.name: Chromo-Weibel instability and QGP isotropization
registry.summary: A quark–gluon plasma with an anisotropic momentum distribution, as produced early in heavy-ion collisions, is unstable to magnetic-type Weibel/filamentation modes, just as anisotropic electron plasmas are (Mrówczyński; Romatschke–Strickland; Arnold, Lenaghan & Moore 2003). The chromo-Weibel instability speeds isotropization in weak-coupling bottom-up thermalization.
registry.breaks: Non-abelian self-interaction changes saturation: growth feeds a cascade to the ultraviolet rather than saturating as in an abelian plasma. At RHIC/LHC couplings its role relative to strong-coupling (holographic) isotropization is debated.

registry.summary: Axion dark matter is hunted with quantum sensors. Haloscopes convert axions into microwave photons at ν=m_ac²/h, read by near-quantum-limited Josephson amplifiers and by squeezed-state receivers that beat the standard quantum limit. Spin-precession experiments (CASPEr, magnetometer networks) look for the axion field acting as an oscillating pseudo-magnetic field on spins.

registry.summary: Sub-GeV dark matter scattering on electrons leaves only a few eV. SENSEI and DAMIC-M use skipper CCDs that read each pixel's charge many times to reach sub-electron noise. Silicon's band gap and pair-creation energy set the threshold, and leakage current and spurious charge are the backgrounds.

registry.name: Tabletop force sensors test sub-millimetre gravity
registry.summary: Large extra dimensions (ADD) and light moduli predict Yukawa-like departures from Newton's inverse-square law below ~1 mm. Precision force sensors bound the strength–range (α, λ) plane: torsion balances, and increasingly atom interferometers and levitated or mechanical quantum sensors.

registry.name: Magic momentum: storage-ring dynamics for g−2
registry.summary: Muon g−2 rings run at the magic momentum (γ≈29.3, p≈3.09 GeV/c), where electrostatic-quadrupole focusing drops out of the Thomas–BMT spin precession. Residual betatron oscillations, momentum spread and pitch corrections are the beam-dynamics systematics. J-PARC's planned design instead uses an ultra-cold, low-emittance beam with no electric focusing.

registry.name: Muon g−2 as precision spin-precession magnetometry
registry.summary: Muon g−2 measures an anomalous spin-precession frequency ω_a against a storage-ring field mapped at the ~0.1 ppm level or better. The field comes from pulsed proton-NMR probes calibrated to shielded-proton standards, the same phase-accumulation principle used in NMR and atomic magnetometers. Electron g−2 uses single-electron quantum-jump spectroscopy in a Penning trap.

registry.name: Colliders as accelerator-physics machines
registry.summary: Every collider measurement depends on a machine designed with accelerator physics. Magnets and RF set the energy frontier, and luminosity sets the event rate, so a process with cross section σ gives events at rate Lσ. The main collider design choices (hadron vs lepton beams, circular vs linear) are accelerator-physics trade-offs.

registry.name: CLOUD: accelerator beams test aerosol nucleation
registry.summary: CERN's CLOUD experiment uses a Proton Synchrotron beam as an adjustable cosmic-ray source in an ultra-clean chamber to measure ion-induced nucleation of atmospheric aerosols. It showed that ions boost nucleation from sulphuric-acid and organic vapours. The proposed cosmic-ray–cloud–climate link is contested, and CLOUD's own modelling finds it too weak to explain recent warming.

registry.name: Magnet and SRF technology set future-collider reach
registry.summary: Accelerator hardware bounds future-collider designs. A ~100 TeV FCC-hh needs ~14–16 T Nb₃Sn or HTS dipoles. FCC-ee, CEPC and ILC rely on high-Q niobium SRF cavities, and CLIC relies on 70–100 MV/m normal-conducting X-band structures. In practice, magnet and cavity R&D decides collider strategy.

registry.name: Muon ionization cooling evades Liouville
registry.summary: Muons are produced with large emittance and live 2.2 μs, so a muon collider needs ionization cooling. Energy loss in absorbers removes momentum in all directions, and RF restores only the longitudinal part, so emittance shrinks. Dissipation evades Liouville's theorem, with multiple scattering as the heating term. MICE demonstrated the effect.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Synchrotron radiation: collider loss, light-source product
registry.summary: Light sources turn relativistic Larmor radiation into X-ray beams, and the same radiation is the energy-loss limit of circular e⁺e⁻ colliders. The loss per turn scales as γ⁴/ρ. That is why FCC-ee and CEPC need ~90–100 km rings, why linear colliders are proposed, and why a muon collider radiates (m_e/m_μ)⁴ less.

registry.name: CLIC X-band structures for VHEE FLASH therapy
registry.summary: High-gradient X-band accelerating structures developed for CLIC are being adapted into compact very-high-energy-electron (VHEE, ~100–200 MeV) machines, for example by the CERN–CHUV collaboration. These could deliver ultra-high-dose-rate FLASH radiotherapy to deep tumours.

registry.name: Dipole field sets the LHC energy
registry.summary: In a fixed tunnel the dipole field sets the beam momentum. 8.33 T Nb–Ti dipoles at 1.9 K on a ~2.8 km bending radius give the design 7 TeV per beam. HL-LHC brings in Nb₃Sn magnets of the 11–12 T class, and hadron colliders beyond it are limited by magnet technology.

registry.name: LHC luminosity from emittance and beta*
registry.summary: LHC luminosity is a beam-dynamics quantity. The beam size at the interaction point is σ*=√(εβ*), so luminosity rises with bunch intensity and falls with emittance and β*. Beam–beam tune shifts, crossing-angle geometry and pile-up limit how far it can be pushed, which is the HL-LHC problem.

registry.name: Superconducting magnet industry: Tevatron to MRI
registry.summary: Clinical MRI uses liquid-helium-cooled Nb–Ti superconducting solenoids, the same conductor technology as hadron-collider dipoles. The Tevatron, the first large superconducting synchrotron, helped create the industrial Nb–Ti cable production behind whole-body MRI magnets. LHC-era Nb₃Sn and HTS development now feeds high-field MRI.

registry.name: Symmetry-aware networks for jets and protein structures
registry.summary: Both fields learn from point clouds whose physics has exact symmetries. Jet tagging uses Lorentz-equivariant graph networks, and AlphaFold 2 uses SE(3)-invariant point attention, so each builds the symmetry into the architecture. Diffusion and flow generative models are used both for fast detector simulation and for protein design.

FEL pulses need integrating detectors instead, because every photon arrives within femtoseconds.

registry.name: Silicon trackers are reverse-biased p–n diodes
registry.summary: Silicon strip and pixel trackers are fully depleted p–n junctions read out by CMOS electronics, so tracker design is device physics: depletion voltage, leakage current, and radiation-induced change of effective doping. Monolithic active pixel sensors such as ALICE ITS2 grew out of commercial CMOS image sensors, and LGADs add avalanche gain for timing.

registry.name: Muography images geological interiors with cosmic muons
registry.summary: Cosmic-ray muon detectors built from particle-physics technology (scintillators, emulsions, gaseous chambers) measure how much muons are attenuated through volcanoes, mountains and pyramids. The result is a map of density times path length that complements seismic tomography for near-surface structure.

registry.name: Photon-counting pixel detectors for spectral CT
registry.summary: Hybrid pixel readout chips from the CERN-hosted Medipix collaboration count single X-ray photons against energy thresholds. Used in CT, they give energy-resolved (spectral) images that separate tissues and contrast agents. Medipix-based MARS scanners have imaged humans, and photon-counting CT is now entering clinical use.

registry.name: Scintillators, SiPMs and timing shared by HEP and TOF-PET
registry.summary: A PET scanner is a coincidence-counting particle detector. Dense fast scintillators (LSO/LYSO, studied by CERN's Crystal Clear collaboration), photodetectors from PMTs to SiPMs, and picosecond timing move between the fields in both directions. TOF-PET's ~200 ps coincidence timing informed HEP crystal timing layers such as CMS LYSO+SiPM, and HEP timing R&D now aims at PET.

registry.name: MSW resonance as a Landau–Zener crossing
registry.summary: Solar-neutrino flavour conversion is a two-level avoided crossing swept by the density gradient. Adiabatic MSW conversion is the case where the system stays on one adiabatic surface.

registry.name: Instanton theory of tunnelling reaction rates
registry.summary: Field theory uses a Euclidean saddle point (the instanton or bounce) for theta-vacuum tunnelling and false-vacuum decay. Chemistry uses the same saddle point in semiclassical and ring-polymer instanton rate theory for hydrogen-atom and proton-transfer tunnelling. It explains large kinetic isotope effects and low-temperature interstellar chemistry.
registry.map: k\simeq A\,e^{-S_E[\bar x]/\hbar},\quad S_E=\int d\tau\left[\tfrac12m\dot x^2+V(x)\right]
registry.breaks: Chemical instantons are periodic orbits on a multidimensional nuclear potential surface with no topological charge. Gauge-theory instantons are classified by winding number and act on field configurations.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ring polymers: imaginary-time path integrals for nuclei
registry.summary: Wick rotation turns a quantum particle's partition function into a classical ring polymer of P beads, the same Euclidean discretization that underlies lattice field theory. Path-integral molecular dynamics and ring-polymer rate theories use it to include zero-point energy and tunnelling of light nuclei in reactions.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Coupled cluster: field-theory diagrams in chemistry
registry.summary: Coupled-cluster theory, now quantum chemistry's gold standard as CCSD(T), was brought into chemistry by Čížek using quantum-field-theory tools. These were second quantization, Goldstone/Feynman-type diagrams, and the linked-cluster theorem that guarantees size extensivity. The exponential ansatz itself came from nuclear many-body theory.

registry.name: PET runs on QED pair annihilation
registry.summary: PET imaging uses the QED process e⁺e⁻→γγ: annihilation at rest gives two 511 keV photons almost back-to-back, and the pair's leftover momentum adds a small acollinearity. Positrons often form positronium first. Its para (2γ) and ortho (3γ) states have tissue-dependent lifetimes, which positronium-lifetime imaging is starting to use.

registry.name: Geometric phase at conical intersections as a gauge field
registry.summary: Adiabatically eliminating the electrons leaves the nuclei moving in a Berry connection. Around a conical intersection the electronic wavefunction changes sign, a molecular Aharonov–Bohm flux that changes vibronic spectra and reaction product distributions. Degenerate electronic manifolds give a non-abelian (Wilczek–Zee) connection with the structure of a Yang–Mills potential.
registry.map: \mathbf A_{mn}(\mathbf R)=i\langle m(\mathbf R)|\nabla_{\mathbf R}n(\mathbf R)\rangle,\quad\oint\mathbf A\cdot d\mathbf R=\pi
registry.breaks: The gauge field is emergent and kinematic. It has no Yang–Mills kinetic term or dynamics of its own, its gauge freedom is just the phase choice of the electronic states, and it exists only within the adiabatic approximation.

registry.name: Quantum-computing targets: lattice gauge theories and molecules
registry.summary: On classical computers, lattice QCD at finite density or in real time runs into the fermion sign problem, and strongly correlated molecules run into exponential Hilbert-space growth. Both are therefore flagship quantum-computing applications. They share fermion-to-qubit encodings, Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation, variational eigensolvers and phase estimation.

registry.name: Membrane bending rigidity runs like an asymptotically free coupling
registry.summary: Thermal undulations make a fluid membrane's bending rigidity fall logarithmically with length scale, just as the coupling of the asymptotically free 2D nonlinear sigma model runs. The membrane persistence length plays the role of the dynamically generated mass gap.
registry.breaks: The fluctuations are thermal, not quantum, and early work disputed the prefactor of the logarithm. Lipid bilayers with κ≈10–20 k_BT have astronomically long persistence lengths, so real membranes never reach the crumpled, confinement-like regime.

registry.name: Electron EDM searches in polar molecules
registry.summary: CP violation beyond the Standard Model would give the electron an electric dipole moment. Heavy polar molecules (ThO, HfF⁺, YbF) amplify it with internal effective fields of order 10–100 GV/cm. Precision molecular spin-precession spectroscopy therefore bounds new CP-violating physics at multi-TeV scales and constrains electroweak baryogenesis.

registry.name: Stochastic cooling enabled the W and Z discovery
registry.summary: Van der Meer's stochastic cooling senses a beam's fluctuations with a pickup and corrects them with a kicker. It made dense antiproton beams possible for CERN's SppS collider, where UA1 and UA2 found the W and Z in 1983 and directly confirmed electroweak theory.

registry.name: Parity violation in chiral molecules
registry.summary: Z-boson exchange between electrons and nuclei should give the two mirror-image forms of a chiral molecule slightly different energies. This parity-violating energy difference is predicted to be tiny and has never been measured spectroscopically. Its proposed role in seeding biological homochirality is contested.

registry.name: Born–Oppenheimer picture of quarkonium hybrids
registry.summary: Heavy-quark hybrids and some tetraquarks are treated like diatomic molecules. The slow heavy quark–antiquark pair plays the nuclei and the gluon and light-quark fields play the electrons. Lattice static potentials carry diatomic term symbols (Σ_g⁺, Π_u, …), and the heavy pair vibrates on them (Born–Oppenheimer EFT).
registry.breaks: The scale separation is modest: gluonic excitation gaps are not much larger than charmonium level spacings. The light fields carry colour and confine, and spin and recoil corrections are much larger than in molecules.

registry.name: Mass and decay evaluations drive nucleosynthesis networks
registry.summary: AME masses, NUBASE/ENSDF half-lives, and Maxwellian-averaged (n,γ) cross sections at kT≈30 keV from evaluated libraries feed the s- and r-process reaction networks. Sensitivity studies rank unmeasured masses and half-lives by their effect on abundances, and that ranking steers measurements at radioactive-beam facilities.

registry.name: Reaction theory feeds evaluated cross-section libraries
registry.summary: Evaluated libraries (ENDF/B, JEFF, JENDL) combine measurements with reaction theory, each with covariances: R-matrix and Breit–Wigner fits in the resolved-resonance region, and Hauser–Feshbach compound-nucleus and optical-model calculations elsewhere. The same activation cross sections set isotope-production yields.

registry.name: Fission-product beta decay: delayed neutrons, decay heat
registry.summary: About 0.65% of ²³⁵U fission neutrons are β-delayed, emitted after precursor half-lives of about 0.2–56 s, and they stretch reactor kinetics to controllable timescales. β decay of fission products also supplies about 6–7% of full power as decay heat just after shutdown, and the reactor antineutrino flux.

registry.name: Fission physics sets reactor criticality
registry.summary: Each fission releases about 200 MeV and about 2.4 prompt neutrons. Reactor multiplication is built from fission and absorption cross sections and ν̄. Pairing energy lets odd-N ²³⁵U fission with thermal neutrons, while ²³⁸U needs fast neutrons above a threshold.

registry.name: Neutron moderation and resonance absorption
registry.summary: Reactor physics is applied low-energy neutron reaction theory. Elastic scattering moderates neutrons (mean lethargy gain ξ, equal to 1 for hydrogen), and Breit–Wigner resonances of ²³⁸U set the resonance-escape probability p. Doppler broadening of those resonances gives the prompt negative fuel-temperature coefficient.
sources: Brown et al. (2018). "ENDF/B-VIII.0: The 8th Major Release of the Nuclear Reaction Data Library with CIELO-project Cross Sections, New Standards and Thermal Scattering Data". *Nucl. Data Sheets* 148, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001)

registry.name: Radiative energy loss: QED in matter vs QCD in plasma
registry.summary: Medium-induced gluon bremsstrahlung (BDMPS-Z) is the QCD counterpart of radiative energy loss in matter, and it inherits the LPM coherence suppression first found in QED showers. Collisional loss plays the role of Bethe–Bloch ionization.
registry.breaks: Radiated gluons carry color and rescatter, so ΔE grows as L² instead of L. The medium is an expanding hot plasma rather than a cold absorber, so q̂ depends on temperature and time instead of being a material constant.

registry.name: Gamma-ray arrays map nuclear level schemes
registry.summary: Compton-suppressed HPGe arrays (Gammasphere, and now AGATA and GRETA with γ-ray tracking), with ≈2 keV resolution at 1.33 MeV, resolve high-spin cascades. That resolution is what revealed rotational and superdeformed bands, band crossings and shell evolution, and the arrays are the workhorse instruments of in-beam structure studies.

registry.name: Gluon saturation sets hydrodynamic initial conditions
registry.summary: The color-glass-condensate picture of high-energy nuclei, with a saturation scale Q_s² ∝ A^{1/3}, underlies initial-state models such as IP-Glasma. Their event-by-event geometric fluctuations become the flow harmonics v_n. The EIC will measure nuclear gluon densities and Q_s directly in e–A collisions.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

registry.name: Trace anomaly: nucleon mass and QGP ε−3P
registry.summary: One operator, the QCD energy-momentum trace including the gluon anomaly, gives both the nucleon mass (an EIC target through threshold J/ψ production) and the QGP interaction measure (ε−3P)/T⁴. Lattice QCD finds the interaction measure peaks just above T_c.
registry.breaks: The proton-mass decomposition is scheme-dependent, and how threshold J/ψ data relate to the gluon anomaly term is disputed.
sources: Accardi et al. (2016). "Electron Ion Collider: The Next QCD Frontier". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 52, 268. [arXiv:1212.1701](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1701)

registry.name: g_A links neutron decay to nucleon structure
registry.summary: g_A = G_A(0) ≈ 1.27 is the nucleon axial form factor at zero momentum transfer. It is measured in neutron-decay asymmetries and computed in lattice QCD. The neutron lifetime depends on g_A and on V_ud, which superallowed 0⁺→0⁺ decays fix independently.

registry.name: Nuclear PDFs as the baseline for jet quenching
registry.summary: Hard probes in A–A collisions are computed with collinear factorization. Nuclear PDFs (shadowing, antishadowing, the EMC effect), fixed by p–A and e–A data, remove initial-state effects so that R_AA isolates final-state energy loss in the QGP.

registry.name: EMC effect tracks short-range NN correlations
registry.summary: The EMC effect is the depletion of nuclear valence-quark distributions at 0.3<x<0.7. Its slope scales linearly across nuclei with the density of short-range-correlated pairs (a_2, from x>1 scattering). Those pairs are mostly np because of the tensor force, which suggests that high-momentum nucleons are the ones modified.
registry.breaks: A correlation, not a proven cause: mean-field modification models also fit the data.

registry.name: Heavy-ion flow and mergers constrain dense matter
registry.summary: Directed and elliptic flow in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions constrains the pressure of symmetric nuclear matter at about 2–4.5 n_0. Combined with chiral EFT and astrophysical data, these flow results tighten the neutron-star EOS. Neutron-star mergers reach similar densities and tens-of-MeV temperatures and are modelled with the same relativistic (viscous) hydrodynamics.
registry.breaks: Collisions probe near-symmetric, hot, transient matter. Neutron stars are cold and very isospin-asymmetric, so the link needs the symmetry energy.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Imaging nuclear deformation with collective flow
registry.summary: In ultracentral collisions of deformed nuclei (²³⁸U, ¹²⁹Xe) and isobars (⁹⁶Ru/⁹⁶Zr), v₂ grows with the ground-state quadrupole deformation β₂² and is sensitive to triaxiality γ and neutron skins. Hydrodynamic flow thus becomes a snapshot probe of low-energy collective structure.

registry.name: QCD crossover vs inhomogeneous Big Bang nucleosynthesis
registry.summary: A first-order cosmological QCD transition (~10 μs after the Big Bang) could have left baryon-density inhomogeneities with neutron–proton segregation, and in the 1980s this motivated inhomogeneous BBN. Lattice QCD shows a crossover at T≈155 MeV for small μ_B, and standard homogeneous BBN with the CMB baryon density fits D and ⁴He, so the scenario has lost its motivation.
registry.map: T_c\approx155\,{\rm MeV}\ (t\sim10\,\mu{\rm s})\ \gg\ T_{\rm BBN}\approx0.07\,{\rm MeV}

registry.name: Neutron-star cores probe cold dense QCD
registry.summary: Lattice QCD cannot reach the low-temperature, high-μ_B corner of the QCD phase diagram (quark-matter cores, color superconductivity, quarkyonic matter) because of the sign problem, and heavy-ion collisions cannot reach it either. Neutron-star masses, radii and tidal deformabilities are the only data there, and a sound speed rising above the conformal value is the sought signature.

registry.name: Neutron lifetime sets primordial helium
registry.summary: The weak n↔p rates freeze out near T≈0.8 MeV at n/p≈1/6. Free-neutron decay then lowers n/p to about 1/7 before the deuterium bottleneck breaks (T≈0.07 MeV), which gives Y_p≈0.25. τ_n normalizes all the weak rates, so the ~9 s beam–bottle lifetime discrepancy feeds directly into the predicted Y_p.

registry.name: Beta equilibrium and Urca cooling in neutron stars
registry.summary: Neutron-star matter sits in β equilibrium (μ_n = μ_p + μ_e), which together with the symmetry energy fixes the proton fraction. Above x_p ≈ 11–15%, direct Urca (n→p e ν̄, e p→n ν) becomes kinematically allowed and cools the star fast; below it only the slower modified Urca process operates.

registry.name: Neutron-rich nuclei form the neutron-star crust
registry.summary: The outer crust is a Coulomb lattice of nuclei that become more neutron-rich with depth, from ⁵⁶Fe through N=50 nuclei near ⁷⁸Ni–⁸²Zn to N=82 isotones. Its composition follows from measured and extrapolated masses. The inner crust starts at neutron drip, where S_n→0.
sources: Wang et al. (2021). "The AME 2020 atomic mass evaluation (II). Tables, graphs and references". *Chinese Phys. C* 45, 030003. [doi:10.1088/1674-1137/abddaf](https://doi.org/10.1088/1674-1137/abddaf)

registry.name: Chiral-EFT neutron matter anchors the neutron-star EOS
registry.summary: Chiral NN+3N forces, solved with quantum Monte Carlo, many-body perturbation theory or coupled cluster, give the pure-neutron-matter energy with quantified truncation errors up to about 1–2 n_0. This fixes the symmetry energy S_0 and its slope L and predicts R_1.4 ≈ 11–13 km. Three-nucleon forces dominate the uncertainty, and above about 2 n_0 the EOS is extrapolated.
registry.breaks: Chiral EFT breaks down as momenta approach the breakdown scale (~500–600 MeV), so above ~2n_0 it gives no control.

registry.name: Nuclear pairing and neutron-star superfluidity
registry.summary: The BCS pairing that causes odd–even mass staggering and reduced rotational moments of inertia in nuclei also makes neutron-star matter superfluid: ¹S₀ neutrons in the inner crust and ³P₂ neutrons in the core. The gaps are of order MeV, and the superfluid controls glitches, the specific heat and neutrino cooling.
registry.breaks: Finite nuclei are smaller than the coherence length, so pairing there is a mesoscopic, fluctuating condensate. Whether Cas A's cooling shows ³P₂ pairing onset is contested.

registry.name: Beta-decay half-lives set the r-process clock

registry.name: Fission recycling terminates the r-process

registry.summary: Short-lived nuclei are studied as radioactive beams on light targets. Interaction cross sections revealed the ¹¹Li halo, knockout momentum distributions give the orbital ℓ and spectroscopic factors, and transfer and Coulomb breakup map shell evolution near the drip lines.

registry.name: Fusion–evaporation reactions make superheavy elements
registry.summary: Superheavy elements are made by cold fusion (Pb/Bi targets) or hot fusion (⁴⁸Ca beams on actinide targets). Cross sections of picobarns to femtobarns are the product of capture over the Coulomb barrier, competition from quasifission, and survival against fission while neutrons evaporate from the compound nucleus. registry.name: Alpha-decay chains identify superheavy elements
registry.summary: New superheavy elements are identified by correlated α-decay chains that end at known nuclides. Geiger–Nuttall (Gamow tunnelling) systematics turn measured Q_α into half-lives, and kinks in Q_α along the chains reveal shell gaps on the way to the island of stability.

registry.name: Radiation damage in reactor materials
registry.summary: Fast neutrons create displacement cascades in fuel cladding, steels and graphite; point-defect production, swelling, embrittlement and stored Wigner energy are solid-state physics that limits reactor lifetimes and fusion first walls.
registry.breaks: Displacement counts overestimate surviving defects because of in-cascade recombination, so molecular dynamics is needed.

registry.name: Neutron transmutation doping of silicon
registry.summary: Irradiating float-zone silicon in a reactor turns 30Si into 31P by neutron capture and beta decay, giving the most uniform n-type doping available, used for high-power devices and thyristors.
registry.breaks: Only n-type doping is possible, and the lattice damage has to be annealed.

registry.name: Semiconductor and scintillator radiation detectors
registry.summary: HPGe and Si detectors are reverse-biased p-n junctions whose energy resolution is set by electron-hole pair statistics (about 3 eV per pair, Fano factor ~0.1); scintillators and halide-perovskite detectors depend on excitons, traps and band gaps.
registry.breaks: Detector-grade operation needs ultrapure crystals with long carrier lifetimes and radiation hardness, priorities different from electronic devices.

registry.name: Colour superconductivity in dense quark matter
registry.summary: At high baryon density the attractive colour-antitriplet channel makes the quark Fermi surface unstable to BCS pairing; the colour-flavour-locked phase is a colour superconductor in which gluons acquire Meissner masses and chiral symmetry breaks, a candidate for neutron-star cores.
registry.breaks: The condensate breaks a non-abelian gauge symmetry and is under control only at asymptotic density; at neutron-star densities it is model-dependent and has no direct experimental confirmation.

registry.name: Viscous electron flow and eta/s in metals vs QGP
registry.summary: In ultraclean conductors electron-electron collisions dominate and charge flows hydrodynamically (Gurzhi effect, negative nonlocal resistance), giving measured electron viscosities that can be set against QGP eta/s in the same Navier-Stokes framework.
registry.breaks: Fermi-liquid electrons are weakly coupled with a long l_ee, so their eta/s is far above the QGP value; momentum relaxation at boundaries and impurities has no QGP counterpart.

registry.name: Spin-vorticity: Lambda polarization and Barnett effect
registry.summary: Global Lambda polarization in off-central collisions shows the QGP is the most vortical fluid known; it aligns spins through the same spin-rotation coupling as the Barnett effect and spin hydrodynamic generation in liquid metals.
registry.breaks: QGP polarization is read from the hadronized final state of a ~10 fm/c fluid in local equilibrium; the spintronic versions involve electron spin, spin-orbit coupling and dissipative spin currents.

registry.name: Planckian dissipation: QGP and strange metals
registry.summary: The QGP's eta/s near hbar/(4 pi k_B) and the strange-metal scattering rate hbar/tau of order k_BT are both 'Planckian' transport set by hbar and T alone, and gauge/gravity duality has been applied to both as a model of strongly coupled matter without quasiparticles.
registry.breaks: Strange-metal resistivity needs momentum relaxation by the lattice and disorder, while eta/s is a momentum-conserving diffusivity; the KSS value is not a proven bound, and holographic models are neither QCD nor cuprates.

registry.name: Chiral condensate modelled on the BCS gap (NJL)
registry.summary: Nambu and Jona-Lasinio built dynamical chiral symmetry breaking by direct analogy with BCS: the quark mass gap is a fermion-pair condensate, and its melting at the QCD crossover is the chiral-restoration signature studied in heavy-ion collisions.
registry.breaks: The chiral condensate pairs particles with antiparticles and breaks a global, not a gauge, symmetry, so it gives Goldstone pions instead of a Meissner effect; the QCD transition is a crossover.

registry.name: Chiral anomaly: CME in QGP and Weyl semimetals
registry.summary: The axial anomaly that would drive a current along B in a chirally imbalanced QGP (the chiral magnetic effect) is the same anomaly equation behind the negative longitudinal magnetoresistance of Weyl and Dirac semimetals, where the effect is observed; in heavy-ion collisions the isobar run found no signal beyond background.
registry.breaks: In the QGP the imbalance comes from gluon topological fluctuations and B lasts ~0.1 fm/c; in Weyl metals it is pumped by parallel E and B and relaxed by internode scattering, and lattice Weyl nodes come in pairs (Nielsen-Ninomiya).

registry.name: Band theory of dripped neutrons in the inner crust
registry.summary: Free neutrons in the inner crust move in the periodic potential of the nuclear lattice, so Bloch band structure gives them an effective mass and entrainment by the crust; band calculations find most neutrons entrained, which feeds the glitch angular-momentum budget.

registry.name: Neutron-star crust as a bcc Coulomb crystal
registry.summary: The outer crust is a body-centred-cubic lattice of neutron-rich nuclei in a degenerate relativistic electron gas; its composition follows from minimizing Madelung plus nuclear energies, and inner-crust calculations use the Wigner-Seitz cell method taken from solid-state physics.
registry.breaks: The lattice 'atoms' are bare nuclei in a uniform relativistic electron gas (no chemical bonding), and the inner crust is penetrated by a neutron superfluid.

registry.name: Crust transport: conductivity, impurities and field decay
registry.summary: Crust thermal and electrical conductivities are computed with metal transport theory (electron-phonon and electron-impurity scattering, Wiedemann-Franz); crust cooling after accretion outbursts shows a well-ordered, high-conductivity lattice, while a disordered pasta layer would be highly resistive.
registry.breaks: The electrons are ultra-relativistic and fields reach 1e15 G, so magnetized quantum transport goes beyond terrestrial regimes.
