registry.name: Crust elasticity, phonons and magnetar oscillations
registry.summary: The crust shear modulus and breaking strain come from the lattice dynamics of the Coulomb crystal (molecular dynamics gives a strain of ~0.1, far above terrestrial metals); crust torsional modes are candidates for magnetar-flare QPOs, and crust strength limits the mountains that would radiate gravitational waves.
registry.breaks: Phonons of a Coulomb crystal in a compressible electron background have a plasma-frequency longitudinal branch, unlike the acoustic phonons of ordinary solids; superfluid neutrons add mixed modes.

registry.name: Nuclear pasta as liquid-crystal-like matter
registry.summary: Rod and slab pasta phases have orientational and partial positional order like columnar and smectic liquid crystals, so their elasticity and topological defects (screw dislocations in slabs) are described with liquid-crystal elastic theory; this sets the pasta shear modulus and viscosity.
registry.breaks: Pasta units are nuclear clusters ordered by Coulomb frustration, not anisotropic molecules; there is no molecular director and thermal fluctuations are weak.

registry.name: Nuclear pasta and block-copolymer microphase separation
registry.summary: Pasta phases (spheres, rods, slabs, gyroid-like and inverted) come from competition between nuclear surface tension and long-range Coulomb energy; block-copolymer melts show the same morphology sequence because the Ohta-Kawasaki functional has the same short-range plus Coulomb-kernel structure.
registry.breaks: Pasta is cold, quantum-degenerate matter with shell effects and electron screening; copolymer morphology is set by chain entropy and connectivity at finite temperature, and kinetics and defects differ.

registry.name: Neutron-star superfluids and superconducting protons
registry.summary: The same gap equation predicts 1S0 neutron superfluidity in the crust, 3P2 neutron pairing and type-II proton superconductivity with flux tubes in the core; these set neutron-star cooling (pair-breaking neutrino emission), specific heat and rotational dynamics. Dilute neutron matter is close to the unitary Fermi gas.
registry.breaks: Gaps are not measured directly and depend strongly on medium polarization and three-nucleon forces; the protons sit in a neutron superfluid with entrainment, a coupling absent in metals.

registry.name: Pulsar glitches as vortex pinning and creep
registry.summary: Glitches are explained by quantized neutron-superfluid vortices pinned to crust nuclei that unpin collectively, and post-glitch relaxation by thermally activated vortex creep: the Anderson-Kim flux-creep physics of type-II superconductors, carried to neutron stars by Anderson himself.
registry.breaks: Neutron vortices are neutral (no flux, no Lorentz force); pinning energies and whether the crustal superfluid can store enough angular momentum (the entrainment problem) are disputed.

registry.name: 3P2 neutron superfluid as triplet p-wave pairing
registry.summary: Spin-triplet 3P2 neutron pairing in neutron-star cores has an anisotropic, multicomponent order parameter like superfluid 3He and the p-wave pairing behind topological superconductors, which raises the question of protected surface modes and half-quantum vortices in neutron stars.

registry.name: Collective tunnelling: fission and Josephson junctions
registry.summary: Spontaneous fission and sub-barrier fusion are tunnelling of a collective coordinate coupled to many intrinsic degrees of freedom, the same dissipative macroscopic-tunnelling problem as the phase of a current-biased Josephson junction (Caldeira-Leggett).

registry.summary: Electronic DFT rests on the QMC energy of the uniform electron gas (LDA); nuclear functionals are anchored the same way to ab initio neutron-matter equations of state, which fix the isovector part of Skyrme EDFs and their neutron-skin and radius predictions.
registry.map: E_{xc}^{\rm LDA}=\int n\,\epsilon_{xc}^{\rm HEG}(n)\,d^3r\ \leftrightarrow\ E_{\rm EDF}\ \text{fitted to}\ E_{\rm PNM}(n)/N
registry.breaks: The electron gas is Coulombic and the LDA is a controlled local limit; neutron matter has spin-isospin-dependent and three-body forces with theory uncertainties, and the map to finite nuclei is a fit, not an exact limit.

registry.name: SRG/IMSRG and Wegner flow equations
registry.summary: The similarity renormalization group that softens nuclear forces and the in-medium SRG that decouples nuclear ground states are the continuous unitary flow equations introduced by Wegner and by Glazek and Wilson, which are also used for impurity and lattice models in condensed matter.
registry.breaks: Nuclear SRG must track the induced three- and higher-body forces of a vacuum interaction; CM flows usually start from a fixed lattice Hamiltonian and track induced couplings differently.
sources: Wegner (1994). "Flow-equations for Hamiltonians". *Ann. Phys. (Leipzig)* 506, 77. [doi:10.1002/andp.19945060203](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19945060203)

registry.name: Shared quantum Monte Carlo toolkit and sign problem
registry.summary: GFMC/AFDMC and nuclear lattice EFT (auxiliary-field Monte Carlo after a Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation) are the projector and determinant QMC used for Hubbard models; approximate SU(4) Wigner symmetry suppresses the nuclear sign problem as particle-hole symmetry does at half filling, and neural-network states now enter both.
registry.map: e^{-\tau\frac C2\rho^2}\propto\int ds\,e^{-\frac{s^2}{2C\tau}}e^{-\tau s\rho}\ \Rightarrow\ Z=\int\mathcal Ds\,\det M[s]
registry.breaks: Nuclear Hamiltonians have strong spin-isospin and three-body operators that cannot be written as one-body densities, which forces constrained-path approximations; CM lattice models have a simple on-site U.

registry.name: Nuclear energy density functionals as Kohn-Sham DFT
registry.summary: Skyrme, Gogny and relativistic mean-field calculations are self-consistent Kohn-Sham-like schemes: nucleon orbitals in a potential that is the functional derivative of an energy density functional fitted to data, extended to pairing through HFB (compare DFT for superconductors).
registry.map: h=\frac{\delta E[\rho,\tau,\mathbf J,\tilde\rho]}{\delta\rho},\ h\phi_i=\varepsilon_i\phi_i\ \leftrightarrow\ v_{\rm xc}=\frac{\delta E_{\rm xc}[n]}{\delta n}
registry.breaks: Nuclei are self-bound with no external potential, so Hohenberg-Kohn applies only to intrinsic densities; nuclear EDFs break and then restore symmetries and are fitted phenomenologically rather than derived from a known exact functional.
sources: Bender, Heenen & Reinhard (2003). "Self-consistent mean-field models for nuclear structure". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 121. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.75.121](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.75.121)

registry.name: Particle-vibration coupling vs electron-phonon coupling
registry.summary: Bohr-Mottelson nuclear field theory couples single nucleons to quantized surface 'phonons' just as electrons couple to lattice phonons; the coupling dresses quasiparticles, fragments strength and adds an induced pairing interaction akin to phonon-mediated BCS glue.
registry.map: H_{pv}=\sum_{\lambda\mu}\kappa_\lambda k(r)Y^*_{\lambda\mu}(\hat r)(b^\dagger_{\lambda\mu}+b_{\lambda\mu})\leftrightarrow\sum g_{\mathbf q}(b^\dagger_{\mathbf q}+b_{-\mathbf q})c^\dagger c
registry.breaks: Nuclear phonons are a few discrete collective modes of the same nucleons: no separate lattice, no Debye cutoff and no Migdal small parameter omega/E_F.
sources: Bohr, Mottelson & Pines (1958). "Possible Analogy between the Excitation Spectra of Nuclei and Those of the Superconducting Metallic State". *Phys. Rev.* 110, 936. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.110.936](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.110.936)

registry.name: Giant dipole resonance and cluster surface plasmon
registry.summary: The nuclear giant dipole resonance (protons oscillating against neutrons) and the Mie surface plasmon of metal clusters are both collective dipole modes that exhaust the Thomas-Reiche-Kuhn sum rule, treated with the same RPA and Goldhaber-Teller/Steinwedel-Jensen pictures.
registry.breaks: The GDR restoring force is the isovector symmetry energy, the plasmon's is Coulomb; Landau damping and escape widths differ in size and origin.
sources: Goldhaber & Teller (1948). "On Nuclear Dipole Vibrations". *Phys. Rev.* 74, 1046. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.74.1046](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.74.1046)

registry.name: Pairing in finite Fermi systems: nuclei and nanograins
registry.summary: Nuclei and nanometre Al grains are both mesoscopic superconductors whose level spacing is comparable to the gap; the exactly solvable Richardson pairing model describes both, and the nuclear odd-even mass effect is the parity effect seen in grain spectroscopy and superconducting single-electron transistors.
registry.breaks: Grains have a Coulomb charging energy and an electron bath; nuclei have two particle species, deformation and spin-orbit-split shells, so level statistics and blocking differ.
sources: Richardson (1963). "A restricted class of exact eigenstates of the pairing-force Hamiltonian". *Phys. Lett.* 3, 277. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(63)90259-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(63)90259-2)

registry.name: Shell structure and magic numbers in clusters and dots
registry.summary: Alkali-metal clusters show magic numbers 8, 20, 40, 58 and quantum dots show shell filling with Hund's rule; both are understood with nuclear tools (mean-field shells, Strutinsky shell corrections, Nilsson-type deformation). Quantum dots are 'artificial atoms' and clusters 'electronic nuclei'.
registry.map: E=E_{\rm LD}+\delta E_{\rm shell},\ \delta E=\sum_i\epsilon_i-\tilde E;\ \text{2D HO dot: }2,6,12,20\ \leftrightarrow\ \text{3D HO: }2,8,20,40
registry.breaks: Electron systems lack spin-orbit-driven magic numbers (no 28, 50, 82) and are Coulomb-repulsive and externally confined; nuclei are self-bound with short-range forces.

registry.name: Landau Fermi-liquid theory of nuclei and nuclear matter
registry.summary: Independent-particle shells survive a strong NN force because the relevant objects are Landau quasiparticles near the Fermi surface; Migdal's theory of finite Fermi systems uses Landau parameters (effective mass, spin-isospin g') as electron Fermi-liquid theory does, and giant resonances are its zero-sound-like modes.
registry.breaks: Nuclei are finite and self-bound with two species and a strong tensor force; quasiparticle lifetimes are short away from the Fermi surface and strength fragmentation is large.
sources: Shankar (1994). "Renormalization-group approach to interacting fermions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 66, 129. [arXiv:cond-mat/9307009](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9307009)

registry.name: Shape phase transitions as finite-size quantum criticality
registry.summary: Along isotopic chains nuclei change from spherical to deformed as the control parameter N varies; Landau theory in quadrupole collective coordinates and the critical-point symmetries E(5)/X(5) treat this as a quantum phase transition with finite-N precursors.
registry.breaks: Nuclei never reach a thermodynamic limit, N is discrete, and there is no spatial correlation length, quantum critical fan or non-Fermi-liquid transport.
sources: Cejnar, Jolie & Casten (2010). "Quantum phase transitions in the shapes of atomic nuclei". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 2155. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.82.2155](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.82.2155)

registry.name: Nuclear pairing is BCS pairing
registry.summary: Odd-even mass staggering, the gap in even-even spectra and reduced moments of inertia follow from the BCS gap equation with a short-range NN attraction near the nuclear Fermi surface; Bohr, Mottelson and Pines carried BCS over to nuclei within a year.
registry.breaks: Nuclei hold only ~10 pairs, so BCS particle-number fluctuations matter (projection needed) and the coherence length exceeds the nucleus; the pairing glue is the bare nuclear force, not a retarded phonon.
sources: Bohr, Mottelson & Pines (1958). "Possible Analogy between the Excitation Spectra of Nuclei and Those of the Superconducting Metallic State". *Phys. Rev.* 110, 936. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.110.936](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.110.936)

registry.name: Rotation vs magnetic field: backbending and Meissner
registry.summary: The Coriolis force on a rotating nucleus acts on time-reversed pairs as a magnetic field acts on Cooper pairs; pairing quenches the moment of inertia below the rigid value (like Meissner screening), and backbending at high spin is the analogue of the critical field that destroys superconductivity.
registry.map: H'=H-\omega J_x\leftrightarrow H-\mu_B\mathbf B\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma;\ \mathcal I<\mathcal I_{\rm rigid}\leftrightarrow\chi<0;\ \omega_c\leftrightarrow H_c
registry.breaks: The cranking 'field' couples to the orbital angular momentum of a finite drop, not to a gauge field; there is no flux expulsion, London length or vortex phase, and the transition is smeared by finite size.
sources: Mottelson & Valatin (1960). "Effect of Nuclear Rotation on the Pairing Correlation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 5, 511. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.5.511](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.5.511)

registry.name: Evaluated reaction-rate libraries for stellar models
registry.summary: Stellar evolution and explosion codes use evaluated thermonuclear rate compilations (REACLIB, NACRE) built from nuclear data and Hauser-Feshbach theory, so evaluation and covariance methods from nuclear data propagate into stellar predictions.
registry.breaks: Many network rates are theoretical; uncertainties are correlated and often lack covariance information.

registry.name: Low-background radiation detectors for dark matter
registry.summary: Dark-matter direct detection uses nuclear-physics detector technology (scintillators, HPGe, noble-liquid ionization) and radiation-protection-grade background control; nuclear-recoil quenching and gamma/neutron backgrounds are nuclear-physics problems.

registry.name: Nuclear radiation detectors as gamma-ray telescopes
registry.summary: MeV gamma-ray astronomy (nuclear lines, GRBs) uses nuclear-spectroscopy detectors: NaI and BGO scintillators, HPGe spectrometers (INTEGRAL/SPI) and Compton telescopes, with the same photoelectric/Compton/pair physics and activation backgrounds.
registry.breaks: Space instruments face cosmic-ray activation and must reject a large instrumental background.

registry.name: PDFs set ultra-high-energy neutrino cross sections
registry.summary: The neutrino-nucleon cross section above ~10 TeV is deep-inelastic scattering dominated by small-x sea quarks and gluons; IceCube's Earth-absorption measurement agrees with PDF-based predictions, and small-x uncertainty (and saturation) sets the high-energy event rate.
registry.breaks: At the highest energies the relevant x lies below HERA's reach, so predictions extrapolate DGLAP or invoke saturation.

registry.name: QGP epoch of the early universe
registry.summary: The universe was a quark-gluon plasma until ~10 microseconds, when it cooled through the QCD crossover at T_c ~ 156 MeV; heavy-ion collisions recreate that matter, and the lattice equation of state measured there fixes the early-universe expansion rate through that epoch.
registry.breaks: Heavy-ion fireballs have mu_B > 0 at lower energies, are tiny and expand in ~10 fm/c, and are not in global equilibrium; the cosmic transition is at mu_B ~ 0 and expands over microseconds.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)

registry.name: Antinuclei: coalescence and absorption for dark matter
registry.summary: Antideuterons and antihelium in cosmic rays would be a near background-free dark-matter signature; coalescence parameters measured in heavy-ion and pp collisions and ALICE's antihelium absorption cross sections set both the expected signal and the cosmic-ray background.
registry.breaks: Coalescence depends on source size, which differs between Galactic dark-matter annihilation and collider systems.

registry.name: Quark-matter cores in massive neutron stars
registry.summary: Model-agnostic EOS inference combining perturbative QCD at high density with nuclear EFT at low density finds the speed of sound and polytropic index in the cores of ~2-solar-mass stars consistent with deconfined quark matter.
registry.breaks: The criterion is a heuristic; hadronic matter with a peaked sound speed can mimic it, so the claim is contested.

registry.summary: The lattice QCD equation of state and susceptibilities, tested against heavy-ion data, give the effective degrees of freedom g_*(T) and g_*s(T) through the QCD crossover, which enter relic-abundance and axion-density calculations.
registry.breaks: Cosmic use needs mu_B ~ 0 and full equilibrium, where lattice QCD is reliable; heavy-ion data mainly validate it.

registry.summary: Air showers contain more muons than hadronic models predict; strangeness enhancement and core-corona collectivity seen in high-multiplicity LHC collisions, implemented in models such as EPOS, are candidate explanations, linking QGP signatures to cosmic-ray composition.

registry.name: Tidal deformability from GW170817 constrains the EOS
registry.summary: The GW170817 inspiral phase measured the binary tidal deformability, limiting neutron-star radii to ~11-13 km and excluding the stiffest nuclear EOS; joint analyses with NICER and nuclear data now bound pressure at twice saturation density.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2018). "GW170817: Measurements of neutron star radii and equation of state". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 161101. [arXiv:1805.11581](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11581)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dense-matter EOS sets neutron-star masses and radii
registry.summary: The TOV equation turns the nuclear EOS into a mass-radius curve; 2-solar-mass pulsars, NICER radii and GW tidal deformabilities constrain matter up to several times saturation density.
sources: Demorest et al. (2010). "A two-solar-mass neutron star measured using Shapiro delay". *Nature* 467, 1081. [doi:10.1038/nature09466](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09466)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2018). "GW170817: Measurements of neutron star radii and equation of state". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 161101. [arXiv:1805.11581](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11581)

registry.name: EOS in core collapse and proto-neutron stars
registry.summary: Core bounce, proto-neutron-star contraction, neutrino-driven explosion and black-hole formation depend on the finite-temperature nuclear EOS (stiffness, symmetry energy, nuclear statistical equilibrium composition).
registry.breaks: Supernova EOS tables need finite temperature and proton fraction 0.05-0.5, beyond the cold beta-equilibrium EOS of neutron stars.
sources: Janka et al. (2007). "Theory of core-collapse supernovae". *Phys. Rep.* 442, 38. [arXiv:astro-ph/0612072](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0612072)

registry.name: Nucleosynthesis yields drive galactic chemical evolution
registry.summary: Galaxy-formation simulations and chemical-evolution models use stellar and explosive yields (alpha elements from core collapse, Fe from Ia, s from AGB, r from mergers) as inputs; alpha/Fe ratios then clock star-formation histories.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

registry.name: Galactic archaeology of r-process-enhanced stars
registry.summary: Europium-rich metal-poor halo stars, the actinide-boost class and the single-event enrichment of the dwarf galaxy Reticulum II test which sites (rare, prolific mergers or collapsars) made the Milky Way's r-process elements and when.
registry.breaks: Merger delay times and natal kicks complicate the link between abundance trends and sites.
sources: Ji et al. (2016). "R-process enrichment from a single event in an ancient dwarf galaxy". *Nature* 531, 610. [arXiv:1512.01558](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01558)

Arnould, Goriely & Takahashi (2007). "The r-process of stellar nucleosynthesis: Astrophysics and nuclear physics achievements and mysteries". *Phys. Rep.* 450, 97. [arXiv:0705.4512](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4512)

registry.name: Magnetar giant flares as r-process sites
registry.summary: Delayed MeV gamma-ray emission after the 2004 SGR 1806-20 giant flare matches radioactive decay of freshly synthesized r-process nuclei in baryon-loaded ejecta, suggesting magnetars contribute a few percent of the r-process.
registry.breaks: Single-event evidence; the ejecta mass and Y_e are inferred from models.
sources: Patel et al. (2025). "Direct Evidence for r-process Nucleosynthesis in Delayed MeV Emission from the SGR 1806–20 Magnetar Giant Flare". *Astrophys. J. Lett.*. [arXiv:2501.09181](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09181)

registry.name: Collapsars as r-process sites
registry.summary: Neutron-rich accretion-disk outflows in collapsars (the engines of long GRBs) may make r-process material comparable to mergers, which would explain early-galaxy enrichment; near-infrared follow-up of long GRBs is testing this.
registry.breaks: Disk-outflow Y_e depends on neutrino transport and magnetic physics that simulations do not yet agree on.
sources: Siegel, Barnes & Metzger (2019). "Collapsars as a major source of r-process elements". *Nature* 569, 241. [arXiv:1810.00098](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.00098)

registry.name: Kilonova AT2017gfo and r-process nucleosynthesis
registry.summary: The optical-infrared kilonova after GW170817 was powered by radioactive decay of freshly made r-process nuclei, and its red component showed lanthanide-rich ejecta, the first direct identification of an r-process site.
registry.map: \kappa_{\rm lanth}\sim10\ \text{cm}^2\text{g}^{-1}\gg\kappa_{\rm Fe};\ t_{\rm peak}\approx\sqrt{\frac{\kappa M}{4\pi vc}}

registry.name: s-process in AGB stars and barium/CEMP binaries
registry.summary: Barium stars and carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP-s) stars got their s-process overabundances by mass transfer from an AGB companion, so binary populations map the s-process yields and neutron exposures of extinct AGB stars.
sources: Escorza et al. (2026). "Stellar nucleosynthesis in the era of large surveys: S-process polluted binaries in GALAH DR4". *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2604.15197](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15197)

registry.name: Stellar evolution drives s-process and burning stages
registry.summary: Burning stages (H, He, C, Ne, O, Si) follow core contraction; thermal pulses in AGB stars release neutrons via 13C(alpha,n) and 22Ne(alpha,n) for the s-process, and the triple-alpha rate through the Hoyle state sets the C/O ratio.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

registry.name: Supernovae as nucleosynthesis sites
registry.summary: Core-collapse supernovae make the alpha elements and iron-peak nuclei through explosive burning and the nu-p and weak r-process; thermonuclear (Ia) supernovae make most of the iron. Ordinary core-collapse ejecta fail to reach the third r-process peak.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

registry.name: Urca processes and neutrino cooling of compact stars
registry.summary: Neutron stars cool by direct and modified Urca beta processes whose rates depend on the proton fraction and pairing; accreting crusts hold Urca shells, and electron capture onto nuclei sets white-dwarf and crust compositions.
registry.map: n\to pe\bar\nu_e,\ pe\to n\nu_e;\ \text{direct Urca if }x_p\gtrsim0.11;\ \epsilon_{\rm dU}\propto T^6,\ \epsilon_{\rm mU}\propto T^8
registry.breaks: The proton fraction and pairing gaps in the core are uncertain, so cooling curves constrain them only jointly.
sources: Langanke & Martínez-Pinedo (2003). "Nuclear weak-interaction processes in stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 819. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203071](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203071)

registry.name: Electron capture and weak rates in core collapse
registry.summary: Electron captures on iron-group and neutron-rich nuclei (Gamow-Teller strength from the shell model) deleptonize the collapsing core and set the homologous-core mass, shock energy and neutrino signal of core-collapse supernovae.
registry.breaks: Gamow-Teller strength of hot, neutron-rich nuclei far from stability is only partly measured; tables extrapolate shell-model and QRPA results.
sources: Langanke & Martínez-Pinedo (2003). "Nuclear weak-interaction processes in stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 819. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203071](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203071)

registry.name: Deuterium burning separates brown dwarfs from planets
registry.summary: The deuterium-burning mass limit (~13 Jupiter masses) is the conventional boundary between giant planets and brown dwarfs; it is set by when the core reaches the D(p,gamma)3He Gamow window before electron degeneracy halts contraction.
registry.breaks: The limit depends on helium and deuterium fraction and metallicity; formation mode, not burning, may be the better planet criterion.
sources: Spiegel, Burrows & Milsom (2011). "The Deuterium-burning Mass Limit for Brown Dwarfs and Giant Planets". *Astrophys. J.* 727, 57. [arXiv:1008.5150](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.5150)

registry.name: Gamow-peak fusion sets stellar structure
registry.summary: Stellar energy generation is set by sub-barrier fusion at the Gamow peak; the steep temperature dependence of the CNO cycle versus pp chain decides convective cores and the main-sequence mass-luminosity relation.
sources: Bethe (1939). "Energy Production in Stars". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 434. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.434](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.434)
Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)

registry.name: Carbon fusion rate and thermonuclear ignition
registry.summary: Carbon ignition in white dwarfs (Type Ia supernovae), carbon flashes and X-ray superbursts depend on the low-energy 12C+12C fusion rate, whose resonant structure below 2 MeV remains uncertain.
registry.breaks: Laboratory data stop above the Gamow window, and electron screening in dense plasmas modifies the rate.
sources: Tan et al. (2024). "Coincident measurement of the C12+C12 fusion cross section via the differential thick-target technique". *Phys. Rev. C* 110, 035808. [doi:10.1103/physrevc.110.035808](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevc.110.035808)

registry.name: Solar neutrinos measure pp-chain and CNO burning
registry.summary: Neutrino fluxes from the pp chain (pp, 7Be, 8B) and the first detection of CNO neutrinos test laboratory fusion cross sections in the solar core; the CNO flux bears on the solar metallicity (abundance) problem raised by helioseismology.
registry.breaks: Interpreting fluxes needs neutrino oscillation (MSW) parameters and the solar model's opacities.
sources: Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)
Borexino Collaboration (2020). "Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun". *Nature* 587, 577. [arXiv:2006.15115](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15115)

registry.name: Fission yields shape r-process patterns and kilonovae
registry.summary: Fission of the heaviest r-process nuclei recycles material to the second peak, shapes the rare-earth abundances and, through 254Cf, can dominate late-time kilonova heating; fission barriers and yields far from stability are a major r-process uncertainty.
registry.breaks: Barriers and fragment yields of neutron-rich actinides come from models without measurements.
sources: Zhu et al. (2018). "Californium-254 and Kilonova Light Curves". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 863, L23. [arXiv:1806.09724](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.09724)

registry.name: Coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering and the neutrino fog
registry.summary: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, observed by COHERENT, gives nuclear recoils indistinguishable from WIMP signals; solar 8B and atmospheric neutrinos thus form the neutrino fog of direct detection, with rates set by the weak charge and neutron form factor.
registry.breaks: The neutrino background is irreducible only for the same recoil spectrum; directionality and target complementarity partly separate it.
sources: COHERENT Collaboration (2017). "Observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering". *Science* 357, 1123. [arXiv:1708.01294](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.01294)

registry.name: Cosmic-ray spallation and Li-Be-B production
registry.summary: Spallation of cosmic-ray C, N, O on interstellar H and He makes Li, Be and B; secondary-to-primary ratios such as B/C measure the grammage traversed and calibrate Galactic propagation, so they rest on nuclear fragmentation cross sections.
registry.breaks: Fragmentation cross sections are known to only 10-20 percent, which now limits AMS-02 propagation analyses.

registry.name: Radioactive heating of kilonova ejecta
registry.summary: Kilonovae are powered by the summed beta decays and fission of thousands of r-process nuclei, giving a heating rate close to t^-1.3; the luminosity therefore measures ejected r-process mass.
registry.breaks: Thermalization efficiency and the uncertain beta-decay rates and masses of neutron-rich nuclei limit the mass inference to a factor of a few.
sources: Metzger et al. (2010). "Electromagnetic Counterparts of Compact Object Mergers Powered by the Radioactive Decay of R-process Nuclei". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 406, 2650. [arXiv:1001.5029](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.5029)
Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [doi:10.1038/nature24453](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24453)

registry.name: 26Al heating and chronometry of the early Solar System
registry.summary: Excess 26Mg in meteoritic inclusions shows live 26Al (t1/2 = 0.72 Myr) was present when the first solids formed; its decay heat melted and differentiated planetesimals, and short-lived radionuclides give Myr-resolution chronologies of disk evolution.
registry.breaks: Dating assumes 26Al was homogeneously distributed in the disk, which is debated.
sources: Lee, Papanastassiou & Wasserburg (1976). "Demonstration of 26Mg excess in Allende and evidence for 26Al". *Geophys. Res. Lett.* 3, 41. [doi:10.1029/GL003i001p00041](https://doi.org/10.1029/GL003i001p00041)

registry.name: Radioactive 56Ni-56Co decay powers supernova light curves
registry.summary: Type Ia and stripped-envelope supernova light curves are powered by 56Ni -> 56Co -> 56Fe decay (6.1 d and 77 d), so the peak luminosity measures the nickel mass (Arnett's rule) and the tail follows the cobalt half-life; 44Ti maps in Cas A trace explosion asymmetry.
registry.map: ^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\xrightarrow{6.1\,\rm d}{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\xrightarrow{77\,\rm d}{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe};\ L_{\rm peak}\approx\dot E_{\rm Ni}(t_{\rm peak});\ L_{\rm tail}\propto e^{-t/111\,\rm d}
registry.breaks: Gamma-ray escape and positron trapping make the deposited luminosity differ from the decay luminosity at late times.
sources: Grefenstette et al. (2014). "Asymmetries in core-collapse supernovae from maps of radioactive 44Ti in CassiopeiaA". *Nature* 506, 339. [arXiv:1403.4978](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.4978)

registry.name: Nuclear masses fix the outer-crust composition
registry.summary: The outer-crust sequence of nuclei (56Fe, 62Ni, ..., 78Ni, 82Zn and beyond toward the drip line) follows from measured and extrapolated masses of neutron-rich nuclei; Penning-trap mass measurements at radioactive-beam facilities move the predicted layers.
registry.breaks: The deeper outer crust needs masses beyond experimental reach, so model mass tables take over.
sources: Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

registry.name: Nuclear structure factors for WIMP-nucleus scattering
registry.summary: Spin-independent and spin-dependent dark-matter rates need nuclear form factors and structure functions computed with the shell model and chiral-EFT currents; the nonrelativistic EFT of direct detection maps each operator onto distinct nuclear responses.
registry.breaks: Two-body currents and nuclear-structure uncertainties grow at large momentum transfer and for odd-unpaired nuclei.
sources: Fitzpatrick et al. (2013). "The Effective Field Theory of Dark Matter Direct Detection". *J. Cosmol. Astropart. Phys.* 02, 004. [arXiv:1203.3542](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3542)

Klos et al. (2013). "Large-scale nuclear structure calculations for spin-dependent WIMP scattering with chiral effective field theory currents". *Phys. Rev. D* 88, 083516. [arXiv:1304.7684](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7684)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Giant-dipole photodisintegration of UHE cosmic-ray nuclei
registry.summary: Ultra-high-energy nuclei are destroyed by photodisintegration when CMB and infrared photons, boosted into the nucleus frame, hit the giant dipole resonance; this shapes the composition and cutoff of the UHECR spectrum alongside the GZK pion threshold for protons.
registry.breaks: Photonuclear cross sections for unstable intermediate nuclei are model-based, and source composition is degenerate with propagation.
sources: Puget, Stecker & Bredekamp (1976). "Photonuclear interactions of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays and their astrophysical consequences". *Astrophys. J.* 205, 638. [doi:10.1086/154321](https://doi.org/10.1086/154321)

registry.name: Fusion and fission share neutronics, blankets and materials
registry.summary: Burning-plasma devices inherit fission-reactor neutron transport, shielding, activation and materials-damage methods and data; fusion's 14 MeV neutrons cause higher displacement and transmutation (helium) damage per neutron than fission spectra.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fusion neutron spectroscopy as plasma diagnostic
registry.summary: Neutron time-of-flight and activation detectors measure ICF and tokamak yields; the Doppler width of the 14.1 MeV neutron line gives the ion temperature and down-scattered neutrons give the fuel areal density.
registry.breaks: Bulk flow and anisotropic motion broaden the line too, so apparent ion temperatures can exceed thermal ones.
sources: Brysk (1973). "Fusion neutron energies and spectra". *Plasma Phys.* 15, 611. [doi:10.1088/0032-1028/15/7/001](https://doi.org/10.1088/0032-1028/15/7/001)

registry.name: Radiation dosimetry in space weather
registry.summary: Solar energetic particle events and trapped radiation are quantified with nuclear dosimetry quantities (absorbed dose, quality factors, LET spectra) to protect astronauts and electronics; detectors aboard spacecraft are nuclear-physics instruments.
registry.breaks: Space fields are mixed and highly variable, and heavy ions dominate biological dose despite small fluences.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Relativistic MHD of QGP in strong magnetic fields
registry.summary: Off-central heavy-ion collisions create fields eB ~ m_pi^2 (about 1e18 G); relativistic MHD codes developed for astrophysical plasmas model how the conducting QGP responds, affecting directed flow and charge-dependent observables.
registry.breaks: The QGP's electrical conductivity is low (sigma ~ 0.01 fm^-1), so the magnetic Reynolds number is small and ideal-MHD flux freezing does not apply.
sources: Inghirami et al. (2016). "Numerical magneto-hydrodynamics for relativistic nuclear collisions". *Eur. Phys. J. C* 76, 659. [arXiv:1609.03042](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03042)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Parton energy loss and heavy-quark diffusion as kinetics
registry.summary: Collisional energy loss of fast partons and heavy-quark diffusion are treated with Fokker-Planck and Langevin equations for a test particle in a plasma, as for fast ions slowing in fusion plasmas; q-hat is the transverse momentum diffusion coefficient.
registry.breaks: Radiative (BDMPS) loss dominates for light partons and has coherence effects with no classical-plasma analogue.
sources: Moore & Teaney (2005). "How much do heavy quarks thermalize in a heavy ion collision?". *Phys. Rev. C* 71, 064904. [arXiv:hep-ph/0412346](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0412346)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: QGP as a colour plasma
registry.summary: Above T_c the QGP screens colour charge and supports collective plasma oscillations like an electromagnetic plasma, with a Debye mass m_D ~ gT and plasma frequency ~ gT/3; this plasma language organizes its thermodynamics and transport.
registry.breaks: Gluons carry colour and self-interact (non-abelian), the coupling near T_c is strong rather than weak, magnetic screening is non-perturbative, and the plasma confines into hadrons below T_c.
sources: Blaizot & Iancu (2002). "The quark-gluon plasma: collective dynamics and hard thermal loops". *Phys. Rep.* 359, 355. [arXiv:hep-ph/0101103](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0101103)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Colour Debye screening melts quarkonia
registry.summary: Debye screening of the heavy-quark potential in the QGP dissolves J/psi and Upsilon states once the screening length falls below their radius, giving sequential suppression ordered by binding energy.
registry.breaks: Quarkonia also acquire imaginary potential (Landau damping width) and regenerate by recombination at the LHC, so suppression is not pure static screening.
sources: Matsui & Satz (1986). "J/ψ suppression by quark-gluon plasma formation". *Phys. Lett. B* 178, 416. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Strongly coupled QGP and strongly coupled plasmas
registry.summary: RHIC's 'perfect liquid' was interpreted as a strongly coupled plasma with Coulomb-like coupling Gamma of order 1-3, borrowing classical strongly coupled plasma phenomenology (liquid-like correlations, low viscosity at intermediate Gamma).
registry.breaks: QGP coupling is quantum and relativistic with colour degrees of freedom; Gamma is not a sharp control parameter, and QGP minimal viscosity has a quantum origin (eta/s ~ hbar/4pi).
sources: Shuryak (2005). "What RHIC experiments and theory tell us about properties of quark-gluon plasma?". *Nucl. Phys. A* 750, 64. [arXiv:hep-ph/0405066](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0405066)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hard thermal loops: non-abelian Vlasov and Landau damping
registry.summary: Hard-thermal-loop effective theory of the QGP is equivalent to colour Vlasov equations for hard particles in soft gauge fields; it gives Debye screening, Landau damping of gluon modes and plasmon dispersion exactly parallel to Vlasov-Maxwell plasma theory.
registry.map: v\cdot\partial_x\,\delta n^a+g\,\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf E^a\frac{dn_0}{dp}=0\ \leftrightarrow\ \partial_tf+\mathbf v\cdot\nabla f+\frac{q}{m}\mathbf E\cdot\nabla_vf=0
registry.breaks: Gauge covariance requires adjoint colour transport and non-abelian field strengths; the theory holds only at weak coupling g << 1, far from RHIC/LHC conditions.
sources: Blaizot & Iancu (2002). "The quark-gluon plasma: collective dynamics and hard thermal loops". *Phys. Rep.* 359, 355. [arXiv:hep-ph/0101103](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0101103)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Weibel-type plasma instabilities in QGP thermalization
registry.summary: Momentum-space anisotropy of the early glasma drives chromo-Weibel instabilities, the non-abelian counterpart of filamentation in anisotropic electromagnetic plasmas, which accelerate isotropization in bottom-up thermalization.
registry.breaks: Non-abelian self-interaction saturates growth differently than in QED plasmas, and the role of instabilities versus scattering in thermalization is debated.
sources: Arnold, Lenaghan & Moore (2003). "QCD plasma instabilities and bottom-up thermalization". *J. High Energy Phys.* 08, 002. [arXiv:hep-ph/0307325](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0307325)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Neutron-star crust as a one-component plasma
registry.summary: The crust ions in a degenerate electron sea are a classical one-component (Yukawa-screened) plasma; it crystallizes at Gamma ~ 175, the same phase diagram in (Gamma, kappa) as dusty-plasma crystals and ultracold neutral plasmas.
registry.breaks: Crust ions sit in a relativistic degenerate electron gas at 1e6-1e14 g/cc and may be quantum (ion plasma temperature) at the deepest layers; dusty plasmas are dissipative and charge-fluctuating.
sources: Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

registry.name: D-T fusion as the energy source of magnetic confinement
registry.summary: Magnetic confinement fusion exists to run nuclear fusion reactions; the D-T cross section, its 3.5 MeV alpha and 14.1 MeV neutron set plasma heating, wall loading and the fuel cycle of tokamaks and stellarators.
registry.map: \mathrm D+\mathrm T\to\alpha(3.5\,\text{MeV})+n(14.1\,\text{MeV});\ P_{\rm fus}=n_Dn_T\langle\sigma v\rangle E_{\rm fus}

registry.name: Ionization-dependent beta decay in stellar plasmas
registry.summary: In hot plasmas nuclei are highly ionized, which opens bound-state beta decay and closes electron capture from atomic orbitals; fully ionized 187Re decays about 1e9 times faster, changing the Re-Os cosmochronometer and s-process branchings.
registry.breaks: Rates depend on plasma ionization balance and continuum electron density, so they need plasma models in addition to nuclear matrix elements.

registry.name: Albedo neutron decay feeds the inner radiation belt
registry.summary: Cosmic rays striking the atmosphere make albedo neutrons, and those that beta-decay inside the magnetosphere leave trapped protons (CRAND), the main source of high-energy protons in Earth's inner radiation belt; the free-neutron lifetime sets the injection rate.
registry.breaks: Radial diffusion and losses, not the source term alone, set belt intensities.
sources: Singer (1958). "Trapped Albedo Theory of the Radiation Belt". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 1, 181. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.1.181](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.1.181)

registry.name: Nuclear reaction rates measured in laser-driven plasmas
registry.summary: Inertial-fusion implosions reach stellar-core temperatures and densities, letting reactions such as T+T and 3He+3He be measured in a thermal plasma environment with plasma screening, complementing accelerator beam-target data.
registry.map: Y=\int n_1n_2\langle\sigma v\rangle(T_i)\,dV\,dt;\ \text{infer }S(E_0)\text{ at Gamow peak}
registry.breaks: Implosion temperatures and densities vary in space and time, so extracting a reactivity requires hydrodynamic modelling.
sources: Casey et al. (2017). "Thermonuclear reactions probed at stellar-core conditions with laser-based inertial-confinement fusion". *Nature Phys.* 13, 1227. [doi:10.1038/nphys4220](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys4220)

registry.name: Fusion yield, alpha heating and ignition in ICF
registry.summary: Inertial fusion needs a hot-spot areal density large enough to stop the 3.5 MeV alphas so that self-heating outruns losses; NIF's 2022 shot exceeded unity target gain. The D-T reactivity and alpha stopping power set the ignition condition.
registry.map: \rho R_{\rm hs}\gtrsim0.3\ \text{g cm}^{-2},\ T_{\rm hs}\gtrsim5\ \text{keV};\ f_{\rm burn}\approx\frac{\rho R}{\rho R+6\ \text{g cm}^{-2}}
registry.breaks: ICF yields are also limited by hydrodynamic instabilities and mix, which are not nuclear physics.
sources: Abu-Shawareb et al. (2024). "Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 065102. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.065102](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.065102)
Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)

registry.name: Fuel cycles: D-T versus D-D, D-3He and p-11B
registry.summary: Choice of fusion fuel trades reactivity against neutron production: D-T ignites at the lowest temperature but makes 80 percent of its energy as neutrons, while D-3He and p-11B are nearly aneutronic but need ~5-10 times higher temperatures where bremsstrahlung losses compete.
registry.map: P_{\rm br}\propto Z_{\rm eff}n_e^2T^{1/2}\ \text{vs}\ P_{\rm fus}\propto n^2\langle\sigma v\rangle;\ \langle\sigma v\rangle_{\rm DT}/\langle\sigma v\rangle_{\rm DD}\sim100
sources: Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)

registry.name: Alpha self-heating and the Lawson criterion
registry.summary: A burning plasma is one in which fusion alphas supply most of the heating; the Lawson/ignition criterion follows from balancing alpha power (from the D-T reactivity) against transport and radiation losses, and alpha populations drive Alfvén eigenmodes.
registry.map: \tfrac14n^2\langle\sigma v\rangle E_\alpha\geq\frac{3nk_BT}{\tau_E}+P_{\rm rad};\ Q=\frac{P_{\rm fus}}{P_{\rm heat}}\to\infty\ \text{(ignition)}
sources: Lawson (1957). "Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor". *Proc. Phys. Soc. B* 70, 6. [doi:10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303](https://doi.org/10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303)

registry.name: Spin-polarized fusion fuel
registry.summary: Aligning D and T nuclear spins raises the D-T cross section by up to 50 percent because the reaction proceeds through the 3/2+ 5He resonance; whether polarization survives plasma depolarization processes is the open question.
registry.breaks: Wall recycling, collisions and magnetic-field inhomogeneity can depolarize fuel; no reactor-scale test exists.
sources: Kulsrud et al. (1982). "Fusion Reactor Plasmas with Polarized Nuclei". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 1248. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1248](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1248)

registry.name: D-T reactivity sets the tokamak operating point
registry.summary: The D-T reactivity peaks near 60-70 keV, but the triple product n T tau_E is minimized near 14 keV, which sets the ion temperature tokamaks aim for and the confinement time they must reach at the beta limit.
registry.map: n\tau_E>\frac{12k_BT}{\langle\sigma v\rangle E_\alpha};\ nT\tau_E\gtrsim3\times10^{21}\ \text{keV s m}^{-3}\ \text{at}\ T\approx14\ \text{keV}
sources: Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)
Lawson (1957). "Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor". *Proc. Phys. Soc. B* 70, 6. [doi:10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303](https://doi.org/10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303)

registry.name: Electron screening of fusion rates in plasmas
registry.summary: Debye screening of the Coulomb barrier by plasma electrons and ions raises stellar fusion rates (Salpeter weak-screening factor); laboratory screening enhancements at low energy exceed the adiabatic prediction, a long-standing puzzle.
registry.breaks: The weak-screening formula fails at strong coupling and in dynamic regimes; lab screening potentials U_e exceed theory by roughly a factor of two.
sources: Salpeter (1954). "Electron Screening and Thermonuclear Reactions". *Aust. J. Phys.* 7, 373. [doi:10.1071/PH540373](https://doi.org/10.1071/PH540373)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Pycnonuclear fusion in strongly coupled plasmas
registry.summary: In white-dwarf interiors and accreted neutron-star crusts (Gamma >> 1) fusion proceeds by zero-point tunnelling between neighbouring lattice ions; the enhancement factors are computed with one-component-plasma Monte Carlo free energies.
registry.breaks: Pycnonuclear rates are uncertain by orders of magnitude because of lattice dynamics, impurities and quantum effects.
sources: Ichimaru (1993). "Nuclear fusion in dense plasmas". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 65, 255. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.65.255](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.65.255)

registry.name: Laser-plasma ion and neutron sources for nuclear physics
registry.summary: Intense laser-plasma interactions accelerate MeV ions and produce bremsstrahlung and neutron bursts that drive nuclear reactions, isotope production and photonuclear experiments with ultrashort, ultradense pulses.
registry.map: E_{\max}^{\rm TNSA}\sim2T_{\rm hot}\ln^2(\cdots),\ T_{\rm hot}\approx m_ec^2(\sqrt{1+a_0^2/2}-1)
registry.breaks: Laser-driven beams have broad spectra and low repetition rates compared with accelerators.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Tritium breeding and neutron transport in blankets
registry.summary: A D-T power plant must breed its tritium from lithium blankets: 6Li(n,t)alpha and 7Li(n,n't)alpha cross sections, neutron multiplication by Be or Pb (n,2n) and transport set the tritium breeding ratio, which must exceed 1.
registry.breaks: Blanket designs depend on evaluated cross sections with nontrivial uncertainties for 14 MeV neutrons and on engineering coverage losses.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Nuclear gamma-ray lines from flare-accelerated ions
registry.summary: Reconnection-accelerated protons and alphas in solar flares hit the solar atmosphere and excite nuclear lines (4.44 MeV 12C, 6.13 MeV 16O) and the 2.223 MeV neutron-capture line, which measure the ion spectrum and composition of reconnection acceleration.
registry.map: p+{}^{12}\mathrm C\to p'+{}^{12}\mathrm C^*(4.44);\ n+p\to d+\gamma(2.223\ \text{MeV})
registry.breaks: Line yields fold together acceleration, transport and target geometry, so the inferred ion spectrum is model-dependent.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: BUU/Vlasov transport for heavy-ion reactions
registry.summary: Intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions are simulated with Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck transport: a Vlasov equation in the nuclear mean field plus a Pauli-blocked collision term; giant resonances appear as nuclear zero sound with Landau damping.
registry.breaks: Nuclear transport uses a self-consistent short-range mean field rather than long-range Coulomb fields, and Pauli blocking with quantum fluctuations makes it semiclassical at best.
sources: Buss et al. (2012). "Transport-theoretical Description of Nuclear Reactions". *Phys. Rep.* 512, 1. [arXiv:1106.1344](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.1344)

registry.name: ECR plasma ion sources for radioactive beams
registry.summary: Electron-cyclotron-resonance plasma ion sources and charge breeders produce the highly charged ions that drive and reaccelerate radioactive-beam facilities (FRIB, ISOLDE), applying magnetized discharge plasma physics to exotic-nucleus production.
registry.breaks: ECR sources are engineered for high charge states, a regime far from processing plasmas.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Applied nuclear physics underpins medical physics
registry.summary: Radiotherapy, nuclear medicine and radiation protection rest on nuclear data, radiation-matter interactions and detector physics developed in applied nuclear physics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Medical cyclotrons and isotope production
registry.summary: Lawrence's cyclotron was built for nuclear reactions and today's compact medical cyclotrons and linacs make PET and SPECT isotopes; yields follow from excitation functions, beam current and target stopping power.
registry.breaks: Target cooling and chemistry, not beam physics, often limit practical yields.
sources: Lawrence & Livingston (1932). "The Production of High Speed Light Ions Without the Use of High Voltages". *Phys. Rev.* 40, 19. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.40.19](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.40.19)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radioisotope thermoelectric generators
registry.summary: RTGs convert 238Pu alpha-decay heat (0.57 W/g, 87.7 yr half-life) into electricity with thermoelectric couples; mission power follows from the decay law multiplied by the thermoelectric efficiency set by ZT.
registry.breaks: Thermocouple degradation, not only isotope decay, sets RTG lifetime.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Evaluated nuclear data for medical applications
registry.summary: Medical isotope choice, activity calculations and dose models need evaluated half-lives, decay schemes, emission spectra and production cross sections from nuclear data libraries.
sources: Brown et al. (2018). "ENDF/B-VIII.0: The 8th Major Release of the Nuclear Reaction Data Library with CIELO-project Cross Sections, New Standards and Thermal Scattering Data". *Nucl. Data Sheets* 148, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001)

registry.name: Isotope production for nuclear medicine and PET
registry.summary: PET and SPECT depend on producing short-lived isotopes (18F, 11C, 68Ga, 99mTc) and theranostic pairs (177Lu, 225Ac) through reactions chosen by cross section, yield, purity and half-life.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Accelerator-driven subcritical systems
registry.summary: A high-power proton accelerator driving a spallation target can sustain a subcritical reactor (k_eff < 1) for transmutation of minor actinides, so beam reliability replaces delayed-neutron control.
registry.map: P_{\rm th}\propto\frac{k_{\rm eff}}{1-k_{\rm eff}}\frac{I_pY_{\rm sp}E_f}{\nu};\ Y_{\rm sp}\approx30\ n/p\ \text{at 1 GeV}
registry.breaks: Beam trips cause thermal cycling, and accelerator reliability requirements are beyond present machines.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Reactor production of 99Mo and supply security
registry.summary: Most 99Mo for 99mTc generators comes from fission of uranium targets in a handful of research reactors; reactor outages caused global shortages and drove conversion to low-enriched targets and accelerator routes.
registry.breaks: Supply is a logistics and policy issue as much as a nuclear-physics one.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radiation detection and dosimetry in the clinic
registry.summary: Clinical dosimetry (ionization chambers, calibration protocols, Gy and Sv) and imaging detectors are nuclear radiation-detection physics applied to patients.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Photon-interaction physics and detectors in CT
registry.summary: CT contrast and dual-energy material decomposition use the same photoelectric versus Compton Z-dependence that governs nuclear gamma spectroscopy, and photon-counting CT uses CdTe detectors from radiation-detection physics.
registry.breaks: Clinical CT energies (20-140 keV) sit below most nuclear gamma lines, and image quality is set by reconstruction and dose trade-offs.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: PET and SPECT detectors are nuclear gamma detectors
registry.summary: Gamma cameras and PET scanners use scintillators (LSO/LYSO, NaI), photomultipliers or SiPMs and coincidence timing from nuclear spectroscopy; time-of-flight PET localizes annihilation along the line of response.
sources: Jan et al. (2004). "GATE: a simulation toolkit for PET and SPECT". *Phys. Med. Biol.* 49, 4543. [arXiv:physics/0408109](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0408109)

registry.name: Bragg peak and dosimetry in radiation therapy
registry.summary: Charged-particle stopping (Bethe formula, Bragg peak) and photon interaction physics determine depth-dose curves; dosimetry calibration underlies treatment delivery.
sources: Wilson (1946). "Radiological Use of Fast Protons". *Radiology* 47, 487. [doi:10.1148/47.5.487](https://doi.org/10.1148/47.5.487)

registry.name: EIC accelerator design: crab cavities, cooling, polarization
registry.summary: Reaching 1e34 luminosity with polarized beams at the EIC requires beam-dynamics advances: crab-crossing to recover luminosity at a large crossing angle, strong hadron cooling against intra-beam scattering, and spin-preserving lattices.
registry.breaks: Physics goals impose polarization and acceptance constraints that conflict with pure luminosity optimization.
sources: Abdul Khalek et al. (2022). "Science Requirements and Detector Concepts for the Electron-Ion Collider". *Nucl. Phys. A* 1026, 122447. [arXiv:2103.05419](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.05419)

registry.name: Spin dynamics of polarized beams
registry.summary: Proton-spin measurements need polarized beams kept polarized through acceleration; spin precession follows the Thomas-BMT equation, depolarizing resonances occur when the spin tune G gamma meets betatron or orbit harmonics, and Siberian snakes cancel them at RHIC.
registry.map: \frac{d\mathbf S}{dt}=\frac{e}{\gamma m}\mathbf S\times\left[(1+G\gamma)\mathbf B_\perp+(1+G)\mathbf B_\parallel\right];\ G\gamma=k\pm Q_y
registry.breaks: Spin and orbit dynamics are coupled nonlinearly; the analogy to betatron resonances holds only near isolated resonances.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Positron emission physics sets PET resolution
registry.summary: PET imaging is beta-plus decay followed by positron thermalization and annihilation; the beta endpoint energy sets the positron range (18F 0.6 mm vs 82Rb ~6 mm) and residual momentum gives annihilation non-collinearity, the two physical limits on PET resolution.
registry.breaks: The positron range depends on tissue density and on the full beta spectrum, not only the endpoint.
sources: Jan et al. (2004). "GATE: a simulation toolkit for PET and SPECT". *Phys. Med. Biol.* 49, 4543. [arXiv:physics/0408109](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0408109)

registry.name: Fission rates as transition-state and Kramers escape
registry.summary: The Bohr-Wheeler fission width is transition-state theory over the fission saddle, and Kramers' escape-rate theory of chemical reactions, applied to nuclear viscosity, explains measured fission delays and pre-scission neutron excess.
registry.breaks: Nuclear dissipation is one-body (wall friction) and temperature-dependent, and the 'reaction coordinate' is a collective shape, not an atomic distance.
sources: Bohr & Wheeler (1939). "The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission". *Phys. Rev.* 56, 426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.56.426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.56.426)

Kramers (1940). "Brownian motion in a field of force and the diffusion model of chemical reactions". *Physica* 7, 284. [doi:10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0031-8914(40)90098-2)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Neutron scattering contrast variation in biophysics
registry.summary: The opposite-sign coherent scattering lengths of H and D let small-angle neutron scattering and neutron crystallography 'match out' parts of protein complexes and membranes and locate hydrogen atoms and protonation states.
registry.map: b_{\rm H}=-3.74\ \text{fm},\ b_{\rm D}=+6.67\ \text{fm};\ \Delta\rho=\rho_{\rm molecule}-\rho_{\rm solvent}(x_{D_2O})
registry.breaks: Large incoherent scattering from hydrogen adds background, and deuteration can perturb biological samples.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Compound-nucleus evaporation and RRKM unimolecular decay
registry.summary: Weisskopf's statistical evaporation of compound nuclei and RRKM theory of unimolecular dissociation share one structure: decay rates are ratios of level densities of transition and parent states, and both show Ericson-type fluctuations when levels overlap.
registry.breaks: Nuclear level densities come from fermionic excitations with pairing and shells; molecular ones are vibrational and rotational, with conservation of angular momentum handled differently.
sources: Weisskopf (1937). "Statistics and Nuclear Reactions". *Phys. Rev.* 52, 295. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.52.295](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.52.295)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ion-beam analysis of surfaces and thin films
registry.summary: Rutherford backscattering, elastic recoil detection, nuclear reaction analysis (15N resonance for hydrogen) and PIXE use nuclear scattering and reactions to measure surface composition and depth profiles quantitatively.
registry.breaks: Depth resolution is limited by energy straggling, and lateral resolution is poor compared with scanning probes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Boron neutron capture therapy
registry.summary: BNCT delivers a thermal-neutron field to tumours loaded with 10B; the 10B(n,alpha)7Li reaction deposits ~2.3 MeV within one cell diameter, so the nuclear cross section and short ion ranges give cellular-level targeting.
registry.breaks: Clinical dose depends on boron biodistribution and accelerator-based epithermal neutron sources rather than on nuclear data alone.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Nuclear interactions in proton and ion therapy
registry.summary: Therapeutic proton and carbon beams undergo nuclear reactions that fragment the beam, deposit dose beyond the Bragg peak and produce prompt gammas and positron emitters (11C, 15O) used for in-vivo range verification.
registry.breaks: Nuclear cross sections for therapy-relevant fragments are known only to 10-20 percent, limiting range-verification accuracy.
sources: Wilson (1946). "Radiological Use of Fast Protons". *Radiology* 47, 487. [doi:10.1148/47.5.487](https://doi.org/10.1148/47.5.487)
Min et al. (2006). "Prompt gamma measurements for locating the dose falloff region in the proton therapy". *Appl. Phys. Lett.* 89, 183517. [doi:10.1063/1.2378561](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2378561)

registry.name: Nuclear resonant scattering at synchrotrons and XFELs
registry.summary: Synchrotron radiation replaced radioactive sources for Mössbauer spectroscopy (nuclear forward scattering, 57Fe at 14.4 keV), and an XFEL resonantly excited the 12.4 keV clock isomer of 45Sc, bringing narrow nuclear transitions into X-ray quantum optics.
registry.map: \Gamma_{\rm nuc}\sim\text{neV}\ \text{vs}\ \Delta E_{\rm SR}\sim\text{meV};\ \text{time-gating separates delayed nuclear signal}
registry.breaks: Only a few low-lying isomers are accessible, and the photon flux in a neV bandwidth is tiny.
sources: Shvyd'ko et al. (2023). "Resonant X-ray excitation of the nuclear clock isomer 45Sc". *Nature* 622, 471. [doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06491-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06491-w)

registry.name: Alpha-particle soft errors in integrated circuits
registry.summary: Alpha particles from trace U and Th in chip packaging and solder deposit charge along their tracks and flip memory bits, a reliability problem found in 1979; cosmic-ray neutrons cause the same single-event upsets via nuclear recoils.
registry.map: Q_{\rm dep}=\frac{e\,\Delta E}{3.6\ \text{eV}}\ \text{(Si)};\ \text{upset if }Q_{\rm coll}>Q_{\rm crit}\sim\text{fC}
registry.breaks: Upset rates depend on device geometry and charge collection, which scale differently at each technology node.
sources: May & Woods (1979). "Alpha-particle-induced soft errors in dynamic memories". *IEEE Trans. Electron Devices* 26, 2. [doi:10.1109/T-ED.1979.19370](https://doi.org/10.1109/T-ED.1979.19370)

registry.name: Radiocarbon, Suess effect and cosmogenic climate proxies
registry.summary: Dilution of atmospheric 14C by fossil carbon (the Suess effect) fingerprints fossil-fuel CO2, and cosmogenic 14C and 10Be records reconstruct past solar activity for climate attribution.
registry.map: ^{14}\mathrm N(n,p)^{14}\mathrm C;\ \Delta^{14}\mathrm C\ \text{falls as fossil (14C-free) CO}_2\ \text{is added}
registry.breaks: Cosmogenic production also depends on the geomagnetic field and on carbon-cycle exchange, which must be modelled.
sources: Suess (1955). "Radiocarbon Concentration in Modern Wood". *Science* 122, 415. [doi:10.1126/science.122.3166.415.b](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.122.3166.415.b)
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radioactive tracers of ocean circulation
registry.summary: Bomb-produced 14C and tritium-3He ages and natural radiocarbon measure ocean ventilation and deep-water ages (about 1000 yr for the deep Pacific), constraining overturning circulation and ocean heat and carbon uptake.
registry.breaks: Tracer ages are mixtures of water-mass ages, so interpretation needs transit-time distributions.
sources: Libby (1946). "Atmospheric Helium Three and Radiocarbon from Cosmic Radiation". *Phys. Rev.* 69, 671. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.69.671](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.69.671)

registry.name: Geoneutrinos and Earth's radiogenic heat
registry.summary: Decays of 238U, 232Th and 40K supply roughly half of Earth's ~47 TW surface heat flow, driving mantle convection and the geodynamo; KamLAND and Borexino geoneutrino fluxes measure this budget directly.
registry.map: H_{\rm rad}=\sum_iN_i\lambda_iQ_i^{\rm heat};\ \bar\nu_e+p\to e^++n\ (E_{\rm th}=1.8\ \text{MeV, misses }^{40}\text{K})
registry.breaks: Inverse beta decay cannot see 40K neutrinos, and mantle versus crust contributions remain uncertain.
sources: KamLAND Collaboration (2011). "Partial radiogenic heat model for Earth revealed by geoneutrino measurements". *Nature Geosci.* 4, 647. [doi:10.1038/ngeo1205](https://doi.org/10.1038/ngeo1205)

registry.name: Decay chains in generators and alpha theranostics
registry.summary: Radionuclide generators (99Mo/99mTc, 68Ge/68Ga) work by transient or secular equilibrium in Bateman decay chains, and targeted alpha therapy with 225Ac must track recoiling daughters along the decay chain.
registry.breaks: Daughter recoil energies (~100 keV) break chemical bonds, so the chain can leave the targeting molecule, which simple Bateman bookkeeping ignores.

registry.name: Coupled cluster: from nuclei to chemistry and back
registry.summary: Coupled-cluster theory was invented for nuclear matter (Coester, Kümmel), developed into the gold standard of quantum chemistry (Cizek, CCSD(T)), and returned to nuclear physics for medium-mass nuclei with chiral forces.
registry.breaks: Nuclear CC must handle three-nucleon forces and self-bound centre-of-mass motion, while chemistry has a fixed nuclear frame and Coulomb-only interactions.
sources: Coester (1958). "Bound states of a many-particle system". *Nucl. Phys.* 7, 421. [doi:10.1016/0029-5582(58)90280-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(58)90280-3)

Čížek (1966). "On the Correlation Problem in Atomic and Molecular Systems. Calculation of Wavefunction Components in Ursell-Type Expansion Using Quantum-Field Theoretical Methods". *J. Chem. Phys.* 45, 4256. [doi:10.1063/1.1727484](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1727484)

registry.name: Radioactive-beam facilities as accelerator systems
registry.summary: Exotic-nucleus research is enabled by accelerator technology: FRIB's superconducting heavy-ion linac, projectile-fragment separators and ISOL post-accelerators deliver drip-line nuclei at rates set by beam power and separator acceptance.
registry.breaks: Production cross sections, not accelerator physics, set the ultimate reach toward the drip line.

registry.name: Halo nuclei and helium trimers: weak-binding universality
registry.summary: Two-neutron halo nuclei (6He, 11Li) and the helium dimer and trimer are both governed by large scattering lengths, so their sizes and Efimov-type three-body states follow universal few-body laws; the excited He trimer is an observed Efimov state.
registry.breaks: Halo nuclei have Pauli-blocked cores and finite-range corrections, and no excited Efimov state of a nucleus has been seen.
sources: Braaten & Hammer (2006). "Universality in few-body systems with large scattering length". *Phys. Rep.* 428, 259. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410417](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410417)

registry.name: Nuclear and molecular rotational bands
registry.summary: Bohr and Mottelson's collective model borrowed the molecular separation of intrinsic and rotational motion: deformed nuclei show E proportional to J(J+1) bands like diatomic rotors, with moments of inertia between irrotational and rigid values.
registry.breaks: Nuclei have no heavy constituents to rotate; collective rotation emerges from the same nucleons, so the adiabatic separation is approximate and pairing reduces the moment of inertia.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Shell model as configuration interaction (quantum chemistry)
registry.summary: The nuclear shell model is configuration interaction in a valence space, diagonalized with the same Lanczos and m-scheme techniques as full CI in quantum chemistry; both face exponential basis growth and use truncation, effective operators and now quantum algorithms.
registry.map: |\Psi\rangle=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha|\Phi_\alpha\rangle,\ H\mathbf c=E\mathbf c;\ \dim\sim\binom{N_{\rm orb}}{N_p}\binom{N_{\rm orb}}{N_n}
registry.breaks: Shell-model interactions are effective, renormalized valence-space operators with isospin; chemistry CI uses bare Coulomb integrals in Gaussian bases.
sources: Caurier et al. (2005). "The shell model as a unified view of nuclear structure". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 77, 427. [arXiv:nucl-th/0402046](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0402046)

registry.name: Nuclear magnetic moments behind MRI
registry.summary: MRI images the precession of nuclear spins; the Larmor frequencies of 1H, 13C, 19F, 23Na and 31P come from nuclear magnetic moments (Schmidt-line shell-model values plus core polarization), first measured by Rabi's resonance method.
registry.breaks: MRI contrast comes from relaxation and chemistry of the environment (T1, T2), not from nuclear structure.

registry.name: Itinerant versus local-moment magnetism
registry.summary: Stoner ferromagnetism and spin-density waves arise from band structure and Fermi surface nesting, contrasting with Heisenberg local moments; RKKY links conduction electrons to local moments.

registry.name: Bloch bands to Berry curvature and Chern numbers
registry.summary: Berry connection defined on Bloch eigenstates over the Brillouin zone gives Chern and Z2 invariants; band theory supplies the Hilbert-space bundle that topology classifies.
