registry.name: DFT as input to DMFT and QMC
registry.summary: Kohn–Sham band structures supply downfolded tight-binding models for DMFT (DFT+DMFT), and QMC benchmarks exchange–correlation functionals; both address the many-electron problem at different accuracy and cost.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: DFT prediction of hydride superconductors
registry.summary: DFT structure search plus linear-response phonons and Eliashberg theory predicted H3S and LaH10 Tc before experiment, a rare first-principles prediction of Tc.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Coulomb blockade and Landauer transport in dots
registry.summary: Quantum-dot conductance is analysed with Landauer–Büttiker and master-equation transport; conductance quantization and resonant tunnelling in mesoscopic wires carry over to dots.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Landauer–Büttiker edge channels
registry.summary: Landauer–Büttiker formalism with chiral edge channels explains quantized Hall resistance, and quantized conductance in mesoscopic wires shares the same transmission-mode counting.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Phonon-mediated pairing
registry.summary: Electron–phonon coupling gives the retarded attraction behind Cooper pairing; the isotope effect and Debye frequency set Tc prefactors in BCS and Eliashberg theory.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: High-frequency hydrogen phonons drive high Tc
registry.summary: Light hydrogen gives very high phonon frequencies and strong electron–phonon coupling, so BCS/Eliashberg Tc scales with the phonon energy scale.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Semiconductor physics in monolayer TMDs
registry.summary: TMD monolayers are direct-gap 2D semiconductors where doping, heterojunctions and carrier statistics carry over, but reduced screening gives huge exciton binding energies beyond the 3D Wannier picture.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Wannier excitons in semiconductors vs TMDs
registry.summary: Excitons are hydrogen-like electron–hole bound states in both; TMD monolayers have nonlocal screening that modifies the Rydberg series.
registry.breaks: In 2D the dielectric screening is nonlocal (Keldysh), so the hydrogenic series fails for excited states.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: 2D materials as topological platforms
registry.summary: Graphene, TMDs and moiré systems host Dirac cones, Chern bands, quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall states, linking low-dimensional materials to topological classification.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Relativistic quantum Hall effect in graphene
registry.summary: Dirac electrons in graphene give half-integer quantum Hall plateaus from the zero-energy n=0 Landau level and Berry phase pi.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Graphene as a 2D Dirac semimetal
registry.summary: Graphene's Dirac points are the 2D counterpart of 3D Weyl/Dirac nodes; both are linear band crossings with Berry phase and relativistic-like quasiparticles.
registry.breaks: Graphene nodes need C2T and are not topologically protected against gap opening by symmetry-breaking substrates; 3D Weyl nodes are stable monopoles of Berry flux.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Weyl/Dirac nodes and graphene Dirac cones
registry.summary: Weyl and Dirac semimetals generalise graphene's Dirac cones to 3D, with Fermi arcs and chiral anomaly replacing edge zero modes and half-integer Hall response.
registry.breaks: Graphene has no Fermi arcs or net chirality per valley pair in the same sense and the nodes are not monopoles.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fractional Chern insulators in moiré bands
registry.summary: Flat Chern bands in twisted MoTe2 and graphene host fractional Chern insulators at zero field, lattice analogues of fractional quantum Hall states with anyonic excitations.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Moiré superlattices as tunable Hubbard simulators
registry.summary: Twisted TMD bilayers realise triangular-lattice Hubbard models with tunable U/W, showing Mott insulators and superconductivity-like phases; magic-angle graphene correlated insulators arise from flat-band Coulomb repulsion.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hofstadter bands and Chern bands in moiré systems
registry.summary: Moiré superlattices produce Hofstadter butterflies at accessible fields and Chern bands with quantized Hall response at zero field, linking Landau levels to flat Chern bands and Wannier diagrams.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kondo effect in quantum dots
registry.summary: A dot with an odd electron number acts as a tunable Anderson impurity, producing a Kondo resonance and unitary conductance at low T that realises single-impurity Kondo physics in a controlled device.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Majorana nanowires and dot arrays
registry.summary: Semiconductor nanowires with spin–orbit coupling, Zeeman field and proximity superconductivity realise Kitaev-chain physics; quantum dot chains build minimal Kitaev chains and probe zero-bias peaks.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Valleytronics and spin-valley locking vs spintronics
registry.summary: Spin–valley locking in TMDs lets valley act as a degree of freedom, analogous to spin; valley Hall effect parallels spin Hall effect via Berry curvature, and magnons and excitons share bosonic transport ideas.
registry.breaks: Valley is not a conserved quantum number against intervalley scattering and lacks a simple torque or conservation law like spin transfer.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Altermagnets: spin splitting and anomalous Hall
registry.summary: Symmetry-enforced spin-split bands in altermagnets generate anomalous Hall responses via Berry curvature despite zero net magnetization, connecting magnetic point-group symmetry to band geometry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Superexchange from the Hubbard model
registry.summary: At half filling and large U the Hubbard model reduces to the Heisenberg antiferromagnet by second-order virtual hopping, deriving Anderson superexchange.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Spin glasses and structural glasses
registry.summary: Frustration and rugged energy landscapes link spin glasses to structural glasses; replica symmetry breaking and random first-order transition theory connect the two.
registry.breaks: Not stated by the analyst.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Order-by-disorder and defect physics across spin and nematic systems
registry.summary: Both study order-parameter manifolds with topological defects (vortices, hedgehogs, disclinations) classified by homotopy; spin ice and nematics share Coulomb-gas-like defect interactions and degenerate manifolds.
registry.breaks: Spin liquids are quantum with fractionalized excitations and entanglement, while nematics are classical thermal systems with Frank elasticity.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum spin liquids as topologically ordered states
registry.summary: Gapped spin liquids host fractionalised spinons and visons with topological ground-state degeneracy; the Kitaev honeycomb model realises Z2 gauge theory with Majorana excitations.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Skyrmion topological Hall effect and emergent fields
registry.summary: Electrons traversing a skyrmion texture acquire a real-space Berry phase, producing an emergent magnetic field and topological Hall effect, the real-space counterpart of momentum-space Berry curvature.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Active nematics
registry.summary: Active nematics combine Frank elasticity and defect dynamics of liquid crystals with active stress, producing spontaneous flows and self-propelled +1/2 disclinations.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: FQHE as prototype topological order
registry.summary: The fractional quantum Hall effect, with Laughlin quasiparticles of fractional charge and statistics, is the archetype of topological order, with chiral edge modes and ground-state degeneracy on a torus.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Majorana zero modes as non-Abelian anyons
registry.summary: Vortex Majorana modes in p+ip superconductors obey Ising non-Abelian statistics, the basis of topological quantum computation and the Moore–Read fractional quantum Hall analogy.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Heavy-fermion quantum critical points
registry.summary: Heavy-fermion metals such as CeCu6-xAux are canonical quantum critical systems, where Kondo breakdown competes with RKKY magnetism in a Doniach phase diagram and yields non-Fermi-liquid behaviour.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Numerical solutions of the Hubbard model
registry.summary: DMFT, DQMC, DMRG and tensor networks were developed and benchmarked on the Hubbard model; DMFT captures the Mott transition as a mean-field in infinite dimensions.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Doped Mott insulator and cuprate superconductivity
registry.summary: Cuprates are doped Mott insulators described by the Hubbard/t-J model; d-wave pairing emerges from superexchange-driven correlations (RVB).
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Strange metal normal state of cuprates
registry.summary: Optimally doped cuprates show T-linear resistivity and a possible quantum critical point under the superconducting dome; non-Fermi-liquid scattering near Planckian bound.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Unconventional superconductivity near a quantum critical point
registry.summary: Iron pnictides show a superconducting dome around a putative antiferromagnetic quantum critical point with T-linear resistivity, suggesting spin-fluctuation pairing as in cuprates and heavy fermions.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: BdG quasiparticles and topological superconductivity
registry.summary: Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonians of BCS theory carry particle-hole symmetry; for p-wave or engineered pairing their topology yields Majorana modes, as in the Kitaev chain.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Fractional Josephson effect
registry.summary: Topological Josephson junctions host Majorana-mediated 4π-periodic current-phase relations, a signature that differs from the 2π conventional Josephson effect.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Band theory of neutrons in the neutron-star crust
registry.summary: Bragg scattering of unbound superfluid neutrons by the nuclear lattice of the inner crust is computed with Bloch's theorem and band-structure methods; the resulting large neutron effective mass (entrainment) reduces the mobile superfluid fraction and challenges crust-only glitch models.
registry.map: \psi_{nk}(\mathbf r+\mathbf R)=e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\psi_{nk}(\mathbf r):\ \text{electrons}\to\text{free neutrons};\ m_n^*/m_n\gg1\ (\text{entrainment})

registry.name: Degenerate Fermi gas: metals and white dwarfs
registry.summary: The same degenerate Fermi-Dirac electron gas gives the Sommerfeld model of metals and the pressure that supports white dwarfs; Fowler applied Fermi statistics to white dwarfs in 1926, before Sommerfeld applied it to metals, and relativistic kinematics turns P~n^{5/3} into P~n^{4/3}, giving the Chandrasekhar mass.
sources: Fowler (1926). "On Dense Matter". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 87, 114. [doi:10.1093/mnras/87.2.114](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/87.2.114)

registry.name: Superionic water ice in ice-giant interiors
registry.summary: Superionic water, an oxygen crystal through which protons diffuse like a liquid, was predicted by ab initio simulation for Uranus and Neptune and identified in laser-shock experiments by nanosecond X-ray diffraction (fcc ice XVIII); it may explain the ice giants' non-dipolar magnetic fields.

registry.name: Coulomb crystallization of white-dwarf cores
registry.summary: Carbon-oxygen ions in a cooling white dwarf freeze into a bcc Coulomb (one-component-plasma) crystal near Gamma~175; Gaia's cooling-sequence pile-up confirmed latent-heat release and phase separation, and the same bcc Coulomb lattice makes up neutron-star crusts.

registry.name: DFT and dielectric response for dark-matter scattering
registry.summary: Dark-matter-electron scattering rates in crystals are computed from DFT crystal form factors and, with screening included, from the energy-loss function Im[-1/eps(q,omega)], so electronic-structure codes directly set direct-detection sensitivities.

registry.name: Ab initio equations of state for giant-planet interiors
registry.summary: DFT-based molecular dynamics provides the hydrogen-helium equation of state and the H-He immiscibility ('helium rain') used in Jupiter and Saturn interior models fitted to Juno and Cassini gravity data; DFT exchange-correlation and band-gap errors directly shift the predicted metallization boundary.

registry.name: Electron transport in white-dwarf and neutron-star matter
registry.summary: Thermal and electrical conductivities of degenerate stellar matter are computed with the Boltzmann/Ziman theory of metals (electron-phonon Umklapp and electron-impurity scattering, Wiedemann-Franz); crust-cooling curves of accreting neutron stars imply a low-impurity, ordered rather than amorphous crust.

registry.name: Single-phonon excitations for sub-MeV dark matter
registry.summary: Below ~MeV the dark matter's momentum transfer is below the inverse lattice spacing, so it scatters by creating single acoustic or optical phonons rather than nuclear recoils; polar crystals (GaAs, sapphire) with dark-photon-coupled optical phonons are proposed targets read out by phonon sensors.
sources: Knapen et al. (2018). "Detection of Light Dark Matter With Optical Phonons in Polar Materials". *Phys. Lett. B* 785, 386. [arXiv:1712.06598](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06598)

registry.name: Crustal shear modes as magnetar QPOs
registry.summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations in magnetar giant-flare tails (tens of Hz) are interpreted as global torsional modes of the crystalline crust, i.e. long-wavelength transverse acoustic phonons of the Coulomb lattice whose speed is set by the shear modulus mu~0.12 n_i Z^2 e^2/a.
sources: Strohmayer & Watts (2005). "Discovery of Fast X-Ray Oscillations during the 1998 Giant Flare from SGR 1900+14". *Astrophys. J.* 632, L111. [arXiv:astro-ph/0508206](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0508206)

registry.name: Debye cooling of crystallized white dwarfs
registry.summary: Once a white-dwarf core crystallizes, its ionic heat capacity follows the Debye phonon law and falls as T^3 below Theta_D, so the oldest white dwarfs cool faster ('Debye cooling'), which shapes the faint end of the luminosity function used for cosmochronology.
sources: Tremblay et al. (2019). "Core crystallization and pile-up in the cooling sequence of evolving white dwarfs". *Nature* 565, 202. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x)

registry.name: Semiconductor targets for dark-matter electron recoils
registry.summary: Silicon and germanium crystals are dark-matter targets: ionization-plus-phonon detectors for nuclear recoils, and single-electron skipper CCDs (SENSEI, DAMIC-M) whose ~1 eV band gap lets sub-GeV dark matter register through electron excitations across the gap.

registry.summary: C60 was discovered in laser-vaporization experiments built to mimic carbon-star chemistry, opening the fullerene-nanotube-graphene family of carbon materials; fullerenes were later found in planetary nebulae and C60+ identified as a diffuse-interstellar-band carrier.

registry.name: Wigner crystals and stellar Coulomb crystals
registry.summary: Electron Wigner crystals in moire TMD superlattices and the ion crystals of white dwarfs and neutron-star crusts are both one-component plasmas that crystallize in a uniform neutralizing background once Coulomb energy beats kinetic energy (large r_s or large Gamma).
registry.breaks: Stellar ions melt classically through thermal fluctuations, while 2D electron Wigner crystals melt quantum mechanically; moire Wigner crystals are pinned to an imposed superlattice and are two-dimensional.

registry.name: Emergent monopoles in spin ice and the monopole problem
registry.summary: Spin-ice excitations behave as deconfined magnetic monopoles with a Coulomb interaction, a condensed-matter realization of the monopoles whose predicted overproduction at grand-unified transitions motivated inflation.
registry.breaks: Spin-ice monopoles source the H field (div M), not B; they are emergent quasiparticles with non-quantized, material-set charge, unlike 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles of a broken gauge group.

registry.name: Skyrmions and cosmic textures
registry.summary: Magnetic skyrmions and cosmological textures are both non-singular topological solitons of a sphere-valued order parameter classified by homotopy (pi_2 for 2D films, pi_3 for 3D cosmic textures); a collapsing texture was proposed to explain the CMB Cold Spot.
registry.breaks: Skyrmions are static, DMI-stabilized and 2D; cosmic textures are 3D, unstable to collapse by Derrick's theorem and scale with the horizon. The Cold Spot texture interpretation is not established.

registry.name: Dust aggregation: from colloids to planetesimals
registry.summary: The first stage of planet formation is aggregation of micron dust grains by Brownian motion and differential drift into fractal aggregates, followed by compaction, bouncing and fragmentation: the cluster-cluster aggregation and contact mechanics studied in colloids and granular matter.

registry.name: Amorphous ices and silicates in disks and dust
registry.summary: Interstellar and protoplanetary grains are largely amorphous: vapour-deposited amorphous solid water and glassy silicates whose crystallization (annealing near the star) and glass-transition kinetics record thermal history and control volatile trapping at snow lines.

registry.name: Kibble-Zurek defects: liquid crystals and the early universe
registry.summary: Kibble's argument that causally disconnected regions choose independent vacua at a symmetry-breaking transition, leaving strings and monopoles whose overabundance inflation must dilute, was tested by quenching nematic liquid crystals and counting disclinations; Zurek's refinement gives defect density from the quench rate.
registry.breaks: Nematic defects form in a dissipative, non-relativistic fluid with no gauge field and coarsen by friction; cosmic defects are relativistic, may be gauge strings, and evolve in an expanding spacetime.

registry.name: Nuclear pasta as a liquid crystal
registry.summary: In the neutron-star mantle, competition between nuclear surface tension and long-range Coulomb repulsion produces rod, slab and bubble 'pasta' phases with the symmetries of columnar and smectic liquid crystals (and of block-copolymer microphases); their elasticity is described with liquid-crystal theory.
registry.breaks: Pasta is ordered by nuclear plus Coulomb forces at ~1e14 g/cm^3 with no solvent or thermal softness; its elastic constants are MeV-scale and the phases sit in a degenerate electron sea.

registry.name: Cosmic-string formation simulated in superfluid 3He
registry.summary: Neutron-absorption hot spots in BCS-paired superfluid 3He re-cool through Tc and nucleate vortex tangles at the rate predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, a laboratory test of defect formation in early-universe phase transitions with a multicomponent order parameter.

registry.name: Primordial plasma and Thomson scattering
registry.summary: Before recombination the universe was a tightly coupled photon–baryon plasma, whose acoustic oscillations imprint the CMB peaks. Thomson scattering off free electrons sets the optical depth, and reionization polarizes the CMB.

registry.name: BAO as sound waves in the primordial plasma
registry.summary: Baryon acoustic oscillations are ion-acoustic-like pressure waves in the coupled photon–baryon fluid. The sound horizon is a standard ruler, and Jeans instability parallels plasma streaming and gravitational instabilities.

registry.name: Magnetically driven AGN jets

registry.name: Reconnection in jets and coronae

registry.name: Turbulence and magnetic fields in clusters

registry.name: Intracluster medium as a weakly collisional plasma
registry.summary: The hot, magnetised intracluster medium has long mean free paths, so pressure anisotropy, firehose and mirror instabilities, and suppressed Spitzer conduction require kinetic treatment. Plasma microinstabilities regulate viscosity and heat transport.

registry.name: Reionization and the intergalactic plasma

registry.name: Galactic dynamo and seed fields

registry.name: Astroparticle sources are astrophysical plasma shocks

registry.name: Plasma wakefield acceleration and astrophysical acceleration

registry.name: Alfvén waves scatter cosmic rays
registry.summary: Cosmic rays stream along field lines and resonantly excite Alfvén waves, which scatter them and set the diffusion coefficient. Self-generated waves confine Galactic cosmic rays and feed back in shock precursors.

registry.name: Turbulent scattering and cosmic-ray transport

registry.name: Cosmic rays and heliospheric particle physics
registry.summary: Galactic cosmic rays propagate through the turbulent magnetised solar wind and heliosphere, where modulation, diffusion and scattering are plasma processes. The same transport theory applies in the Galaxy.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Diffusive shock acceleration of cosmic rays
registry.summary: First-order Fermi acceleration at collisionless shocks yields a power-law spectrum p^-(3r/(r-1)) with index near 2 for strong shocks, and explains the cosmic-ray spectrum from supernova remnants. Magnetic-field amplification enables acceleration toward the knee.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: FRB emission as coherent plasma processes

registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: GRB afterglows from relativistic collisionless shocks

registry.name: Planetary interiors at megabar pressures

registry.name: Magnetised accretion disks and the MRI

registry.name: Disk MRI from ideal-MHD Alfvén dynamics

registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Stellar interiors and atmospheres are plasmas
registry.summary: Stars are self-gravitating plasmas. Their equation of state, opacity, transport, convection, magnetism and winds draw on plasma physics, and fusion burning links to laboratory fusion.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dense matter equations of state in the lab
registry.summary: Laser-driven shocks and X-ray Thomson scattering probe warm dense matter relevant to white-dwarf and giant-planet interiors. Laboratory equations of state calibrate dense-plasma models for compact objects.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Pulsar wind nebulae and relativistic shocks
registry.summary: Pulsar winds terminate in relativistic shocks that accelerate pairs and power synchrotron nebulae such as the Crab. These are testbeds for relativistic shock acceleration and magnetic reconnection in striped winds.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Stellar nucleosynthesis and fusion burning
registry.summary: Stars burn by thermonuclear fusion with Gamow-peak reaction rates, and fusion devices target the same reactions. Laboratory D-T burning plasmas are self-heated by alphas, like stellar cores.
registry.breaks: Stars confine by gravity at about 10^7 K and long timescales, while devices use magnetic fields at 10^8 K and lack gravitational stability.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rayleigh–Taylor mixing in supernovae and ICF
registry.summary: Hydrodynamic instabilities at accelerating interfaces occur in core-collapse explosions and in ICF capsule implosions. Scaled laser experiments reproduce supernova mixing, and the shared physics is Rayleigh–Taylor and Richtmyer–Meshkov growth.
registry.breaks: ICF has ablation stabilization and sharp interfaces, while supernovae involve gravity, neutrinos and nuclear burning.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Supernova remnant shocks
registry.summary: Supernova remnants are the canonical sites of collisionless shocks, with magnetic-field amplification, thin X-ray rims and gamma-ray emission. They are the leading candidate sources of Galactic cosmic rays.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Solar magnetism as MHD
registry.summary: Sunspots, flux emergence, flares and coronal structure are MHD phenomena. Frozen-in flux, reconnection and Alfvén waves describe the Sun's magnetic activity.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: The solar dynamo and the solar cycle
registry.summary: The 11-year solar cycle is produced by a dynamo in which differential rotation (the Ω-effect) and helical convection (the α-effect) regenerate field. Helioseismology constrains the rotation profile that feeds mean-field models.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Solar flares as reconnection
registry.summary: Solar flares and CMEs release stored magnetic energy by reconnection, per the standard CSHKP model. The Sweet–Parker rate is too slow, which motivated plasmoid and collisionless reconnection.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Sun to heliosphere
registry.summary: The Sun drives the solar wind, coronal mass ejections and space weather. Helioseismology and coronal physics set the boundary conditions for heliospheric plasma models.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Parker wind and coronal heating
registry.summary: The corona, with its heating problem, is the base of the Parker wind. Alfvén-wave turbulence and reconnection are candidate heaters, and the transonic wind solution follows from hydrodynamic equations.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Blackbody radiation and radiative equilibrium
registry.summary: Both rest on Planck blackbody radiation and radiative transfer: the CMB is a relic thermal spectrum, Earth's climate set by balance of absorbed sunlight and outgoing thermal radiation.
registry.breaks: The CMB is a decoupled relic freely streaming; Earth's emission is non-equilibrium and gray-body with strong absorption bands.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Inverse problems and tomographic reconstruction
registry.summary: Weak-lensing mass maps and CT/MRI reconstruction are regularized linear inverse problems, using Kaiser–Squires-type inversion, Wiener filtering and sparsity priors.
registry.breaks: Lensing has sparse noisy sampling and shape noise; CT has controlled acquisition geometry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quantum sensors for dark matter
registry.summary: Axion and light dark-matter searches use SQUIDs, atomic magnetometers, NV centres, atomic clocks and interferometers; quantum-sensing techniques set sensitivity, including squeezing.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Low-background detectors and scintillation
registry.summary: Scintillators, liquid xenon and time-of-flight photodetection developed for particle and dark-matter detection also drive PET detector design; low-noise photosensors cross over.
registry.breaks: Dark-matter detectors require extreme radiopurity and keV thresholds; PET needs high rate at 511 keV.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Jets and undulator radiation
registry.summary: Relativistic jets emit synchrotron and inverse-Compton radiation, with Doppler boosting; undulators and FELs give coherent, narrow-band versions of the same radiation by accelerated charges.
registry.breaks: Jet emission is incoherent and broadband; FELs achieve coherence via microbunching.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Turbulence in stratified fluids
registry.summary: Intracluster gas and the oceans are stratified turbulent fluids, with buoyancy-driven mixing and internal gravity waves described by Brunt–Väisälä frequency.
registry.breaks: Cluster gas is magnetized, weakly collisional plasma with cooling and AGN feedback.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Statistical inference of dynamical systems
registry.summary: Galactic archaeology and biophysical data analysis both use Bayesian inference and machine learning on large noisy catalogues; Gaia phase-space modelling parallels inference in living-systems data.
registry.breaks: The shared element is generic statistical practice.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rossby waves and density waves
registry.summary: Both feature large-scale rotating-fluid wave patterns: Rossby waves from the beta effect in atmospheres, and spiral density waves in rotating galactic disks with differential rotation, with analogous dispersion structure.
registry.breaks: Galactic disks are self-gravitating and collisionless stars; Rossby waves are restoring-force vorticity waves in a fluid.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cosmic accelerators versus machines
registry.summary: Diffusive shock acceleration and Fermi mechanisms are natural counterparts of laboratory accelerators; the Hillas criterion parallels the size-times-field limit on achievable energy.
registry.breaks: Cosmic acceleration is stochastic, shock-based and power-law; machines use coherent, controlled RF fields.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Synchrotron radiation in nature and the lab
registry.summary: Relativistic electrons in magnetic fields emit synchrotron radiation, identical physics in AGN jets, pulsar nebulae and storage-ring light sources, with the same critical-frequency scaling.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cosmic rays and air showers in the atmosphere
registry.summary: Cosmic rays are detected through extensive air showers developing in the atmosphere; cosmic-ray ionisation is also proposed to affect atmospheric electricity and cloud nucleation.
registry.breaks: Cosmic-ray cloud seeding is weak and disputed.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cosmic-ray and hadron-therapy interactions
registry.summary: Heavy-ion transport, nuclear fragmentation and Bragg-peak energy loss are shared: galactic cosmic-ray shielding for astronauts uses the same codes and radiobiology as carbon-ion therapy.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Coherent emission from bunched charges
registry.summary: FRB models invoke coherent curvature or maser emission from bunched charges, resembling coherent synchrotron radiation and FEL microbunching where power scales as N².
registry.breaks: FRB coherence mechanism is unsettled; FELs rely on a known collective instability.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Planet spectra as molecular spectroscopy
registry.summary: Identifying planetary atmospheric species relies on laboratory rovibrational line lists and selection rules; the same spectroscopy underlies remote sensing of planets and exoplanets.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Planetary climate as Earth climate physics
registry.summary: Energy balance, greenhouse effect and feedbacks developed for Earth apply to other planets and exoplanets, setting equilibrium temperatures and habitability.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Physical limits of life and biosignatures
registry.summary: Habitability asks which physical constraints (energy, chemistry, thermodynamics) permit life; physics of living systems quantifies those limits, such as energy use, noise and information processing.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Habitable zone from climate feedbacks
registry.summary: Habitable-zone edges are set by radiative-convective climate physics: runaway greenhouse from water-vapour feedback and ice-albedo snowball transitions, as in Earth climate models.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Spectroscopic databases serve exoplanet retrievals
registry.summary: Line lists such as HITRAN and ExoMol, from quantum-chemistry and spectroscopy, are essential inputs for interpreting JWST exoplanet spectra.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Transmission spectra as molecular absorption
registry.summary: Exoplanet transmission and emission spectra are decoded using molecular line lists, cross sections and Raman/collision-induced absorption knowledge from molecular spectroscopy.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Greenhouse and inversion physics on other worlds
registry.summary: Greenhouse trapping, lapse rates and temperature inversions explain exoplanet thermal structure just as they do Earth's atmosphere.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radiative transfer codes from Earth to exoplanets
registry.summary: Radiative-convective models, correlated-k opacities and general circulation models built for Earth climate are reused for exoplanet atmospheres and retrievals.
registry.breaks: Earth-tuned assumptions (water condensation, near-1 bar) fail for hot Jupiters and non-solar compositions.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Astrochemistry in disks
registry.summary: Disk chemistry and the delivery of volatiles depend on gas-phase and grain-surface reaction rates, ion-molecule kinetics and snow lines, drawing on reaction-dynamics rate theory.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Grain-surface chemistry and catalysis
registry.summary: H2 formation and ice mantle chemistry on dust grains proceed via adsorption, diffusion and Langmuir–Hinshelwood reactions, the same surface-science mechanisms as in heterogeneous catalysis.
registry.breaks: Interstellar grains are at ~10 K with quantum tunnelling, in ultra-low-density gas.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rotating stratified turbulence in disks and atmospheres
registry.summary: Protoplanetary-disk vortices, zonal flows and Rossby wave instability parallel geophysical vortices and jets in rotating shear flows; Coriolis dynamics governs both.
registry.breaks: Disks involve magnetorotational turbulence, dust coupling and self-gravity.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Milankovitch cycles and orbital forcing
registry.summary: Secular orbital perturbations change Earth's eccentricity, obliquity and precession, modulating insolation and driving glacial cycles.
registry.breaks: Climate response is nonlinear, with ice-sheet feedbacks.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Neutron-star asteroseismology and crust elasticity
registry.summary: Neutron-star crusts support shear modes and quakes analogous to earthquakes; magnetar giant-flare quasi-periodic oscillations are interpreted as crustal torsional modes, as in seismology.
registry.breaks: Crust is a Coulomb lattice at nuclear densities with extreme magnetic fields and superfluid coupling.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Positron annihilation and gamma detection
registry.summary: Positron annihilation producing 511 keV photons is used in PET and is observed in the Galactic 511 keV line; gamma-ray instrumentation overlaps with nuclear-medicine detectors, such as Compton cameras.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Opacities and equations of state
registry.summary: Stellar and planetary interiors require atomic opacities and equations of state computed with electronic-structure methods, including density functional and molecular dynamics for warm dense matter.
registry.breaks: Stellar plasmas are partially ionized at high temperature, beyond standard ground-state quantum chemistry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Convection and radiative-convective structure
registry.summary: Stellar envelopes and planetary atmospheres share Schwarzschild/lapse-rate stability criteria and mixing-length convection; the adiabatic gradient decides radiative versus convective layers.
registry.breaks: Stars have radiation pressure, ionization and nuclear sources; atmospheres have moisture and rotation constraints.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Solar forcing of climate
registry.summary: Solar luminosity, its variability and the faint young Sun set the incoming flux in Earth's energy balance; solar cycle irradiance variations give a small forcing term.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dynamo theory: Sun and geodynamo
registry.summary: Solar and geodynamo both arise from MHD induction in convecting conducting fluid, with rotation and helicity (alpha-omega effect) driving field generation and reversals.
registry.breaks: Solar dynamo is turbulent with strong stratification and a 11-yr cycle; geodynamo has low Rossby number and the solid inner core.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Helioseismology and seismology inversions
registry.summary: Both infer interior structure from observed wave modes and travel times via inversion: p-modes for the Sun, body and surface waves and normal modes for Earth. Methods and the mathematics of tomography parallel each other.
registry.breaks: Solar modes are stochastically excited acoustic waves in a fluid; Earth has shear waves, discontinuities and sparse source locations.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Strongly coupled plasma models for HED matter
registry.summary: One-component plasma, Yukawa fluids and molecular-dynamics results from dusty and ultracold plasmas supply structure factors and transport coefficients used to interpret X-ray Thomson scattering and equations of state.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Warm dense matter as strongly coupled plasma
registry.summary: Warm dense matter sits at coupling parameter Gamma of order 1 and degeneracy of order 1, the regime where one-component plasma models and dusty-plasma analogues apply. HED experiments probe this regime.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Alpha self-heating and ignition in ICF and MCF
registry.summary: Both routes aim at burning plasmas dominated by alpha heating, with ignition set by alpha deposition exceeding losses. They differ in the confinement mechanism: inertia, with a rho-R criterion, versus magnetic fields, with a nTtau criterion.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Burning-plasma physics across confinement schemes
registry.summary: Alpha heating, thermal-instability feedback and the Lawson criterion are shared concepts. Fuel assembly by compression is replaced by long-pulse steady confinement.
registry.breaks: ICF burn lasts about 100 ps and is limited by hydrodynamic disassembly. MCF burn is quasi-steady and limited by transport, MHD stability and exhaust.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rayleigh–Taylor instability in ICF and MHD interchange
registry.summary: Rayleigh–Taylor growth at the ablation front and in the hot spot parallels the interchange instability, where bad field curvature acts as effective gravity.
registry.breaks: Ablation stabilises ICF RT growth. The interchange instability is set by field-line curvature and pressure gradient, not by an acceleration.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ponderomotive force in wakefields
registry.summary: The ponderomotive force of a laser pulse expels electrons and excites the wake. Relativistic self-focusing and channeling guide the pulse.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Collisional absorption and ionization
registry.summary: Collisional (inverse bremsstrahlung) heating of electrons by an oscillating field and the resulting ionization avalanche follow the same physics in RF discharges and laser-produced plasmas.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Parametric instabilities in laser plasmas
registry.summary: Stimulated Raman and Brillouin scattering and two-plasmon decay are three-wave couplings of light with Langmuir and ion-acoustic waves. They limit laser coupling in ICF.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Wakefields as driven Langmuir waves
registry.summary: A wakefield is a driven plasma oscillation at the plasma frequency with phase velocity equal to the driver velocity. The wave-breaking field sets the scale of the accelerating gradient.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Streamer and dielectric-barrier breakdown
registry.summary: Townsend avalanche and streamer breakdown in atmospheric DBDs and jets follow the same Paschen breakdown physics as low-pressure processing discharges, but at much higher pd and collisionality.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Debye sheaths in processing plasmas
registry.summary: Debye shielding sets the sheath thickness at electrodes and wafers. The Bohm criterion and Child–Langmuir law determine ion energy and flux in etching and deposition.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Guiding-centre drifts in toroidal confinement
registry.summary: Grad-B and curvature drifts in a torus cause vertical charge separation, so a rotational transform is needed. Trapped-particle banana orbits arise from the mirror force and adiabatic invariants, and they set neoclassical transport.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Laboratory and fusion dynamo relaxation
registry.summary: Reversed-field pinch and spheromak relaxation show a dynamo-like conversion of helicity. Stellarators avoid the dynamo by using external coils.
registry.breaks: Stellarators are not dynamos. The mapping applies to the RFP and spheromak, not to stellarator confinement.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Quasi-symmetry and omnigeneity from guiding-centre motion
registry.summary: Quasi-symmetry makes the guiding-centre Hamiltonian depend on |B| only through a symmetric combination, so a conserved canonical momentum confines particles as in a tokamak. Omnigeneity confines trapped orbits.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Alfvén physics in tokamaks
registry.summary: Alfvén waves and continuum damping underlie fast-ion-driven Alfvén eigenmodes, and frozen-in flux constrains tokamak equilibria and disruption dynamics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: MHD equilibrium and stability of tokamaks
registry.summary: Grad–Shafranov equilibrium, the safety factor, and kink, ballooning and interchange stability come from ideal MHD energy principles. They set the Troyon beta limit and the Kruskal–Shafranov current limit.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Sawteeth, tearing modes and disruptions
registry.summary: Sawtooth crashes, neoclassical tearing modes and the thermal and current quench of disruptions involve resistive reconnection and magnetic island formation. The Kadomtsev model is a reconnection model.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gyrokinetic codes for astrophysical turbulence
registry.summary: Gyrokinetic theory built for tokamak drift waves was adapted to astrophysical plasmas, for example the Alfvénic cascade in the solar wind, using the same low-frequency anisotropic ordering.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Gyrokinetics from Vlasov theory
registry.summary: Gyrokinetics is the Vlasov–Maxwell system averaged over gyro-phase using adiabatic invariants. It keeps Landau-type wave-particle resonances and drives drift-wave turbulence and zonal flows.
registry.map: \partial_t f+\mathbf v\cdot\nabla f+\tfrac{q}{m}(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)\cdot\partial_{\mathbf v}f=0
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Landau resonance in drift-wave transport
registry.summary: Landau damping and the resonant wave-particle energy exchange set the growth and saturation of ITG and TEM modes. Collisionless zonal-flow damping, the Rosenbluth–Hinton residual, is also a kinetic effect.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Geodynamo as the source of the magnetosphere
registry.summary: Earth's magnetic field, produced by the geodynamo, forms the magnetospheric cavity. Its dipole nature sets the radiation belts and the aurora geometry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Solar dynamo and the heliospheric field
registry.summary: The solar dynamo generates the cycle-varying field that the wind drags out into the Parker spiral and the heliospheric current sheet. The cycle modulates wind structure and space weather.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: MHD waves as the low-frequency limit of plasma waves
registry.summary: Alfvén and magnetosonic waves are the low-frequency fluid limits of the kinetic cold-plasma dispersion relation, which includes whistlers and ion cyclotron waves at higher frequency.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Reconnection across space plasmas
registry.summary: Reconnection powers solar flares, coronal mass ejections and magnetospheric substorms. It also appears in the heliospheric current sheet and in particle acceleration in astrophysical sources.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Relativistic reconnection as particle accelerator
registry.summary: Relativistic reconnection in pulsar winds, jets and magnetar flares accelerates non-thermal particles through X-point and plasmoid dynamics. It competes with diffusive shock acceleration.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Dayside and tail reconnection in the Dungey cycle
registry.summary: Reconnection at the magnetopause and in the magnetotail drives the Dungey cycle, substorms and flux transfer events. MMS directly observed the electron diffusion region.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Space weather driven by reconnection
registry.summary: Southward interplanetary magnetic field opens the magnetosphere via dayside reconnection. This loads the tail and drives geomagnetic storms.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Kinetic dissipation of MHD cascades
registry.summary: At ion and electron scales the MHD cascade becomes a kinetic Alfvén wave cascade. Landau damping, in the form of transit-time damping, and cyclotron resonance remove energy, with a gyrokinetic description such as the one used in tokamaks.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Solar wind as an MHD turbulence laboratory
registry.summary: In situ spacecraft measurements of solar wind fluctuations test anisotropic Alfvénic cascade theories such as Goldreich–Sridhar and critical balance. The spectrum and its kinetic-scale break are also linked to coronal heating.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Turbulent heating of the corona and wind
registry.summary: Alfvén-wave turbulence cascades energy to ion-kinetic scales, where it heats ions by cyclotron or stochastic processes. This is a leading explanation for coronal and solar wind heating.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Streaming instabilities in shocks and cosmic rays
registry.summary: Weibel, Bell and cosmic-ray streaming instabilities amplify magnetic fields and scatter particles at collisionless shocks, enabling diffusive shock acceleration.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Adiabatic invariants and radiation belts
registry.summary: Gyration, bounce and drift motion with conserved adiabatic invariants trap particles in the van Allen belts. Violating an invariant by ULF waves or substorm injection drives radial transport and acceleration.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ring current and drifts
registry.summary: The ring current is the westward drift of ions and eastward drift of electrons, driven by gradient and curvature drifts in the dipole field. It depresses the surface field in storms, measured by Dst.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: High-pressure equations of state for planetary cores
registry.summary: Laser-shock and diamond-anvil experiments measure iron's equation of state and melting at core pressures, calibrating seismically inferred inner-core density and temperature.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Charged-particle stopping power
registry.summary: Alpha and ion energy deposition in dense plasma and Bragg-peak dose deposition in tissue both follow Bethe-type stopping physics, with plasma screening modifying stopping in hot targets.
registry.breaks: Free-electron collective response in plasmas changes stopping relative to bound-electron tissue.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Laser-driven particle and radiation sources
registry.summary: Intense lasers in plasma drive electron and ion beams and betatron or undulator-like radiation, producing compact versions of accelerator and light-source outputs.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radiation by accelerated charges
registry.summary: Betatron radiation in plasma, relativistic Thomson scattering and undulator radiation all derive from the Liénard–Liparticle radiation formula for accelerated relativistic charges.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Laser-driven ion acceleration for proton therapy
registry.summary: Target-normal sheath acceleration produces MeV-scale protons from laser-irradiated foils, targeted at Bragg-peak therapy, though current energies and reproducibility fall short.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Accelerator physics applied to plasma acceleration
registry.summary: Emittance, beta-function matching, energy spread and staging from conventional beam dynamics are the figures of merit for plasma-accelerated beams.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Plasma wakefields as compact accelerators
registry.summary: Plasma wakefield accelerators replace RF cavities with plasma waves sustaining GV/m gradients; beam dynamics, emittance and staging concepts from accelerator physics govern their beam quality.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Betatron oscillations in ion channel
registry.summary: Beam electrons in the plasma ion-channel focusing field undergo betatron oscillations with the same envelope equations as strong focusing lattices, with focusing strength set by plasma density.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Plasma-driven free-electron lasers
registry.summary: Plasma-accelerated beams and betatron emission are being used to drive FELs and X-ray sources, but the FEL's tight emittance and energy-spread demands challenge plasma beams.
registry.breaks: Plasma beams' percent-level energy spread typically exceeds the FEL Pierce parameter tolerance.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Compact accelerators for radiotherapy
registry.summary: Laser-plasma ion and electron beams are proposed as compact sources for proton therapy and FLASH radiotherapy, but stability and energy spread remain limiting.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Plasma processing for device fabrication
registry.summary: Plasma etching, deposition and ion implantation-related processes pattern and build transistors and solar cells; sheath physics sets ion energy and anisotropy of etched features.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Plasma–surface interactions and plasma catalysis
registry.summary: Plasma radicals and ions adsorb, react and sputter at surfaces, linking discharge physics to adsorption, surface reactions and plasma-assisted catalysis.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Plasma medicine and biological response
registry.summary: Cold atmospheric plasmas deliver reactive oxygen and nitrogen species to cells and tissue, so biological sensing and response physics determines therapeutic and toxic outcomes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Non-equilibrium plasma chemistry and reaction kinetics
registry.summary: Electron-impact dissociation, vibrational excitation and radical reactions in cold plasmas follow state-resolved rate theory and potential-energy-surface concepts, with electron temperature far above gas temperature.
registry.breaks: Rate theories assuming a single Boltzmann temperature fail when electron and gas temperatures differ strongly.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Surface chemistry underlying plasma etching
registry.summary: Etch and deposition rates and selectivity are set by adsorption, ion-enhanced surface reactions and sputter yields studied in surface science.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Neutral beam injectors as ion accelerators
registry.summary: Neutral beam heating of fusion plasmas relies on ion source, electrostatic acceleration and neutraliser technology developed in accelerator physics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Hamiltonian field-line flow and storage-ring dynamics
registry.summary: Magnetic field lines in toroidal devices form a Hamiltonian system with islands and KAM surfaces, as do particle orbits in storage rings with nonlinear resonances.
registry.breaks: Field-line flow has no physical particle dynamics, and rotational transform plays the role of tune.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Superconducting magnets and RF technology
registry.summary: Tokamaks and accelerators share superconducting magnet technology (Nb3Sn, NbTi, HTS) and RF heating or klystron sources, with cross-fertilised cryogenics and power systems.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Drift waves and Rossby waves
registry.summary: Drift waves in magnetized plasma obey the Hasegawa–Mima equation, mathematically identical to the Charney–Hasegawa–Mima quasi-geostrophic equation, with zonal flows paralleling atmospheric jets.
registry.breaks: Plasma drift waves involve adiabatic electron response and finite Larmor radius, with no direct atmospheric counterpart.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Planetary dynamos in Earth science
registry.summary: Earth's field generation and reversals are a dynamo problem in rotating convecting conducting fluid, linking geophysics to MHD dynamo theory.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rotating convective flows and quasi-geostrophy
registry.summary: Core convection under rapid rotation is Taylor–Proudman constrained, mirroring geostrophic balance and Rossby-wave dynamics in the atmosphere, with Lorentz force replacing part of the Coriolis balance.
registry.breaks: Magnetic field and Lorentz force alter the force balance (magnetostrophic), and there is no atmospheric analogue of induction.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Rotating stratified turbulence
registry.summary: Ocean and core flows both exhibit rotation-dominated turbulence with inverse cascades and large-scale coherent structures, offering shared numerical and scaling tools.
registry.breaks: Core flows are electrically conducting with Lorentz feedback, absent in oceans.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Geodynamo and the liquid outer core
registry.summary: Earth's magnetic field is sustained by convective dynamo action in the liquid iron outer core, whose structure and inner-core growth are constrained by seismology.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Seismic constraints on dynamo core
registry.summary: Seismic models give core radius, inner-core size and density jump, supplying boundary conditions and energy budget for geodynamo simulations.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Alfvén waves and Rossby waves
registry.summary: Magnetic tension restoring Alfvén waves parallels the Coriolis restoring force of inertial and Rossby waves, and both reduce to similar dispersion structures in rotating or magnetized media.
registry.breaks: Alfvén waves are non-dispersive, while Rossby and inertial waves are strongly dispersive and anisotropic differently.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Turbulent cascades in anisotropic media
registry.summary: Anisotropic MHD cascades and quasi-2D geostrophic turbulence both develop strong anisotropy and inverse or dual transfers under a strong organizing field or rotation.
registry.breaks: MHD has forward energy cascade in 3D with critical balance, differing from atmospheric inverse energy cascade.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Space charge and beam plasma physics
registry.summary: Intense charged beams behave as non-neutral plasmas with Debye length, plasma frequency, space-charge tune shift and Coulomb-crystal ordering in cooled ion beams.
registry.breaks: Beams are non-neutral and lack quasi-neutrality, so screening and collective response differ from true plasmas.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Vlasov description of beams
registry.summary: Collective beam dynamics uses the Vlasov equation in phase space, with Landau damping of coherent modes via tune spread, equivalent to plasma Landau damping.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Beam instabilities as streaming instabilities
registry.summary: Two-stream, Weibel and head-tail or microwave instabilities in beams share the kinetic-instability machinery of plasma physics, including Landau damping used to stabilise bunches.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ionospheric and radiative propagation in plasma
registry.summary: Electromagnetic wave propagation in ionised media, with plasma frequency cutoff, underlies ionospheric reflection and remote sensing, alongside atmospheric radiative physics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Adiabatic invariants and magnetic focusing
registry.summary: Gyration, mirror trapping and adiabatic invariants in plasma map onto betatron motion, Courant–Snyder invariants and magnetic confinement in storage rings and traps.
registry.breaks: Accelerator lattices use alternating-gradient focusing with no plasma-style collective response.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: SRF cavities and superconducting magnets with SQUIDs
registry.summary: Superconducting technology (niobium, cryogenics, flux control) is shared by accelerator cavities/magnets and SQUID sensors; SRF cavities also serve as quantum and dark-matter sensors.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Superconducting magnets in MRI and accelerators
registry.summary: NbTi superconducting magnet and cryogenic technology developed for accelerators is the basis of clinical MRI magnets; both need field homogeneity and quench protection.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Cyclotron isotope production for PET
registry.summary: Medical cyclotrons produce short-lived PET radioisotopes such as 18F and 11C, linking accelerator sources and targets to radiopharmaceutical supply.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Linacs and cyclotrons for radiotherapy
registry.summary: Medical linacs, proton cyclotrons and synchrotrons, and superconducting magnets/RF are accelerator technology deployed clinically; the Bragg-peak beam delivery rests on accelerator design.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radiotherapy demands on accelerator design
registry.summary: Radiotherapy drives compact, reliable accelerator design: energy variation, FLASH dose rates, gantry-mounted superconducting magnets for proton and carbon-ion therapy.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Resonances and chaos in beams and fluids
registry.summary: Nonlinear resonances, Hamiltonian chaos and dynamic aperture in storage rings parallel Rossby-wave resonant interactions and predictability limits in atmospheric flow.
registry.breaks: Beam dynamics is conservative Hamiltonian; atmosphere is dissipative and forced.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Beam optics in proton therapy gantries
registry.summary: Twiss parameters, emittance and focusing lattices determine spot size, beam transport and pencil-beam scanning in proton and carbon-ion therapy beamlines and gantries.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Synchrotron characterisation of battery materials
registry.summary: Operando X-ray diffraction, absorption and tomography at synchrotrons track phase transformations and degradation in electrodes and solid electrolytes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Free-electron laser vs. stimulated emission lasers
registry.summary: FEL gain from SASE microbunching is collective stimulated emission by free electrons, analogous to semiconductor laser gain but without bound-state inversion.
registry.breaks: FEL gain is classical bunching in an undulator, tunable and not tied to band gaps or carrier recombination.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Synchrotron crystallography and XFEL structures
registry.summary: Synchrotron macromolecular crystallography, SAXS and XFEL serial femtosecond crystallography supply most protein structures and time-resolved dynamics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: X-ray and ultrafast spectroscopy at light sources
registry.summary: Synchrotron and FEL pulses drive X-ray absorption, photoelectron and pump-probe ultrafast spectroscopies of molecules, extending optical multidimensional spectroscopy to X-ray wavelengths.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Operando X-ray probes of catalysts and surfaces
registry.summary: Ambient-pressure XPS, grazing-incidence diffraction and XAS at synchrotrons characterise surface structure and working catalysts in situ.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Synchrotron phase-contrast and microtomography
registry.summary: Synchrotron coherent beams enable phase-contrast imaging and microCT, the research precursor of coherence-based X-ray contrast and CT reconstruction methods.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: First-principles design of energy materials
registry.summary: DFT and wavefunction methods predict electrode voltages, ion barriers, thermoelectric band structures and perovskite properties for materials screening.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Surface chemistry of electrodes and catalysts
registry.summary: Adsorption, interfaces and electrocatalysis govern battery SEI layers, hydrogen storage and fuel cells, linking surface science to energy materials.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Atom-interferometer gravimetry for geophysics
registry.summary: Atom-interferometric and superconducting gravimeters measure gravity variations used in geodesy, mass transport and subsurface density mapping.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: MRI and NV/atomic magnetometry share spin resonance
registry.summary: MRI relies on nuclear magnetic resonance and Bloch dynamics; NV and atomic magnetometers use the same spin-precession and Ramsey/spin-echo sequences, and SQUIDs enable ultra-low-field MRI and MEG.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Photovoltaic carriers and electron-transfer kinetics
registry.summary: Charge separation and recombination in organic and perovskite cells follow Marcus-type electron transfer, paralleling band-based drift-diffusion treatments.
registry.breaks: Inorganic crystalline cells use delocalised bands rather than hopping.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Semiconductor photodetectors in PET
registry.summary: Silicon photomultipliers and CdZnTe detectors in time-of-flight PET and gamma cameras are semiconductor p-n junction devices operated in avalanche regimes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Membrane elasticity and protein-lipid coupling
registry.summary: Helfrich bending elasticity governs membrane deformation by proteins, channels and motors; mechanosensitive channels bridge molecular structure and membrane mechanics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Elastography and tissue mechanics
registry.summary: Ultrasound and MR elastography measure shear-wave speed to infer tissue stiffness, the continuum viscoelasticity that cell and tissue mechanics studies as a driver of mechanotransduction.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Electronic structure meets force fields and ML structure
registry.summary: Quantum chemistry parametrises force fields and QM/MM methods for biomolecules; ML potentials and structure predictors learn from such data.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Electron transfer in proteins and Marcus theory
registry.summary: Marcus theory of electron transfer governs biological redox chains in respiration and photosynthesis, with reorganisation energy and tunnelling through protein.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Energy landscapes and rate theory
registry.summary: Protein folding landscapes and potential energy surfaces share Kramers/transition-state rate theory, barrier crossing and funnel concepts; force spectroscopy uses Bell-Evans extensions.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Noise and kinetic proofreading at single molecules
registry.summary: Gene-expression noise and kinetic proofreading are stochastic-kinetics ideas observed directly by single-molecule counting and enzyme-turnover measurements.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Feedbacks and tipping in living and climate systems
registry.summary: Feedback loops, bistability and noise-induced transitions describe both gene circuits and climate tipping elements such as AMOC collapse and albedo feedback.
registry.breaks: Climate has no replicates and poorly constrained dynamics, unlike controlled biological circuits.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Single-molecule FRET and spectroscopy
registry.summary: Single-molecule fluorescence and FRET descend from molecular spectroscopy: Förster dipole coupling, photophysics, and Raman or single-molecule detection, with time-resolved methods probing conformational dynamics.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Single-molecule force spectroscopy and barrier crossing
registry.summary: Pulling experiments measure barrier heights and rates of unfolding, interpreted via Kramers theory and Bell-Evans models; Jarzynski and Crooks relations recover free energies.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radiation damage to DNA at molecular scale
registry.summary: Radiobiology of strand breaks and repair, and LET dependence of carbon ions, connects to single-molecule studies of DNA mechanics and repair enzymes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Optical tweezers and fluorescence microscopy lineage
registry.summary: Biomedical optics and single-molecule biophysics share fluorescence, interferometric detection and light-scattering techniques; OCT coherence gating parallels interferometric nanoscale tracking.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Molecular absorption and the greenhouse effect
registry.summary: Greenhouse forcing arises from vibrational-rotational absorption bands of CO2, H2O and CH4; line strengths and selection rules from spectroscopy feed radiative transfer codes.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Circulation, convection and cloud feedback
registry.summary: Hadley circulation, convection and jet shifts control water vapour, lapse rate and cloud feedbacks and thus climate sensitivity.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Geostrophic rotating stratified flow
registry.summary: Atmosphere and ocean obey the same rotating, stratified primitive equations: geostrophic balance, Rossby waves, Ekman layers and baroclinic instability, with western boundary currents mirroring jets.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Geodynamo and rotating convection
registry.summary: Core convection in the geodynamo and atmospheric or oceanic convection are rotating, buoyancy-driven flows controlled by Rossby, Ekman and Rayleigh numbers with Taylor-column constraints.
registry.breaks: Geodynamo includes magnetic Lorentz forces and a much lower Ekman number.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Ocean heat uptake and climate response
registry.summary: Ocean heat uptake and AMOC set the transient climate response and delay equilibrium warming given by radiative forcing and feedbacks.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Tsunami and ocean wave propagation from earthquakes
registry.summary: Seafloor earthquakes generate tsunamis and tides and waves share shallow-water wave dynamics, linking source seismology to ocean wave propagation.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Tomography across scales
registry.summary: Seismic travel-time tomography and CT reconstruction solve the same linear inverse problem with regularisation and iterative solvers.
registry.breaks: Seismic rays bend and coverage is sparse, unlike controlled CT geometry.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Seismic and ultrasound wave imaging
registry.summary: Seismic tomography and ultrasound imaging both invert travel times and scattered waves in elastic media; elastography uses shear waves just as seismology does, and full-waveform inversion appears in both.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Tomographic reconstruction shared by CT and PET
registry.summary: CT and PET/SPECT both reconstruct images from line integrals via Radon transform, filtered back-projection and iterative statistical methods such as MLEM; PET adds attenuation correction from CT.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Image-guided radiotherapy and treatment planning
registry.summary: CT supplies electron density for dose calculation and cone-beam CT, MRI-linacs and PET guide targeting; image quality and dose trade-offs are shared.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Image quality, SNR and resolution across modalities
registry.summary: Resolution, contrast-to-noise and point-spread/MTF frameworks, plus Fourier-domain k-space and OCT sampling, unify MRI, ultrasound and optical imaging; photoacoustic reconstruction resembles tomography.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

registry.name: Radionuclide therapy and dosimetry
registry.summary: Internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy uses the same absorbed-dose, Monte Carlo transport and radiobiology as external beam; PET/SPECT quantify the uptake.
registry.review: interim: not yet reviewed by a specialist

themes.title: Analogue gravity — horizons in fluids and condensates
themes.summary: Sound in a flowing fluid propagates on an effective curved spacetime; where the flow outruns sound there is a horizon that should emit thermal phonons — a laboratory test of the kinematics behind Hawking radiation.

themes.title: Black-hole thermodynamics, information and holography
themes.summary: Black holes have a temperature and an entropy, which puts G, ħ, c and k_B in one formula and turns gravity into a problem of statistical mechanics and quantum information — culminating in holography, where spacetime geometry encodes entanglement.

themes.title: Neutron stars — where six branches meet
themes.summary: A neutron star cannot be described by any one branch — general relativity sets its structure, nuclear and particle physics its equation of state, condensed matter its crust and superfluids, plasma physics its magnetosphere, and astrophysics and gravitational waves are how we measure it.

themes.title: Pairing across scales — metals, nuclei, neutron stars and cold atoms
themes.summary: BCS pairing is a property of any degenerate Fermi system with an attraction near its Fermi surface; the same gap equation describes superconductors (meV), atomic nuclei and neutron-star matter (MeV) and ultracold Fermi gases (nK).

themes.title: Path integrals — quantum amplitudes and partition functions
themes.summary: Rotating time to imaginary values turns Feynman's sum over histories into a Boltzmann-weighted partition function, so quantum field theory in D dimensions becomes classical statistical mechanics in D dimensions — the basis of lattice QCD, quantum Monte Carlo and instanton physics.

themes.title: The renormalization group and universality
themes.summary: One idea for two fields — couplings that run with energy in quantum field theory, and critical exponents shared by unrelated systems in statistical mechanics — joined exactly by the Euclidean field theory ↔ statistical model correspondence.

themes.title: Symmetry breaking and the Higgs–Anderson mechanism
themes.summary: A superconductor and the electroweak vacuum are the same kind of state — a condensate that hides a gauge symmetry, gives the gauge field a mass and turns the would-be Goldstone mode into its longitudinal polarization.

themes.title: Geometric phases, gauge fields and band topology
themes.summary: The Berry phase of a slowly transported quantum state has the mathematics of a gauge field; integrated over a crystal's Brillouin zone it becomes a quantized Chern number — the quantum Hall conductance — and its monopoles are Weyl points.
